## ===== blueprint/src/chapter/Complexity/Diagonalization/Ladner.tex =====

\section{Diagonalization --- Ladner}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.Diagonalization.Ladner
This module develops Ladner's theorem by delayed diagonalization: it pads SAT by a
slowly growing index function $H$, defined as the least machine index that correctly
recognises the padded language on short inputs within its indexed polynomial clock,
and shows that the padded language $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ is neither in $\mathsf{P}$ nor
$\mathsf{NP}$-hard when $\mathsf{P}\ne\mathsf{NP}$. It also supplies the padding parser,
the shrinking argument that turns a reduction from SAT into a polynomial-time decider,
and the polynomial-time preparation of the bounded candidate test.

\begin{definition}[Padded SAT language]
\lean{Complexity.padSAT}
\label{Complexity.padSAT}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT}
For a function $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, the padded language $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ is the set
of Boolean strings of the form $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$:
a satisfiable encoded formula, followed by a single separator bit $0$, followed by
$|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}$ ones.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in padded SAT]
\lean{Complexity.mem_padSAT_iff}
\label{Complexity.mem_padSAT_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Complexity.padSAT}
\difficulty{1}
For every function $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and every Boolean string $y$, the string $y$
belongs to the padded language $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ if and only if there is $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$
with $y=\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Padded membership depends on shorter exponents]
\lean{Complexity.padSAT_congr}
\label{Complexity.padSAT_congr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.mem_padSAT_iff, Complexity.padSAT}
\difficulty{3}
For functions $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, let $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ be the set of strings
$\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. Let $h,g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$
and let $y$ be a Boolean string such that $h(m)=g(m)$ for every $m<|y|$. Then
$y\in\mathrm{SAT}_h$ if and only if $y\in\mathrm{SAT}_g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Ladner's machine enumeration]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerMachine}
\label{Complexity.ladnerMachine}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.expCode, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM}
For $i\in\mathbb N$, the machine $M_i$ is the finite-state Boolean Turing machine obtained
by decoding the little-endian binary digits of $i$ with a fixed uniform machine code for
one-work-tape Boolean machines (a code whose decoded machines admit a uniformly clocked
simulator).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unfolding the machine enumeration]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerMachine_eq}
\label{Complexity.ladnerMachine_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.expCode, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM}
\difficulty{1}
For every $i\in\mathbb N$, the $i$-th machine $M_i$ of Ladner's enumeration equals the
finite-state Boolean machine obtained by decoding the binary digits of $i$ with the fixed
uniform machine code.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Ladner's delayed index function]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerH}
\label{Complexity.ladnerH}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.padSAT, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
Write $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$), let $M_i$ be the machine decoded
from the binary digits of $i$, and say that $M$ accepts $x$ within $t$ steps if it halts
within $t$ steps with output the single bit $1$. The function $H:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ is
defined by strong recursion: $H(n)$ is the least $i<\ell(\ell(n))$ such that for every
Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and
only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_{H'}$, where $H'$ agrees with $H$ below $n$ and is $0$ elsewhere;
if no such $i$ exists, $H(n)=\ell(\ell(n))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Defining equation of the delayed index]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerH_eq}
\label{Complexity.ladnerH_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.padSAT_congr, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
\difficulty{5}
Let $H$ be Ladner's delayed index function, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$, $M_i$ the
machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$, and $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ the strings
$\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{H(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. For every $n$, $H(n)$ is the
least $i<\ell(\ell(n))$ such that for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$
halts within $i\,|x|^i$ steps with output $1$ if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_H$; if no
such $i$ exists, $H(n)=\ell(\ell(n))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Double-logarithmic cap on the delayed index]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerH_le}
\label{Complexity.ladnerH_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.ladnerH_eq}
\difficulty{3}
Let $H$ be Ladner's delayed index function. For every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$H(n)\le\lfloor\log_2\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor\rfloor$ (with $\log_2 0$ read as $0$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The Ladner language]
\lean{Complexity.SAT_H}
\label{Complexity.SAT_H}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.padSAT}
The language $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ is SAT padded by Ladner's delayed index function $H$: it
consists of the strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{H(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{definition}

\label{Complexity.SAT_H_eq}
\leanok

padded language of all strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{H(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Empty word is never padded]

\end{theorem}

\leanok

\leanok

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A polynomial decider yields a correct index]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_correct_index}
\label{Complexity.ladner_correct_index}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.SAT_H, Complexity.SAT_H_eq, Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.ladner_indexed_deadline, Complexity.ladner_pad_nil, Complexity.ladner_padded_index, Complexity.mem_P_iff_one_work_tape, Complexity.padSAT, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.decidesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.not_computesInTime_zero, Turing.FinTM.toCodeTM, Turing.FinTM.toCodeTM_computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator_of_mem, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator_of_not_mem}

$x$, $M_i$ halts within $i\,|x|^i$ steps with output $1$ if and only if

\begin{theorem}[A globally correct index bounds the selector]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_selector_bound}
\label{Complexity.ladner_selector_bound}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.ladnerH_eq, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.padSAT, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be Ladner's delayed index function, $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ the corresponding padded SAT
language, and $M_i$ the machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$. Suppose $i$ is an

\begin{theorem}[Delayed index is bounded if the language is in P]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerH_bounded_of_mem_P}
\label{Complexity.ladnerH_bounded_of_mem_P}
\leanok

\begin{theorem}[Preparing a fixed polynomial clock]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_fixed_clock_preparation}

\begin{definition}[Padding parser]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_parse}
\label{Complexity.ladner_parse}
\leanok
The padding parser takes a Boolean string $y$. If $y$ contains a $0$, it returns the pair
$(p,t)$ with $y=p\,0\,1^t$, where $p$ is the prefix before the last $0$ of $y$ and $t$ is
the number of ones after it; if $y$ contains no $0$, it fails.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Padding syntax test]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_padSyntax}
\label{Complexity.ladner_padSyntax}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse}
For a function $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and a Boolean string $y$, the padding syntax test
is the bit that is $1$ exactly when $y$ can be written as $p\,0\,1^t$ (with $p$ the prefix
before the last $0$) and $t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Serialized padding parse]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_parseWord}
\label{Complexity.ladner_parseWord}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ denote the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings and
$\mathrm{bin}(t)$ the binary expansion of $t$. For a Boolean string $y$, the serialized
parse is the empty string if $y$ contains no $0$, and otherwise is
$\langle 1,\langle p,\mathrm{bin}(t)\rangle\rangle$, where $y=p\,0\,1^t$ with $p$ the
prefix before the last $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One shrinking round]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_smallSAT, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with
components $\pi_1(S),\pi_2(S)$ of a string $S$, and for a property $Q$ let $[Q]$ be the bit
that is $1$ exactly when $Q$ holds. For $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, a string function $f$ and
$B,K\in\mathbb N$, the shrinking round sends a state $S$ to $S$ itself if $\pi_1(S)$ is
nonempty; otherwise, with $x=\pi_2(S)$, it returns $\langle[\,|x|<K\wedge x\in\mathrm{SAT}\,],
\varepsilon\rangle$ if $|x|<K$; $\langle 0,\varepsilon\rangle$ if $f(x)$ contains no $0$, or
if $f(x)=p\,0\,1^t$ (split at the last $0$) with $t\ne|p|^{h(|p|)}$; and otherwise
$\langle[\,|p|<B\wedge p\in\mathrm{SAT}\,],\varepsilon\rangle$ if $|p|<B$ and
$\langle\varepsilon,p\rangle$ if $|p|\ge B$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Shrinking invariant]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv}
\label{Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings. For Boolean
strings $x$ and $S$, the shrinking invariant holds when either $S=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$
for some string $y$ with $|y|\le|x|$ and $y\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$, or
$S=\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle$ for a single bit $b$ with $b=1\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Shrinking measure]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrinkMeasure}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrinkMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1(S),\pi_2(S)$ be the components of a Boolean string $S$ decoded as a
self-delimiting pair (empty if $S$ is not a pair). The shrinking measure of $S$ is
$\mu(S)=|\pi_2(S)|+1$ if $\pi_1(S)$ is empty, and $\mu(S)=0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

$\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. If $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ is
$\mathsf{NP}$-hard, then there is a polynomial-time computable string function $f$ such that
$x\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff f(x)\in\mathrm{SAT}_h$ for every Boolean string $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Large exponents force short prefixes]

$r\ge B$, $n\ge A\,2^d+2$, $m\ge B$, and $m^{h(m)}\le A\,(n+1)^d$. Then $m^2\le n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reductions into padded SAT shrink prefixes]

\begin{theorem}[Correct terminal answers respect the shrinking ledger]

\leanok

\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv, Complexity.ladner_pad_membership, Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_shrinkMeasure, Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep, Complexity.ladner_shrink_terminal_result, Complexity.ladner_smallSAT, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a string function with
$x\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff f(x)\in\mathrm{SAT}_h$ for all $x$ (where $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ is the set of
strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$), and let $B,K$ with
$K\ge 2$ be such that $|p|<|x|$ whenever $|x|\ge K$, $f(x)=p\,0\,1^t$ (split at the last $0$),
$t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$ and $|p|\ge B$. Let $\sigma$ be the shrinking round for $h,f,B,K$, $\mu$ the
shrinking measure ($|\pi_2(S)|+1$ if $\pi_1(S)$ is empty, else $0$) and $I_x$ the shrinking
invariant ($S=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$ with $|y|\le|x|$ and the same SAT answer as $x$,
or $S=\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle$ with $b=1\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$). Then for all strings
$x,S$ with $I_x(S)$: $I_x(\sigma(S))$ holds, $\mu(\sigma(S))<\mu(S)$ whenever $\mu(S)>0$, and
$\sigma(S)=S$ whenever $\mu(S)=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial shrinking state satisfies the invariant]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrink_initial}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrink_initial}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings. For every
Boolean string $x$, the state $\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle$ satisfies the shrinking
invariant for $x$: there is $y$ with $\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$,
$|y|\le|x|$, and $y\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear size bound along the shrinking orbit]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrink_orbit_size}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrink_orbit_size}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.iterate_invariant, Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv, Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep, Complexity.ladner_shrink_initial, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, $f$ a string function, $B,K\in\mathbb N$, and $\sigma$ the
shrinking round for $h,f,B,K$. For strings $x,S$, let $I_x(S)$ be the shrinking invariant:
$S=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$ with $|y|\le|x|$ and $y\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$,
or $S=\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle$ for a bit $b$ with $b=1\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$. If
$I_x(S)$ implies $I_x(\sigma(S))$ for all $x,S$, then for every string $x$ and every
$j\in\mathbb N$, $|\sigma^{j}(\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle)|\le 4(|x|+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Shrinking orbit ends with the SAT answer]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrink_final_readout}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrink_final_readout}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.iterate_invariant, Complexity.BinArith.iterate_measure_eq_zero, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv, Complexity.ladner_shrinkMeasure, Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep, Complexity.ladner_shrink_initial, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, $f$ a string function, $B,K\in\mathbb N$, $\sigma$ the
shrinking round for $h,f,B,K$, $\mu$ the shrinking measure ($|\pi_2(S)|+1$ if $\pi_1(S)$ is
empty, else $0$) and $I_x$ the shrinking invariant for $x$. Suppose that for all strings
$x,S$ with $I_x(S)$, $I_x(\sigma(S))$ holds, $\mu(\sigma(S))<\mu(S)$ whenever $\mu(S)>0$, and
$\sigma(S)=S$ whenever $\mu(S)=0$. Then for every string $x$, the first component of
$\sigma^{|x|+1}(\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle)$ is the one-bit string that is $1$ exactly when
$x\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Shrinking puts SAT in P]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrinking_transfer}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrinking_transfer}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_iterate, Complexity.P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep, Complexity.mem_P_of_test, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_id, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, $f$ a string function, $B,K\in\mathbb N$, and $\sigma$ the
shrinking round for $h,f,B,K$, with $\langle u,v\rangle$ the pairing and $\pi_1$ its first
component. Suppose $\sigma$ is polynomial-time computable,
$|\sigma^{j}(\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle)|\le 4(|x|+1)$ for every string $x$ and every
$j\le|x|+1$, and $\pi_1(\sigma^{|x|+1}(\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle))$ is the one-bit string
that is $1$ exactly when $x\in\mathrm{SAT}$, for every $x$. Then $\mathrm{SAT}\in\mathsf{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Numeric memo values]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_values}
\label{Complexity.ladner_values}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.decWords, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
For a Boolean string $T$, decode $T$ as a list of strings by repeatedly taking the first
component of a self-delimiting pair and continuing with the second component until the
remainder is empty; the memo values of $T$ are the natural numbers whose little-endian
binary expansions are these strings, in order.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Enumeration of short words]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shortWords}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shortWords}
\leanok
For every $a\in\mathbb N$, the short-word list of $a$ is the list whose entries are, for
$r=0,1,\dots,2^{a+1}-2$ in order, the little-endian binary expansion of $r+1$ with its last
(most significant) bit deleted.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Stage selection from memo values]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_stage}
\label{Complexity.ladner_stage}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.padSAT, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
Let $v=(v_0,\dots,v_{n-1})$ be a list of natural numbers of length $n$, write
$\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$), let $M_i$ be the machine decoded from
the binary digits of $i$, and let $\mathrm{SAT}_v$ be SAT padded by the exponent function
$m\mapsto v_m$ (read as $0$ for $m\ge n$). The stage value of $v$ is the least
$i<\ell(\ell(n))$ such that for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ halts
within $i\,|x|^i$ steps with output $1$ if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_v$; if no such $i$
exists, it is $\ell(\ell(n))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Candidate index test]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_candidate}
\label{Complexity.ladner_candidate}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.ladner_values, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$, and $M_i$ the machine decoded
from the binary digits of $i$. For a string $S$ put $n=|\pi_1(S)|$,
$i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))$ and $v$ the memo values of $\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$. The candidate
bit of $S$ is $1$ exactly when $v$ has length $n$, $i<\ell(\ell(n))$, and for every string $x$
with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ halts within $i\,|x|^i$ steps with output $1$ if and only if $x$
lies in SAT padded by $m\mapsto v_m$ (with $v_m=0$ out of range).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Valid simulator query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_validQuery}
\label{Complexity.ladner_validQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. A string $S$ is a valid
query when $\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and
$|\pi_2(\pi_2(S))|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Code of a guarded query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryCode}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryCode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladner_validQuery, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, $\mathrm{bin}(i)$ the canonical binary expansion of $i$, and
$\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. For a string $S$, the query code is
$\mathrm{bin}(\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S))))$ if $\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))<
\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and $|\pi_2(\pi_2(S))|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$, and the empty string
otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Input of a guarded query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryInput}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryInput}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_validQuery, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. For a string $S$, the
query input is $\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$ if $\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and
$|\pi_2(\pi_2(S))|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$, and the empty string otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Deadline of a guarded query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryDeadline}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryDeadline}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladner_validQuery, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. For a string $S$ put
$i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))$ and $x=\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$. The query deadline is $i\,|x|^i$
if $i<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and $|x|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$, and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Serialized guarded query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryPrep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryPrep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_queryCode, Complexity.ladner_queryDeadline, Complexity.ladner_queryInput, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing with components $\pi_1,\pi_2$,
$\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of a little-endian binary word, $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ the binary
expansion of $n$, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. For a string $S$ put
$i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))$ and $x=\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$. The serialized query is
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(i\,|x|^i),\mathrm{bin}(i)\rangle,x\rangle$ when
$i<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and $|x|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$, and
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(0),\varepsilon\rangle,\varepsilon\rangle$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Candidate context guard]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_ctxGuard}
\label{Complexity.ladner_ctxGuard}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladner_values, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. A string $C$ passes the
context guard when $|\pi_1(C)|$ equals the number of memo values encoded by
$\pi_2(\pi_2(C))$ and $\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(C)))<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(C)|))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Verdict on a single ranked word]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_wordVerdict}
\label{Complexity.ladner_wordVerdict}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.ladner_ctxGuard, Complexity.ladner_values, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$, and $M_i$ the machine decoded
from the binary digits of $i$. For a string $C$ and $r\in\mathbb N$, let $x$ be the binary
expansion of $r+1$ with its last bit deleted, $i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(C)))$ and $v$ the
memo values of $\pi_2(\pi_2(C))$. The verdict is $1$ exactly when $C$ passes the context
guard ($|\pi_1(C)|$ equals the length of $v$ and $i<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(C)|))$),
$|x|\le\ell(|\pi_1(C)|)$, and $M_i$ halts within $i\,|x|^i$ steps with output $1$ if and only
if $x$ lies in SAT padded by $m\mapsto v_m$ (with $v_m=0$ out of range).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Number of short-input queries]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryCount}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryCount}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD}
For a Boolean string $C$ with first pair component $\pi_1(C)$, the query count is
$2^{\lfloor\log_2|\pi_1(C)|\rfloor+1}-1$ (with $\log_2 0$ read as $0$).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial state of the candidate scan]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_testInit}
\label{Complexity.ladner_testInit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_queryCount, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with first
component $\pi_1$. For a string $C$, with $q=2^{\lfloor\log_2|\pi_1(C)|\rfloor+1}-1$, the
initial scan state is $\langle C,\langle 1^{q},\langle\varepsilon,1\rangle\rangle\rangle$,
recording the context, the remaining count in unary, the empty completed rank, and the
conjunction flag $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One step of the candidate scan]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_testStep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_testStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_wordVerdict, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing with components $\pi_1,\pi_2$. For a
state $S$, put $C=\pi_1(S)$, $m=\pi_1(\pi_2(S))$, $k=\pi_1(\pi_2(\pi_2(S)))$ and
$g=\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(S)))$. If $m$ is empty the step returns $S$; otherwise it returns
$\langle C,\langle m',\langle k1,c\rangle\rangle\rangle$, where $m'$ is $m$ with its first
bit removed, $k1$ is $k$ with a $1$ appended, and $c$ is the one-bit string
$(g_0\wedge V(C,|k|))$, with $g_0$ the first bit of $g$ ($0$ if $g$ is empty) and $V(C,r)$
the single-word verdict of $C$ at rank $r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Output of the candidate scan]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_testOut}
\label{Complexity.ladner_testOut}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairSndD}
For a Boolean string $S$, with $\pi_2$ the second component of a self-delimiting pair, the
scan output is $\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(S)))$, the conjunction flag of a scan state.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Short-word enumeration is complete]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shortWords_complete}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shortWords_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le, Complexity.LogProg.lt_two_pow_bits, Complexity.ladner_bits_prepend, Complexity.ladner_shortWords}
\difficulty{5}
For $a\in\mathbb N$, let $W_a$ be the list of the little-endian binary expansions of
$r+1$, with the last bit deleted, for $0\le r\le 2^{a+1}-2$. Then for every Boolean string
$x$, $x$ occurs in $W_a$ if and only if $|x|\le a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the short-word scan]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shortWords_count}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shortWords_count}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_shortWords}
\difficulty{3}
For $a\in\mathbb N$, let $W_a$ be the list of the little-endian binary expansions of $r+1$,
with the last bit deleted, for $0\le r\le 2^{a+1}-2$. For every $n\in\mathbb N$, the list
$W_{\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor}$ has length at most $2(n+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Squares are bounded by powers of two]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_square_le_power}
\label{Complexity.ladner_square_le_power}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $k$, the square of $k$ is at most $2^{k+1}$, that is,
$k^2\le 2^{k+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cubic bound on short indexed deadlines]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_short_deadline}
\label{Complexity.ladner_short_deadline}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_square_le_power}
\difficulty{5}
Write $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$). For natural numbers $n,i,m$ with
$i<\ell(\ell(n))$ and $m\le\ell(n)$, we have $i\,m^i\le n^3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial envelope of the simulation cost]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_numeric_envelope}
\label{Complexity.ladner_numeric_envelope}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_short_deadline, Turing.length_bits_le_self}
\difficulty{4}
Write $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$) and $\mathrm{bin}(i)$ for the
binary expansion of $i$. For natural numbers $D,n,i$ and a Boolean string $x$ with
$i<\ell(\ell(n))$ and $|x|\le\ell(n)$,
\[
  D\,\bigl(|\mathrm{bin}(i)|+|x|+i\,|x|^i+1\bigr)^D\;\le\;D\,4^D\,(n+1)^{3D}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absorbing a composition clock]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_composition_clock}
\label{Complexity.ladner_composition_clock}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For all natural numbers $C,q,A,e,n$,
\[
  2C\,(n+1)^q+A\,(n+1)^e+2\;\le\;(2C+A+2)\,(n+1)^{\max(q,e)}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Floor logarithm via binary length]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_log_eq_bits_length}
\label{Complexity.ladner_log_eq_bits_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_eq_log}
\difficulty{3}
For every $n\in\mathbb N$, $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor=|\mathrm{bin}(n)|-1$, where $\mathrm{bin}(n)$
is the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$ (empty for $n=0$), $\lfloor\log_2 0\rfloor$
is read as $0$, and subtraction is truncated at $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Binary floor logarithm is polynomial-time]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_binary_log_FP}
\label{Complexity.ladner_binary_log_FP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_normBits, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_sub, Complexity.BinArith.sub_pairEncode, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.ladner_lengthBits_FP, Complexity.ladner_log_eq_bits_length, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const}
\difficulty{3}
For a Boolean string $w$ let $\mathrm{val}(w)$ denote the value of a little-endian binary word $w$ (high-order zeros allowed), and let $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$. The map
$w\mapsto\mathrm{bin}(\lfloor\log_2\mathrm{val}(w)\rfloor)$, with $\log_2 0$ read as $0$, is
computable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential-time SAT decider from a linear verifier]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_short_SAT_machine}
\label{Complexity.ladner_short_SAT_machine}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.exists_proj_decider, Complexity.mem_P_iff, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime}
\difficulty{4}
Suppose there is a language $V\in\mathsf P$ such that for every Boolean string $x$, $x\in\mathrm{SAT}$ if and only if $xu\in V$ for some Boolean string $u$ with $|u|=|x|+1$. Then there are $a,d,b\in\mathbb N$ and a finite-state Boolean Turing machine $E$ that
decides SAT within $b\,2^{m+1}\bigl(a\,(2m+2)^d+(2m+2)^2\bigr)$ steps on every input of length
$m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Short SAT search clock is polynomial]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_short_SAT_envelope}
\label{Complexity.ladner_short_SAT_envelope}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For all natural numbers $a,b,d,n,m$ with $m\le\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\log_2 0$ read as $0$),
\[
  b\,2^{m+1}\bigl(a\,(2m+2)^d+(2m+2)^2\bigr)\;\le\;2b\,(a\,2^d+4)\,(n+1)^{d+3}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Simulating polynomially prepared queries]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_simulation_on_image}
\label{Complexity.ladner_simulation_on_image}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.expCode, Complexity.ladner_composition_clock, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iff, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_on_image, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings and $\mathrm{bin}(t)$
the binary expansion of $t$. Fix the uniform machine code, write $M_\alpha$ for the machine it
decodes from a string $\alpha$, and let $D$ be its simulation degree: its universal simulator
decides, on input $\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$, whether $M_\alpha$ halts
on $x$ within $t$ steps with output $1$, using at most $D\,(|\alpha|+|x|+t+1)^D$ steps. Let
$c,\iota$ be string functions and $\tau$ a map from strings to $\mathbb N$ such that
$z\mapsto\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(\tau(z)),c(z)\rangle,\iota(z)\rangle$ is polynomial-time
computable, and suppose there are $A,e$ with
$D\,(|c(z)|+|\iota(z)|+\tau(z)+1)^D\le A\,(|z|+1)^e$ for every string $z$. Then the map sending
$z$ to the one-bit string that is $1$ exactly when $M_{c(z)}$ halts on $\iota(z)$ within
$\tau(z)$ steps with output $1$ is computable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[SAT on logarithmically short images]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_short_SAT_on_image}
\label{Complexity.ladner_short_SAT_on_image}
\leanok

$(\alpha,y,t)=(\mathrm{bin}(i),x,i\,|x|^i)$ if $i<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and
$|x|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$, and $(\alpha,y,t)=(\varepsilon,\varepsilon,0)$ otherwise. Then
$D\,(|\alpha|+|y|+t+1)^D\le D\,4^D\,(|S|+1)^{3D}$.
\end{theorem}

Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair); the memo values of a string $T$ are the numbers whose little-endian binary expansions are the successive first components obtained by repeatedly splitting $T$ as a pair and continuing with the second component until the remainder is empty. exactly when $t=|p|^{v_{|p|}}$.

$S\mapsto V(\pi_1(S),|\pi_2(S)|)$ is polynomial-time computable, then so is $\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Doubling fuel for the query count]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryFuel}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryFuel}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair), and let $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$. For a string $C$, the query fuel $F(C)$ is the one-bit string $1$ if
$\pi_1(C)$ is empty, and $\mathrm{bin}(|\pi_1(C)|)$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryFuel_length}

Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair), let $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$, and let $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$). For a string $C$ let $F(C)$ be $1$ if $\pi_1(C)$ is empty and
$\mathrm{bin}(|\pi_1(C)|)$ otherwise. Then $|F(C)|=\ell(|\pi_1(C)|)+1$.
\end{theorem}

For a string $C$ let $F(C)$ be $1$ if $\pi_1(C)$ is empty and
$\mathrm{bin}(|\pi_1(C)|)$ otherwise. Then $2^{|F(C)|}\le 2(|C|+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Initial state of the query-count generation]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_countInit}
\label{Complexity.ladner_countInit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_queryFuel, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with first component
$\pi_1$, and let $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$. For a string $C$, with $F(C)$ the one-bit string $1$ if $\pi_1(C)$ is
empty and $\mathrm{bin}(|\pi_1(C)|)$ otherwise, the initial count state is
$\langle C,\langle F(C),\varepsilon\rangle\rangle$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One doubling round of the query count]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_countStep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_countStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair). For a state $S$ put $C=\pi_1(S)$, $r=\pi_1(\pi_2(S))$, $a=\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$ and
$a'=a\,a\,1$. The doubling round returns $S$ if $r$ is empty, and otherwise returns
$\langle C,\langle r',b\rangle\rangle$, where $r'$ is $r$ without its first bit and $b=a'$ if
$|a'|\le 2(|C|+1)$, $b=a$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings. For a string $T$, the
initial selection state is $\langle T,\langle\varepsilon,\langle\varepsilon,\varepsilon\rangle\rangle\rangle$,
recording the table, an empty unary rank and an empty completion flag.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One round of stage selection]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_selectStep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_selectStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_candidate, Complexity.ladner_selectCtx, Complexity.ladner_values, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair), let $\mathrm{val}(w)$ denote the value of a little-endian binary word $w$, $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$), and $M_i$ denote the machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$ by the fixed uniform machine code, where $M_i$ is said to accept $x$ within $t$ steps if it halts on $x$ within $t$ steps with output the single bit $1$; the memo values of a string $T$ are the numbers whose little-endian binary expansions are the successive first components obtained by repeatedly splitting $T$ as a pair and continuing with the second component until the remainder is empty; for a list $v$ of natural numbers, $\mathrm{SAT}_v$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{v_{|\psi|}}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$, where $v_m$ is read as $0$ when $m$ is out of range; and the candidate bit $\chi(C)$ of a string $C$ is $1$ exactly when, with $n=|\pi_1(C)|$, $i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(C)))$ and $v$ the memo values of $\pi_2(\pi_2(C))$, the list $v$ has length $n$, $i<\ell(\ell(n))$, and for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_v$. Finally,
the selection round $\lambda$ acts on a state $S$ as follows: put $T=\pi_1(S)$, let $k$ be the number of memo values of $T$, and put $\rho=\pi_1(\pi_2(S))$ (the rank), $f=\pi_1(\pi_2(\pi_2(S)))$ (the flag) and $c=\ell(\ell(k))$ (the cap); then $\lambda(S)=S$ if $f$ is nonempty; otherwise, if $|\rho|<c$, $\lambda(S)$ is $\langle T,\langle\rho,\langle 1,\mathrm{bin}(|\rho|)\rangle\rangle\rangle$ when $\chi(\langle 1^{k},\langle\mathrm{bin}(|\rho|),T\rangle\rangle)=1$ and $\langle T,\langle\rho1,\langle\varepsilon,\varepsilon\rangle\rangle\rangle$ when it is $0$; and if $|\rho|\ge c$, $\lambda(S)=\langle T,\langle\rho,\langle 1,\mathrm{bin}(c)\rangle\rangle\rangle$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Output of a selection state]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_selectOut}
\label{Complexity.ladner_selectOut}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairSndD}
For a Boolean string $S$, with $\pi_2$ the second component of a self-delimiting pair (empty if
the string is not a pair), the selection output is $\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(S)))$, the recorded index of
a completed selection state.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial memo state]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_memoInit}
\label{Complexity.ladner_memoInit}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings. For a Boolean string
$z$, the initial memo state is $\langle 1^{|z|},\varepsilon\rangle$: the length of $z$ in unary
together with an empty table.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One memo-table extension]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_memoStep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_memoStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_stage, Complexity.ladner_values, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair), let $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$), and $M_i$ denote the machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$ by the fixed uniform machine code, where $M_i$ is said to accept $x$ within $t$ steps if it halts on $x$ within $t$ steps with output the single bit $1$; the memo values of a string $T$ are the numbers whose little-endian binary expansions are the successive first components obtained by repeatedly splitting $T$ as a pair and continuing with the second component until the remainder is empty; for a list $v$ of natural numbers, $\mathrm{SAT}_v$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{v_{|\psi|}}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$, where $v_m$ is read as $0$ when $m$ is out of range; and for a list $v$ of natural numbers of length $k$, the stage value $s(v)$ is the least $i<\ell(\ell(k))$ such that for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(k)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_v$, and $s(v)=\ell(\ell(k))$ if there is no such $i$. The memo step sends a state $S$
to $\langle\pi_1(S),\,\pi_2(S)\,\langle\mathrm{bin}(s(v)),\varepsilon\rangle\rangle$, where $v$ is
the list of memo values of $\pi_2(S)$ and the second component is the concatenation of
$\pi_2(S)$ with $\langle\mathrm{bin}(s(v)),\varepsilon\rangle$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Verifier for padded SAT]

before the last $0$ of $\pi_1(S)$, where $t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$, $|\pi_2(S)|=|p|+1$ and
$p\,\pi_2(S)\in V$.
\end{definition}

## ===== blueprint/src/chapter/Complexity/Diagonalization/NTimeDiagonalizer.tex =====

\section{Diagonalization --- NTime Diagonalizer}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.Diagonalization.NTimeDiagonalizer
This module builds the lazy diagonalizer of the nondeterministic time hierarchy theorem
[AB09, \S3.2, Figure 3.1]. It fixes the pure stage structure (the ladder $\ell_0 = 2$,
$\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(T^*_i)^2}$ with budgets $T^*_i$, the stage of an input length, the code each
stage diagonalizes against, and the stage query), and develops the machine-level toolkit used to
compute the stage query in time linear in $g(n) + 1$: normal-form configurations, hosted phases,
copy, clear, rewind, comparison and emission rows, released and clocked calls, and their
embeddings into a larger host machine.

\begin{definition}[Budget of a stage]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget}
\leanok
For a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a natural number $\ell$ (the bottom ladder value
of a stage), let $a = \ell + 1$. The budget of the stage is $T^* = (f(a) + a + 1)^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Budget formula]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget_eq}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget}
\difficulty{1}
For every function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$, the budget of
the stage with bottom ladder value $\ell$ equals $(f(\ell + 1) + (\ell + 1) + 1)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The ladder]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget}
For a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, write $B_f(\ell) = (f(\ell+1) + \ell + 2)^2$ for
the stage budget. The ladder of $f$ is the sequence $(\ell_i)_{i \ge 0}$ defined by $\ell_0 = 2$
and $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{B_f(\ell_i)^2}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The ladder starts at two]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_zero}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder}
\difficulty{1}
For every function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the first rung of the ladder of $f$ (the
sequence $\ell_0 = 2$, $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$) is $\ell_0 = 2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Next rung of the ladder]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_succ}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $B_f(\ell) = (f(\ell+1) + \ell + 2)^2$ be the stage
budget, and let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$, with $\ell_0 = 2$. Then for every $i$,
$\ell_{i+1} = 2^{B_f(\ell_i)^2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The ladder more than doubles]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.two_mul_lt_ladder_succ}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.two_mul_lt_ladder_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_succ}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$, given by
$\ell_0 = 2$ and $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{B^2}$ with $B = (f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^2$. Then
$2\ell_i < \ell_{i+1}$ for every $i \in \mathbb{N}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The ladder dominates its index]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.le_ladder}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.le_ladder}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_zero, Turing.NTimeDiag.two_mul_lt_ladder_succ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$, given by
$\ell_0 = 2$ and $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$. Then $i + 2 \le \ell_i$ for
every $i \in \mathbb{N}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The ladder is strictly increasing]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_strictMono}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_strictMono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.two_mul_lt_ladder_succ}
\difficulty{2}
For every $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the ladder of $f$, given by $\ell_0 = 2$ and
$\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$, is strictly increasing: $i < j$ implies
$\ell_i < \ell_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Every length lies below some rung]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.exists_le_ladder_succ}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.exists_le_ladder_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.le_ladder}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$, given by
$\ell_0 = 2$ and $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$
there is an index $i$ with $n \le \ell_{i+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Stage of a length]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.stage}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.stage}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.exists_le_ladder_succ}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$, given by
$\ell_0 = 2$ and $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$. The stage $s_f(n)$ of a length
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ is the least index $i$ with $n \le \ell_{i+1}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The stage brackets its length]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.stage_spec}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.stage_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.exists_le_ladder_succ, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_zero, Turing.NTimeDiag.stage}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$ (with $\ell_0 = 2$ and
$\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$), and let $s_f(n)$ be the least $i$ with
$n \le \ell_{i+1}$. If $n \ge 3$, then $\ell_{s_f(n)} < n \le \ell_{s_f(n)+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The stage is determined by its bracket]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.stage_eq}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.stage_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.exists_le_ladder_succ, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_strictMono, Turing.NTimeDiag.stage}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$ (with $\ell_0 = 2$ and
$\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$), and let $s_f(n)$ be the least $i$ with
$n \le \ell_{i+1}$. For all $n, i \in \mathbb{N}$, if $\ell_i < n \le \ell_{i+1}$ then
$s_f(n) = i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Short lengths lie in stage zero]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.stage_of_le_two}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.stage_of_le_two}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.exists_le_ladder_succ, Turing.NTimeDiag.le_ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.stage}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$ (with $\ell_0 = 2$ and
$\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$), and let $s_f(n)$ be the least $i$ with
$n \le \ell_{i+1}$. If $n \le 2$, then $s_f(n) = 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Code diagonalized at a stage]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode}
\leanok
For a stage index $i \in \mathbb{N}$, let $j$ be the first component of the image of $i$ under the
standard unpairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$. The code of stage $i$
is the binary word $\alpha_i$ obtained from the binary expansion of $j + 1$ (least significant
bit first) by deleting its last, most significant, bit.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Stage code formula]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode_eq}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode}
\difficulty{1}
For every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the code of stage $i$ equals the binary expansion (least
significant bit first) of $j + 1$ with its last bit removed, where $j$ is the first component
of the standard unpairing of $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Every code recurs at unboundedly many stages]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode_frequently}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode_frequently}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode}
\difficulty{5}
For a stage index $i$, let $\alpha_i$ denote the binary expansion (least significant bit first)
of $j + 1$ with its most significant bit removed, where $j$ is the first component of the
standard unpairing of $i$. Then for every binary word $\alpha$ and every $N \in \mathbb{N}$
there is a stage $i \ge N$ with $\alpha_i = \alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The stage query]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.query}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.query}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.stage, Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $f, g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$, let $s_f(n)$ be the
stage of a length $n$, let $\alpha_i$ be the code of stage $i$, and let
$B_f(\ell) = (f(\ell+1) + \ell + 2)^2$ be the stage budget. Write $\langle u, v \rangle$ for the
pairing encoding of binary words and $\mathrm{bin}(m)$ for the binary expansion of $m$. The stage
query $q_{f,g}(x)$ of a binary word $x$ is defined as follows. If $x = 1^n$ with $n \ge 3$, put
$i = s_f(n)$; then $q_{f,g}(x)$ is the bit $1$ followed by
$\langle\langle \mathrm{bin}(B_f(\ell_i)), \alpha_i\rangle, 1^{\ell_i + 1}\rangle$ when
$n = \ell_{i+1}$, and the bit $0$ followed by
$\langle\langle \mathrm{bin}(g(n)), \alpha_i\rangle, 1^{n + 1}\rangle$ otherwise. On every other
input, $q_{f,g}(x)$ is the empty word.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Stage query on unary inputs]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.query_eq}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.query_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.budget, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.query, Turing.NTimeDiag.stage, Turing.NTimeDiag.stageCode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f, g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, with ladder $(\ell_i)$ of $f$, stage function $s_f$,
stage codes $\alpha_i$, stage budget $B_f(\ell) = (f(\ell+1) + \ell + 2)^2$, pairing encoding
$\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ and binary expansion $\mathrm{bin}$. For every $n \ge 3$, with
$i = s_f(n)$, the stage query of $1^n$ is the bit $1$ followed by
$\langle\langle \mathrm{bin}(B_f(\ell_i)), \alpha_i\rangle, 1^{\ell_i+1}\rangle$ if
$n = \ell_{i+1}$, and is the bit $0$ followed by
$\langle\langle \mathrm{bin}(g(n)), \alpha_i\rangle, 1^{n+1}\rangle$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stage query off its guard is empty]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.query_of_not_guard}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.query_of_not_guard}
\leanok

Let $f, g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $x$ be a binary word that is not of the form $1^n$
with $n \ge 3$. Then the stage query $q_{f,g}(x)$ of the lazy diagonalizer is the empty word.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded language of a halting NDTM is in NTIME]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.acceptLang_mem_NTIME}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.acceptLang_mem_NTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
\difficulty{1}
Let $D$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let
$K \in \mathbb{N}$ and $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If on every binary input $x$ every
computation branch of $D$ halts within $K(g(|x|) + 1)$ steps, then the language of all $x$ that
$D$ accepts within $K(g(|x|) + 1)$ steps belongs to $\mathbf{NTIME}(g(n) + 1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stage query reduces to unary words]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_guard}

\leanok

$|x| \ge 3$, and $q_{f,g}(x)$ is the empty word otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear-time unary guard decider]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_guard_decider}

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Full stage query from its unary part]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_query_of_main}

\leanok

\begin{theorem}[Next rung as a fourth power]

Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$, given by
$\ell_0 = 2$ and $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{B^2}$ with budget $B = (f(\ell_i + 1) + \ell_i + 2)^2$. Then for
every $i$, $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{X^4}$ where $X = f(\ell_i + 1) + (\ell_i + 1) + 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of earlier rungs]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_ledger}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_ledger}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.two_mul_lt_ladder_succ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$, given by
$\ell_0 = 2$ and $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$. For every $s \in \mathbb{N}$,
\[ \sum_{h < s} \ell_{h+1} \le 2\,\ell_s. \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Value of the all-ones counter]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_ones_val}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_ones_val}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every $m \in \mathbb{N}$, the word $1^m$, read as a binary numeral, has value $2^m - 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Value of zeros followed by a one]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_rung_val}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_rung_val}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every $m \in \mathbb{N}$, the word $0^m 1$, read as a binary numeral with the least
significant digit first, has value $2^m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The all-ones counter is large enough]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_ones_ge}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_ones_ge}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.lt_two_pow_bits}
\difficulty{4}
For all $n, D \in \mathbb{N}$, writing $|\mathrm{bin}(m)|$ for the length of the binary expansion
of $m$,
\[ D(n + 1) \le 2^{|\mathrm{bin}(n)| + |\mathrm{bin}(D)|} - 1. \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Install-call bound for small arguments]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_call_bound}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_call_bound}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.length_bits_le_self}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $c, c', a, n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $a \le n$ and
$f(a) \le n$. Writing $|\mathrm{bin}(m)|$ for the length of the binary expansion of $m$,
\[ c'\bigl(c(f(a) + 1) + a + |\mathrm{bin}(f(a))| + 1\bigr) \le c'(c + 2)(n + 1). \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential lower bound on the ladder]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_two_pow_le_ladder}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_two_pow_le_ladder}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.ladder_zero, Turing.NTimeDiag.two_mul_lt_ladder_succ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$, given by
$\ell_0 = 2$ and $\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$. Then $2^{i+1} \le \ell_i$ for
every $i \in \mathbb{N}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stage index is below the logarithm]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_stage_lt_log}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_stage_lt_log}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_two_pow_le_ladder, Turing.NTimeDiag.stage, Turing.NTimeDiag.stage_spec}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $(\ell_i)$ be the ladder of $f$ (with $\ell_0 = 2$ and
$\ell_{i+1} = 2^{(f(\ell_i+1) + \ell_i + 2)^4}$), and let $s_f(n)$ be the least $i$ with
$n \le \ell_{i+1}$. For every $n \ge 3$, $s_f(n) < \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Timeout certificate]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_timeout_cert}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_timeout_cert}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_call_bound, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_ones_ge}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $c, c', a, n, t \in \mathbb{N}$, and write
$|\mathrm{bin}(m)|$ for the length of the binary expansion of $m$. Suppose $a \le n$,
$t \le c'(c(f(a) + 1) + a + |\mathrm{bin}(f(a))| + 1)$, and
$2^{|\mathrm{bin}(n)| + |\mathrm{bin}(c'(c+2))|} - 1 < t$. Then $n < f(a)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Normal-form configuration]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
For a multi-tape machine with $K$ work tapes over the binary alphabet, an input $x$, a state $s$,
an input-head position $p \in \{0, \dots, |x| + 1\}$, work-tape contents $T$ (a partial map from
tape index and integer cell to bits), work-head positions $P$ and an output word $o$, the
normal-form configuration $\langle s, p, T, P, o \rangle$ is the live configuration with state
$s$ and exactly these input head, tapes, heads and output.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Renaming states of normal-form configurations]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC_mapState}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC_mapState}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\varphi : S \to S'$ be a map of state sets. For a live configuration
$\langle s, p, T, P, o \rangle$ of a $K$-tape machine on input $x$, with state $s$, input head
$p$, work tapes $T$, work heads $P$ and output $o$, renaming its state along $\varphi$ yields
$\langle \varphi(s), p, T, P, o \rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A hosted phase is a segment]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted'}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted'}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_state_ne_none_of_le, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC_mapState, Turing.Segment, Turing.phaseHostTM, Turing.phaseHostTM_run, Turing.segment_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(M_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of $K$-tape machines with state sets $\Phi_i$, and let $H$ be
the phase host with start state $q_0$ and redirect table $r$: $H$ runs on tagged states
$(i, s)$, takes one stationary silent step to $r_i(s)$ when this is defined, and otherwise
follows $M_i$. Fix a phase $k$ and an input $x$, and write $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the
live configuration with state $s$, input head $p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$.
Suppose $M_k$ runs from $\langle e, p, T, P, o\rangle$ to $\langle s', p', T', P', o'\rangle$ in
$t$ steps, $r_k(s') = q'$, and $r_k$ is undefined on every state of this run before time $t$.
Let $F$ be a set of host states containing no tagged state $(k, s)$ for any $s$ visited by
$M_k$'s run up to time $t$. Then $H$ runs from $\langle (k, e), p, T, P, o\rangle$ to
$\langle q', p', T', P', o'\rangle$ in exactly $t + 1$ steps, with no state in $F$ before time
$t + 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A hosted phase avoids foreign states]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted', Turing.Segment, Turing.phaseHostTM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $(M_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of $K$-tape machines with state sets $\Phi_i$, and let $H$ be
the phase host with start state $q_0$ and redirect table $r$ (a redirected state takes one
stationary silent step to its target; any other tagged state $(i, s)$ follows $M_i$). Write
$\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with state $s$, input head
$p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. Suppose $M_k$ runs from
$\langle e, p, T, P, o\rangle$ to $\langle s', p', T', P', o'\rangle$ in $t$ steps,
$r_k(s') = q'$, and $r_k$ is undefined on every state of the run before time $t$. Then for every
set $F$ of host states that contains no state $(k, s)$, $H$ runs from
$\langle (k, e), p, T, P, o\rangle$ to $\langle q', p', T', P', o'\rangle$ in exactly $t + 1$ steps
without visiting $F$ before time $t + 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A hosted last phase is a segment]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted_last}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted_last}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_state_ne_none_of_le, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC_mapState, Turing.Segment, Turing.phaseHostTM, Turing.phaseHostTM_run_le, Turing.segment_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(M_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of $K$-tape machines with state sets $\Phi_i$, and let $H$ be
the phase host with start state $q_0$ and redirect table $r$ (a redirected state takes one
stationary silent step to its target; any other tagged state $(i, s)$ follows $M_i$). Write
$\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with state $s$, input head
$p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. Suppose $M_k$ runs from
$\langle e, p, T, P, o\rangle$ to $\langle s', p', T', P', o'\rangle$ in $t$ steps and $r_k$ is
undefined on every state of the run before time $t$. Let $F$ be a set of host states containing
no tagged state $(k, s)$ with $s$ visited by the run before time $t$. Then $H$ runs from
$\langle (k, e), p, T, P, o\rangle$ to $\langle (k, s'), p', T', P', o'\rangle$ in exactly $t$
steps, with no state in $F$ before time $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Run of a hosted phase]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted_run}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_hosted, Turing.phaseHostTM, Turing.segment_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $(M_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of $K$-tape machines with state sets $\Phi_i$, and let $H$ be
the phase host with start state $q_0$ and redirect table $r$ (a redirected state takes one
stationary silent step to its target; any other tagged state $(i, s)$ follows $M_i$). Write
$\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with state $s$, input head
$p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. If $M_k$ runs from
$\langle e, p, T, P, o\rangle$ to $\langle s', p', T', P', o'\rangle$ in $t$ steps,
$r_k(s') = q'$, and $r_k$ is undefined on every state of the run before time $t$, then $H$ run
for $t + 1$ steps from $\langle (k, e), p, T, P, o\rangle$ reaches
$\langle q', p', T', P', o'\rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Writing at the end of a buffer appends]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_patch_end}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_patch_end}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append_shift, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_eq, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_eq_none_of_not_mem}
\difficulty{4}
For a binary word $w$, let $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ be the tape holding $w$ in cells
$0, \dots, |w| - 1$ and blank elsewhere. Let $u, w$ be binary words and $p = |u|$. The tape whose
cell $q$ holds $\mathrm{buf}(w)(q - p)$ for $p \le q < p + |w|$ and $\mathrm{buf}(u)(q)$ otherwise
equals $\mathrm{buf}(uw)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Buffer of a mapped word]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_bufferTape_map}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_bufferTape_map}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_eq}
\difficulty{2}
For a binary word $w$, let $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ be the tape holding $w$ in cells
$0, \dots, |w| - 1$ and blank elsewhere. For every map $g$ on bits and every cell
$z \in \mathbb{Z}$, the cell $z$ of $\mathrm{buf}(g(w))$, where $g$ is applied letterwise, is the
image under $g$ of cell $z$ of $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ (blank if that cell is blank).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Redirect guard from a first-visit cut]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_guard_of_cut}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_guard_of_cut}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a multi-tape machine with state set $S$, let $c$ be a configuration, $t \in \mathbb{N}$,
$d \in S$, and let $r$ be a partial map on $S$ that is undefined on every state other than $d$.
If the run of $M$ from $c$ is not in state $d$ at any time $u < t$, then $r$ is undefined on
every state that this run occupies at any time $u < t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mapped copy appending to a word]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_copy}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_copy}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_bufferTape_map, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_patch_end, Turing.copyMapTM, Turing.copyMapTM_run_ofCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{src} \ne \mathrm{dst}$ be two of $K$ work tapes, and let $g$
be a map on bits. Consider the mapped-copy machine that copies the word under the head of
$\mathrm{src}$, letterwise through $g$, onto $\mathrm{dst}$ starting at its head, and returns both
heads. Write $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ for the tape holding $w$ in cells $0, \dots, |w| - 1$ and blank
elsewhere, and $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with state
$s$, input head $p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. If tape $\mathrm{src}$ is
$\mathrm{buf}(w)$ with its head at $0$ and tape $\mathrm{dst}$ is $\mathrm{buf}(u)$ with its head
at $|u|$, then from the start state the machine reaches, after exactly $2|w| + 2$ steps and not
before, its exit state with tape $\mathrm{dst}$ replaced by $\mathrm{buf}(u \, g(w))$ and the
input head, all other tapes, all heads and the output unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mapped copy overwriting a word]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_copy_over}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_copy_over}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_eq_none_of_not_mem, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_bufferTape_map, Turing.copyMapTM, Turing.copyMapTM_run_ofCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{src} \ne \mathrm{dst}$ be two of $K$ work tapes, and let $g$
be a map on bits. Consider the mapped-copy machine that copies the word under the head of
$\mathrm{src}$, letterwise through $g$, onto $\mathrm{dst}$ starting at its head, and returns both
heads. Write $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ for the tape holding $w$ in cells $0, \dots, |w| - 1$ and blank
elsewhere, and $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with state
$s$, input head $p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. Let $u, w$ be binary words with
$|u| \le |w|$. If tape $\mathrm{src}$ is $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ and tape $\mathrm{dst}$ is
$\mathrm{buf}(u)$, both heads at $0$, then from the start state the machine reaches, after exactly
$2|w| + 2$ steps and not before, its exit state with tape $\mathrm{dst}$ replaced by
$\mathrm{buf}(g(w))$ and everything else unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mapped move appending to a word]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_transfer}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_transfer}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_eq_none_of_not_mem, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nil, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_bufferTape_map, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_patch_end, Turing.transferMapTM, Turing.transferMapTM_run_ofCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{src} \ne \mathrm{dst}$ be two of $K$ work tapes, and let $g$
be a map on bits. Consider the mapped-transfer machine that copies the word under the head of
$\mathrm{src}$, letterwise through $g$, onto $\mathrm{dst}$ starting at its head, blanking each
source cell on the return pass. Write $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ for the tape holding $w$ in cells
$0, \dots, |w| - 1$ and blank elsewhere, and $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live
configuration on input $x$ with state $s$, input head $p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output
$o$. If tape $\mathrm{src}$ is $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ with its head at $0$ and tape $\mathrm{dst}$ is
$\mathrm{buf}(u)$ with its head at $|u|$, then from the start state the machine reaches, after
exactly $2|w| + 2$ steps and not before, its exit state with tape $\mathrm{src}$ blank, tape
$\mathrm{dst}$ equal to $\mathrm{buf}(u \, g(w))$, and everything else unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Clearing a word]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_clear}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_clear}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_eq_none_of_not_mem, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nil, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.clearTM, Turing.clearTM_run_ofCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K \in \mathbb{N}$, let $i$ be one of $K$ work tapes, and consider the clearing machine that
blanks the word under the head of tape $i$ and returns its head. Write $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ for the
tape holding $w$ in cells $0, \dots, |w| - 1$ and blank elsewhere, and
$\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with state $s$, input head
$p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. If tape $i$ is $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ with its head at
$0$, then from the start state the machine reaches, after exactly $2|w| + 2$ steps and not
before, its exit state with tape $i$ entirely blank and everything else unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Appending a constant word]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_writeConst}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_writeConst}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_patch_end, Turing.WritePhase, Turing.writeConstTM, Turing.writeConstTM_run_ofCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K \in \mathbb{N}$, let $i$ be one of $K$ work tapes, let $w_0$ be a fixed binary word, and
consider the constant-writer machine that writes $w_0$ on tape $i$ from its head and returns the
head. Write $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ for the tape holding $w$ in cells $0, \dots, |w| - 1$ and blank
elsewhere, and $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with state
$s$, input head $p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. If tape $i$ is $\mathrm{buf}(u)$
with its head at $|u|$, then from the first writing state the machine reaches, after exactly
$2|w_0| + 2$ steps and not before, its exit state with tape $i$ equal to $\mathrm{buf}(u w_0)$ and
everything else, including the head of tape $i$, unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rewinding a head]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_rewind}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.rewindTM, Turing.rewindTM_run_ofCfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $K \in \mathbb{N}$, let $i$ be one of $K$ work tapes, and consider the rewinding machine that
moves the head of tape $i$ left to the start of its word. Write $\mathrm{buf}(u)$ for the tape
holding $u$ in cells $0, \dots, |u| - 1$ and blank elsewhere, and $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$
for the live configuration on input $x$ with state $s$, input head $p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$
and output $o$. If tape $i$ is $\mathrm{buf}(u)$ with its head at $n \le |u|$, then from the start
state the machine reaches, after exactly $n + 2$ steps and not before, its exit state with the
head of tape $i$ at $0$ and everything else unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Embedded run as a transported run]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_embed_gen}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_embed_gen}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg_eq, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{2}
Let $M$ be an $m$-tape machine with state set $S$, and let $\sigma$ be an injection from its $m$
tapes into $K$ host tapes; the embedded machine runs $M$ on the host tapes $\sigma(0), \dots,
\sigma(m - 1)$ and forwards every emission to the host output. Write
$\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with state $s$, input head
$p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. For every $t$, the embedded run for $t$ steps from
$\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ is the configuration whose state and input head are those of
$M$'s run for $t$ steps from $\langle s, p, T \circ \sigma, P \circ \sigma, \varepsilon\rangle$,
whose tape and head $\sigma(i)$ are that run's tape and head $i$, whose other tapes and heads are
those of $T$ and $P$, and whose output is $o$ followed by that run's output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Embedded run in normal form]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_embed}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_embed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_embed_gen, Turing.embedEmitCfg_eq, Turing.embedEmitTM}
\difficulty{2}
Let $M$ be an $m$-tape machine and $\sigma$ an injection from its tapes into $K$ host tapes; the
embedded machine runs $M$ on the host tapes selected by $\sigma$ and forwards its emissions to
the host output. Write $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with
state $s$, input head $p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. Suppose $M$ runs in $t$ steps
from $\langle s, p, T \circ \sigma, P \circ \sigma, \varepsilon\rangle$ to
$\langle s', p', T_0, P_0, o'\rangle$, and let $T', P'$ agree with $T_0, P_0$ on the selected
tapes ($T'(\sigma(i)) = T_0(i)$, $P'(\sigma(i)) = P_0(i)$) and with $T, P$ on every unselected
tape. Then the embedded machine runs in $t$ steps from $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ to
$\langle s', p', T', P', o\, o'\rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[States of an embedded run]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_embed_state}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_embed_state}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NTimeDiag.qyC, Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_embed_gen, Turing.embedEmitTM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be an $m$-tape machine and $\sigma$ an injection from its tapes into $K$ host tapes; the
embedded machine runs $M$ on the host tapes selected by $\sigma$ and forwards its emissions to
the host output. Write $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with
state $s$, input head $p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. For every time $u$, the state
of the embedded run from $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ after $u$ steps equals the state of $M$'s
run from $\langle s, p, T \circ \sigma, P \circ \sigma, \varepsilon\rangle$ after $u$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A released call in normal form]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_call}

Let $C$ be a finite deterministic $k$-tape machine over bits with states $\mathit{entry}$ and
$\mathit{exit}$, and let $x, a, b$ be binary words. For a state $q$ and a word $w$, the seam
configuration $\mathrm{seam}(q, w)$ on input $x$ has state $q$, input head at $1$, tape $0$

for some $t > 0$ the run of $C$ from $\mathrm{seam}(\mathit{entry}, a)$ is not in $\mathit{exit}$

Consider the release adapter of $C$ at $\mathit{entry}$: a machine with a fresh start state that
performs $\mathit{entry}$'s action and then runs a tagged copy of $C$. Started in its fresh state
with the tapes, heads and output of $\mathrm{seam}(\mathit{entry}, a)$, it is at time $t$ in the
tagged copy of $\mathit{exit}$ with the tapes, heads and output of $\mathrm{seam}(\mathit{exit}, b)$,
and it is not in that state at any earlier time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[States of the length comparison]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.QyCmp}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.QyCmp}
\leanok
The control states of the length-comparison machine: a forward scanning state, a return state
for each verdict in $\{<, =, >\}$, and a live exit state for each verdict.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Length-comparison machine]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyCmpTM}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyCmpTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.NTimeDiag.QyCmp}
For $K \in \mathbb{N}$ and two work tapes $a, b$ among $K$, the length-comparison machine starts
with the heads of $a$ and $b$ on the first cells of two words. In the scanning state it moves
both heads right in lockstep while both read a symbol; at the first blank under either head it
records the verdict ($<$ if only $a$ reads a blank, $=$ if both do, $>$ if only $b$ does) and
moves both heads left in lockstep until tape $a$ reads a blank, then moves them right once and
enters the exit state of the verdict, where it idles. It never writes, never moves the input head
and never emits.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lockstep head vector]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyAt2}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyAt2}
\leanok
For a head-position vector $P$ over $K$ work tapes, two tapes $a, b$ and an integer $i$, the
lockstep head vector is $P$ with the heads of $a$ and $b$ both set to $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Moving both compared heads]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyAt2_move}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyAt2_move}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyAt2}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ be a head-position vector over $K$ work tapes, $a, b$ two tapes, $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, and
$d \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$ with integer value $d_{\mathbb{Z}}$. Let $P^{a,b}_i$ be $P$ with the heads
of $a$ and $b$ set to $i$. Moving the heads of $a$ and $b$ of $P^{a,b}_i$ by $d$ and leaving all
other heads in place gives $P^{a,b}_{i + d_{\mathbb{Z}}}$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_cmp_run}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_cmp_run}
\leanok

(lockstep scan right while both heads read symbols, then lockstep return, then the exit state of
the verdict). Write $\mathrm{buf}(w)$ for the tape holding $w$ in cells $0, \dots, |w| - 1$ and
blank elsewhere, and $\langle s, p, T, P, o\rangle$ for the live configuration on input $x$ with
state $s$, input head $p$, work tapes $T$, heads $P$ and output $o$. If tape $a$ is
$\mathrm{buf}(u)$ and tape $b$ is $\mathrm{buf}(v)$, both heads at $0$, then from the scanning
state the machine reaches, after exactly $2\min(|u|, |v|) + 2$ steps, the exit state for the
comparison of $|u|$ with $|v|$, with input head, tapes, heads and output unchanged; and at no
earlier time is it in any exit state.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[States of the emitter]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.QyEm}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.QyEm}
\leanok
For natural numbers $n_p, n_s, r$, the control states of the emitter are: a prefix state for each
position $0, \dots, n_p$; a reading state; a holding state for each bit; a copying state for each
bit and each count $0, \dots, r$; a suffix state for each position $0, \dots, n_s$; and an exit
state.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The emitter machine]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyEmitTM}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyEmitTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.NTimeDiag.QyEm}
For $K \in \mathbb{N}$, a work tape $i$, fixed binary words $\mathit{pre}$ and $\mathit{suf}$,
$r \in \mathbb{N}$ and a flag $\delta$, the emitter is the $K$-tape machine that first emits
$\mathit{pre}$; then scans the word under the head of tape $i$, emitting each symbol $r + 1$
times, except that when $\delta$ is set it omits the last symbol (detected by one cell of
look-ahead); then emits $\mathit{suf}$ and enters its exit state, whose action halts. It never
writes and never moves the input head.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Body emitted by the emitter]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyBody}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qyBody}
\leanok
For a flag $\delta$, $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and a binary word $w$, let $w'$ be $w$ with its last
symbol removed if $\delta$ is set, and $w$ otherwise. The emitter body is the word obtained from
$w'$ by replacing each symbol $c$ with $c^{r+1}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Zero displacement leaves heads in place]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_noMove}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_noMove}
\leanok

For every head-position vector $P$ over $K$ work tapes, moving every head by $0$ yields $P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Moving one head right]
\lean{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_moveOne}
\label{Turing.NTimeDiag.qy_moveOne}
\leanok

For every head-position vector $P$ over $K$ work tapes and every tape $i$, moving head $i$ by
$+1$ and every other head by $0$ yields $P$ with entry $i$ replaced by $P_i + 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The clocked released call]

$\mathit{exit}$. Write $\mathrm{seam}(q, w)$ for the configuration on a given input with state
$q$, input head at $1$, tape $0$ holding $w$, other tapes blank, heads at $0$ and empty output.
There is a $(k+1)$-tape machine $H$ with finitely many states (a step clock running the release
adapter of $C$ at $\mathit{entry}$ on its first $k$ tapes, with a binary counter on its last tape),
a start-state map, and injective families of finish and timeout states, no finish state equal to
a timeout state, with the following property. Let $x, a, b$ be binary words and $t > 0$ such that
the run of $C$ on input $x$ from $\mathrm{seam}(\mathit{entry}, a)$ avoids $\mathit{exit}$
strictly between times $0$ and $t$ and equals $\mathrm{seam}(\mathit{exit}, b)$ at time $t$. Let
$m \in \mathbb{N}$ and start $H$ with $\mathrm{seam}(\mathit{entry}, a)$ (fresh state) on the body
tapes and the all-ones word $1^m$ under the counter head. If $t \le 2^m - 1$, then within
$5t + 2m + 2$ steps $H$ reaches its finish state for the tagged $\mathit{exit}$, with
$\mathrm{seam}(\mathit{exit}, b)$ on the body tapes and the counter cells overwritten by some
word of length $m$. If $t > 2^m - 1$, then within $5(2^m - 1) + 2m + 2$ steps $H$ reaches some
timeout state with empty output. In both cases no finish or timeout state occurs earlier.
\end{theorem}
