For natural numbers $k$, $n$, and $r$, let $C_{k,n}$ be the finite type of canonical
oracle-machine tables. If $r<|C_{k,n}|$, the definition returns the well-formed Boolean
oracle Turing machine represented by the table at index $r$ in the enumeration of
$C_{k,n}$; if $r\ge |C_{k,n}|$, it returns the default Boolean oracle Turing machine.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decoded oracle table machine]
\lean{Complexity.decodeOracleTable}
\label{Complexity.decodeOracleTable}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.oracleTableAt, Turing.FinOracleTM}
For each natural number $j$, decode the oracle machine obtained by first unpairing $j$,
then unpairing the second coordinate, and using the resulting three natural numbers as
the work-tape count, state count, and table index, respectively.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Ranking and Decoding Oracle Machines]
\lean{Complexity.decodeOracleTable_rank}
\label{Complexity.decodeOracleTable_rank}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CanonTab, Complexity.canonTabFintype, Complexity.decodeOracleTable, Complexity.oracleTableAt, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k,n$ be natural numbers and let a well-formed oracle Turing machine with $k$
ordinary work tapes, Boolean alphabet, and state set of size $n$ be given. If this
machine is assigned its index in the finite enumeration of such machines, then decoding
the natural-number code obtained by pairing $k$, $n$, and that index returns the same
finite oracle machine, with its three distinguished states and transition function
unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Oracle machine enumeration]
\lean{Complexity.oracleEnumeration}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p003-b006,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p004-b004
}
\label{Complexity.oracleEnumeration}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.decodeOracleTable, Turing.FinOracleTM}
For each natural number $i$, take the first coordinate in the fixed pairing
decomposition of $i$ and decode that natural number as an oracle table machine.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Pairing preserves the decoded oracle table]
\lean{Complexity.oracleEnumeration_pair}
\label{Complexity.oracleEnumeration_pair}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.decodeOracleTable, Complexity.oracleEnumeration}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $j$ and $r$, the oracle machine with index obtained by pairing
$j$ and $r$ is the machine decoded from $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Enumeration of Finite Oracle Machines]
\lean{Complexity.exists_finOracleTM_enumeration}
\label{Complexity.exists_finOracleTM_enumeration}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CanonTab, Complexity.canonTabFintype, Complexity.decodeOracleTable, Complexity.decodeOracleTable_rank, Complexity.oracleEnumeration, Complexity.oracleEnumeration_pair, Turing.OracleTM.relabel, Turing.OracleTM.relabel_computesInTime, Turing.OracleTM.relabel_wellFormed, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime}
\difficulty{5}
There is a sequence $(N_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ of finite oracle Turing machines over the
binary alphabet such that, for every finite binary oracle machine $M$ and every natural
number $i_0$, there is an index $i\ge i_0$ for which $N_i$ and $M$ compute exactly the
same outputs within exactly $t$ steps, for every binary oracle language, binary input
and output strings, and natural number $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A Missing Bit String of Prescribed Length]
\lean{Complexity.exists_length_not_mem}
\label{Complexity.exists_length_not_mem}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $Q$ be a finite list of binary strings with
$|Q|<2^n$. Then there is a binary string $z$ of length $n$ that does not occur in $Q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A Length Exceeding Exponential and Polynomial Bounds]
\lean{Complexity.exists_fresh_len}
\label{Complexity.exists_fresh_len}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For every pair of natural numbers $i,b$, there is a natural number $n$ such that $b<n$,
$i+2\le n$, and $n^i+i<2^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Stage data]
\lean{Complexity.StageData}
\label{Complexity.StageData}
\leanok
A stage datum consists of a finite set of finite Boolean strings and a natural-number
bound.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Positive finite oracle]
\lean{Complexity.posOracle}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b003,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b004
}
\label{Complexity.posOracle}
\leanok
For a finite set $P$ of finite Boolean strings, the associated language consists exactly
of the strings in $P$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fresh length]
\lean{Complexity.freshLen}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b003,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b004
}
\label{Complexity.freshLen}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.exists_fresh_len}
For natural numbers $i$ and $b$, choose a natural number witnessing the property that
there is a fresh length for $i$ and $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Properties of the chosen length]
\lean{Complexity.freshLen_spec}
\label{Complexity.freshLen_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.exists_fresh_len, Complexity.freshLen}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $i$ and $b$, let $m$ be the length chosen so that $b<m$, $i+2\le m$,
and $m^i+i<2^m$. Then these three inequalities hold for $m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Stage query list]
\lean{Complexity.stageQ}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b003,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b004
}
\label{Complexity.stageQ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.StageData, Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.posOracle, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.queriesWithin}
Let $N$ be a sequence of finite Boolean oracle machines, let $i$ be a natural number,
and let $d$ be stage data with finite set $P$ and bound $b$. The stage query list is the
list of queries made by machine $N(i)$, using the oracle consisting of $P$, on the
all-true Boolean input of length $L$, within $L^i+i$ steps, where $L$ is the fresh
length chosen for $i$ and $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on the stage query list]
\lean{Complexity.stageQ_length}
\label{Complexity.stageQ_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.StageData, Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.freshLen_spec, Complexity.stageQ, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.queriesWithin_length_le}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a sequence of finite oracle Turing machines, let $i$ be a natural number, and
let $d$ be stage data. The number of queries in the list produced at stage $i$ using $d$
is strictly less than $2^{\mathrm{freshLen}(i,d.\mathrm{bound})}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Stage witness string]
\lean{Complexity.stageWit}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b003,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b004
}
\label{Complexity.stageWit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.StageData, Complexity.exists_length_not_mem, Complexity.stageQ_length, Turing.FinOracleTM}
Let $N$ be a sequence of finite Boolean oracle machines, let $i$ be a natural number,
and let $d$ be stage data. Choose a Boolean string whose length is not the length of any
query in the stage query list for $N$, $i$, and $d$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length and avoidance of the stage witness]
\lean{Complexity.stageWit_spec}
\label{Complexity.stageWit_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.StageData, Complexity.exists_length_not_mem, Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.stageQ, Complexity.stageQ_length, Complexity.stageWit, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a sequence of finite oracle Turing machines, let $i$ be a natural number, and
let $d$ be stage data. The witness selected for this stage is a Boolean string of length
$	ext{freshLen}(i,d.	ext{bound})$ that does not occur among the queries made by the
$i$th machine during this stage.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance at a stage]
\lean{Complexity.StageAccepts}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b003,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b004
}
\label{Complexity.StageAccepts}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.StageData, Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.posOracle, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime}
For a sequence $N$ of finite oracle Turing machines with Boolean input symbols, a stage
index $i$, and stage data $d$, acceptance means that the $i$th machine, with oracle
consisting of the positive strings in $d$, halts on the all-true input of length
$	ext{freshLen}(i,d.	ext{bound})$ within $	ext{freshLen}(i,d.	ext{bound})^i+i$ steps and
outputs the one-symbol string $[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One stage update]
\lean{Complexity.stageStep}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b003,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b004
}
\label{Complexity.stageStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.StageAccepts, Complexity.StageData, Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.stageWit, Turing.FinOracleTM}
Given a sequence $N$ of finite oracle Turing machines over Boolean symbols, an index
$i\in\mathbb N$, and stage data $d$, the updated stage data has positive set equal to
the current positive set if the $i$th machine accepts at stage $i$; otherwise it adjoins
the selected witness string. Its bound is the maximum of
$\text{freshLen}(i,d.\text{bound})$ and $\text{freshLen}(i,d.\text{bound})^i+i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Iterated stage construction]
\lean{Complexity.stage}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b003,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b004
}
\label{Complexity.stage}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.StageData, Complexity.stageStep, Turing.FinOracleTM}
For a sequence $N$ of finite oracle Turing machines over Boolean symbols, define stage
data recursively by starting with empty positive set and bound $0$ at stage $0$, then
obtaining stage $i+1$ by applying the stage update at index $i$ to stage $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Stage-generated oracle language]
\lean{Complexity.bgsOracle}
\statementsource{BGS75}{
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b003,
  pdf-2459e3840724-p006-b004
}
\label{Complexity.bgsOracle}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.stage, Turing.FinOracleTM}
For a sequence $N$ of finite oracle Turing machines over Boolean symbols, the associated
oracle language consists of exactly those Boolean strings that belong to the positive
set at some stage of the recursive stage construction.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Successive Positive Sets Are Nested]
\lean{Complexity.stage_pos_succ}
\label{Complexity.stage_pos_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.stage, Complexity.stageStep, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(N_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a sequence of finite-state oracle Turing machines, and let $i$ be
a nonnegative integer. Every string positive at stage $i$ is positive at stage $i+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of Positive Sets]
\lean{Complexity.stage_pos_mono}
\label{Complexity.stage_pos_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.stage, Complexity.stage_pos_succ, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(N_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a sequence of finite-state oracle Turing machines, and let $i\le
j$ be nonnegative integers. Every string positive at stage $i$ is positive at stage $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Successor stage bound]
\lean{Complexity.stage_bound_succ}
\label{Complexity.stage_bound_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.stage, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{1}
For every sequence $N$ of finite oracle Turing machines and every $i\in\mathbb{N}$, the
bound at stage $i+1$ is the maximum of the fresh length chosen from $i$ and the bound at
stage $i$, and the $i$th power of that stage bound plus $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of stage bounds]
\lean{Complexity.stage_bound_mono}
\label{Complexity.stage_bound_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.freshLen_spec, Complexity.stage, Complexity.stage_bound_succ, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{4}
For every sequence $N$ of finite oracle Turing machines and natural numbers $i\le j$,
the bound at stage $i$ is at most the bound at stage $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Growth of Later Stage Lengths]
\lean{Complexity.stage_later}
\label{Complexity.stage_later}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.freshLen_spec, Complexity.stage, Complexity.stage_bound_mono, Complexity.stage_bound_succ, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $(N_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a sequence of finite-state oracle Turing machines, and let $i<j$
be nonnegative integers. If $n_r$ denotes the fresh length chosen at stage $r$ using
that stage's bound, then $n_i^i+i<n_j$ and $n_i<n_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[New Positive Strings at a Stage]
\lean{Complexity.stage_new}
\label{Complexity.stage_new}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.StageAccepts, Complexity.stage, Complexity.stageStep, Complexity.stageWit, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(N_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a sequence of finite-state oracle Turing machines, let $i$ be a
nonnegative integer, and let $z$ be a Boolean string. If $z$ is positive at stage $i+1$
but not positive at stage $i$, then $z$ is the witness selected at stage $i$, and
machine $N_i$ does not accept its specified unary input within $n_i^i+i$ steps relative
to the stage-$i$ positive-set oracle, where $n_i$ is the fresh length for that stage.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[First entry into the stage sets]
\lean{Complexity.exists_entry}
\label{Complexity.exists_entry}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.bgsOracle, Complexity.stage, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N=(N_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ be a sequence of finite oracle Turing machines over the
binary alphabet, with each machine’s query, positive-answer, and negative-answer states
pairwise distinct. Let $P_i$ be the positive set at stage $i$ of the stage construction
determined by $N$, and let $B=\bigcup_{i\in\mathbb N}P_i$. Every binary word $z\in B$
belongs to $P_{s+1}$ but not to $P_s$ for some $s\in\mathbb N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length of a Newly Added Word]
\lean{Complexity.entry_length}
\label{Complexity.entry_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.stage, Complexity.stageWit_spec, Complexity.stage_new, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a sequence of finite oracle Turing machines over the binary alphabet, and let
$s$ be a natural number. If a binary word $z$ belongs to the positive set at stage $s+1$
but not to the positive set at stage $s$, then its length is the fresh length determined
by $s$ and the bound stored in the stage data at stage $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Consistency of Stage Queries]
\lean{Complexity.stage_consistent}
\label{Complexity.stage_consistent}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.bgsOracle, Complexity.entry_length, Complexity.exists_entry, Complexity.posOracle, Complexity.stage, Complexity.stageQ, Complexity.stageWit_spec, Complexity.stage_later, Complexity.stage_new, Complexity.stage_pos_mono, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.length_le_of_mem_queriesWithin}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(N_i)_{i\ge 0}$ be a sequence of finite-state oracle Turing machines, and let $S_i$
be the finite set of positive strings at stage $i$. Use the stage-$i$ oracle whose
language is $S_i$, and run $N_i$ on the unary input of length $n_i$, where $n_i$ is the
fresh length chosen for stage $i$ and its current bound; let $Q_i$ be the list of query
strings it makes during the first $n_i^i+i$ steps. Every $z\in Q_i$ belongs to $S_i$ if
and only if it belongs to $S_j$ for some stage $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Transfer Between Stage and Limit Oracles]
\lean{Complexity.stage_transfer}
\label{Complexity.stage_transfer}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.bgsOracle, Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.posOracle, Complexity.stage, Complexity.stage_consistent, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_agree_queriesWithin}
\difficulty{3}
Let $(N_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a sequence of finite-state oracle Turing machines, let $i$ be a
nonnegative integer, and let $y$ be a Boolean string. Running $N_i$ with the union of
all stage-positive sets as oracle on the unary input of length $n_i$ halts within
$n_i^i+i$ steps with output $y$ if and only if running it with the stage-$i$
positive-set oracle on that same input halts within the same number of steps with output
$y$, where $n_i$ is the fresh length chosen for stage $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Unary witness strings of fixed length]
\lean{Complexity.mem_unaryWitnessLang_replicate}
\label{Complexity.mem_unaryWitnessLang_replicate}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.unaryWitnessLang}
\difficulty{4}
Let $B$ be a language of bit strings and let $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The unary string
consisting of $n$ copies of $1$ belongs to the unary witness language of $B$ if and only
if $B$ contains a bit string of length $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance and Unary Witness Exclusion]
\lean{Complexity.stage_flip}
\label{Complexity.stage_flip}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.StageAccepts, Complexity.bgsOracle, Complexity.entry_length, Complexity.exists_entry, Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.mem_unaryWitnessLang_replicate, Complexity.stage, Complexity.stageStep, Complexity.stageWit, Complexity.stageWit_spec, Complexity.stage_later, Complexity.stage_new, Complexity.stage_transfer, Complexity.unaryWitnessLang, Turing.FinOracleTM, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(N_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a sequence of finite-state oracle Turing machines and let $i$ be
a nonnegative integer. Write $n_i$ for the fresh length chosen at stage $i$ from its
stage bound, and let $B$ be the language of strings that are unary words of some length
$n$ for which a length-$n$ Boolean string belongs to the oracle. Then $N_i$, using the
union of all stage-positive sets as its oracle, accepts the unary input of length $n_i$
within $n_i^i+i$ steps and outputs the one-symbol word $[\mathrm{true}]$ if and only if
the unary input of length $n_i$ does not belong to $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stage Time Bound Dominates]
\lean{Complexity.stage_dominates}
\label{Complexity.stage_dominates}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.freshLen_spec, Complexity.stage, Turing.FinOracleTM}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(N_j)_{j\ge0}$ be a sequence of finite-state oracle Turing machines, and let
$c,k,i$ be nonnegative integers satisfying $k+1+2c\le i$. If $n_i$ is the fresh length
chosen at stage $i$ using that stage's bound, then $c(n_i^k+1)\le n_i^i+i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[An oracle separating nondeterministic and deterministic polynomial time]
\lean{Complexity.exists_oracle_ne}
\label{Complexity.exists_oracle_ne}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NPOracle, Complexity.POracle, Complexity.bgsOracle, Complexity.exists_finOracleTM_enumeration, Complexity.freshLen, Complexity.stage, Complexity.stage_dominates, Complexity.stage_flip, Complexity.unaryWitnessLang, Complexity.unaryWitnessLang_mem_NPOracle, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinOracleTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{6}
There exists a language $B$ of binary strings such that the language consisting of
strings $1^n$ for which some binary string of length $n$ belongs to $B$ is in
nondeterministic polynomial time relative to oracle $B$, but is not in deterministic
polynomial time relative to oracle $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle separation and equality]
\lean{Complexity.baker_gill_solovay}
\label{Complexity.baker_gill_solovay}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EXPCOM, Complexity.NPOracle, Complexity.POracle, Complexity.POracle_EXPCOM_eq_NPOracle_EXPCOM, Complexity.exists_oracle_ne}
\difficulty{4}
There is a Boolean language $A$ for which deterministic and nondeterministic polynomial
time with oracle $A$ coincide, and there is a Boolean language $B$ for which these two
oracle complexity classes differ.
\end{theorem}

## ===== blueprint/src/chapter/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Basic.tex =====

\section{Space Complexity --- Foundations}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Basic
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Foundations: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Basic}.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Foundations: Results}

\begin{definition}[Deterministic space complexity class]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b002
}
\statementsource{BGW70}{
  pdf-b9fb35a232af-p003-b001,
  pdf-b9fb35a232af-p004-b001,
  pdf-b9fb35a232af-p005-b001
}
\statementsource{BGS75}{pdf-2459e3840724-p004-b006}
\label{Complexity.SPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace}
For a function $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{SPACE}(s)$ be the class of
Boolean languages $L$ for which there exist a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite
Turing machine that decides $L$ using at most $c\,s(n)$ space on inputs of length $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of space classes]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE.mono}
\label{Complexity.SPACE.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s_1,s_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $s_1(n)\le s_2(n)$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
then every language decidable in space $s_1$ up to a constant factor is also decidable
in space $s_2$ up to a constant factor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indexed language]
\lean{Complexity.indexLang}
\label{Complexity.indexLang}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
For a predicate $p$ on pairs consisting of a Boolean string $x$ and a natural number
$i$, the indexed language contains exactly those strings that encode a pair $(x,	ext{the
binary expansion of }i)$ for which $p(x,i)$ holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Monotonicity of the logarithmic bound]
\lean{Complexity.logSpace_mono}
\label{Complexity.logSpace_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{3}
If $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ and $a\le b$, then $\ell(a)\le\ell(b)$, where
$\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ for positive $n$ and $\ell(0)=1$.
\end{definition}

%%% added by the blueprint pipeline
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Foundations: Further results}

\begin{definition}[Computing within a space bound]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed}
A finite Turing machine $M$ computes a function $f$ within space bound $s$ if, for every
Boolean string $x$, there is a time $t$ at which $M$ outputs $f(x)$ and uses at most
$s(|x|)$ space, measured from its initial configuration on $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Deciding within a space bound]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b001
}
\label{Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
A finite Turing machine $M$ decides a language $L$ of Boolean strings within space bound
$s$ if, on every Boolean input string $x$, it computes the one-symbol Boolean indicator
of whether $x$ belongs to $L$, using at most $s(|x|)$ space.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of space bounds]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.mono}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $f$ map Boolean words

\begin{theorem}[Zero space with no work tapes]

\begin{definition}[Logarithmic space bound]

\begin{definition}[Logarithmic-space languages]

space at most logarithmic in the input length.

\label{Complexity.ImplicitlyLogspaceComputable}

\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.indexLang}
A function $f$ from Boolean strings to Boolean strings is implicitly logarithmic-space
computable if there are natural numbers $C,c$ such that $|f(x)|\le C(|x|+1)^c$ for every
input $x$, and both of the following languages are in logarithmic space: the language of
encodings of $(x,i)$ for which the $i$th output bit of $f(x)$ is true (taking an
out-of-range bit to be false), and the language of encodings of $(x,i)$ for which
$i<|f(x)|$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Computing in space, unfolded]

Let $M$ be a finite deterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, $f$ a function from
Boolean words to Boolean words, and $s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. Then $M$ computes $f$ in space
$s$ if and only if for every Boolean input $x$ there is a time $t$ at which $M$, started on
$x$, has halted with output $f(x)$, having visited at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells (summed over
its work tapes) during its first $t$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Turing.FinTM.decidesInSpace_iff}

Boolean words, and $s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. Then $M$ decides $L$ in space $s$ if and only if

whose letter is $1$ if $x\in L$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

deterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet that decides $L$ visiting at most
$c\,s(n)$ work-tape cells on inputs of length $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Formula for the logarithmic bound]
\lean{Complexity.logSpace_eq}
\label{Complexity.logSpace_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, the logarithmic space bound of $n$ equals
$\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$, where $\lfloor\log_2 0\rfloor$ is taken to be $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Logarithmic bound versus binary length]
\lean{Complexity.logSpace_le_size_succ}
\label{Complexity.logSpace_le_size_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, writing $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ for the integer part of the
base-$2$ logarithm (with value $0$ at $n=0$) and $\mathrm{size}(n)$ for the number of binary
digits of $n$ (with $\mathrm{size}(0)=0$), one has
$\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1\le\mathrm{size}(n)+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic space as a space class]
\lean{Complexity.LOGSPACE_eq}
\label{Complexity.LOGSPACE_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{1}
The class $\mathrm{L}$ of languages decidable in logarithmic space equals
$\mathrm{SPACE}(\ell)$, where $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ (with
$\lfloor\log_2 0\rfloor=0$); that is, a Boolean language lies in $\mathrm{L}$ exactly when
some finite deterministic Turing machine decides it visiting at most $c\,\ell(n)$ work-tape
cells on inputs of length $n$, for some constant $c$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath}
\label{Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_stepLang, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.Cfg.inWindow_init, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_of_acceptsWithin, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil, Turing.outSummary_eq_accept_iff, Turing.pairEncode}

Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $L$ be a
language of Boolean strings, and let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume that for every
input $x$, the machine halts after some common number $T$ of steps on every choice
string of length $T$, uses at most $sp(|x|)$ work-tape cells on every such run, and
accepts exactly the inputs in $L$. For any Boolean string $x$ and natural number $s$
with $sp(|x|)\le s$, we have $x\in L$ if and only if there are a natural number $t$ and
a sequence of natural numbers $(c_i)_{i\ge0}$ such that $t\le
3((|Q|+1)(|x|+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k)$, the code $c_0$ describes the initial
configuration of $N$ on $x$ within window $s$, each consecutive pair $c_i,c_{i+1}$ for
$i<t$ describes a valid one-step transition between configurations within that window,
the code $c_t$ describes a halted accepting configuration within that window, and

tapes, $Q$ is the finite state set, and $W$ is the codec's fixed chunk width for $N$.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Codec --- Checks: further results}

\begin{definition}[Edge-code check]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.EdgeChk}
\label{Complexity.Codec.EdgeChk}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.ValidChk, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.hH}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, header width $h_H$ and chunk width $W=W(N)=h_H+3k+1$, let $x$ and $w$ be Boolean
words and $s\in\mathbb N$. The edge-code check holds of $w$ when $w$ passes the validity check
for inputs of length $|x|$ at window radius $s$, and some work tape $i<k$ has its head flag set
in the first cell or in the last cell of $w$'s chunk region: the letter of $w$ at position
$h_H+3i+2$ or at position $2sW+h_H+3i+2$ is $1$ (out-of-range letters read as $0$).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Unfolding the edge-code check]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.edgeChk_def}
\label{Complexity.Codec.edgeChk_def}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.EdgeChk, Complexity.Codec.ValidChk, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.hH}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, header width $h_H$ and chunk width $W=W(N)=h_H+3k+1$, let $x$ and
$w$ be Boolean words and $s\in\mathbb N$. The edge-code check holds of $w$ if and only if $w$
passes the validity check for inputs of length $|x|$ at radius $s$ and there is a work tape
$i<k$ such that the letter of $w$ at position $h_H+3i+2$ or at position $2sW+h_H+3i+2$ is $1$
(out-of-range letters read as $0$).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Head flags in a configuration word]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.getD_cfgWord_head}
\label{Complexity.Codec.getD_cfgWord_head}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.W_eq, Complexity.Codec.cellOf_head, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord, Complexity.Codec.chunkBit_tape, Complexity.Codec.getD_cfgWord_chunk, Complexity.Codec.hH, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, header width $h_H$ and chunk width $W=W(N)=h_H+3k+1$.
Let $x$ be a Boolean input, $s\in\mathbb N$, $C$ a configuration of $N$ on $x$, $j<2s+1$ and
$i<k$. Then the letter at position $Wj+h_H+3i+2$ of the radius-$s$ code word of $C$ is $1$ if
and only if the head of work tape $i$ in $C$ is at position $j-s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Edge-code check characterizes edge configurations]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.edgeChk_iff}
\label{Complexity.Codec.edgeChk_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.EdgeChk, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord, Complexity.Codec.getD_cfgWord_head, Complexity.Codec.hH, Complexity.Codec.validChk_iff, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, header width $h_H$ and chunk width $W=W(N)=h_H+3k+1$,
let $x$ be a Boolean input, $s\in\mathbb N$ and $w$ a Boolean word. The edge-code check
(validity for inputs of length $|x|$ at radius $s$, plus a $1$ at position $h_H+3i+2$ or
$2sW+h_H+3i+2$ of $w$ for some work tape $i$) holds of $w$ if and only if $w$ is the radius-$s$
code word of some configuration $C$ of $N$ on $x$ that lies in the radius-$s$ window (every work
head within distance $s$ of the origin and every work cell farther out blank) and has some work
head at position $p$ with $\abs{p}=s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Edge-code language through the check]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.edgeLang_iff}
\label{Complexity.Codec.edgeLang_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.EdgeChk, Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.edgeChk_iff, Complexity.Codec.edgeLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_codeLang_iff, Complexity.Codec.mem_edgeLang_iff, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, header width $h_H$ and chunk width $W=W(N)=h_H+3k+1$,
let $x,w$ be Boolean words and $s\in\mathbb N$. The word
$\langle x,\langle w,\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$ belongs to the edge-code language of $N$
(the triples $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(c),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$ with $c$ the
radius-$s$ code of a configuration of $N$ on $x$ in the radius-$s$ window having a work head at
$-s$ or $s$) if and only if $w$ passes the edge-code check: it passes the validity check for
inputs of length $|x|$ at radius $s$, and for some work tape $i$ the letter of $w$ at position
$h_H+3i+2$ or $2sW+h_H+3i+2$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Syntactic conditions on edge-tail instructions]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.EdgeOK}
\label{Complexity.Codec.EdgeOK}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.LogProg.Ins}
A predicate on the instructions of a register program with $21$ registers, $2$ oracle deciders
and the codec program's labels for a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$: an equality
test between registers $r$ and $s$ satisfies it exactly when $r\ne s$; an oracle call
satisfies it exactly when its list of argument registers has no repetitions; the three
instructions comparing a register's binary expansion with a payload word of the input never
satisfy it; and every other instruction always satisfies it.
\end{definition}

word, $B$ a natural number, $\ell$ a label of the $21$-register codec program for $N$, and
$v$ an assignment of naturals to the $21$ registers with $v(r)\le B$ for every $r$. If the
codec program in edge-code mode has at $\ell$ an instruction $I$ such that every equality test
in $I$ compares two distinct registers, every oracle call in $I$ has pairwise distinct argument
registers, and $I$ is not one of the three input-comparison instructions, then the live
configuration at $\ell$ with registers $v$ satisfies the bounded-run guard on input $y$: it
meets the program's syntactic preconditions and all its registers are at most $B$.
\end{lemma}

\section{Space Complexity --- Codec --- Langs}

\begin{definition}[Valid configuration encoding language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.validLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.validLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The
valid-configuration language consists of Boolean strings $y$ for which there exist a
Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $c,s$ such that $y$ is the pair encoding of $x$
and the pair encoding of the binary representations of $c$ and $s$, and there is a
configuration $C$ of $N$ on input $x$ that lies in the window of size $s$ and has
configuration code $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial configuration encoding language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.initLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.initLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The
initial-configuration encoding language consists of Boolean strings $y$ for which there
exist a Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $c,s$ such that $y$ is the pair encoding
of $x$ and the pair encoding of the binary representations of $c$ and $s$, and the
initial configuration of $N$ on input $x$ has configuration code $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Accepting configuration encoding language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The
accepting-configuration encoding language consists of Boolean strings $y$ for which
there exist a Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $c,s$ such that $y$ is the pair
encoding of $x$ and the pair encoding of the binary representations of $c$ and $s$, and
there is a configuration $C$ of $N$ on input $x$ that lies in the window of size $s$,
has configuration code $c$, has no current state, and has output consisting of the
single Boolean value true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One-step configuration encoding language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.stepLang}
\label{Complexity.Codec.stepLang}

Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The
one-step configuration language consists of Boolean strings $y$ for which there exist a
Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $c,c',s$ such that $y$ is the nested pair
encoding of $x$ and the binary representations of $c,c',s$, and there are configurations
$C,C'$ of $N$ on input $x$ such that $C$ lies in the window of size $s$ and has code
$c$, $C'$ follows $C$ in one machine step, $C'$ also lies in that window, and $C'$ has
code $c'$.
\end{definition}

configurations $C,C'$ on input $x$ such that $C$ lies within window $s$ and has code
$c$, $C'$ is obtained from $C$ by one step of $N$ and lies within window $s$, and $C'$
has code $c'$.
\end{theorem}

and $Q1$ to $2n+2+4W(N)s+2W(N)$, $F$ to that quantity plus $2w_P(n)$, and $U$ to that
quantity plus $2w_P(n)+4$; and setting $Pos$ to $pos$. Every other register retains its
value from $R$.

Let $j$ be the first element of the two-element index set $\mathrm{Fin}(2) = \{0, 1\}$; thus $j=0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Second index in a two-element set]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.jBit}
\label{Complexity.Codec.jBit}
\leanok
Let $j$ be the second element of the two-element index set $\mathrm{Fin}(2) = \{0, 1\}$; thus $j=1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Code modes]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.CMode}
\label{Complexity.Codec.CMode}
\leanok
Define a five-element type of code modes, with one mode for valid codes, one for the
initial code, one for accepting codes, one for step pairs, and one for codes whose work head
lies on the boundary of the window (edge mode).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Copy-loop labels]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.CpId}
\label{Complexity.Codec.CpId}
\leanok
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the finite type of copy-loop labels, whose 29 distinct elements are
“A,” “B,” “Q1s,” “Cap,” “Q2,” “N1,” “Tn,” “E,” “Ts,” “F,” “Tw,” “U,” “Q1f,” “E2,” “Ts2,” “F2,”
“Tw2,” “U2,” “Q1f2,” “Tpos,” “Q3,” “Q4,” “Q1a,” “Q2a,” “Uc,” “Tsc,” “Ue,” “Qe,” and “Te.”
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Scale-loop labels]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.ScId}
\label{Complexity.Codec.ScId}
\leanok
Let $\mathrm{ScId}$ be the finite type of scale-loop labels, consisting of seven distinct
labels, denoted $E$, $F$, $E_2$, $F_2$, $\mathrm{In}$, $C$, and $E_e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Increment-chain labels]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.IcId}
\label{Complexity.Codec.IcId}
\leanok
Let $\mathrm{IcId}$ be the finite type of increment-chain labels, with nine constructors,
denoted $E$, $U$, $E_2$, $U_2$, $C$, $E_h$, $K_e$, $S_1$, and $S_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Data codec labels]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.DcId}
\label{Complexity.Codec.DcId}
\leanok
Let $\mathrm{DcId}$ be the three-element type whose elements are $S$, $Pos$, and $Pos2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Comparison phase tags]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.PmPh}
\label{Complexity.Codec.PmPh}
\leanok
The type of comparison-phase tags has eight forms: `start`, `eq`, `inc`, `eq2`, `decR`
and `incR` each carrying a Boolean parameter, and `decN` and `eq3`.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Virtual-adder states]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.VAd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.VAd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.AdSt, Complexity.Codec.VSt, Complexity.Codec.hH}
For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, a virtual-adder state is an augmented
state whose underlying state is a virtual-machine state, with a pointer and an array of
$h_H(N)+3k$ cells; the pointer ranges from $0$ through $h_H(N)+3k$, and each cell stores
a pair of Booleans.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Simulation-adder states]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.SAd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.SAd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.AdSt, Complexity.Codec.SSt, Complexity.Codec.hH}
For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, a simulation-adder state is an
augmented state whose underlying state is a simulation state, with a pointer and an
array of $h_H(N)+3k$ cells; the pointer ranges from $0$ through $h_H(N)+3k$, and each
cell stores a pair of Booleans.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Machine simulation labels]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Lab}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Lab}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CpId, Complexity.Codec.DcId, Complexity.Codec.IcId, Complexity.Codec.PmPh, Complexity.Codec.SAd, Complexity.Codec.SInfo, Complexity.Codec.ScId, Complexity.Codec.VAd, Complexity.Codec.VSt, Complexity.Codec.W}
For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, the label type is generated by the
rejection and acceptance labels; labels for length scanning and incrementing; and
parameterized labels for the prefix, copying, counting, decrementing, simulation, and
input-processing routines. Its constructors also include labels indexed by states or
configurations of $N$, finite register indices, Boolean flags, and the comparison-phase
tags.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Unconditional label jump]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.goto}
\label{Complexity.Codec.goto}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.rZ, Complexity.LogProg.Ins}
For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ and a label $\ell$, the instruction
associated with $\ell$ is a zero-test on the distinguished register $r_Z$ whose two
branches both go to $\ell$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Copy destination register]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.cpDst}
\label{Complexity.Codec.cpDst}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CpId, Complexity.Codec.rA, Complexity.Codec.rB, Complexity.Codec.rCap, Complexity.Codec.rE, Complexity.Codec.rE2, Complexity.Codec.rF, Complexity.Codec.rF2, Complexity.Codec.rN1, Complexity.Codec.rQ1, Complexity.Codec.rQ2, Complexity.Codec.rQ3, Complexity.Codec.rQ4, Complexity.Codec.rT, Complexity.Codec.rU}
For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, the copy-identifier type has the
constructors
$A,B,Q1s,Cap,Q2,N1,Tn,E,Ts,F,Tw,U,Q1f,E2,Ts2,F2,Tw2,U2,Q1f2,Tpos,Q3,Q4,Q1a,Q2a,Uc,Tsc$.
The destination-register map sends these, respectively, to
$r_A,r_B,r_{Q1},r_{Cap},r_{Q2},r_{N1},r_T,r_E,r_T,r_F,r_T,r_U,r_{Q1},r_{E2},r_T,r_{F2},r_T,r_U,r_{Q1},r_T,r_{Q3},r_{Q4},r_{Q1},r_{Q2},r_U,r_T$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Copy source register]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.cpSrc}
\label{Complexity.Codec.cpSrc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CpId, Complexity.Codec.rA, Complexity.Codec.rB, Complexity.Codec.rE, Complexity.Codec.rE2, Complexity.Codec.rF, Complexity.Codec.rF2, Complexity.Codec.rL, Complexity.Codec.rN1, Complexity.Codec.rP, Complexity.Codec.rPos, Complexity.Codec.rS, Complexity.Codec.rWp}
For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, the copy-identifier type has the
constructors
$A,B,Q1s,Cap,Q2,N1,Tn,E,Ts,F,Tw,U,Q1f,E2,Ts2,F2,Tw2,U2,Q1f2,Tpos,Q3,Q4,Q1a,Q2a,Uc,Tsc$.
The source-register map sends these, respectively, to
$r_P,r_P,r_P,r_L,r_L,r_A,r_{N1},r_A,r_S,r_E,r_{Wp},r_F,r_F,r_B,r_S,r_{E2},r_{Wp},r_{F2},r_{F2},r_{Pos},r_A,r_B,r_A,r_A,r_A,r_S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial virtual-adder configuration]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.vAd0}
\label{Complexity.Codec.vAd0}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.VAd, Complexity.Codec.vInit}
For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, the initial virtual-adder
configuration has underlying state $vInit(N)$, pointer $0$, and every cell stores
$(\mathrm{false},\mathrm{false})$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial address state]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.sAd0}
\label{Complexity.Codec.sAd0}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.SAd, Complexity.Codec.sInit}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, the initial
address state consists of two copies of the initial state $sInit(N)$, head position $0$,
and a tape of length $hH(N)+3k$ whose entries are all $(\mathrm{false},\mathrm{false})$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Successor labels for copy identifiers]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.cpNext}
\label{Complexity.Codec.cpNext}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CpId, Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.vAd0}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape alphabet. Define a
function from the copy identifiers to control labels by assigning
$A,B,Q1s,Cap,Q2,N1,Tn,E,Ts,F,Tw,U,Q1f$ respectively to the labels for scanning the first
and second registers, copying the capacity, testing the counter, testing the $S$
down-counter, halving $N$, testing the halving counter, copying $Ts$, scanning $E$,
copying $Tw$, scanning $F$, incrementing $U$ at position $0$, and testing the $Pos$
down-counter. Assign $E2,Ts2,F2,Tw2,U2,Q1f2,Tpos,Q3,Q4,Q1a,Q2a,Uc,Tsc$ respectively to
copying $Ts2$, scanning $E2$, copying $Tw2$, scanning $F2$, incrementing $U2$ at
position $0$, testing the $Pos2$ down-counter, decrementing the input counter, copying
$Q4$, clearing the first verification register, copying $Q2a$, testing the initial
verification state, copying $Tsc$, and scanning $C$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decrement-control pointer]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.dcPtr}
\label{Complexity.Codec.dcPtr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.DcId, Complexity.Codec.rQ1, Complexity.Codec.rQ2}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, the
decrement-control pointer sends $S$ to the register position $16$ and sends both $Pos$
and $Pos2$ to position $15$, among the $21$ register positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decrement-control base positions]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.dcBase}
\label{Complexity.Codec.dcBase}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.DcId, Complexity.Codec.rE, Complexity.Codec.rE2, Complexity.Codec.rP}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, the base-position
map sends $S$ to register position $1$, $Pos$ to position $7$, and $Pos2$ to position
$9$, among the $21$ register positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decrement-control accumulator positions]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.dcAcc}
\label{Complexity.Codec.dcAcc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.DcId, Complexity.Codec.rPos, Complexity.Codec.rPos2, Complexity.Codec.rS}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, the
accumulator-position map sends $S$ to register position $4$, $Pos$ to position $11$, and
$Pos2$ to position $12$, among the $21$ register positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decrement-control strides]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.dcStride}
\label{Complexity.Codec.dcStride}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.DcId}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, the stride
assigned to $S$ is $1$, while the strides assigned to $Pos$ and $Pos2$ are both $2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Upper bound on decrement strides]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.dcStride_le}
\label{Complexity.Codec.dcStride_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.DcId, Complexity.Codec.dcStride}
\difficulty{4}
For every decrement instruction identifier, its stride is at most $2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Decrement-control descent labels]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.dcDowns}
\label{Complexity.Codec.dcDowns}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.DcId, Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.dcStride, Complexity.Codec.dcStride_le}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, a
decrement-control identifier $c$ and natural number $i$ determine a label as follows: if
$i$ is less than the stride assigned to $c$, the label is the descent label for $c$ at
index $i$; otherwise, it is the read label for $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decrement-control increment labels]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.dcIncs}
\label{Complexity.Codec.dcIncs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.DcId, Complexity.Codec.Lab}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, a
decrement-control identifier $c$, a Boolean value $b$, and a natural number $i$
determine a label as follows: if $i<2$, the label is the increment label for $c$ and $b$
at index $i$; otherwise, it is the scale label for $c$ and $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Next labels for counter operations]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.dcNext}
\label{Complexity.Codec.dcNext}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.DcId, Complexity.Codec.Lab}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, define a
label-valued map on the three counter identifiers by sending $S$ to the copy label for
$N1$, $Pos$ to the first length-test label, and $Pos2$ to the input-zero label.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Source register for scaling operations]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.scSrc}
\label{Complexity.Codec.scSrc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.ScId, Complexity.Codec.rT}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, define the
source-register map for scaling identifiers to be constant: every identifier is assigned
register $13$ among the $21$ registers.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Destination registers for scaling operations]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.scDst}
\label{Complexity.Codec.scDst}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.ScId, Complexity.Codec.rE, Complexity.Codec.rE2, Complexity.Codec.rF, Complexity.Codec.rF2, Complexity.Codec.rU}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, define the
destination-register map on the six scaling identifiers by assigning $E,F,E2,F2,In,C$
respectively to registers $7,8,9,10,14,14$ among the $21$ registers.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Scaling factors]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.scFactor}
\label{Complexity.Codec.scFactor}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.ScId, Complexity.Codec.W}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, let $h$ be the
number of pairs consisting of an optional state of $N$ and one of three head positions,
and put $W=h+3k+1$, where $k$ is the number of tapes. Define the scaling factors for
$E,F,E2,F2,In,C$ to be respectively $4W,2,4W,2,2,2W$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Upper bound for scan factors]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.scFactor_le}
\label{Complexity.Codec.scFactor_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.ScId, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.scFactor}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ and every scan identifier $c$, the
scan factor associated with $c$ is at most four times the width $W$ of the machine's
encoding.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Increment labels up to a scaling factor]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.scIncs}
\label{Complexity.Codec.scIncs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.ScId, Complexity.Codec.scFactor, Complexity.Codec.scFactor_le}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, a scaling
identifier $c$, and a natural number $i$, let $q_c$ be its scaling factor. If $i<q_c$,
assign the label that increments counter $c$ at position $i$; otherwise assign the label
for counter $c$ itself.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Next labels for scaling operations]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.scNext}
\label{Complexity.Codec.scNext}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.ScId, Complexity.Codec.W}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, define the
next-label map on the scaling identifiers by sending $E$ to the first increment-check
label for counter $E$, $F$ to the first clearing label, $E2$ to the corresponding first
increment-check label for $E2$, $F2$ to the second clearing label, $In$ to the
input-reading label, and $C$ to the first increment-check label for counter $C$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Registers for increment counters]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.icReg}
\label{Complexity.Codec.icReg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.IcId, Complexity.Codec.rE, Complexity.Codec.rE2, Complexity.Codec.rU}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, define the
register map on the five increment-counter identifiers $E,U,E2,U2,C$ to take the
respective values $7,14,9,14,14$, among the $21$ registers.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Increment-counter sizes]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.icCount}
\label{Complexity.Codec.icCount}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.IcId, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.hH}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape alphabet, let $h$ be the
number of pairs consisting of an optional state of $N$ and one of three head positions,
and put $W=h+3k+1$, where $k$ is the number of tapes. Define the sizes for identifiers
$E,U,E2,U2,C$ to be respectively $2W,4,2W,4,2(h+2)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Bound on Increment Counts]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.icCount_le}
\label{Complexity.Codec.icCount_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.IcId, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.icCount}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and let
$k$ be its number of work tapes. Write $H$ for the number of head descriptors and
$W=H+3k+1$. For every increment-count identifier $c$, its associated count is at most
$4W$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Next label for an instruction counter]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.icNext}
\label{Complexity.Codec.icNext}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.IcId, Complexity.Codec.Lab}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The map
from instruction identifiers to labels sends $E$ to the copy label for $F$, $U$ to the
length-check label, $E2$ to the copy label for $F2$, $U2$ to the second length-check
label, and $C$ to the center-read label.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Label at an instruction index]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.icL}
\label{Complexity.Codec.icL}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.IcId, Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.icCount, Complexity.Codec.icCount_le, Complexity.Codec.icNext}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $c$
be an instruction identifier, and let $i$ be a natural number. If $i$ is less than the
instruction count assigned to $c$, the resulting label is the indexed instruction label
at position $i$; otherwise it is the next label assigned to $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Continuation label for a prefix scan]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.prCont}
\label{Complexity.Codec.prCont}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CMode, Complexity.Codec.Lab}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $m$
be one of the four code modes (valid, initial, accepting, or step-pair), let
$p\in\{0,1,2\}$, and let $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. For $k=0$ or $1$, the label tests position
$p$ with Boolean parameter false or true, respectively; for $k=2$, it scans at position
$p$. For $k=3$, it selects the copy label for $A$ when $p=0$, the copy label for $B$
when $p=1$ and $m$ is the step-pair mode, the copy label for $Q1s$ when $p=1$ in any
other mode or when $p=2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Prefix-scan advancement label]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.prAdvL}
\label{Complexity.Codec.prAdvL}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CMode, Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.prCont}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $m$
be one of the four code modes (valid, initial, accepting, or step-pair), let
$p\in\{0,1,2\}$ and $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, and let $i$ be a natural number. If $i=0$, the
label is the advancement label indexed by $p$ and $k$; if $i>0$, it is the continuation
label determined by $m$, $p$, and $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Second verifier advancement label]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.vA2}
\label{Complexity.Codec.vA2}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.VAd}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $s$
be a verifier address state, and let $i$ be a natural number. If $i<2$, the label is the
second advancement label for $s$, indexed by $i$; otherwise it is the test label for
$s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[First verifier advancement label]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.vA1}
\label{Complexity.Codec.vA1}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.VAd, Complexity.Codec.vA2}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $s$
be a verifier address state, and let $i$ be a natural number. If $i<2$, the label is the
first advancement label for $s$, indexed by $i$; otherwise it is the second advancement
label for $s$ at index $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Verifier transition function]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.δV}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.VAd, Complexity.Codec.adStep, Complexity.Codec.vChunk}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. The
verifier transition function maps a verifier address state and a pair of Boolean input
symbols to the state obtained by applying one address step using the verifier chunk
associated with $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Simulation transition function]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.δS}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Gs, Complexity.Codec.SAd, Complexity.Codec.SInfo, Complexity.Codec.adStep, Complexity.Codec.sChunk}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let
$I$ consist of a verifier state and an optional Boolean value. The simulation transition
function maps an address state and a pair of Boolean input symbols to the state obtained
by applying one address step using the simulation chunk determined by $N$ and $I$, with
its Boolean parameter set first to false and then to true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Second simulation advance label]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.sA2}
\label{Complexity.Codec.sA2}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.SAd, Complexity.Codec.SInfo}
For a machine $N$, simulation information $I$, Boolean flags $f_0,f_1$, simulation state
$st$, and natural number $i$, define a label as follows: if $i<2$, it is the second
advance label carrying $I,f_0,f_1,st$ and the index $i$; otherwise it is the simulation
test label carrying $I,f_0,f_1,st$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[First simulation advance label]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.sA1}
\label{Complexity.Codec.sA1}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.SAd, Complexity.Codec.SInfo, Complexity.Codec.sA2}
For a machine $N$, simulation information $I$, Boolean flags $f_0,f_1$, simulation state
$st$, and natural number $i$, define a label as follows: if $i<2$, it is the first
advance label carrying $I,f_0,f_1,st$ and the index $i$; otherwise it is the second
simulation advance label with the same data and index $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Next simulation phase]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.pmNext}
\label{Complexity.Codec.pmNext}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.Codec.SInfo, Complexity.Codec.sAd0}
For a machine $N$, simulation information $I$, and Boolean values $b,f,r$, define the
next label to be the simulation test label carrying $I,f,r$ and the initial simulation
state when $b$ is true; when $b$ is false, define it to be the phase label carrying $I$,
flags $\mathrm{true},r$, and starting phase.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Register Program for the Codec]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.CA}
\label{Complexity.Codec.CA}
\leanok

For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ and a mode $m$ chosen from the four
cases valid, initial, accepting, and step, define a register program with $21$ registers
and two deciders by the instruction assigned to each label. The labels and their
instructions are precisely those in the definition: the program scans and validates
encoded inputs, performs register updates and decider calls, and returns a Boolean
answer according to the selected mode.
\end{definition}

%%% added by the blueprint pipeline
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Codec --- Machine: further results}

Throughout, $N$ is a nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$
work tapes and state set $Q$, and $\mathcal{A}^m_N$ is the codec register machine of $N$
in mode $m$: an abstract register machine with $21$ registers (among them $A$, $S$, $T$,
$U$, $Q_1$, $Q_3$, $Z$), a length oracle and a bit oracle for its input, and an
instruction at every label. The statements below give its instructions at the labels of
the edge-code tail, together with the parameters of the copy, scale and increment loops
that tail uses.

\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.CMode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet and $m$ any mode.
In the codec register machine $\mathcal{A}^m_N$ of $N$ in mode $m$, the instruction at the
accepting label $\mathsf{acc}$ halts with answer $\mathsf{true}$.
\end{lemma}

\section{Space Complexity --- Codec --- Parse}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec.Parse
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Codec --- Parse: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec.Parse}.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Codec --- Parse: Results}

\begin{definition}[Input-dependent computation bound]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.bnd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.bnd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W}
For a Boolean nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ and a Boolean list $y$, define the
bound $B_N(y)=(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$, where $W_N$ is the machine-dependent width parameter.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[A list length bound]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.length_le_bnd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.length_le_bnd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.bnd}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and let $y$ be a
finite Boolean string. If $W$ is the machine-dependent quantity defined by the codec,
then $|y| \le (8W+8)(|y|+1)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recovering a bit from the encoded first component]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.pe_getD_fst}
\label{Complexity.Codec.pe_getD_fst}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairEncode_getD, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
For bit strings $u,v$ and an index $i<|u|$, the bit of their self-delimiting pairing at
position $2i$ is $u_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recovering a bit from the encoded second component]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.pe_getD_snd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.pe_getD_snd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairEncode_getD_snd, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
For bit strings $u,v$ and any natural number $j$, the bit of their self-delimiting
pairing at position $2|u|+2+j$ equals the bit of $v$ at position $j$, with positions
beyond a string's end interpreted as false.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Dropping the encoded first component]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.pe_drop}
\label{Complexity.Codec.pe_drop}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.dbl, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode_eq_dbl}
\difficulty{3}
For any bit strings $u$ and $v$, dropping the first $2|u|+2$ bits from their
self-delimiting pairing $\langle u,v\rangle$ yields exactly $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Canonicality from the default last bit]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.canon_of_getLastD}

\difficulty{1}
Let $w$ be a finite Boolean string. If its last bit, with the convention that the
default value for the empty string is true, is true, then either $w$ is empty or its
final bit is true.
\end{lemma}

default if the list is empty, is true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Value bound from bit width]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.bitsVal_le_of_width}
\label{Complexity.Codec.bitsVal_le_of_width}

\begin{lemma}[Final bit of a canonical word]

\leanok

\begin{lemma}[Well-shaped inputs are nested pairs]

\label{Complexity.Codec.Shape1.eq}

\difficulty{1}
Let $y,x,w$ be Boolean strings and $s\in\mathbb{N}$, and write
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ for the pair encoding and $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ for the binary
expansion of $n$. Suppose $y=\langle x,\langle w,\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle$ and
$|\mathrm{bin}(s)|\le|\mathrm{bin}(|y|)|$. Then
$y=\langle x,\langle w,\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Width check of well-shaped inputs]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.Shape1.width}
\label{Complexity.Codec.Shape1.width}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Shape1}
\difficulty{1}
Let $y,x,w$ be Boolean strings and $s\in\mathbb{N}$, and write
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ for the pair encoding and $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ for the binary
expansion of $n$. Suppose $y=\langle x,\langle w,\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle$ and
$|\mathrm{bin}(s)|\le|\mathrm{bin}(|y|)|$. Then the binary expansion of $s$ is no longer
than the binary expansion of $|y|$, that is, $|\mathrm{bin}(s)|\le|\mathrm{bin}(|y|)|$.
\end{lemma}

$i<|w|$, the input bit at the base offset by the stride times $i$ equals the $i$th bit
of $w$. Then the codec program in the given mode, starting at its decode-test
instruction with assignment $v$, reaches its next instruction for $c$ with the pointer
reset to its base value and the accumulator equal to the binary value of $w$, leaving
all other registers unchanged. Every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the
program's safety condition and has all register values at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Bit encoding of a cell]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.chunkBit}
\label{Complexity.Codec.chunkBit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CellV, Complexity.Codec.hH, Complexity.Codec.hdNum}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let a cell
value contain an optional head descriptor and, for each tape, an optional Boolean symbol
and a Boolean marker. For each natural number $t$, define the encoded bit as follows:
if $t<h_H(N)$, it records whether the head descriptor has index $t$. Otherwise set
$i=\lfloor(t-h_H(N))/3\rfloor$. If $i<k$, the remainder of $t-h_H(N)$ upon division
by $3$ selects, for tape $i$, the symbol-presence bit, its Boolean value (false if
absent), or its marker, for remainders $0,1,2$, respectively. If $i\ge k$,
the bit is true.
\end{definition}

\section{Space Complexity --- Constructible}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Constructible
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Constructible: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Constructible}.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Constructible: Results}

\begin{definition}[Space-constructible functions]
\lean{Complexity.SpaceConstructible}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b003}
\label{Complexity.SpaceConstructible}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace}
A function $S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is space constructible if $\lfloor\log_2
n\rfloor+1\le S(n)$ for every natural number $n$, and there exist a positive natural
number $c$ and a finite Boolean Turing machine that, on every Boolean input $x$, outputs
the binary representation of $S(|x|)$ using at most $cS(|x|)$ work-tape cells.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the binary expansion]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_bits_length}
\label{Complexity.b3a_bits_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le_log, Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonzero natural number $n$, the length of its binary digit list equals
$\log_2(n)+1$, where $\log_2(n)$ denotes the integer logarithm used in the definition of
logarithmic space.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[B3a Word]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_word}
\label{Complexity.b3a_word}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, the associated Boolean word is the list whose first entry is
true and whose remaining entries are the binary digits of $n$ after its first digit is
removed.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the B3a word]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_word_length}
\label{Complexity.b3a_word_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.b3a_bits_length, Complexity.b3a_word, Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, the word formed by placing a true bit before the tail of
the binary expansion of $n$ has length $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Restricting buffer tape contents]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_buffer_restrict}
\label{Complexity.b3a_buffer_restrict}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean word $w$ and integer cell position $z$, restricting the buffer's
contents to positions satisfying $0\le z<|w|$ leaves its value at $z$ unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Overwrite the first buffer cell]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_buffer_overwrite}
\label{Complexity.b3a_buffer_overwrite}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean word $w$ and integer cell position $z$, the tape obtained from the
buffer for $w$ by writing true at cell $0$ has the same contents as the buffer storing
the word formed by replacing the first symbol of $w$ with true (or using the one-symbol
word true when $w$ is empty).
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Initial configuration with stored word]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_cfg}
\label{Complexity.b3a_cfg}

Let $k$ be a positive number of work tapes, let $S$ be a state set, and let $s\in S$ and
$x,w$ be Boolean words. Define a configuration on input $x$ in state $s$ with output
empty, with the first work tape initialized to contain $w$, and with every other work
tape blank.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[State renaming of the initial buffer configuration]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_cfg_map}
\label{Complexity.b3a_cfg_map}

Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $S,T$ be sets, let $f:S\to T$, let $s\in S$, and let
$x,w$ be Boolean words. Renaming the state of the initial $k$-tape configuration on
input $x$, with $w$ stored on the first work tape, by $f$ gives exactly the
corresponding configuration with initial state $f(s)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Embedding the initial buffer configuration]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_embed_cfg}
\label{Complexity.b3a_embed_cfg}
\leanok

tapes and Boolean symbols, and let $\iota$ be an injection from the $m$ tape indices
into the $k$ tape indices such that $\iota(0)=0$. For any $s\in S$ and Boolean words
$x,w$, embedding the configuration with initial state $s$ and $w$ on its first tape into

\begin{lemma}[Space bound for an embedded machine]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_embed_space}

\leanok

Let $m,k$ be natural numbers, let $S$ be a set, let $R$ be a machine with $m$ work tapes

\begin{lemma}[Space bound for sequential machine composition]
\lean{Complexity.b3a_seam_space}
\label{Complexity.b3a_seam_space}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.seamCompTM_visitedByTapeHead_ofCfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $S,T$ be sets, let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $R,Q$ be machines with $k$ work tapes
and Boolean symbols, with exit state $e_x\in S$ for $R$ and entry state $e_y\in T$ for
$Q$. Suppose configurations $d,e$ of $R$ on a Boolean input satisfy $R^a(d)=e$, the
state of $e$ is $e_x$, and no earlier run $R^u(d)$ for $u<a$ has state $e_x$. Then the
machine that runs $R$ until its exit state and switches to $Q$ at entry state $e_y$,
started from $d$ with its states relabeled into the left side of $S\oplus T$, uses at
most $\operatorname{space}_R(d,a)+\operatorname{space}_Q(e',b)$ space through time
$a+1+b$, for every $b\in\mathbb N$, where $e'$ is $e$ with its state replaced by $e_y$.
\end{lemma}

reached the exit state at any earlier time $u<t$, and its total space use through time

\begin{theorem}[Space constructibility, unfolded]

binary representation of $S(|x|)$ using at most $c\,S(|x|)$ work-tape cells.

\begin{definition}[Transition of the tail transducer]
\lean{Complexity.scp_tailδ}
\label{Complexity.scp_tailδ}
\leanok
Define the transition function of a one-pass transducer with Boolean state set
$\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and Boolean input bits: from every state, on every
input bit, the next state is $\mathrm{true}$, recording that the first bit has been read.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Emission of the tail transducer]
\lean{Complexity.scp_tailO}
\label{Complexity.scp_tailO}
\leanok
Define the emission function of a one-pass transducer with Boolean state set: in state
$\mathrm{false}$ it emits nothing on any input bit, and in state $\mathrm{true}$ it emits
the input bit $b$ itself.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The tail transducer copies after the first bit]
\lean{Complexity.scp_transduce_copy}
\label{Complexity.scp_transduce_copy}

\uses{Complexity.scp_tailO, Complexity.scp_tailδ, Complexity.transduce, Complexity.transduce_of_copy}
\difficulty{1}
Let $T$ be the one-pass transducer with Boolean states whose transition always moves to
state $\mathrm{true}$ and which, in state $q$ on input bit $b$, emits $b$ when $q$ is
$\mathrm{true}$ and emits nothing when $q$ is $\mathrm{false}$. For every Boolean word
$l$, running $T$ on $l$ from state $\mathrm{true}$ outputs exactly $l$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The tail transducer computes the tail]
\lean{Complexity.scp_transduce_tail}
\label{Complexity.scp_transduce_tail}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.scp_tailO, Complexity.scp_tailδ, Complexity.scp_transduce_copy, Complexity.transduce, Complexity.transduce_cons, Complexity.transduce_nil}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T$ be the one-pass transducer with Boolean states whose transition always moves to
state $\mathrm{true}$ and which, in state $q$ on input bit $b$, emits $b$ when $q$ is
$\mathrm{true}$ and emits nothing when $q$ is $\mathrm{false}$. For every Boolean word
$x$, running $T$ on $x$ from state $\mathrm{false}$ outputs the tail of $x$, that is,
$x$ with its first symbol removed (the empty word when $x$ is empty).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Power bound for the tail length]
\lean{Complexity.scp_tail_pow_le}
\label{Complexity.scp_tail_pow_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $c$ and every Boolean word $x$, writing $\mathrm{tail}(x)$ for
$x$ with its first symbol removed (the empty word when $x$ is empty), we have
$(|\mathrm{tail}(x)|+1)^c\le |x|^c+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Value of the polynomial branch]
\lean{Complexity.scp_value}
\label{Complexity.scp_value}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $c\ge 1$ be a natural number and let $x$ be a Boolean word, and write
$\mathrm{tail}(x)$ for $x$ with its first symbol removed. Take the binary expansion of
$1$ if $x$ is empty, and otherwise the binary expansion of the length
$1+(|\mathrm{tail}(x)|+1)^c$ of the all-true word consisting of one true bit followed by
$(|\mathrm{tail}(x)|+1)^c$ true bits. In both cases the result equals the binary
expansion of $|x|^c+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic time bound for the polynomial machine]
\lean{Complexity.scp_time_arith}
\label{Complexity.scp_time_arith}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $c,c_L,t,n,P,N$ be natural numbers with $P\le N+1$ and $t\le n$. Then
\[
  (n+1)+t+2+(5c+5)P+P+2+(P+2)+(P+1)+2+c_L(P+2)\;\le\;(5c+20+3c_L)(N+n+1).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic space bound for the polynomial machine]
\lean{Complexity.scp_space_arith}
\label{Complexity.scp_space_arith}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}

\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of work-tape windows]

natural number $s'\ge s$, all its work-tape heads lie in $[-s',s']$ and its work tapes
are blank outside that larger interval.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Winning computation prefix]

\label{Complexity.ExpBFS.WinRun}

Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $x$ be a finite binary input,
let $s\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $w$ be a finite binary string. The string $w$ is a winning
computation prefix within window radius $s$ if, for every integer $j$ with $0\le j\le
|w|$, the configuration reached from the initial configuration on input $x$ after
reading the first $j$ choice bits of $w$ lies in the window of radius $s$.
\end{definition}

$x$ be a binary input, and let $s$ be any natural number. The initial configuration of
$N$ on $x$ has every work-tape head in $[-s,s]$ and has blank contents at all work-tape
cells outside that interval.
\end{lemma}

the configuration reached after the choice string $wb$ also lies in that window, then
every configuration reached along every prefix of $wb$ lies in the window of radius $s$.

\begin{lemma}[Characterization of window runs]
\lean{Complexity.ExpBFS.winRun_iff}
\label{Complexity.ExpBFS.winRun_iff}

\uses{Complexity.ExpBFS.WinRun, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $x$
be a Boolean input, let $s\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $w$ be a Boolean choice string. Then
$w$ is a window run of $N$ on $x$ at radius $s$ if and only if, for every $j\le|w|$, the
configuration that $N$ reaches from its initial configuration on $x$ after following
the first $j$ choices of $w$ lies in the window of radius $s$: every work-head position
has absolute value at most $s$, and every work-tape cell outside $[-s,s]$ is blank.
\end{lemma}

\end{lemma}

\section{Space Complexity --- Hierarchy}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Hierarchy
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Hierarchy: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Hierarchy}.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Hierarchy: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Universal Simulation with a Space Bound]
\lean{Complexity.space_universal}
\label{Complexity.space_universal}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.pairEncode}
There exists a finite-state binary Turing machine $S$ such that for every binary word
$\alpha$ there is a positive integer $C$ with the following property: for every
$s,t\in\mathbb{N}$ and binary words $x,y$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on
input $x$ after exactly $t$ steps with output $y$ and uses at most $s$ work-tape cells
by that time, then $S$ halts on input $\langle
\mathrm{bin}(s),\langle\alpha,x\rangle\rangle$ with output $y$ at some time and uses at
most $Cs$ work-tape cells by then. Here $\mathrm{bin}(s)$ is the little-endian binary
representation of $s$, and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the specified self-delimiting
pairing of binary words.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space hierarchy theorem]
\lean{Complexity.space_hierarchy}
\label{Complexity.space_hierarchy}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SpaceConstructible}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be space-constructible functions. Suppose that for
every $A\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an $N$ such that $A f(n)\le g(n)$ for every $n\ge N$.
Then $\mathrm{SPACE}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{SPACE}(g)$, where each class
consists of languages decidable by a finite binary Turing machine using at most a
constant multiple of the indicated space bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict inclusion of log space in polynomial space]
\lean{Complexity.LOGSPACE_ssubset_PSPACE}
\label{Complexity.LOGSPACE_ssubset_PSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.PSPACE}
The class of languages decidable by finite Turing machines using space bounded by a
constant multiple of $\log_2(n)+1$ is a proper subset of the class of languages
decidable using space bounded by a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ for some natural number
$c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear space differs from NP]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE_linear_ne_NP}
\label{Complexity.SPACE_linear_ne_NP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.SPACE}
The class of binary languages decidable by finite Turing machines using space bounded by
a constant multiple of the input length plus one is not equal to the class of languages
having polynomially bounded witnesses verifiable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

decoded from $\alpha$ halts on $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ by time $t$ with output $y$ having visited at
most $s$ cells, $U_0$ halts on $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ at some time with output $y$ having visited
at most $C(s+1)$ cells. Let $L$ be a binary language decided by a finite binary machine within space
