Let a finite sequence of segments be given, each consisting of a Boolean word and a
Boolean flag. For a segment index $s$ within this sequence, suppose a tape position is
valid: positions at the left or right boundary are always valid, and a position at a
cell is valid when its cell index is less than that segment's word length. For any move
direction, the resulting segment index remains within the sequence, and the resulting
position is valid for that segment.
\end{lemma}

\lean{Complexity.LogProg.vpos_right_last}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.vpos_right_last}

position immediately to the right of that segment is one position beyond the length of

\begin{lemma}[Offset and segment length bound]

For natural numbers $N,p$ with $p<N+2$, and for a movement sign $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$, the

\begin{lemma}[Virtual head movement agrees with tape movement]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.vpos_tmove}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.vpos_tmove}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.Valid, Complexity.LogProg.cellOff, Complexity.LogProg.moveInputPos_val, Complexity.LogProg.off, Complexity.LogProg.off_add_rlen_le, Complexity.LogProg.off_succ, Complexity.LogProg.rlen, Complexity.LogProg.rlen_false, Complexity.LogProg.rlen_true, Complexity.LogProg.seg, Complexity.LogProg.tmove, Complexity.LogProg.vpos, Complexity.LogProg.vpos_right_last, Complexity.LogProg.vword, Complexity.LogProg.wlen, Turing.moveInputPos}

\begin{definition}[Symbol at a tape position]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.vsym}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.vsym}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.seg}
For a list of segments and an index $s$, the symbol at the left boundary is absent when
$s=0$ and otherwise is true. At a cell with index $c$, it is the Boolean at index $c$ in
the selected segment's list, if present. At the right boundary, it is false when a next
segment exists and is absent otherwise.

\begin{lemma}[Virtual input symbol at a segment position]

## ===== blueprint/src/chapter/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Machines/Program.tex =====

\section{Space Complexity --- Machines --- Program}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Program
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Machines --- Program: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Program}.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Machines --- Program: Results}

\begin{definition}[Virtual input mode]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.Mode}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.Mode}
\leanok
A virtual-input mode is one of two choices: use the whole input, doubled, or use the
leading run of $1$s in the input as a plain segment.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[First virtual-input segment]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Mode, Complexity.LogProg.Seg}
For a mode and Boolean word $x$, the first segment is the pair $(x,1)$ in whole-input
mode, and the pair consisting of the leading run of $1$s in $x$ and $0$ in unary-prefix
mode.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Argument word segmentation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.argSegs}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.argSegs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Seg}
For a list of Boolean words, the argument segments are empty for an empty list, and
consist of the sole word paired with $0$ for a one-word list. For a list with at least
two words, the first word is paired with $1$, followed by the argument segments of the
remaining words.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the Argument Segmentation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.length_argSegs}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.length_argSegs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.argSegs}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite list of Boolean words, the segmentation into argument segments has the
same length as the original list.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Segments formed from argument words]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.seg_argSegs}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.seg_argSegs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.argSegs, Complexity.LogProg.seg, Complexity.LogProg.seg_cons_succ}
\difficulty{5}
Let $w_0,\ldots,w_{n-1}$ be a list of Boolean words, and form its argument segments by
marking each word except the last as doubled. For every index $i<n$, segment $i$ is the
pair consisting of $w_i$ and the flag that is true exactly when $i+1<n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Oracle call specification]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Mode}
A call specification for a program with $m$ registers, $d$ deciders, and state set
$\Lambda$ consists of a decider indexed among the $d$ choices, a virtual-input mode, an
ordered list of register indices, and a state to enter after a positive answer and a
state to enter after a negative answer.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Register program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.RProg}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.RProg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
A register program with $m$ registers, $d$ deciders, and state set $\Lambda$ consists of
an $m$-work-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet and a partial assignment of
oracle-call specifications to states.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Virtual call segments]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.callSegs}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.callSegs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec, Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0, Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.argSegs}
Given a call specification, a Boolean input word $x$, and a word $W_i$ for each of its
$m$ registers, the call’s segment list consists of the initial segment selected by the
call mode and $x$, followed by the segments formed from the words of the registers
listed in the call specification, in their listed order.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the Call Segmentation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.length_callSegs}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.length_callSegs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs}
\difficulty{1}
For a call specification with argument list of length $q$, and for any input word and
assignment of words to registers, the resulting list of call segments has length $q+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Program simulation states]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.CSt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.CSt}
\leanok
Given sets $\Lambda$ and $SD$ and a nonnegative integer $m$, define the program
simulation states to be the states of five forms: a program state labelled by an element
of $\Lambda$; a decider simulation state carrying a program label, a decider state, an
index in $\{0,\ldots,m\}$, two Boolean flags, and an optional Boolean result; two return
states, each carrying a program label, such an index, and two Boolean flags; and a
register return state carrying the same data as a return state together with a register
index in $\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$ and a Boolean scan flag.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Signed virtual-tape step]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.gstep}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.gstep}
\leanok
For Boolean flags
$\mathit{dbl},\mathit{last},\mathit{first},\mathit{par},\mathit{dir},\mathit{isChar}$
and a natural-number counter $s$, define a transition on signs as follows. Zero leaves
$(s,\mathit{par},\mathit{dir})$ unchanged and outputs zero. A positive sign, when
reading a character, changes the parity to true and outputs zero if $\mathit{dbl}$ is
true and parity is false; otherwise it sets parity to false, direction to true, and
outputs positive. For a positive sign not reading a character, if direction is true it
leaves the triple unchanged and outputs zero when $\mathit{last}$ is true, and otherwise
increments $s$, sets parity to true and direction to false, and outputs zero; if
direction is false it sets parity to false and direction to true and outputs positive. A
negative sign, when reading a character, sets parity to false and outputs zero if
$\mathit{dbl}$ is true and parity is true; otherwise it sets parity to true, direction
to false, and outputs negative. For a negative sign not reading a character, if
direction is true it sets parity to true, direction to false, and outputs negative; if
direction is false and $\mathit{first}$ is true it leaves the triple unchanged and
outputs zero; otherwise it decrements $s$, sets parity to false and direction to true,
and outputs zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Clamping into a finite range]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.toFin}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.toFin}
\leanok
For natural numbers $m$ and $s$, the associated element of $\mathrm{Fin}(m+1)$ is the
natural number $\min(s,m)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Segment doubling flag]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.segDbl}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.segDbl}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec}
Given a call specification and a natural-number segment index $s$, define a Boolean flag
that is true exactly when either $s=0$ and the call mode is whole-input, or $s>0$ and
$s$ is less than the number of listed argument registers.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Register assigned to a segment]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.segReg}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.segReg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec}
Given a call specification with $m$ registers, a natural-number segment index $s$, and
$0<m$, assign to the segment the $(s-1)$-st listed register when that position exists,
and otherwise assign register $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Character-read flag]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.isCharRead}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.isCharRead}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Mode}
Given a mode, a natural-number segment index $s$, and an optional Boolean read symbol,
define a flag that is true exactly when the read symbol is true and $s=0$ in unary-first
mode; in every other case it is true exactly when a read symbol is present.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Virtual tape symbol]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.virtSym}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.virtSym}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Mode, Complexity.LogProg.isCharRead}
Given a mode, a natural-number segment index $s$, a natural number $n$ of segments, a
direction flag, and an optional Boolean read symbol, define an optional virtual symbol
as follows. If the read counts as a character, return true when $s=0$ in unary-first
mode, and otherwise return the read symbol. If it does not count as a character, then in
the forward direction return no symbol when $s+1=n$, and false otherwise; in the reverse
direction return no symbol when $s=0$, and true otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Register movement]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.regMove}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.regMove}
\leanok
For $m\in\mathbb{N}$, a register index $r\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, and a movement
$v\in\{-1,0,1\}$, define an action on the $m$ registers that writes nothing and moves
register $r$ by $v$, leaving every other register’s head stationary.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Next return state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.nextRet}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.nextRet}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec}
Given a call specification with argument list $A$, a program location $\ell$, a segment
index $s\in\{0,\ldots,m\}$, Boolean values $d$ and $b$, and a natural number $a$, define
the next control state to be the return state that restores register $a$ if $a<|A|$ and
$a<m$. Otherwise, it is the program state selected by $b$: the positive-answer state
when $b$ is true and the negative-answer state when $b$ is false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Idle decider action]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.dIdle}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.dIdle}
\leanok
For a natural number $k_D$, define the action on each of $k_D$ decider work tapes to
write nothing and leave its head stationary.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Compiled transition function]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ctr}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ctr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.RProg, Complexity.LogProg.dIdle, Complexity.LogProg.gstep, Complexity.LogProg.isCharRead, Complexity.LogProg.nextRet, Complexity.LogProg.regMove, Complexity.LogProg.segDbl, Complexity.LogProg.segReg, Complexity.LogProg.toFin, Complexity.LogProg.virtSym, Turing.Action, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders, let $D$ be a Turing
machine with $k_D$ work tapes, and choose an initial state for each decider. Define a
transition function for control states consisting of ordinary program states,
call-simulation states, and return states, with $m+k_D$ work tapes. At an ordinary state
without a call, it performs the program’s transition on the first $m$ tapes and leaves
the remaining tapes idle; at a call, it initializes the selected decider simulation and
moves each listed argument-register head left. During simulation it runs the selected
decider on the encoded virtual input, applies the segment and head-movement update,
records the first emitted Boolean answer, and either continues simulation or begins the
return procedure if the decider halts. The return states rewind the input head and
restore the argument-register heads in order before continuing at the positive- or
negative-answer program state; transitions at states whose program location no longer
specifies a call halt.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Compiled Turing machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.compileTM}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.compileTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.RProg, Complexity.LogProg.ctr, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders, let $\ell_0$ be its
initial program location, let $D$ be a Turing machine with $k_D$ work tapes, and choose
an initial state for each decider. Define the compiled Turing machine with $m+k_D$ work
tapes and control states for the compiled simulation: its initial state is the ordinary
program state at $\ell_0$, and its transition function is the compiled transition
function determined by $P$, $D$, and the chosen decider initial states.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embedding a machine configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.seam}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.seam}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Turing.Cfg}
Given a configuration $c$ of a machine with $m$ work tapes on a Boolean input, define a
configuration of the compiled machine on the same input by mapping any present state to
the corresponding ordinary program state and retaining the input-head position and
output. The first $m$ work-tape contents and head positions are retained, while each of
the additional $k_D$ tapes is blank everywhere and has its head at position $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Compiled machine initial configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.seam_init}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.seam_init}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.RProg, Complexity.LogProg.compileTM, Complexity.LogProg.seam, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a register program, $D$ a deterministic multi-tape machine, $l_0$ a program
state, and $q_0$ a map assigning a state of $D$ to each decider index. For every Boolean
input word $x$, the compiled machine's initial configuration on $x$ equals the seam
formed from the initial configuration of $P$ on $x$ with start state $l_0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Compiled Step at a Program Node]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.step_seam_prog}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.step_seam_prog}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.RProg, Complexity.LogProg.compileTM, Complexity.LogProg.ctr, Complexity.LogProg.dIdle, Complexity.LogProg.seam, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a register program, $D$ a decider, and $q_0$ a choice of initial decider
state for each decider index. If a configuration $c$ of $P$ is at state $l$ and $l$ is
not a call node, then one step of the machine compiled from $P$ and $D$, started from
the configuration obtained by extending $c$ with idle decider tapes and marking its
state as the program state $l$, equals the extension of the configuration reached by one
step of $P$'s ordinary machine at $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Halting state under the seam construction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.seam_state_none}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.seam_state_none}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.seam, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c$ be a configuration of an $m$-tape Turing machine on a fixed Boolean input, and
suppose its state is absent, which denotes that the machine has halted. Then the state
of the configuration obtained by the seam construction is also absent.
\end{lemma}

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Machines --- Program: further results}

\begin{lemma}[Equal arguments give equal virtual inputs]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.callSegs_congr}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.callSegs_congr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs}
\difficulty{1}
Let $cs$ be a call specification for register programs with $m$ registers, $d$
deciders and state set $\Lambda$, and let $cs'$ be one for $m'$ registers, $d'$ deciders
and state set $\Lambda'$. Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $W$ and $W'$ assign a
Boolean word to each of the $m$, respectively $m'$, registers. If $cs'$ and $cs$ have
the same virtual-input mode, and the list of words that $W'$ assigns to the argument
registers of $cs'$ (in order) equals the list of words that $W$ assigns to the argument
registers of $cs$, then the virtual-input segment lists of the two calls on $x$ (with
register words $W'$ and $W$ respectively) are equal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Compiled transition at a call node]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.compileTM_tr_prog_call}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.compileTM_tr_prog_call}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec, Complexity.LogProg.RProg, Complexity.LogProg.compileTM, Complexity.LogProg.ctr, Complexity.LogProg.dIdle, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders over a state set
$\Lambda$, let $\ell_0\in\Lambda$, let $D$ be a deterministic Turing machine over the
Boolean alphabet with $k_D$ work tapes, and let $q_0$ assign a state of $D$ to each of
the $d$ decider indices. Let $\ell\in\Lambda$ be a call node of $P$ with call
specification $cs$. Then, whatever (possibly blank) symbols are read on the input tape
and on the $m+k_D$ work tapes, the transition of the compiled machine of $P$ (start
location $\ell_0$, decider $D$, start states $q_0$) from the program state $\ell$ keeps
the input head in place, writes nothing on any work tape, moves the head of every
register listed among the arguments of $cs$ one cell left while keeping all other
register heads and all $k_D$ decider heads in place, emits no output, and enters the
simulation state for the call at $\ell$ with decider state $q_0$ of the decider chosen
by $cs$, segment index $0$, parity flag false, direction flag true, and no recorded
answer.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Compiled transition at the first return step]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.compileTM_tr_ret1}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.compileTM_tr_ret1}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.RProg, Complexity.LogProg.compileTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders over a state set
$\Lambda$, let $\ell_0\in\Lambda$, let $D$ be a deterministic Turing machine over the
Boolean alphabet with $k_D$ work tapes, and let $q_0$ assign a state of $D$ to each of
the $d$ decider indices. For every $\ell\in\Lambda$, segment index
$s\in\{0,\ldots,m\}$, Boolean flags $\mathrm{dir}$ and $\mathrm{res}$, and any (possibly
blank) symbols read on the input tape and the $m+k_D$ work tapes, the transition of the
compiled machine from the first return state with data $(\ell,s,\mathrm{dir},\mathrm{res})$
moves the input head one cell left, writes nothing and keeps every work-tape head in
place, emits no output, and enters the input-rewind return state with the same data
$(\ell,s,\mathrm{dir},\mathrm{res})$.
\end{lemma}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Sim}.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Machines --- Sim: Results}

\begin{definition}[Track position]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.wlen}
For a list of segments and a segment index $s$, define the track position of the left
boundary to be $-1$, the position of cell $c$ to be $c$, and the position of the right
boundary to be the length of segment $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Cell-position indicator]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.TPos.isCell}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.TPos.isCell}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.TPos}
Define a Boolean indicator on track positions that is true for cell positions and false
for either boundary position.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Consistency of a track position]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.Consistent}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.Consistent}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.seg}
Let $S$ be a list of segments, let $s$ be a segment index, and let
$a,b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Define a predicate on track positions by
requiring the left boundary to have direction $b=\mathrm{false}$ and the right boundary
to have direction $b=\mathrm{true}$. At a cell with parity $p$, require $p=a$ whenever
the flag of segment $s$ is true.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Agreement of abstract and tape-head moves]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.gstep_tmove}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.gstep_tmove}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Consistent, Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.Valid, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.isCell, Complexity.LogProg.gstep, Complexity.LogProg.seg, Complexity.LogProg.tmove, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos, Complexity.LogProg.wlen}
\difficulty{6}
Let $S$ be a finite list of segments, let $s<	ext{length}(S)$, and let $t$ be a
tape-head position valid for segment $s$. Let $p,d	ext{ be Boolean flags such that }t$
is consistent with them: at the left boundary $d=	ext{false}$, at the right boundary
$d=	ext{true}$, and at a cell in a doubled segment its parity flag equals $p$. For any
movement $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$, apply the abstract update rule using segment $s$'s doubling
flag, whether $s$ is the last or first segment, and whether $t$ is a cell; denote its
new segment index, flags, and movement output by $s',p',d',m'$. Also apply the tape-head
move to obtain position $t'$. Then $s'$ is the segment index of $t'$, and $t'$ is
consistent with $p',d'$. Moreover, either $s'=s$ and the coordinate of $t'$ equals the
coordinate of $t$ plus $m'$, or $m'=0$ and the move crosses a segment boundary: from the
right boundary of segment $s$ to the left boundary of segment $s+1$, or from the left
boundary of segment $s$ to the right boundary of the preceding segment.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Input symbol by head position]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.inputSymbol_eq}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.inputSymbol_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM.inputSymbol_at}
\difficulty{4}
For any configuration on a Boolean input word $x$, the symbol under its input head
equals `none` when the head position is zero; otherwise it is the optional symbol of $x$
at index one less than the head position.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Entries within the initial true run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.takeWhile_true_getElem?}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean list $x$ and natural number $c$, if $c$ is less than the length of the
initial run of true entries in $x$, then the entry of $x$ at index $c$ is present and
true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Entry after the initial true run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.takeWhile_true_end}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.takeWhile_true_end}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean list $x$, the entry immediately after its initial run of true entries
is either absent or false.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Whole-Input Segment in Whole Mode]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0_whole}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0_whole}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Mode, Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0}
\difficulty{1}
Let $md$ be a mode equal to the whole-input mode, and let $x$ be a bit string. The
initial segment selected by $md$ from $x$ is $x$ itself, with its doubling flag set to
true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First-Component Segment in Unary Mode]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0_unaryFst}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0_unaryFst}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Mode, Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0}
\difficulty{1}
Let $md$ be a mode equal to the unary-first mode, and let $x$ be a bit string. The
initial segment selected by $md$ from $x$ is the leading run of $1$s in $x$, with its
doubling flag set to false.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Initial segment of a call]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.seg_callSegs_zero}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.seg_callSegs_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.seg}
\difficulty{1}
Let a call specification have a mode, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $W$ assign a
Boolean word to each register. Segment $0$ of the call's segment list is the initial
segment selected by the mode from $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Argument segments in a call]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.seg_callSegs_succ}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.seg_callSegs_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.seg, Complexity.LogProg.seg_argSegs, Complexity.LogProg.seg_cons_succ}
\difficulty{3}
Let a call specification have an ordered argument-register list, let $x$ be a Boolean
input, and let $W$ assign a Boolean word to each register. For any index $a$ less than
the length of the argument list, segment $a+1$ in the call's segment list is the pair
consisting of the word assigned by $W$ to argument register $a$, and a flag that is true
exactly when $a+1$ is less than the length of the argument list.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Doubling flag of a call segment]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.segDbl_eq}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.segDbl_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.seg, Complexity.LogProg.segDbl, Complexity.LogProg.seg_callSegs_succ, Complexity.LogProg.seg_callSegs_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let a call specification have a mode and an ordered list of argument registers, and let
$x$ be a Boolean input and $W$ assign a Boolean word to each register. For any index $s$
strictly less than one plus the number of argument registers, the flag indicating
whether segment $s$ is doubled equals the second component of segment $s$ in the list
formed from the mode's initial segment and the argument segments.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the first call segment]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.wlen_zero_le}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.wlen_zero_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.seg_callSegs_zero, Complexity.LogProg.wlen}
\difficulty{4}
For any call specification, input bit string $x$, and assignment $W$ of a bit string to
each register, the length of the first segment in the resulting call segments is at most
the length of $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Register of an argument segment]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.segReg_eq}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.segReg_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.segReg}
\difficulty{3}
Let a call specification have an ordered list of argument registers, and suppose there
is at least one register. For an index $s$ with $0<s\le$ the length of that list, the
register assigned to segment $s$ is the argument register at zero-based position $s-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Work-tape register position]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.regPos}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.regPos}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos, Complexity.LogProg.wlen}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration with $m$ work tapes, let a call specification select an
ordered list of registers, let $W$ assign a bit string to each register, and let $s$ and
$t$ be a segment index and track position. For register $r$, its position is the
position in $c_0$ if $r$ is not selected. If it is selected, write $j$ for its index in
the selected list plus one: its position is the length of segment $j$ when $j<s$, is
$-1$ when $s<j$, and is the track position at segment $s$ when $s=j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Input-head position]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.inPos}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.inPos}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos, Complexity.LogProg.wlen}
Let a call specification and register-word assignment determine the segments of a
virtual input, and let $s$ be a segment index with track position $t$. The input-head
position is the track position at segment $0$, shifted by one and converted to a natural
number, when $s=0$; when $s\ne0$, it is the length of segment $0$ plus one.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Relation between simulated tracks]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.TrackRel}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.TrackRel}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.Consistent, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.Valid, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.inPos, Complexity.LogProg.regPos, Complexity.LogProg.vpos, Complexity.LogProg.vword, Turing.Cfg}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration with $m$ work tapes, and let $g$ and $d$ be configurations
of machines with respectively $m+k_D$ and $k_D$ work tapes, on the input and virtual
input determined by a call specification and register-word assignment. A track relation
at segment $s$, parity $a$, direction $b$, and track position $t$ requires that $s$ be
among the call's segments, that $t$ be valid and consistent there, and that the
simulated and virtual input-head positions agree with their prescribed positions. It
also requires the first $m$ work tapes and their head positions in $g$ to match $c_0$
and the prescribed register positions, the remaining tapes and head positions in $g$ to
match those of $d$, and the output of $g$ to equal the output of $c_0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Simulation relation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SimRel}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SimRel}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TrackRel, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.vword, Turing.Cfg}
Let $g$ and $d$ be configurations as in the track relation, and fix a program node and a
call specification with its register-word assignment. They are related for simulation if
there exist a decider state $q$, a segment index $s$, Boolean parity and direction
values, and a track position $t$ such that $g$ is in the corresponding simulation state,
carrying the first bit of $d$'s output when present, $d$ is in state $q$, and the two
configurations satisfy the track relation at those parameters.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Halting relation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.HaltRel}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.HaltRel}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TrackRel, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.vword, Turing.Cfg}
Let $g$ and $d$ be configurations as in the track relation, and fix a program node and a
call specification with its register-word assignment. They satisfy the halting relation
if there exist a segment index $s$, Boolean parity and direction values, and a track
position $t$ such that $g$ is in the return state carrying the first bit of $d$'s
output, or false if that output is empty; $d$ has halted; and the configurations satisfy
the track relation at those parameters.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Reading the Simulated Track]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.track_read}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.track_read}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.Consistent, Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0, Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0_unaryFst, Complexity.LogProg.Mode.seg0_whole, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.Valid, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.isCell, Complexity.LogProg.TrackRel, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.inPos, Complexity.LogProg.inputSymbol_eq, Complexity.LogProg.isCharRead, Complexity.LogProg.length_callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.regPos, Complexity.LogProg.segReg, Complexity.LogProg.segReg_eq, Complexity.LogProg.seg_callSegs_succ, Complexity.LogProg.seg_callSegs_zero, Complexity.LogProg.takeWhile_true_end, Complexity.LogProg.takeWhile_true_getElem?, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos, Complexity.LogProg.virtSym, Complexity.LogProg.vsym, Complexity.LogProg.vword, Complexity.LogProg.wlen, Complexity.LogProg.wlen_zero_le, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{6}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration, let a call specification select a list of argument
registers, and let $W$ assign a Boolean word to each register. Assume each selected
register in $c_0$ stores its assigned word and the selected registers are distinct.
Suppose a configuration $g$ of the combined machine and a decider configuration $d$ are
related as follows: the current segment index is within the list of call segments, the
track position is valid and consistent with the parity and direction, the two input-head
positions represent the same virtual position, the original work tapes and their head
positions are preserved or positioned according to the track representation, the decider
tapes and head positions agree with $d$, and the output is unchanged. Define $r$ to be
the symbol read from $g$'s input head when the segment index is zero, and otherwise the
symbol under the corresponding argument-register head when such a register exists
(taking $r$ to be blank if there is no register). Then the machine reads a character
exactly when the track position is a cell, and the virtual symbol determined by the read
symbol, mode, segment, and direction equals the symbol represented by that track
position.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounds on a Track Position]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos_bounds}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos_bounds}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.Valid, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos, Complexity.LogProg.wlen}
\difficulty{3}
Let a list of segments and a segment index determine a segment length $L$. For any valid
track position, its associated integer position lies between $-1$ and $L$, inclusive.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Register position after a track move]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_after}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_after}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.regPos, Complexity.LogProg.segReg, Complexity.LogProg.segReg_eq, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos}
\difficulty{6}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration with $m$ registers, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let a
call specification with an ordered list of argument registers determine the virtual
input segments from $x$ and register words $W$. Assume the argument list has no
repetitions, $m>0$, and $s$ is at most the length of that list. For a register $r$, a
track position $tp$, a sign $mv\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and a second track position $T2$, suppose
either $G1=s$ and the track position of $T2$ equals that of $tp$ plus $mv$, or $mv=0$
and one of the following holds: $G1=s+1$, $tp$ is the right boundary and $T2$ the left
boundary; or $G1+1=s$, $tp$ is the left boundary and $T2$ the right boundary. Then the
register position at segment index $G1$ and track position $T2$ equals its position at
index $s$ and $tp$, plus $mv$ exactly when $s\ne0$ and $r$ is the argument register
selected at index $s$; otherwise the position is unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Input head position after a segment move]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.inPos_after}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.inPos_after}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.Valid, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.inPos, Complexity.LogProg.moveInputPos_val, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos_bounds, Complexity.LogProg.wlen_zero_le, Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be an input word, let a call specification and register words determine a list
of segments, and let $s$ be a segment index. A track position is valid at an index when
it is a boundary or a cell within that segment. Suppose $tp$ is valid at $s$, $T_2$ is
valid at $G_1$, and either $G_1=s$ with the track coordinate of $T_2$ equal to that of
$tp$ plus the movement $mv$, or $mv=0$ and the positions cross between the right
boundary of segment $s$ and the left boundary of segment $s+1$, or between the left
boundary of segment $s$ and the right boundary of segment $s-1$. If the input head
position $p$ encodes track position $tp$ at segment $s$, then after moving the input
head by $mv$ when $s=0$ (and by zero otherwise), its position encodes $T_2$ at segment
$G_1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Head of an appended optional bit]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.head?_append_toList}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean list $l$ and optional Boolean $o$, the head of the list obtained by
appending the elements of $o$ to $l$ is the head of $l$ if it exists, and otherwise is

\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[One-step preservation of call simulation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.sim_step}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.sim_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.HaltRel, Complexity.LogProg.RProg, Complexity.LogProg.SimRel, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.Valid, Complexity.LogProg.TPos.isCell, Complexity.LogProg.TrackRel, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.compileTM, Complexity.LogProg.ctr, Complexity.LogProg.gstep, Complexity.LogProg.gstep_tmove, Complexity.LogProg.head?_append_toList, Complexity.LogProg.inPos_after, Complexity.LogProg.inputSymbol_vpos, Complexity.LogProg.length_callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.regPos_after, Complexity.LogProg.seg, Complexity.LogProg.segDbl_eq, Complexity.LogProg.segReg, Complexity.LogProg.tmove, Complexity.LogProg.tmove_valid, Complexity.LogProg.toFin, Complexity.LogProg.track_read, Complexity.LogProg.vpos, Complexity.LogProg.vpos_tmove, Complexity.LogProg.vsym, Complexity.LogProg.vword, Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{7}
Let $P$ be a program with $m$ registers and $d$ possible deciders, let $D$ be a decider
with $k_D$ work tapes and state set $S_D$, and choose an initial state for each decider.
Fix a call state $l$, a call specification $c_s$, an initial program configuration
$c_0$, and register words $W(r)$. Suppose $P$ makes the specified call at $l$, each
argument register's tape initially stores its corresponding word $W(r)$, and the
argument list has no repetitions. Suppose also that a combined configuration $g$ and
decider configuration $d_c$ are related as follows: the combined machine is in the
simulation state corresponding to $l$ and the decider's current state; the decider is
nonhalting; and for some valid position in the virtual input, the two input-head
positions, register tapes and heads, decider tapes and heads, and output agree with the
prescribed segment-by-segment simulation correspondence. After one step of $D$, if the
decider remains nonhalting, the resulting combined and decider configurations satisfy
the same simulation relation. If the decider halts, the resulting combined configuration
instead satisfies the return relation: the combined machine is ready to rewind the
input, the decider is halted, and the same tape, head-position, and output
correspondence holds.
\end{theorem}

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Machines --- Sim: further results}

\begin{lemma}[Track position of a left boundary]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos_left}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos_left}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos}
\difficulty{1}
For every list of segments and segment index $s$, the real head position (in register
coordinates) assigned to the left-boundary track position of segment $s$ is $-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Track position of a cell]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos_cell}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos_cell}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos}
\difficulty{1}
For every list of segments, segment index $s$, cell index $c\in\mathbb{N}$ and parity bit
$p$, the real head position (in register coordinates) assigned to the cell track
position $(c,p)$ of segment $s$ is $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Track position of a right boundary]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos_right}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.trackPos_right}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos, Complexity.LogProg.wlen}
\difficulty{1}
For every list of segments and segment index $s$, the real head position (in register
coordinates) assigned to the right-boundary track position of segment $s$ is the length
of the word of segment $s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Consistency at a left boundary]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.consistent_left_iff}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.consistent_left_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Consistent, Complexity.LogProg.Seg}
\difficulty{1}
For every list of segments, segment index $s$, and Booleans $a$ (stored parity) and $b$
(direction of the last track move), the left-boundary track position of segment $s$ is
consistent with $a$ and $b$ if and only if $b$ is false, i.e. the last move went left.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Consistency at a right boundary]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.consistent_right_iff}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.consistent_right_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Consistent, Complexity.LogProg.Seg}
\difficulty{1}
For every list of segments, segment index $s$, and Booleans $a$ (stored parity) and $b$
(direction of the last track move), the right-boundary track position of segment $s$ is
consistent with $a$ and $b$ if and only if $b$ is true, i.e. the last move went right.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Consistency at a cell]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.consistent_cell_iff}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.consistent_cell_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Consistent, Complexity.LogProg.Seg, Complexity.LogProg.seg}
\difficulty{1}
For every list of segments, segment index $s$, cell index $c$, parity bit $p$, and
Booleans $a$ (stored parity) and $b$ (direction), the cell track position $(c,p)$ of
segment $s$ is consistent with $a$ and $b$ if and only if $p=a$ whenever segment $s$ is
flagged as doubled.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Input-head position in the leading segment]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.inPos_zero}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.inPos_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.inPos, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos}
\difficulty{1}
Let a call specification with $m$ registers, an input bit string $x$, and an assignment
$W$ of a bit string to each register determine the segments of the call's virtual input.
For every track position $t$, the prescribed real input-head position while the virtual
head is in segment $0$ at $t$ equals the register-coordinate position of $t$ in segment
$0$ plus one, converted to a natural number (negative values becoming $0$).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Input-head position beyond the leading segment]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.inPos_of_ne_zero}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.inPos_of_ne_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.inPos, Complexity.LogProg.wlen}
\difficulty{1}
Let a call specification with $m$ registers, an input bit string $x$, and an assignment
$W$ of a bit string to each register determine the segments of the call's virtual input.
For every segment index $s\neq 0$ and every track position $t$, the prescribed real
input-head position while the virtual head is in segment $s$ at $t$ equals the length of
the word of segment $0$ plus one.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Unfolding the simulation relation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.simRel_iff}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.simRel_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.SimRel, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TrackRel, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.vword, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration of a machine with $m$ work tapes on input $x$, let $l$ be a
program node, let a call specification and an assignment $W$ of words to the registers
determine a virtual input, let $g$ be a configuration on $x$ of the compiled machine with
$m+k_D$ work tapes, and let $d$ be a configuration with $k_D$ work tapes of a decider on
the virtual input. Then $g$ and $d$ are in the simulation relation if and only if there
exist a decider state $q$, a segment index $s\le m$, Booleans $a,b$ and a track position
$t$ such that $g$ is in the simulation state for node $l$ with decider state $q$, segment
$s$, parity $a$, direction $b$ and the first output bit of $d$ (if any), $d$ is in state
$q$, and $g$, $d$ satisfy the track relation relative to $c_0$ at $s,a,b,t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Unfolding the halting relation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.haltRel_iff}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.haltRel_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.HaltRel, Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.TrackRel, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.vword, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration of a machine with $m$ work tapes on input $x$, let $l$ be a
program node, let a call specification and an assignment $W$ of words to the registers
determine a virtual input, let $g$ be a configuration on $x$ of the compiled machine with
$m+k_D$ work tapes, and let $d$ be a configuration with $k_D$ work tapes of a decider on
the virtual input. Then $g$ and $d$ are in the halting relation if and only if there
exist a segment index $s\le m$, Booleans $a,b$ and a track position $t$ such that $g$ is
in the first return state for node $l$ with segment $s$, direction $b$ and the first
output bit of $d$ (false if $d$ has no output), $d$ has halted, and $g$, $d$ satisfy the
track relation relative to $c_0$ at $s,a,b,t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Position of a non-argument register]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_of_not_mem}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_of_not_mem}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.regPos}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration with $m$ work tapes (registers), and let a call specification
with argument registers $r_1,\dots,r_k$ and an assignment of words to registers be given.
For every segment index $s$ and track position $t$, if register $r$ is not among the
arguments, then the prescribed head position of $r$ during the simulation at segment $s$
and track position $t$ equals the head position of work tape $r$ in $c_0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Position of an earlier argument register]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_of_lt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_of_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.regPos, Complexity.LogProg.wlen}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration with $m$ registers on input $x$, and let a call specification
with argument list $(r_1,\dots,r_k)$ and an assignment $W$ of words to registers be given,
determining the segments of the call's virtual input. Let $r$ be an argument register
whose first occurrence in the list is $r_i$, so that its segment is $i$. For every
segment index $s>i$ and track position $t$, the prescribed head position of $r$ during
the simulation at segment $s$ and track position $t$ is the length of the word of
segment $i$, i.e. its right end.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Position of a later argument register]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_of_gt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_of_gt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.regPos}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration with $m$ registers, and let a call specification with
argument list $(r_1,\dots,r_k)$ and an assignment of words to registers be given. Let $r$
be an argument register whose first occurrence in the list is $r_i$, so that its segment
is $i$. For every segment index $s<i$ and track position $t$, the prescribed head
position of $r$ during the simulation at segment $s$ and track position $t$ is $-1$,
i.e. its left end.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Position of the current argument register]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_of_eq}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.regPos_of_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.TPos, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.regPos, Complexity.LogProg.trackPos}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c_0$ be a configuration with $m$ registers on input $x$, and let a call specification
with argument list $(r_1,\dots,r_k)$ and an assignment $W$ of words to registers be given,
determining the segments of the call's virtual input. Let $r$ be an argument register
whose first occurrence in the list is $r_i$, and let $s=i$. For every track position $t$,
the prescribed head position of $r$ during the simulation at segment $s$ and track
position $t$ equals the register-coordinate position of $t$ in segment $s$.
\end{lemma}

## ===== blueprint/src/chapter/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Padding.tex =====

\section{Space Complexity --- Padding}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Padding
This module proves the space form of the padding argument: if $L \in \mathrm{SPACE}(S)$,
then the language of members of $L$ padded by $C(|x|+1)^d$ ones lies in $\mathrm{SPACE}(T)$ for every
$T$ that is at least linear and dominates $S$ at the padded length. The proof builds a
logspace validator for padded words, a logspace bank answering queries about the first component,
and a simulation of the decider for $L$ on that component read as a virtual input.

\begin{definition}[Padded language]
\lean{Complexity.padLang}
\label{Complexity.padLang}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ be a language and let $\mathrm{pad} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$.
The padded language $\mathrm{Pad}(L,\mathrm{pad})$ is the set of all strings
$\langle x, 1^{\mathrm{pad}(|x|)}\rangle$ with $x \in L$, where $\langle a,b\rangle$ denotes the self-delimiting pair encoding (every bit of $a$ doubled, then $01$, then $b$).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the padded language]
\lean{Complexity.mem_padLang_iff}
\label{Complexity.mem_padLang_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.padLang, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$, let $\mathrm{pad} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and let
$y \in \{0,1\}^*$. Then $y$ belongs to the padded language $\mathrm{Pad}(L,\mathrm{pad})$ if and
only if there is some $x \in L$ with $y = \langle x, 1^{\mathrm{pad}(|x|)}\rangle$, where $\langle a,b\rangle$ denotes the self-delimiting pair encoding (every bit of $a$ doubled, then $01$, then $b$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padded words]
\lean{Complexity.epadValid}
\label{Complexity.epadValid}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$. A binary string $y$ is called $(C,d)$-padded if
$y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ for some binary string $a$, where $\langle a,b\rangle$ denotes the self-delimiting pair encoding (every bit of $a$ doubled, then $01$, then $b$).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Language of padded words]
\lean{Complexity.epadV}
\label{Complexity.epadV}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadValid}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$. The language $V_{C,d}$ is the set of all $(C,d)$-padded binary
strings, that is, of all strings $\langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ with $a \in \{0,1\}^*$,
where $\langle a,b\rangle$ denotes the self-delimiting pair encoding (every bit of $a$ doubled, then $01$, then $b$).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Membership in the padded-word language]
\lean{Complexity.epad_mem_V}
\label{Complexity.epad_mem_V}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadV, Complexity.epadValid}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and $y \in \{0,1\}^*$. Then $y$ lies in the language $V_{C,d}$ of
$(C,d)$-padded words if and only if $y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ for some binary
string $a$, where $\langle a,b\rangle$ denotes the self-delimiting pair encoding (every bit of $a$ doubled, then $01$, then $b$).
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Virtual input of a padded word]
\lean{Complexity.epadVirt}
\label{Complexity.epadVirt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadValid, Complexity.pairFstD}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$. For a binary string $y$, the virtual input $\mathrm{virt}_{C,d}(y)$ is
the first component $a$ of $y$ when $y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ is a
$(C,d)$-padded word, and the empty string otherwise; here $\langle a,b\rangle$ denotes the self-delimiting pair encoding (every bit of $a$ doubled, then $01$, then $b$).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Query languages of the bank]
\lean{Complexity.epadQ}
\label{Complexity.epadQ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.epadValid, Complexity.pairFstD, Turing.pairDecode}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\mu \in \{0,1\}$ be a mode. The language $Q_{C,d,\mu}$
consists of the strings $z = \langle y, w\rangle$ (with $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ the
self-delimiting pair encoding) such that $w$ is empty or ends in $1$, $|w|$ is at most the length
of the binary representation of $|y|$, and $y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ is
$(C,d)$-padded, and moreover: in mode $\mu = 0$, $\mathrm{val}(w) < |a|$; in mode $\mu = 1$, the
letter of $a$ at position $\mathrm{val}(w)$ is $1$ (letters beyond the end count as $0$). Here
$\mathrm{val}(w)$ is the value of $w$ read as a little-endian binary numeral.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Virtual input of a padded word is its first component]
\lean{Complexity.epadVirt_of_valid}
\label{Complexity.epadVirt_of_valid}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadValid, Complexity.epadVirt, Complexity.pairFstD}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $y$ be a $(C,d)$-padded binary string, i.e.
$y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ for some $a$ in the self-delimiting pair encoding. Then
the virtual input of $y$ (the first component of $y$ if $y$ is $(C,d)$-padded, the empty string
otherwise) equals the first component $a$ of $y$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Virtual input of an unpadded word is empty]
\lean{Complexity.epadVirt_of_not_valid}
\label{Complexity.epadVirt_of_not_valid}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadValid, Complexity.epadVirt}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $y$ be a binary string that is not of the form
$\langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ in the self-delimiting pair encoding. Then the virtual input
of $y$ (the first component of $y$ if $y$ has this form, the empty string otherwise) is the
empty string.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Virtual input is no longer than the input]
\lean{Complexity.epadVirt_length_le}
\label{Complexity.epadVirt_length_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadValid, Complexity.epadVirt, Complexity.epadVirt_of_not_valid, Complexity.epadVirt_of_valid, Complexity.length_pairFstD_le}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and $y \in \{0,1\}^*$. The virtual input of $y$ (its first component
$a$ if $y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ in the self-delimiting pair encoding, and the
empty string otherwise) has length at most $|y|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Membership in a bank language for a decoded pair]
\lean{Complexity.epad_mem_Q_iff}
\label{Complexity.epad_mem_Q_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.epadQ, Complexity.epadValid, Complexity.pairFstD, Turing.pairDecode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mu \in \{0,1\}$, and let $z$ be a binary string that decodes as
the self-delimiting pair $z = \langle y, w\rangle$. Then $z \in Q_{C,d,\mu}$ if and only if $w$ is
empty or ends in $1$, $|w|$ is at most the bit length of $|y|$, $y$ is $(C,d)$-padded (that is,
$y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ for some $a$), and the mode condition holds, where $a$ is the first component of $y$: if $\mu = 1$ the letter of $a$ at position $\mathrm{val}(w)$
is $1$, and if $\mu = 0$ then $\mathrm{val}(w) < |a|$, where $\mathrm{val}(w)$ is the
little-endian binary value of $w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Non-pairs are not in a bank language]
\lean{Complexity.epad_not_mem_Q}
\label{Complexity.epad_not_mem_Q}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadQ, Turing.pairDecode}
\difficulty{2}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\mu \in \{0,1\}$. If a binary string $z$ does not decode as a
self-delimiting pair $\langle y, w\rangle$, then $z$ does not belong to the bank language
$Q_{C,d,\mu}$, whose members are all of this pair form.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bank answers on genuine queries]
\lean{Complexity.epad_query_mem_iff}
\label{Complexity.epad_query_mem_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal_bits, Complexity.LogProg.canon_bits, Complexity.LogProg.drop_canon, Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_mono, Complexity.epadQ, Complexity.epadValid, Complexity.epad_mem_Q_iff, Complexity.pairFstD, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C, d, i \in \mathbb{N}$, $\mu \in \{0,1\}$ and $y \in \{0,1\}^*$ with $i \le |y|$, and write
$\mathrm{bin}(i)$ for the binary representation of $i$. Then
$\langle y, \mathrm{bin}(i)\rangle \in Q_{C,d,\mu}$ if and only if $y$ is $(C,d)$-padded, i.e.
$y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ for some $a$, and, for its first component $a$: in mode
$\mu = 1$ the letter $a_i$ is $1$ (letters beyond the end count as $0$), and in mode $\mu = 0$
we have $i < |a|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Instructions with unconditional step preconditions]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.epadOk}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.epadOk}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins}
Let $\iota$ be an instruction of an abstract register machine. The predicate
$\mathrm{Ok}(\iota)$ holds exactly when either $\iota$ is an equality test between two distinct
registers, or $\iota$ is a decider call whose argument registers are pairwise distinct, or
$\iota$ is any other instruction except the three tests that compare a register's binary
representation with a component of the input (for which it fails).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Step preconditions from a well-formed instruction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.epad_preS}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.epad_preS}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.epadOk, Complexity.LogProg.preS_of_ins}
\difficulty{2}
Let $A$ be an abstract register machine, $x$ an input, and $\ell$ a label whose instruction is an
equality test of two distinct registers, a decider call with pairwise distinct argument
registers, or any instruction other than the three tests comparing a register with a component
of the input. Then every configuration of $A$ at label $\ell$, with arbitrary register contents
and answer, satisfies the syntactic step preconditions of $A$ on $x$ (equality tests compare
distinct registers, decider calls use pairwise distinct argument registers, and input-comparison
tests are applied only to well-formed inputs).
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness of the ones-scanning loop]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.epad_ones_loop}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.epad_ones_loop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.single, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.arm_chain, Complexity.LogProg.astep_call, Complexity.LogProg.astep_inc, Complexity.LogProg.astep_jeq, Complexity.LogProg.epad_preS, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le, Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₁, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A$ be an abstract register machine with an oracle answering its decider calls, run on input
$x$. Let $p, \ell, c$ be pairwise distinct registers, $j$ a decider, $s \ge 1$ and $B$ natural
numbers, and suppose that label $\mathsf{test}$ jumps to $\mathsf{exit}$ if $p = \ell$ and to
$\mathsf{read}$ otherwise, $\mathsf{read}$ calls decider $j$ on $\langle x, \mathrm{bin}(p)\rangle$
and goes to $\mathsf{inc}$ on $1$ and to $\mathsf{fail}$ on $0$, $\mathsf{inc}$ increments $c$ and
goes to $\mathsf{adv}_0$, each $\mathsf{adv}_i$ with $i < s$ increments $p$ and goes to
$\mathsf{adv}_{i+1}$, and $\mathsf{adv}_s = \mathsf{test}$. Then for every string $w$ and register
contents $v$ with all registers at most $B$, $v(\ell) = v(p) + s|w|$, $v(c) + |w| \le B$, and
oracle answers $w_i$ for decider $j$ on $\langle x, \mathrm{bin}(v(p) + s i)\rangle$ for all
$i < |w|$: if every letter of $w$ is $1$, the machine runs from $\mathsf{test}$ with $v$ to
$\mathsf{exit}$ with $p$ set to $v(\ell)$ and $c$ set to $v(c) + |w|$; and if some letter of $w$ is
$0$, it runs from $\mathsf{test}$ with $v$ to $\mathsf{fail}$ with some register contents that are
at most $B$ and agree with $v$ outside $p$ and $c$. In both cases every configuration along the run satisfies the syntactic step preconditions (equality tests compare distinct registers and decider calls use pairwise distinct argument registers) and has all register values at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness of the multiplication loop]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.epad_mul_loop}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.epad_mul_loop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.single, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.astep_dec, Complexity.LogProg.astep_jz, Complexity.LogProg.epad_preS, Complexity.LogProg.registerCopy_loop, Complexity.LogProg.registerScale_loop, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A$ be an abstract register machine with an oracle, run on input $x$, let $k, t, p, q$ be
pairwise distinct registers and $B \in \mathbb{N}$, and suppose its labels are programmed as
follows: $\mathsf{ml}$ jumps to $\mathsf{exit}$ if $k = 0$ and to $\mathsf{md}$ otherwise;
$\mathsf{md}$ decrements $k$ and goes to $\mathsf{addt}$; $\mathsf{addt}$ jumps to $\mathsf{sct}$ if
$t = p$ and to $\mathsf{addb}$ otherwise; $\mathsf{addb}$ increments $t$ and goes to
$\mathsf{addt}$; $\mathsf{sct}$ jumps to $\mathsf{ml}$ if $t = 0$ and to $\mathsf{scd}$ otherwise;
$\mathsf{scd}$ decrements $t$ and goes to $\mathsf{sci}$; $\mathsf{sci}$ increments $q$ and goes to
$\mathsf{sct}$. Then for every $K \in \mathbb{N}$ and register contents $v$ with $v(k) = K$,
$v(t) = 0$, all registers at most $B$ and $v(q) + K\,v(p) \le B$, the machine runs from
$\mathsf{ml}$ with $v$ to $\mathsf{exit}$ with $k$ set to $0$, $q$ set to $v(q) + K\,v(p)$ and all
other registers unchanged, and every configuration along the run satisfies the syntactic step preconditions (equality tests compare distinct registers and decider calls use pairwise distinct argument registers) and has all register values at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness of the powering loop]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.epad_pow_loop}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.epad_pow_loop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.single, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.astep_clr, Complexity.LogProg.astep_dec, Complexity.LogProg.astep_jz, Complexity.LogProg.epad_mul_loop, Complexity.LogProg.epad_preS, Complexity.LogProg.registerCopy_loop, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $A$ be an abstract register machine with an oracle, run on input $x$, let $B \in \mathbb{N}$,
and let $n, e, k, t, p, q$ be registers such that $k, t, p, q$ are pairwise distinct, $e$ differs
from $n, k, t, p, q$, and $n$ differs from $k, p, q$. Suppose its labels are programmed as follows:
$\mathsf{pw}$ jumps to $\mathsf{exit}$ if $e = 0$ and to $\mathsf{pd}$ otherwise; $\mathsf{pd}$
decrements $e$ and goes to $\mathsf{mktest}$; $\mathsf{mktest}$ jumps to $\mathsf{ml}$ if $k = n$
and to $\mathsf{mkbump}$ otherwise; $\mathsf{mkbump}$ increments $k$ and goes to $\mathsf{mktest}$;
the multiplication block $\mathsf{ml}, \mathsf{md}, \mathsf{addt}, \mathsf{addb}, \mathsf{sct},
\mathsf{scd}, \mathsf{sci}$ (which adds $k \cdot p$ to $q$, using $t$ as scratch) exits to
$\mathsf{mv}$; $\mathsf{mv}$ clears $p$ and goes to $\mathsf{mvtest}$; $\mathsf{mvtest}$ jumps to
$\mathsf{mvc}$ if $p = q$ and to $\mathsf{mvbump}$ otherwise; $\mathsf{mvbump}$ increments $p$ and
goes to $\mathsf{mvtest}$; and $\mathsf{mvc}$ clears $q$ and goes to $\mathsf{pw}$. Then for every
$E \in \mathbb{N}$ and register contents $v$ with $v(e) = E$, $v(q) = v(k) = v(t) = 0$,
$v(n) \ge 1$, all registers at most $B$ and $v(p)\,v(n)^E \le B$, the machine runs from
$\mathsf{pw}$ with $v$ to $\mathsf{exit}$ with $e$ set to $0$, $p$ set to $v(p)\,v(n)^E$ and all
other registers unchanged, and every configuration along the run satisfies the syntactic step preconditions (equality tests compare distinct registers and decider calls use pairwise distinct argument registers) and has all register values at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Labels of the validity block]
\lean{Complexity.EPadVL}
\label{Complexity.EPadVL}
\leanok
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$. The label set of the validity block is the finite set consisting of the
pair-scan labels $\mathsf{scan}$, $\mathsf{first}$, $\mathsf{test}_b$, $\mathsf{read}_b$ and
$\mathsf{adv}_{k,\sigma}$ ($b, \sigma \in \{0,1\}$, $k < 4$), the copy-and-halve labels
$\mathsf{cptest}, \mathsf{cpbump}, \mathsf{half}_1, \mathsf{half}_2$, the ones-scan labels
$\mathsf{ostest}, \mathsf{osread}, \mathsf{osinc}, \mathsf{osadv}_\sigma$, the constant-loading
labels $\mathsf{cinc}_i$ ($i < C$) and $\mathsf{dinc}_i$ ($i < d$), fifteen labels of the power
loop, and the comparison label $\mathsf{cmp}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Enumeration of the validity-block labels]
\lean{Complexity.epadVLAll}
\label{Complexity.epadVLAll}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$. The enumeration of the validity block's labels is the explicit finite
list containing each pair-scan, copy-and-halve and ones-scan label, the labels
$\mathsf{cinc}_i$ for $i < C$, the labels $\mathsf{dinc}_i$ for $i < d$, all power-loop labels and
the comparison label.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finiteness of the validity-block labels]
\lean{Complexity.epadVLFintype}
\label{Complexity.epadVLFintype}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL, Complexity.epadVLAll}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$. The set of labels of the validity block is given the structure of a
finite set, with every label appearing in the explicit enumeration of the validity block's
labels.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Stride of the validity block]
\lean{Complexity.epadS}
\label{Complexity.epadS}
\leanok
For a flag $\sigma \in \{0,1\}$, the stride $s(\sigma)$ is defined to be $2$ if $\sigma = 1$ (the
doubled first field of a query) and $1$ if $\sigma = 0$ (the input itself).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Targets of the pair-scan advance chains]
\lean{Complexity.epadAdvEnd}
\label{Complexity.epadAdvEnd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\iota$ map the validity-block labels into a label set
$\Lambda$. For $k \in \{0,1,2,3\}$, the end target of advance chain $k$ is the image under $\iota$
of $\mathsf{test}_0$ if $k = 0$, of $\mathsf{test}_1$ if $k = 1$, of $\mathsf{scan}$ if $k = 2$, and
of $\mathsf{cptest}$ if $k = 3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Pair-scan advance chains]
\lean{Complexity.epadAdv}
\label{Complexity.epadAdv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL, Complexity.epadAdvEnd}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\iota$ map the validity-block labels into a label set $\Lambda$,
let $\sigma \in \{0,1\}$ be the stride flag and $k \in \{0,1,2,3\}$. Step $i$ of advance chain $k$
is the label $\iota(\mathsf{adv}_{k,0})$ if $i = 0$, the label $\iota(\mathsf{adv}_{k,1})$ if
$i = 1$ and $\sigma = 1$, and otherwise the end target of chain $k$, namely the image under
$\iota$ of $\mathsf{test}_0$, $\mathsf{test}_1$, $\mathsf{scan}$ or $\mathsf{cptest}$ for
$k = 0, 1, 2, 3$ respectively.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Ones-scan advance chain]
\lean{Complexity.epadOsAdv}
\label{Complexity.epadOsAdv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\iota$ map the validity-block labels into a label set $\Lambda$,
and let $\sigma \in \{0,1\}$ be the stride flag. Step $i$ of the ones-scan advance chain is
$\iota(\mathsf{osadv}_0)$ if $i = 0$, $\iota(\mathsf{osadv}_1)$ if $i = 1$ and $\sigma = 1$, and
$\iota(\mathsf{ostest})$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Chain loading the exponent]
\lean{Complexity.epadDI}
\label{Complexity.epadDI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\iota$ map the validity-block labels into a label set
$\Lambda$. Step $j$ of the chain loading $d$ is $\iota(\mathsf{dinc}_j)$ if $j < d$ and
$\iota(\mathsf{pw})$, the entry of the power loop, otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Chain loading the coefficient]
\lean{Complexity.epadCI}
\label{Complexity.epadCI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL, Complexity.epadDI}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\iota$ map the validity-block labels into a label set
$\Lambda$. Step $j$ of the chain loading $C$ is $\iota(\mathsf{cinc}_j)$ if $j < C$, and otherwise
the first step of the chain loading $d$, namely $\iota(\mathsf{dinc}_0)$ if $d > 0$ and
$\iota(\mathsf{pw})$ if $d = 0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Code of the validity block]
\lean{Complexity.epadValCode}
\label{Complexity.epadValCode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL, Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.epadAdvEnd, Complexity.epadCI, Complexity.epadDI}
Let $\sigma \in \{0,1\}$ be a stride flag with stride $s = s(\sigma) \in \{1,2\}$, let
$C, d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\iota$ map the validity-block labels into a label set $\Lambda$, and
let $\mathsf{yes}, \mathsf{no} \in \Lambda$. The validity block assigns to each validity-block
label an instruction of an abstract register machine with $18$ registers and $2$ deciders: using
register $0$ as pointer, register $1$ as limit and decider $0$ to read the letter at the
pointer, it parses the scanned word as a pair $\langle a,b\rangle$ (going to $\mathsf{no}$ if it
is malformed), advancing the pointer by $s$ per letter; it copies the pointer into register $2$
and halves it (once if $s = 1$, twice if $s = 2$) to obtain $|a|+1$; it scans $b$, going to $\mathsf{no}$ on a
$0$ and counting its ones in register $3$; it loads $C$ into register $4$ and $d$ into register
$8$ by chains of increments; it runs the powering loop (scratch registers $5$, $6$, $7$) to make
register $4$ equal to $C(|a|+1)^d$; and it finally goes to $\mathsf{yes}$ if registers $3$ and $4$
are equal and to $\mathsf{no}$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Padding test for a decoded pair]
\lean{Complexity.epad_valid_iff_of_decode}
\label{Complexity.epad_valid_iff_of_decode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadValid, Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $y$ be a binary string that decodes as the self-delimiting pair
$y = \langle a, b\rangle$. Then $y$ is $(C,d)$-padded, i.e. of the form
$\langle a', 1^{C(|a'|+1)^d}\rangle$ for some $a'$, if and only if $b = 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Non-pairs are not padded]
\lean{Complexity.epad_not_valid_of_decode}
\label{Complexity.epad_not_valid_of_decode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadValid, Turing.pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode}
\difficulty{2}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$. If a binary string $y$ does not decode as a self-delimiting pair
$\langle a, b\rangle$, then $y$ is not $(C,d)$-padded, i.e. not of the form
$\langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ for any $a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Characterisation of a run of ones]
\lean{Complexity.epad_eq_replicate_iff}
\label{Complexity.epad_eq_replicate_iff}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $b$ be a binary string and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $b = 1^n$ if and only if every letter
$b_i$ with $i < |b|$ is $1$ and $|b| = n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness of the validity block]
\lean{Complexity.epad_val_run}
\label{Complexity.epad_val_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL, Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.single, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.alignedPair_loop, Complexity.LogProg.arm_chain, Complexity.LogProg.astep_half, Complexity.LogProg.astep_jeq, Complexity.LogProg.epad_ones_loop, Complexity.LogProg.epad_pow_loop, Complexity.LogProg.epad_preS, Complexity.LogProg.registerCopy_loop, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le, Complexity.epadAdv, Complexity.epadCI, Complexity.epadDI, Complexity.epadOsAdv, Complexity.epadS, Complexity.epadValCode, Complexity.epadValid, Complexity.epad_eq_replicate_iff, Complexity.epad_not_valid_of_decode, Complexity.epad_valid_iff_of_decode, Complexity.pairEncode_getD_snd, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairDecode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{7}
Let $A$ be an abstract register machine with $18$ registers and $2$ deciders and an oracle

stride $s = s(\sigma)$ ($1$ if $\sigma = 0$, $2$ if $\sigma = 1$), and suppose that $A$, on the
image of an embedding $\iota$ of the validity-block labels, carries the validity-block code for
$\sigma, C, d$ with exits $\mathsf{yes}, \mathsf{no}$. Let $y$ be a binary string such that decider
$0$ answers $y_j$ on $\langle x, \mathrm{bin}(s j)\rangle$ for all $j < |y|$, let

$v'$, agreeing with $v$ on registers $9, \dots, 17$ and with all registers at most $B$, such that
the machine runs from $\iota(\mathsf{scan})$ with $v$ to $\mathsf{yes}$ with $v'$ if
$y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$ for some $a$ (in which case $v'(2) = |a| + 1$) and to

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Extra labels of the validator]
\lean{Complexity.EPadVX}
\label{Complexity.EPadVX}
\leanok
The extra labels of the validator are the elements of the four-element set
$\{\mathsf{lscan}, \mathsf{linc}, \mathsf{yes}, \mathsf{no}\}$: the two labels of the input-length
count and the two answering labels.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finiteness of the validator's extra labels]
\lean{Complexity.epadVXFintype}
\label{Complexity.epadVXFintype}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVX}
The set $\{\mathsf{lscan}, \mathsf{linc}, \mathsf{yes}, \mathsf{no}\}$ of extra labels of the
validator is given the structure of a finite set, enumerated by the list of its four
elements.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Validator for padded words]
\lean{Complexity.epadVA}
\label{Complexity.epadVA}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadVL, Complexity.EPadVX, Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.epadValCode}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$. The validator is the abstract register machine with $18$ registers and
$2$ deciders whose labels are the validity-block labels together with
$\mathsf{lscan}, \mathsf{linc}, \mathsf{yes}, \mathsf{no}$: label $\mathsf{lscan}$ calls decider
$1$ on $\langle x, \mathrm{bin}(r_1)\rangle$ and goes to $\mathsf{linc}$ on $1$ and to the block's
$\mathsf{scan}$ on $0$; $\mathsf{linc}$ increments register $1$ and returns to $\mathsf{lscan}$; the
validity-block labels carry the validity-block code at stride $1$ with exits $\mathsf{yes}$ and
$\mathsf{no}$; and $\mathsf{yes}$, $\mathsf{no}$ halt with answers $1$ and $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Input deciders of the register machines]
\lean{Complexity.epadIn}
\label{Complexity.epadIn}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.inputBitLang, Complexity.inputLenLang}
The pair of input languages consists, at index $0$, of the bit language
$\{\langle u, \mathrm{bin}(i)\rangle : u_i = 1\}$ (letters beyond the end of $u$ count as $0$)
and, at index $1$, of the length language $\{\langle u, \mathrm{bin}(i)\rangle : i < |u|\}$, where
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the self-delimiting pair encoding and $\mathrm{bin}(i)$ is the
binary representation of $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Input deciders are logspace]
\lean{Complexity.epadIn_mem}
\label{Complexity.epadIn_mem}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.epadIn, Complexity.inputBitLang, Complexity.inputBitLang_mem, Complexity.inputLenLang, Complexity.inputLenLang_mem}
\difficulty{2}
For each $j \in \{0,1\}$, the $j$-th input language (for $j = 0$ the bit language
$\{\langle u, \mathrm{bin}(i)\rangle : u_i = 1\}$, for $j = 1$ the length language
$\{\langle u, \mathrm{bin}(i)\rangle : i < |u|\}$) belongs to $\mathsf{l}$, the class of languages
decidable in logarithmic space.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Oracle of the input deciders]
\lean{Complexity.epadOr}
\label{Complexity.epadOr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadIn, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
The oracle of the register machines sends a decider index $j \in \{0,1\}$ and a binary string $V$
to $1$ if $V$ belongs to the $j$-th input language (the bit language for $j = 0$, the length
language for $j = 1$) and to $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Answers of the input deciders]
\lean{Complexity.epadIn_answer}
\label{Complexity.epadIn_answer}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.epadOr, Complexity.indicator_inputBitLang, Complexity.indicator_inputLenLang, Complexity.inputBitLang, Complexity.inputLenLang, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $y$ be a binary string and $p \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $\mathrm{bin}(p)$ be the binary
representation of $p$. On the query $\langle y, \mathrm{bin}(p)\rangle$, the oracle of decider $0$
(the bit language) returns the letter $y_p$, taken to be $0$ when $p \ge |y|$, and the oracle of
decider $1$ (the length language) returns $1$ exactly when $p < |y|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial register bound]
\lean{Complexity.epad_bound}
\label{Complexity.epad_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For all natural numbers $C$, $d$ and $n$,
\[ C(n+1)^d + d + 4n + 4 \le (C + d + 8)(n+1)^{d+1}. \]
\end{lemma}
