\begin{definition}[Labels of the bank]
\lean{Complexity.EPadBX}
\label{Complexity.EPadBX}
\leanok
The set of bank labels outside the validity block is a finite set comprising labels for counting
the input length, for scanning the outer pair, for copying and halving registers, for checking
the index word's tail, for decoding the index, for computing the seek limit, for the strided
seek, and the two answering labels $\mathsf{yes}$ and $\mathsf{no}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Enumeration of the bank labels]
\lean{Complexity.epadBXAll}
\label{Complexity.epadBXAll}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadBX}
The enumeration of the bank's labels is an explicit finite list in which every bank label
outside the validity block appears, including each instance of the labels indexed by a bit or by
an element of $\{0,1,2,3\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finiteness of the bank labels]
\lean{Complexity.epadBXFintype}
\label{Complexity.epadBXFintype}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadBX, Complexity.epadBXAll}
The set of bank labels outside the validity block is given the structure of a finite set, with
every label appearing in the explicit enumeration of the bank labels.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Targets of the outer pair scan]
\lean{Complexity.epadZEnd}
\label{Complexity.epadZEnd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadBX}
For $k \in \{0,1,2,3\}$, the target of advance $k$ of the bank's outer pair scan is the bank
label $\mathsf{ztest}_0$ if $k = 0$, $\mathsf{ztest}_1$ if $k = 1$, $\mathsf{zscan}$ if $k = 2$,
and $\mathsf{c1t}$ if $k = 3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bank register machine]
\lean{Complexity.epadBA}
\label{Complexity.epadBA}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.EPadBX, Complexity.EPadVL, Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.epadValCode, Complexity.epadZEnd}
Let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\mu \in \{0,1\}$. The bank is the abstract register machine with
$18$ registers and $2$ deciders (the input bit and input length deciders) that, on input $z$,
counts $|z|$ into register $9$, parses $z$ as a pair $\langle y, w\rangle$ (rejecting otherwise),
sets register $1$ to $2|y|$, rejects unless $w$ is empty or ends in $1$ and $|w|$ is at most the
bit length of $|y|$, decodes $\mathrm{val}(w)$ into register $13$, runs the validity block at
stride $2$ on $y$ (rejecting unless $y = \langle a, 1^{C(|a|+1)^d}\rangle$), and then seeks
position $\mathrm{val}(w)$ in steps of $4$: it rejects if $\mathrm{val}(w) \ge |a|$, and otherwise
accepts in mode $\mu = 0$ and answers letter $4\,\mathrm{val}(w)$ of $z$ in mode $\mu = 1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness of the bank's final phase]
\lean{Complexity.epad_bank_post}

with $4n + 1 \le B$. Let $v$ be register contents with all registers at most $B$, $v(2) = n+1$,
$v(13) = i$ and $v(15) = v(16) = v(17) = 0$. Then the bank register machine in mode $\mu$, run on
input $z$ with the input deciders as oracle from label $\mathsf{q1t}$ with $v$, halts with answer

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness of the bank's first phase]

label $\mathsf{lscan}$ with all registers $0$. If $z$ is not a self-delimiting pair, it reaches
$\mathsf{no}$. If $z = \langle y, w\rangle$ and it is not the case that $w$ is empty or ends in

\begin{theorem}[Padding transfers space bounds]
\lean{Complexity.mem_SPACE_padLang}
\label{Complexity.mem_SPACE_padLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE_eq, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.epadV, Complexity.epadValid, Complexity.epadVirt, Complexity.epadVirt_of_valid, Complexity.epad_V_mem, Complexity.epad_mem_V, Complexity.epad_run, Complexity.logSpace, Complexity.logSpace_le_succ, Complexity.mem_SPACE_iff, Complexity.mem_padLang_iff, Complexity.padLang, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond_spaceUsed, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const_spaceUsed, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.computesInSpace_iff, Turing.FinTM.decidesInSpace_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{5}
Let $S, T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, where $\mathrm{SPACE}(f)$ denotes the class of languages
decided by a multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet using at most $c\,f(n)$ work-tape
cells on inputs of length $n$, for some constant $c$. Let $L \in \mathrm{SPACE}(S)$, let $C, d \in \mathbb{N}$, and suppose that $T$ satisfies $S(n) \le T(2n + 2 + C(n+1)^d)$ for all $n$ and $m + 1 \le T(m)$ for all $m$. Then the
padded language $\{\langle x, 1^{C(|x|+1)^d}\rangle : x \in L\}$, with $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$
the self-delimiting pair encoding (bits of $x$ doubled, then $01$, then the pad), lies in
$\mathrm{SPACE}(T)$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{Complexity.SpaceConstructible}
For every natural number $c$ with $1\leq c$, the function $n\mapsto n^c+1$ is space
constructible: for every $n$, its logarithmic space bound is at most $n^c+1$, and there
exist a positive natural number $d$ and a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet
that, on every Boolean input $x$, outputs the binary representation of $|x|^c+1$ using
at most $d(|x|^c+1)$ work-tape cells.
\end{theorem}

  {Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_s}

  {pdf-c8033d2fd705-p004-b001}
\uses{Complexity.NSPACE, Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SpaceConstructible}
Let $S\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $\log_2 n+1\le S(n)$ for every $n$, and
suppose that for some positive integer $c$ there is a finite deterministic Turing
machine that, on every binary input $x$, outputs the binary representation of $S(|x|)$
using at most $cS(|x|)$ work-tape cells. Then every language decidable by a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine using at most a constant multiple of $S(n)$ work-tape
cells is decidable by a finite deterministic Turing machine using at most a constant
multiple of $S(n)^2$ work-tape cells.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of polynomial space classes]
\lean{Complexity.PSPACE_eq_NPSPACE}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b005,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p004-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b002,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b003
}
\label{Complexity.PSPACE_eq_NPSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NPSPACE, Complexity.NPSPACE_subset_PSPACE, Complexity.PSPACE, Complexity.PSPACE_subset_NPSPACE}
\difficulty{1}
The class of languages decidable by deterministic finite Turing machines using at most a
polynomial number of work-tape cells equals the class of languages decidable by
nondeterministic finite Turing machines using at most a polynomial number of work-tape
cells. In both classes, the polynomial bound has the form $c(n^d+1)$ for some natural
numbers $c,d$, and the nondeterministic machines must halt within some finite number of
steps on every branch for each input.
\end{theorem}

%%% added by the blueprint pipeline
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Savitch: further results}

\begin{theorem}[Savitch's theorem above logarithmic space]
\lean{Complexity.savitch_of_logSpace_le}
\label{Complexity.savitch_of_logSpace_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.mono, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.deepen_contract, Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_SPACE, Complexity.NSPACE, Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.logSpace, Complexity.logSpace_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1\le S(n)$ for every
natural number $n$. Then every language of binary strings decidable by a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine using at most $cS(n)$ space on inputs of length $n$, for
some constant $c$, is also decidable by a finite deterministic Turing machine using at
most $c'S(n)^2$ space on inputs of length $n$, for some constant $c'$; that is,
$\mathrm{NSPACE}(S)\subseteq\mathrm{SPACE}(S^2)$. No space-constructibility of $S$ is
assumed.
\end{theorem}

## ===== blueprint/src/chapter/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/SavitchARM/Deepen.tex =====

\section{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Deepen}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Deepen
This module builds a register machine that decides any language accepted by a
nondeterministic machine in space $\mathit{sp}$ without computing $\mathit{sp}$: for radii
$s=1,2,\dots$ it runs Savitch's midpoint-reachability search once to test whether a configuration
touching the edge of the radius-$s$ window is reachable, and, once none is, runs the search again to
decide acceptance. Its registers stay within $O\bigl((\mathit{sp}(|x|)+\log|x|+1)^2\bigr)$ binary
digits, which is the hypothesis used to derive Savitch's theorem for every space bound at least
logarithmic.

\begin{definition}[Contract of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DeepenContract}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DeepenContract}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
For a language $L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$ and a function $\mathit{sp}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, the
deepening contract for $L$ and $\mathit{sp}$ is the proposition that there exist $m,d\in\mathbb{N}$,
a finite label set $\Lambda$ with decidable equality, an abstract register machine $D$ with $m$
registers, $d$ deciders and labels $\Lambda$, a start label $l_0\in\Lambda$, languages
$A_0,\dots,A_{d-1}$ all in $\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{SPACE}(\lambda)$, and a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$, such that
for every input $x\in\{0,1\}^*$ the machine $D$, run on $x$ with the indicator functions of the
$A_j$ as oracles from label $l_0$ with every register $0$, halts with answer $[x\in L]$ along a run in
which every configuration before halting satisfies the syntactic preconditions of its instruction
and every register value $r$ satisfies
$|\mathrm{bin}(r+1)|\le C\,(\mathit{sp}(|x|)+\lambda(|x|)+1)^2$. Here
$\lambda(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ (with $\lambda(0)=1$) and $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ is the binary
representation of $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Labels of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, the label set $\Lambda_c$ of the iterative-deepening machine is the finite set
consisting of: two copies of the labels of Savitch's search machine, one for the edge block and one
for the accept block; seven setup labels (an input-length scan, its increment, an increment of the
length-of-length counter, a zero test, a halving step, a second counter increment, and setting the
radius to $1$); for each block flag $f\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ the block-preparation
labels, namely $21$ register-clear labels, seven phases for each of the copy loops (radius into the
sum, counter into the sum, $c$ width copies indexed by $i<c$, radius into the block, width into the
block, width into the shift counter), nine phases of the shift loop, and single labels for one sum
increment, clearing the block's width, clearing and then setting the block's code bound to $1$, and
clearing the block's three node registers; a next-radius label; and an answer label for each bit
$b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Block register inclusion]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\leanok
The map $\rho:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\{0,\dots,24\}$ is the inclusion $\rho(r)=r$; it identifies the $18$
registers of Savitch's search block with the first $18$ of the $25$ registers of the
iterative-deepening machine.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of the block register inclusion]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ_inj}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ_inj}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\difficulty{1}
The inclusion $\rho:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\{0,\dots,24\}$, $\rho(r)=r$, is injective.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Own registers avoid the block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ_ne}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ_ne}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\rho:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\{0,\dots,24\}$ be the inclusion $\rho(r)=r$. For every
$r\in\{0,\dots,17\}$ and every $r'\in\{0,\dots,24\}$ with $r'\ge 18$, we have $\rho(r)\ne r'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Copy loop of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCopyI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCopyI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
Let $c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $a,b\in\{0,\dots,24\}$ be registers, let $e\in\Lambda_c$ be an exit label
and let $k_0,\dots,k_6\in\Lambda_c$ be labels. The copy loop is the family of seven instructions
indexed by $j\in\{0,\dots,6\}$: ($0$) if register $a$ is zero go to $k_4$, else to $k_1$; ($1$)
decrement $a$ and go to $k_2$; ($2$) increment $b$ and go to $k_3$; ($3$) increment the scratch
register $24$ and go to $k_0$; ($4$) if register $24$ is zero exit to $e$, else go to $k_5$; ($5$)
decrement register $24$ and go to $k_6$; ($6$) increment $a$ and go to $k_4$. Placed at the labels
$k_j$, it is designed to add the value of $a$ to $b$, restoring $a$ through register $24$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Shift loop of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpShlI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpShlI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rK}
Let $c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $e\in\Lambda_c$ be an exit label and let $k_0,\dots,k_8\in\Lambda_c$ be
labels. Writing $K=9$ for the code-bound register of the search block, the shift loop is the family
of nine instructions indexed by $j\in\{0,\dots,8\}$: ($0$) if register $20$ is zero exit to $e$,
else go to $k_1$; ($1$) decrement register $20$, go to $k_2$; ($2$) if register $K$ is zero go to
$k_6$, else to $k_3$; ($3$) decrement $K$, go to $k_4$; ($4$) increment register $24$, go to $k_5$;
($5$) increment register $24$, go to $k_2$; ($6$) if register $24$ is zero go to $k_0$, else to
$k_7$; ($7$) decrement register $24$, go to $k_8$; ($8$) increment $K$, go to $k_6$. Each round
doubles $K$ and decrements register $20$, so the loop is designed to multiply $K$ by $2$ raised to
the initial value of register $20$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Successor of a register clear]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCbEx}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCbEx}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, a block flag $f$ and $i\in\{0,\dots,20\}$, the successor label of the $i$-th
register clear of block preparation $f$ in $\Lambda_c$ is the $(i+1)$-th register-clear label of
preparation $f$ if $i+1<21$, and otherwise phase $0$ of the copy loop of preparation $f$ that adds
the radius to the sum register.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Successor of a width copy]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCtEx}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCtEx}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, a block flag $f$ and $i<c$, the successor label of the $i$-th width copy of
block preparation $f$ in $\Lambda_c$ is phase $0$ of the $(i+1)$-th width copy if $i+1<c$, and
otherwise phase $0$ of the copy loop of preparation $f$ that writes the radius into the search
block.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[First width copy]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCt0}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCt0}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$ and a block flag $f$, the first width-copy label of block preparation $f$ in
$\Lambda_c$ is phase $0$ of the $0$-th width copy if $c>0$, and otherwise phase $0$ of the copy
loop of preparation $f$ that writes the radius into the search block.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Entry label of a search block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpIn}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpIn}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$ and a block flag $f$, the entry label of block $f$ in $\Lambda_c$ is the
outer-search entry label of Savitch's search machine in the edge-block copy when $f$ is false, and
in the accept-block copy when $f$ is true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exits of the edge block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpkE}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpkE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, the exit map of the edge block sends a bit $b$ to a label of $\Lambda_c$: the
next-radius label if $b$ is true (an edge code is reachable), and the first register-clear label of
the accept block's preparation if $b$ is false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decider rerouting of the edge block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσE}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσE}
\leanok
The map $\sigma_E:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,1,2,3,4\}$ is given by $\sigma_E(0)=0$, $\sigma_E(1)=1$,
$\sigma_E(2)=4$ and $\sigma_E(3)=3$; it makes the search's accepting-code decider read the
edge-code decider instead.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decider rerouting of the accept block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσA}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσA}
\leanok
The map $\sigma_A:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,1,2,3,4\}$ is the inclusion $\sigma_A(j)=j$ for
$j\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Iterative-deepening register machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.Ins.embed, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCbEx, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCopyI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCt0, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCtEx, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpIn, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpShlI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpkE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσA, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rK, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rM, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rU, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rw}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, the iterative-deepening machine $D_c$ is the abstract register machine with
$25$ registers, $5$ deciders and label set $\Lambda_c$ defined as follows. On the edge-block labels
it runs Savitch's search machine with registers included by $\rho(r)=r$, deciders rerouted by
$\sigma_E=(0,1,4,3)$, and an answer $b$ replaced by a jump (testing register $24$) to the next-radius
label if $b$ is true or to the accept block's preparation if $b$ is false; on the accept-block
labels it runs the same search with deciders rerouted by $\sigma_A=(0,1,2,3)$ and answers $b$
replaced by jumps to the answer label for $b$. The setup counts $|x|$ into register $21$ by
repeatedly querying decider $0$ and incrementing, sets register $22$ to $1$, halves register $21$
down to $0$ while incrementing register $22$ each time, and increments the radius register $23$
before entering the edge block's preparation. The preparation of block $f$ clears registers
$0,\dots,20$, sets register $18$ to $s+\ell+1$ (radius $s$ in register $23$, $\ell$ in register
$22$), adds register $18$ to register $19$ $c$ times, copies the radius into the block's radius
register $7$ and register $19$ into the block's width register $8$, sets the block's code bound
register $9$ to $1$, copies register $19$ into register $20$, runs the shift loop, clears the block's
registers $10$, $11$, $12$, and enters block $f$. The next-radius label increments register $23$ and
returns to the edge block's preparation, and the answer label for $b$ halts with answer $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Deciders of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.edgeLang, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Complexity.inputLenLang, Turing.FinNDTM}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean alphabet, the five decider languages
$A_0,\dots,A_4$ are: $A_0$ the input-length language
$\{\langle u,\mathrm{bin}(i)\rangle : i<|u|\}$; $A_1$ the initial-code language of $N$; $A_2$ the
accepting-code language of $N$; $A_3$ the step-pair language of $N$; and $A_4$ the edge-code
language of $N$ (codes at radius $s$ of window-bounded configurations with some work head at
position $\pm s$).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle answers of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean alphabet, the oracle family is the
map sending $j\in\{0,\dots,4\}$ and a word $V\in\{0,1\}^*$ to the indicator $[V\in A_j]$, where
$A_0,\dots,A_4$ are the input-length, initial-code, accepting-code, step-pair and edge-code
languages of $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle answer is membership]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Turing.FinNDTM}
\difficulty{2}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, and let
$A_0,\dots,A_4$ be its input-length, initial-code, accepting-code, step-pair and edge-code
languages. For every $j\in\{0,\dots,4\}$ and every word $V$, the oracle answer $[V\in A_j]$ is true
if and only if $V\in A_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rerouted oracle step relation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_rel}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_rel}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.stepRel_iff_mem, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rel_iff_orc, Turing.FinNDTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, let
$\sigma:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,\dots,4\}$ satisfy $\sigma(3)=3$, let $x\in\{0,1\}^*$ and $s\in\mathbb{N}$.
Then for all $u,v\in\mathbb{N}$, decider $\sigma(3)$ of $N$'s five-language oracle family accepts
$\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bin}(u),\langle\mathrm{bin}(v),\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$ if and
only if $u,v$ are related by the step relation of $N$ on $x$ at radius $s$, i.e.\ that encoding lies
in the step-pair language of $N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rerouted initial-code test]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_initO}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_initO}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.initO_iff_orc, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{2}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, let
$\sigma:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,\dots,4\}$ satisfy $\sigma(1)=1$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^*$ and
$s,u\in\mathbb{N}$. Decider $\sigma(1)$ of $N$'s five-language oracle family accepts
$\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bin}(u),\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle$ if and only if that word lies in the
initial-code language of $N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rerouted accepting-code test]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_accO}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_accO}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.accO_iff_orc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet with decider languages
$A_0,\dots,A_4$, let $\sigma:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,\dots,4\}$ and $j\in\{0,\dots,4\}$ with
$\sigma(2)=j$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^*$ and $s,v\in\mathbb{N}$. Decider $\sigma(2)$ of the oracle
family accepts $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bin}(v),\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle$ if and only if that
word lies in $A_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preconditions of simple instructions]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_pre}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_pre}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD, Complexity.LogProg.preS_of_ins}
\difficulty{3}
Let $c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be an input, let $l\in\Lambda_c$ be a label and $v$ a register
assignment, and consider the iterative-deepening register machine $D_c$ (with $25$ registers, $5$ deciders and $c$ copies of the width step). If the instruction of $D_c$ at $l$ is an increment, a clear or an
answer instruction, then the configuration at label $l$ with registers $v$ and no answer yet
satisfies the syntactic preconditions of $D_c$ on $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Increment step of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_inc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_inc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_pre, Complexity.LogProg.astep_inc}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $o$ be an oracle family for five deciders, let $x$ be an input, and
consider the iterative-deepening register machine $D_c$ (with $25$ registers, $5$ deciders and $c$ copies of the width step). If the instruction of $D_c$ at label $l$ increments register $r$ and continues at
$l'$, and every register of $v$ is at most $B$, then there is a run of $D_c$ on $x$ with oracle family $o$ all of whose configurations before the last satisfy the syntactic preconditions of their instructions and have every register at most $B$ from label $l$ with registers
$v$ to label $l'$ with registers $v[r\mapsto v(r)+1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Clear step of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_clr}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_clr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_pre, Complexity.LogProg.astep_clr}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $o$ be an oracle family for five deciders, let $x$ be an input, and
consider the iterative-deepening register machine $D_c$ (with $25$ registers, $5$ deciders and $c$ copies of the width step). If the instruction of $D_c$ at label $l$ clears register $r$ and continues at $l'$,
and every register of $v$ is at most $B$, then there is a run of $D_c$ on $x$ with oracle family $o$ all of whose configurations before the last satisfy the syntactic preconditions of their instructions and have every register at most $B$ from label $l$ with registers $v$ to
label $l'$ with registers $v[r\mapsto 0]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Split register file]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt}
\leanok
For $b:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $o:\{0,\dots,6\}\to\mathbb{N}$, the register file
$\mathrm{St}(b,o):\{0,\dots,24\}\to\mathbb{N}$ assigns $b(r)$ to each register $r<18$ and
$o(r-18)$ to each register $r\ge 18$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Split register file on block registers]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_ρ}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_ρ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\difficulty{3}
For $b:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $o:\{0,\dots,6\}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{St}(b,o)$ be
the register file on $\{0,\dots,24\}$ equal to $b$ below $18$ and to $o(\cdot-18)$ from $18$ on,
and let $\rho(r)=r$ include $\{0,\dots,17\}$ into $\{0,\dots,24\}$. Then
$\mathrm{St}(b,o)(\rho(r))=b(r)$ for every $r\in\{0,\dots,17\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Split register file on own registers]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_own}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_own}
\leanok

the register file on $\{0,\dots,24\}$ equal to $b$ below $18$ and to $o(\cdot-18)$ from $18$ on.
If $r\in\{0,\dots,24\}$ and $i\in\{0,\dots,6\}$ satisfy $r=18+i$, then $\mathrm{St}(b,o)(r)=o(i)$.

the register file on $\{0,\dots,24\}$ equal to $b$ below $18$ and to $o(\cdot-18)$ from $18$ on,
and let $\rho(r)=r$. For every $r\in\{0,\dots,17\}$ and $a\in\mathbb{N}$, updating

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Largest code width of the deepening run]

$k_N$, a function $\mathit{sp}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and an input $x$, the largest code width is
$W=(k_N+1)\bigl(\mathit{sp}(|x|)+1+(1+|\mathrm{bin}(|x|)|)+1\bigr)$, where $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ is the
binary representation of $n$.

For all $k,s\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\mathit{sp}(|x|)+1-s=k$ and

\begin{theorem}[Deepening machine meets the contract]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.deepen_contract}

\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet that decides $L$ in space $\mathit{sp}$ (on every input $x$ every computation branch halts and visits at most $\mathit{sp}(|x|)$ work-tape cells, and $x\in L$ iff some branch accepts). Then there
exist an abstract register machine $D$ with finitely many labels, a start label $l_0$, finitely many
decider languages all in $\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{SPACE}(\lambda)$, and a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$
such that for every input $x$, the machine $D$ run on $x$ with the indicators of those languages as
oracles, from $l_0$ with every register $0$, halts with answer $[x\in L]$ along a run in which every
configuration before halting satisfies the syntactic preconditions of its instruction and every
register value $r$ satisfies $|\mathrm{bin}(r+1)|\le C\,(\mathit{sp}(|x|)+\lambda(|x|)+1)^2$;
here $\lambda(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ and $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ is the binary representation of
$n$. One may take as deciders the input-length, initial-code, accepting-code, step-pair and edge-code
languages of $N$, and $C=9(k_N+1)^2+2$ with $k_N$ the code-length constant of $N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Machine register state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St}
\leanok
A machine state is an assignment of a natural number to each of eighteen registers: the
input-length counter; the base $|x|+2$; the exponent counter and power accumulator; a
scratch register and the copy-and-shift scratch register; a loop counter; the window
radius; the code width (the recursion depth) and its bound $2^w$; the source and target
codes of the current node; its midpoint and level; the stack of saved endpoints, whose
digits have width $w$; the stack of phase bits; the last popped endpoint; and a scratch
register for the pop routine.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Register vector of a state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St}
For each machine state, its register vector is the vector of length $18$ whose entries,
in order, are the input-length counter, the base, the exponent counter, the power
accumulator, the two scratch registers, the loop counter, the window radius, the code
width, the code bound, the source code, the target code, the midpoint, the level, the
saved-endpoints stack, the phase-bit stack, the last popped endpoint, and the
pop-routine scratch register.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform register bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St}
For a natural number $B$ and a machine state with counters and registers
$n,a,X,P,T,Z,C,s,w,K,U,V,M,I,SE,SP,E,Q$, the state is bounded by $B$ exactly when each
of these eighteen quantities is at most $B$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Register vector respects the bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd.toV}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd.toV}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV}
\difficulty{4}
Let $B$ be a natural number and let a machine state have all eighteen registers at most
$B$. Then every coordinate of its register vector is at most $B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Move-loop sites]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.MvS}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.MvS}
\leanok
Let a move-loop site be one of the following finitely many operations: copy $n$ into
$a$; copy a product from $T$ into $P$, with a Boolean parameter; copy $P$ into $w$; copy
either $U$ or $V$ into the endpoint stack, according to a Boolean parameter; copy the
doubled phase stack from $T$ into $SP$, with a Boolean parameter; copy $M$ into $V$;
copy $V$ into $U$; copy the popped endpoint $E$ into $V$; move the last endpoint-stack
digit into $E$, with a Boolean parameter; copy the remaining stack from $T$ into $SE$,
with a Boolean parameter; copy $V$ into $M$; copy $E$ into $V$; copy $E$ into $U$; copy
$U$ into $M$; or copy $E$ into $U$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Copy-loop sites]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CpS}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CpS}
\leanok
Let a copy-loop site be one of the following finitely many operations: choose the
multiplier, either $P$ or $a$, according to a Boolean parameter, and copy it into
counter $C$; copy $P$ into accumulator $T$, with a Boolean parameter; copy $P$ into
radius $s$; copy $w$ into $C$ for the shift count used to form $K=2^w$; copy $w$ into
level $I$; copy $w$ into $C$ for shifting the endpoint stack, with a Boolean parameter;
copy $SE$ into $T$ for popping, with a Boolean parameter; copy $w$ into $C$ for the
stack-halving count, with a Boolean parameter; copy the halved stack from $T$ into $Q$,
with a Boolean parameter; or copy $w$ into $C$ for shifting $Q$, with a Boolean
parameter.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Shift-loop sites]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.ShS}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.ShS}
\leanok
A shift-loop site is one of three operations: multiply $K$ by $2^w$; multiply the
endpoint stack $SE$ by $2^w$ to make room for a digit, with a Boolean parameter; or
multiply $Q$ by $2^w$ to shift back the stack with its last digit removed, with a
Boolean parameter.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Machine-program labels]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CpS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.MvS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.ShS}
For a natural number $E$, let the program-label type consist of the labels for the
setup, search, recursion, return, and stack operations: input scanning and counter
updates; power and multiplication loops; initialization and outer-search tests and
queries; root, accept, and reject operations; recursive calls and base-case tests;
midpoint iteration and phase handling; and the move, doubling, subtraction, halving,
copy, and shift loops. The label for the $j$th exponent-counter increment is
parameterized by $j$ in the range $0\le j\le E$, and the move, doubling, subtraction,
halving, copy, and shift loop labels carry, respectively, a move site and phase in
$\{0,1,2\}$, a Boolean and phase in $\{0,1,2,3\}$, a Boolean and phase in $\{0,1,2\}$, a
Boolean and phase in $\{0,1,2\}$, a copy site and phase in $\{0,1,\ldots,6\}$, or a
shift site and phase in $\{0,1,\ldots,8\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Source register of each move]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.MvS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rM, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rP, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rSE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rT, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rU, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rn}
For a move site, define its source-register index in a register file indexed from $0$ to
$17$ as follows: the source indices for copying $n$ to $a$, $T$ to $P$, $P$ to $w$, the
selected endpoint to $SE$, $T$ to $SP$, $M$ to $V$, $V$ to $U$, $E$ to $V$, $SE$ to $E$,
$T$ to $SE$, $V$ to $M$, $E$ to $V$, $E$ to $U$, $U$ to $M$, and $E$ to $U$ are,
respectively, $0,4,3,10$ or $11$ (according to the Boolean choice),
$4,12,11,16,14,4,11,16,16,10,16$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Destination register of each move]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.MvS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rM, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rP, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rSE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rSP, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rU, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.ra, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rw}
For a move site, define its destination-register index in a register file indexed from
$0$ to $17$ as follows: the destination indices for copying $n$ to $a$, $T$ to $P$, $P$
to $w$, the selected endpoint to $SE$, $T$ to $SP$, $M$ to $V$, $V$ to $U$, $E$ to $V$,
$SE$ to $E$, $T$ to $SE$, $V$ to $M$, $E$ to $V$, $E$ to $U$, $U$ to $M$, and $E$ to $U$
are, respectively, $1,3,8,14,15,11,10,11,16,14,12,11,10,12,10$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exit label of each move loop]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.MvS}
For each move site, define its exit program label as follows: copying $n$ into $a$ exits
to the first increment of $a$; copying $T$ into $P$ exits to the $w$-copy loop when the
Boolean parameter is true and otherwise to the power test; copying $P$ into $w$ exits to
clearing $a$; pushing an endpoint into $SE$ exits to the corresponding doubling loop;
pushing $T$ into $SP$ exits to incrementing the phase when its Boolean parameter is true
and otherwise to the descent loop; copying $M$ into $V$ exits to decrementing the level;
the two phase-$0$ success copies exit successively to the second success copy and then
to the level decrement; popping the last endpoint digit into $E$ exits to copying the
remaining stack into $SE$; that remaining-stack copy exits to restoring the level; the
phase-$0$ failure copies exit to the next midpoint and then to the midpoint loop; the
phase-$1$ success copy exits to the root-return test; and the phase-$1$ failure copies
exit to the next midpoint and then to the midpoint loop. The exit labels for the stack
push and pop operations retain their Boolean parameter, and the level-restoration label
also retains its Boolean parameter.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Source registers for copy operations]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpSrc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpSrc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CpS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rP, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rSE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rT, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.ra, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rw}
For each copy-operation site, assign a source register among the 18 registers as
follows: multiplication into the counter uses the power register when the Boolean
parameter is true and the base register otherwise; multiplication into the accumulator
and setup of the radius use the power register; setup, root, push, and both pop-count
operations use the width register; popping the stack into the accumulator uses the stack
register, and moving the halved stack into the quotient register uses the accumulator
register.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Destination registers for copy operations]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpDst}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpDst}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CpS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rC, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rQ, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rT, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rs}
For each copy-operation site, assign its destination among the 18 registers as follows:
multiplication into the counter, setup of the shift value, push, and both pop-count
operations target the counter register; multiplication into the accumulator and popping
the stack into the accumulator target the accumulator register; setup of the radius
targets the radius register; the root operation targets the level register; and moving
the halved stack into the quotient register targets the quotient register.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exit labels for copy operations]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpExit}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpExit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CpS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb}
For each copy-operation site, assign its continuation label as follows: either
multiplication site continues at the corresponding multiplication test; radius setup
continues at phase $0$ of the squaring multiplication site; shift-value setup continues
at phase $0$ of the shift of the setup register; root-level copying continues at the
recursive-call label; pushing continues at phase $0$ of the corresponding push shift;
copying the stack during a pop continues at phase $0$ of the first pop-count copy; the
first pop-count copy continues at phase $0$ of the corresponding halving operation;
copying the halved stack continues at phase $0$ of the second pop-count copy; and the
second pop-count copy continues at phase $0$ of the corresponding pop shift.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Registers used by shift operations]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.shReg}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.shReg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.ShS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rK, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rQ, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rSE}
For each shift-operation site, assign its register among the 18 registers: shifting the
setup value uses the setup register, pushing uses the stack register, and popping uses
the quotient register.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exit labels for shift operations]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.shExit}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.shExit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.ShS}
For each shift-operation site, assign its continuation label as follows: shifting the
setup value continues at the outer search label; pushing continues at phase $0$ of the
corresponding saved-endpoint move; and popping continues at phase $0$ of the
corresponding subtraction operation. The label type is parameterized by a natural number
$E$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Instruction phases for a register move]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb}
Let $E$ be a natural number, let $s$ and $d$ be registers among 18 registers, let $x$ be
an exit label, let $m$ assign a label to each of three phases, and let $j$ be one of
those phases. The instruction at phase $j$ is a zero test on register $s$, branching to
$x$ if it is zero and to phase $1$ otherwise when $j=0$; it decrements $s$ and continues
to phase $2$ when $j=1$; and in the remaining phase it increments $d$ and returns to
phase $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Instruction phases for a doubling move]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dmI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dmI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb}
Let $E$ be a natural number, let $s$ and $d$ be registers among 18 registers, let $x$ be
an exit label, let $m$ assign a label to each of four phases, and let $j$ be one of
those phases. At phase $0$, test whether $s$ is zero, branching to $x$ if so and to
phase $1$ otherwise; at phase $1$, decrement $s$ and continue to phase $2$; at phase
$2$, increment $d$ and continue to phase $3$; and at phase $3$, increment $d$ and return
to phase $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Instruction phases for subtraction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.sbI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.sbI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb}
Let $E$ be a natural number, let $q$ and $r$ be registers among 18 registers, let $x$ be
an exit label, let $m$ assign a label to each of three phases, and let $j$ be one of
those phases. At phase $0$, test whether $q$ is zero, branching to $x$ if so and to
phase $1$ otherwise; at phase $1$, decrement $q$ and continue to phase $2$; and in the
remaining phase, decrement $r$ and return to phase $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Halving-loop instruction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.hvI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.hvI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb}
For a natural number $E$, two registers $c,r
ame$ in a set of $18$ registers, an exit label $e$, a function $m$ assigning one of the
labels $m(0),m(1),m(2)$ to each phase, and a phase $j\in\{0,1,2\}$, define the
instruction as follows: at phase $0$, branch on whether register $c$ is zero, going to
$e$ if it is and to $m(1)$ otherwise; at phase $1$, decrement $c$ and go to $m(2)$; at
phase $2$, halve register $r$ and go to $m(0)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Copy-loop instruction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rZ}
For a natural number $E$, source and destination registers $s,d$ among $18$ registers,
an exit label $e$, a function $m$ assigning a label to each of seven phases, and a phase
$j\in\{0,1,\ldots,6\}$, define the instruction by these cases: at phase $0$, branch on
whether $s=0$, going to $m(4)$ if so and to $m(1)$ otherwise; at phase $1$, decrement
$s$ and go to $m(2)$; at phase $2$, increment $d$ and go to $m(3)$; at phase $3$,
increment a scratch register $z$ and go to $m(0)$; at phase $4$, branch on whether
$z=0$, going to $e$ if so and to $m(5)$ otherwise; at phase $5$, decrement $z$ and go to
$m(6)$; at phase $6$, increment $s$ and go to $m(4)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Shift-loop instruction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.shI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.shI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rC, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rZ}
For a natural number $E$, a register $r$ among $18$ registers, an exit label $e$, a
function $m$ assigning a label to each of nine phases, and a phase
$j\in\{0,1,\ldots,8\}$, define the instruction by these cases: at phase $0$, branch on
whether the loop counter $c$ is zero, going to $e$ if so and to $m(1)$ otherwise; at
phase $1$, decrement $c$ and go to $m(2)$; at phase $2$, branch on whether $r=0$, going
to $m(6)$ if so and to $m(3)$ otherwise; at phase $3$, decrement $r$ and go to $m(4)$;
at phase $4$, increment the scratch register $z$ and go to $m(5)$; at phase $5$,
increment $z$ and go to $m(2)$; at phase $6$, branch on whether $z=0$, going to $m(0)$
if so and to $m(7)$ otherwise; at phase $7$, decrement $z$ and go to $m(8)$; at phase
$8$, increment $r$ and go to $m(6)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Savitch machine program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A}

For a natural number $E$, define a register-machine program with $18$ registers, four
deciders, and labels in the family indexed by $E$. At each label it supplies the
corresponding instruction: the program scans the input length, computes its parameters
and code bound, searches pairs of codes, and performs the recursive reachability
procedure using the move, copy, shift, doubling, subtraction, and halving loops
specified by the labels.
\end{definition}

%%% added by the blueprint pipeline
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Machine: further results}

\begin{theorem}[Savitch machine has no input-format checks]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A_noVal}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A_noVal}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dmI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.hvI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.sbI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.shI}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $E$, every label $l$ of the Savitch register-machine program
with parameter $E$ (which has $18$ registers), every register $r$, and every label $l'$,
the instruction of the program at $l$ is neither the plain-input format check of
register $r$ continuing to $l'$ nor the paired-input format check of register $r$
continuing to $l'$. Consequently the program can halt only by returning an answer.
\end{theorem}

## ===== blueprint/src/chapter/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/SavitchARM/Reach.tex =====

\section{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Reach}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Reach
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Reach: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Reach}.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Reach: Results}

\begin{definition}[Bounded recursive reachability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p004-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p007-b002
}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach}
\leanok
For a natural number $K$ and a binary relation $R$ on the natural numbers, define
reachability at level $0$ by $u=v$ or $R(u,v)$. At level $i+1$, declare $u$ and $v$
related when there is some $m<K$ such that $u$ is related to $m$ at level $i$ and $m$ is
related to $v$ at level $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Reachability Along a Chain]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reach_of_chain}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p007-b002,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b001
}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reach_of_chain}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach}
\difficulty{5}
Let $K,T$ be natural numbers, let $R$ be a relation on the natural numbers, and let $c$
be a sequence of natural numbers. Define reachability at level $0$ to mean equality or
one $R$-step; at each higher level, two points are reachable if there is an intermediate
number less than $K$ such that each pair of successive points is reachable at the
preceding level. Suppose $R(c_j,c_{j+1})$ for every $j<T$, and $c_j<K$ for every $j\le
T$. Then for all natural numbers $i,j,t$ with $j+t\le T$ and $t\le 2^i$, the points
$c_j$ and $c_{j+t}$ are reachable at level $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reachability Gives Reflexive Transitive Reachability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reflTransGen_of_reach}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reflTransGen_of_reach}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K$ be a natural number and $R$ a relation on the natural numbers. If $u$ reaches
$v$ at any level under the recursively defined reachability relation—where level $0$
allows equality or one $R$-step and each higher level composes two reachability steps
through an intermediate point below $K$—then $v$ is reachable from $u$ by a finite
sequence of $R$-steps, allowing a sequence of length zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Configuration Count Bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.configBound_le}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.configBound_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.configBound}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with $k$
work tapes and state set $Q$. For natural numbers $n,E$, if $|Q|+2+9k\le E$, then
\[3(|Q|+1)(n+2)\,3^{k(2(n+2)^E+1)}(2(n+2)^E+1)^k\le 2^{(n+2)^{2E}}.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Code Width Bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.codeWidth_le}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.codeWidth_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.codeK, Complexity.logSpace, Complexity.logSpace_le_succ, Turing.FinNDTM}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with $k$
work tapes and state set $Q$. Put $H=3(|Q|+1)$ and $C=2(2(H+3k+1))+2$. For natural
numbers $n,E$, if $2C\le E$, then $C\big((n+2)^E+\log_2(n)+1\big)\le(n+2)^{2E}$, where
$\log_2(n)$ denotes the natural-number logarithm appearing in the definition of
logarithmic space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial Radius Bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.radius_le}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.radius_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $n,k,c,E$, if $k+c+1\le E$, then $c(n^k+1)\le(n+2)^E$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Language membership and bounded configuration reachability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mem_iff_reach}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mem_iff_reach}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.codeK, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_iff_codeChain, Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reach_of_chain, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reflTransGen_of_reach, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.configBound, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and a finite state set,
and suppose $N$ decides a language $L$ within space bound $\mathrm{sp}$. Let $x$ be a
Boolean string, and let $s,w\in\mathbb{N}$. Write $q$ for the number of states of $N$,
set $d=2\bigl(3(q+1)+3k+1\bigr)+2$, and define $B=3(q+1)(|x|+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k$. If
$\mathrm{sp}(|x|)\le s$, $d\bigl(s+\lfloor\log_2|x|\rfloor+2\bigr)\le w$, and $B\le
2^w$, then $x\in L$ if and only if there are natural numbers $u,v<2^w$ whose encodings
with $x$ and $s$ represent, respectively, the initial configuration and an accepting
configuration of $N$, and $v$ is reachable from $u$ through the encoded one-step
configuration relation at recursive depth $w$, with intermediate codes less than $2^w$.
\end{theorem}

%%% added by the blueprint pipeline
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Reach: further results}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded walks give bounded chains]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.chain_of_walkLe}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.chain_of_walkLe}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.WalkLe, Complexity.walkLe_succ_iff_head, Complexity.walkLe_zero_iff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $R$ be a binary relation on $\mathbb{N}$, and let $c<K$. For
all $j,t\in\mathbb{N}$, if $t$ is reachable from $c$ by a walk of at most $j$ edges of
$R$ whose vertices after $c$ all lie below $K$, then there are $T\le j$ and a sequence
$f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $f(0)=c$, $f(T)=t$, $R(f(i),f(i+1))$ for every $i<T$,
and $f(i)<K$ for every $i\le T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Paths give midpoint reachability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reach_of_reflTransGen}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reach_of_reflTransGen}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.chain_of_walkLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reach_of_chain, Complexity.reach_iff_walkLe}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $R$ be a binary relation on $\mathbb{N}$ such that
$R(a,b)$ implies $a<K$ and $b<K$. Define midpoint reachability by: $u$ reaches $v$ at
level $0$ if $u=v$ or $R(u,v)$, and $u$ reaches $v$ at level $i+1$ if there is $m<K$
such that $u$ reaches $m$ and $m$ reaches $v$ at level $i$. If $u<K$ and $v$ is
reachable from $u$ by zero or more $R$-steps, then $u$ reaches $v$ at every level $i$
with $K\le 2^i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Encoded machine relation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b001}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a function from four deciders and Boolean words to truth values,
let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $s,u,v$ be natural numbers. Define $u$ to be related
to $v$ (with parameter $s$ and input $x$) exactly when decider number $3$ accepts the
encoding of $x$, the canonical binary expansions of $u$ and $v$, and the canonical
binary expansion of $s$, nested as a sequence of pairs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Configuration invariant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b002}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St}
For natural numbers $s,w,i$ and a machine configuration $\sigma$, the invariant requires
its input-length, base, exponent, power, scratch, loop-counter, pop-scratch, and
popped-endpoint registers all to be zero. It also requires the radius to equal $s$, the
width to equal $w$, the code bound to equal $2^w$, the source and target codes to be
less than $2^w$, the midpoint to be at most $2^w$, the level to equal $i$, the endpoint
stack to be less than $2^{w(w-i)}$, and the phase stack to be less than $2^{w-i}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential size bounds]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts}
\leanok

\end{lemma}

\end{lemma}

$SE<2^{w(w-(i+1))}$; and $SP<2^{w-(i+1)}$. If $M<2^w$ and $M_1\le2^w$, then there is a
finite run from the phase-zero failure label with registers given by the state obtained
from $\mathrm{st}$ by replacing $V$ with $M$, $M$ with $M_1$, and $E$ with the old value
of $V$, to the loop label with registers given by the state obtained from $\mathrm{st}$
by replacing $M$ with $M+1$; every configuration strictly before the endpoint satisfies
the guard with bound $2^{w^2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Phase-One Success Return Path]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1T}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b004,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b002
}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1T}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mv_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq}
\difficulty{3}
Let $E,s,w,i$ be natural numbers with $s\le w$ and $i+1\le w$, let
$\mathrm{orc}:\mathrm{Fin}(4)\to\mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Bool})\to\mathrm{Bool}$ be an
oracle, let $x$ be a Boolean list, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a machine state satisfying
the invariant $\mathrm{Inv}(s,w,i+1,\mathrm{st})$. For every $M_2\le 2^w$, the machine
$A(E)$ has a finite run from the configuration whose control state is the phase-one
success state, whose registers agree with $\mathrm{st}$ except that $U=M$, $M=M_2$, and
$E$ equals the original value of $U$, and whose result is unset, to the configuration
whose control state is the successful return state and whose registers agree with
$\mathrm{st}$ except that $M=M_2$, again with unset result; throughout the run, every
configuration before the final one satisfies the input precondition and has all
registers at most $2^{w^2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Phase-one failure loop]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1F}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1F}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mv_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a natural number, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle with four indices and
Boolean-word queries, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $s,w$ be natural numbers with
$s\le w$. Let $i$ be a natural number with $i+1\le w$, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a
machine state satisfying the following conditions: $n,a,X,P,T,Z,C,Q,E$ are zero; its
radius is $s$, width is $w$, and code bound is $2^w$; its source and target codes are
less than $2^w$, its midpoint is at most $2^w$, and its level is $i+1$; its
saved-endpoints stack is less than $2^{w(w-(i+1))}$ and its phase stack is less than
$2^{w-(i+1)}$. Suppose also that $M<2^w$ and $M_2\le 2^w$. Starting at label $a1F$ with
the source code replaced by the old midpoint $M$, the midpoint replaced by $M_2$, and
the popped endpoint set to the old source code, the machine can reach label $loop$ with
the midpoint increased from its original value by one and every other register equal to
its value in $\mathrm{st}$. Every configuration strictly before the endpoint has all
registers at most $2^{w^2}$ and satisfies the machine's validity condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Preservation under midpoint update]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.setM}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.setM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St}
\difficulty{1}
Let $s,w,i$ be natural numbers, and let a machine state satisfy the invariant with
parameters $s,w,i$. If a natural number $M'$ satisfies $M'\le 2^w$, then replacing the
state's midpoint register by $M'$ leaves the invariant satisfied.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Equivalent bounded witnesses]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $R_1,R_2$ be predicates on natural numbers and let $a,K\in\mathbb{N}$. If it is not
the case that both $R_1(a)$ and $R_2(a)$ hold, then there exists an $m$ with $a+1\leq
m<K$ satisfying both predicates if and only if there exists an $m$ with $a\leq m<K$
satisfying both predicates.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Recursive midpoint search loop]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.loop_spec}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b001}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.loop_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CallOK, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.setM, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.desc1, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.desc2, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail0F, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1F, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1T, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{6}
Let $E,s,w,i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ be an oracle on four indices and bit
strings, and let $x$ be a bit string. Suppose $s\le w$, $i+1\le w$, and the
recursive-call property holds at level $i$. For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and register
state $\mathrm{st}$ satisfying the level-$(i+1)$ invariant and $\mathrm{st}.M+k=2^w$,
there is an $M'\le 2^w$ and a finite run, guarded by bound $2^{w^2}$ before its final
configuration, from label $\mathrm{loop}$ with registers $\mathrm{st}$ and no answer to
label $\mathrm{rt}(b)$ with registers equal to $\mathrm{st}$ except that $M=M'$, and no
answer, where $b$ is true exactly when there exists $m$ with $\mathrm{st}.M\le m<2^w$
such that the level-$i$ reachability relation holds from $\mathrm{st}.U$ to $m$ and from
$m$ to $\mathrm{st}.V$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CallOK, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.setM, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.base_spec, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.loop_spec, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E,s,w$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle with four indices and
Boolean-word inputs, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean word. If $s\le w$, then for every
natural number $i\le w$ and every register state $\mathrm{st}$ satisfying the level-$i$
invariant for $s,w$, there is a natural number $M'\le 2^w$ such that the program $A(E)$
has a finite execution from label $\mathrm{cl}$, starting with register vector $\mathrm{st}$ and no
answer, to the return label whose Boolean value is the truth value of level-$i$
reachability from $\mathrm{st}.U$ to $\mathrm{st}.V$ with bound $2^w$ and relation determined by the
step oracle, $x$, and $s$. Every preterminal configuration satisfies the program guard
and has all registers at most $2^{w^2}$; the final register vector agrees with $\mathrm{st}$
except that its midpoint register is $M'$.
\end{theorem}

%%% added by the blueprint pipeline
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Recursion: further results}

\begin{theorem}[Step relation as an oracle query]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rel_iff_orc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rel_iff_orc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle with four decider indices $0,1,2,3$ on Boolean-word
inputs, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $s,u,v$ be natural numbers. The step relation
determined by $\mathrm{orc}$, $x$ and $s$ holds between $u$ and $v$ if and only if decider
$3$ of $\mathrm{orc}$ accepts the nested pair encoding
$\langle x,\langle \mathrm{bin}(u),\langle \mathrm{bin}(v),\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$,
where $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ is the binary representation of $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Outer state initialization]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p004-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b004
}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, let the outer state be the state initialized using $s$
and $w$, with its source code set to $u$, its target code set to $v$, and its midpoint
set to $M$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial oracle acceptance]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle mapping indices in $\{0,1,2,3\}$ and Boolean strings to
truth values, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $s,u$ be natural numbers. The oracle
accepts at index $1$ the pair encoding of $x$ and the pair encoding of the binary
expansions of $u$ and $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance oracle condition]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle mapping indices in $\{0,1,2,3\}$ and Boolean strings to
truth values, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $s,v$ be natural numbers. The oracle
accepts at index $2$ the pair encoding of $x$ and the pair encoding of the binary
expansions of $v$ and $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Source register of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_U}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_U}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the source-code register of the outer state with
parameters $s,w,u,v,M$ equals $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Target register of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_V}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_V}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the target-code register of the outer state with
parameters $s,w,u,v,M$ equals $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Outer-search midpoint register]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_M}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_M}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the midpoint register of the outer-search state
determined by these values equals $M$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Initial recursion level]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_I}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_I}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the recursion-level register of the outer-search
state determined by these values is $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Outer-search code bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_K}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_K}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the code-bound register of the outer-search state
determined by these values equals $2^w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Width register of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_w}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_w}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the width register of the outer state with parameters
$s,w,u,v,M$ equals $w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Radius register of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_s}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_s}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the radius register of the outer state with parameters
$s,w,u,v,M$ equals $s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bound on the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_bd}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_bd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.zero, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts}
\difficulty{3}
Let $s,w,u,v,M$ be natural numbers such that $s\le w$, $u\le 2^w$, $v\le 2^w$, and $M\le
2^w$. Then every register of the outer state with parameters $s,w,u,v,M$ is at most
$2^{w^2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariant of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_inv}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_inv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.zero, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt}
\difficulty{3}
Let $s,w,u,v,M$ be natural numbers with $u<2^w$, $v<2^w$, and $M\le 2^w$. The state
obtained from the outer state with parameters $s,w,u,v,M$ by setting its level register
to $w$ has all scratch, input-length, exponent, power, loop, and popped-endpoint
registers equal to zero; its radius and width registers are $s$ and $w$, its code-bound
register is $2^w$, its source and target registers are less than $2^w$, its midpoint
register is at most $2^w$, its level register is $w$, its endpoint stack is less than
$2^{w(w-w)}$, and its phase stack is less than $2^{w-w}$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.ret, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.step, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.zero, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.contH, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cp_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.gb_of, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_K, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_U, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_V, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_s, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_w, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₂, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{7}
Let $E,s,w,u$ be natural numbers, let $b_0$ be a Boolean, let $	ext{orc}$ be an oracle
assigning a Boolean answer to each of four deciders and each Boolean word, and let $x$
be a Boolean word. Assume $s\le w$, $u<2^w$, and that for every $M\le 2^w$, the machine
$A(E)$ started at its next-source-search state with register values given by the outer
state $(s,w,u,0,M)$ halts with answer $b_0$, while every configuration before halting
satisfies the program guard with register bound $2^{w^2}$. Then, for every $k,v,M$ such
that $v+k=2^w$ and $M\le 2^w$, the machine started at its outer target-search state with
register values given by $(s,w,u,v,M)$ halts with answer equal to $b_0$ or the assertion
that some $v'$ satisfies $v\le v'<2^w$, the accepting-code oracle accepts $v'$, and
there is a depth-$w$ reachability from $u$ to $v'$ using the relation $R(a,b)$ that
holds exactly when the step oracle accepts the encoded triple $(a,b,s)$. Throughout the
run before halting, every configuration satisfies the same guard with bound $2^{w^2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting behavior of the outer source search]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p004-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b004,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b002
}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.ret, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.step, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.gb_of, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_K, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_U, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_s, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerV_run, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₂, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{7}
Let $s,w$ be natural numbers with $s\le w$. For every $k,u,M$ such that $u+k=2^w$ and
$M\le 2^w$, the machine started at its outer source-search label, with registers
initialized to the outer state having parameters $s,w,u,0,M$, halts with the Boolean
answer that is true exactly when there exist $u',v$ such that $u\le u'<2^w$, the
initial-code oracle accepts $u'$, the accepting-code oracle accepts $v$, and there is a
path of reachability of depth $w$ from $u'$ to $v$ through codes below $2^w$. Throughout
the run before halting, every register is at most $2^{w^2}$ and each configuration
satisfies the machine's precondition.
\end{theorem}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV_zero, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setup_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a natural number with $1\le E$, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let
$\mathrm{orc}$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four query types and each Boolean
word. Suppose that for every natural number $k\le |x|$, the answer to query type $0$ on
the encoding of $x$ and the binary word for $k$ is true exactly when $k<|x|$. The
register program, started in its scan state with all registers zero and no answer, halts
with the Boolean value of the following proposition: there are $u,v<2^{(|x|+2)^{2E}}$
such that query type $1$ accepts $u$ as an initial code and query type $2$ accepts $v$
as an accepting code, both at radius $(|x|+2)^E$, and $u$ reaches $v$ in $(|x|+2)^{2E}$
levels under the relation specified by query type $3$ at that radius, with intermediate
codes bounded by $2^{(|x|+2)^{2E}}$. Throughout the run, every register value is at most
$2^{((|x|+2)^{2E})((|x|+2)^{2E})}$.
\end{theorem}

%%% added by the blueprint pipeline
\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Search: further results}

\begin{theorem}[Initial-code oracle test]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.initO_iff_orc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.initO_iff_orc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mathrm{orc}$ assign a truth value to each pair of an index in $\{0,1,2,3\}$ and a
Boolean string, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $s,u\in\mathbb{N}$. Writing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ for the pair encoding of Boolean strings and
$\mathrm{bin}(n)$ for the binary expansion of $n$, the initial-code oracle test for
$\mathrm{orc}$, $x$, $s$, $u$ holds if and only if
$\mathrm{orc}\bigl(1,\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bin}(u),\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle\bigr)$
is true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Accepting-code oracle test]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.accO_iff_orc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.accO_iff_orc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mathrm{orc}$ assign a truth value to each pair of an index in $\{0,1,2,3\}$ and a
Boolean string, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $s,v\in\mathbb{N}$. Writing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ for the pair encoding of Boolean strings and
$\mathrm{bin}(n)$ for the binary expansion of $n$, the accepting-code oracle test for
$\mathrm{orc}$, $x$, $s$, $v$ holds if and only if
$\mathrm{orc}\bigl(2,\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bin}(v),\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle\bigr)$
is true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Register vector of the outer-search file]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_toV}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_toV}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.upd_M, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.upd_U, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.upd_V, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rM, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rU, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt}
\difficulty{2}
Let $s,w,u,v,M\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $\rho$ be the $18$-entry register vector of the
Savitch register machine's setup file, in which every register is zero except the
window radius ($s$), the code width ($w$) and the code bound ($2^w$). Then the register
vector of the outer-search file, which is the setup file with source code $u$, target
code $v$ and midpoint $M$, equals $\rho$ with the source-code entry replaced by $u$, then
the target-code entry replaced by $v$, then the midpoint entry replaced by $M$.
\end{theorem}
