## ===== blueprint/src/chapter/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/SavitchARM/Window.tex =====

\section{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Window}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Window
Savitch-style midpoint reachability over configuration codes at a window radius $s$ decides
membership once $s$ bounds the decider's space; when the space bound is not known, the radius is
found by iterative deepening, testing at each $s=1,2,\dots$ whether a configuration with a work
head on the edge $\pm s$ of the window is reachable. This module proves the two facts the
deepening needs: if no such edge configuration is reachable, membership is midpoint
reachability at radius $s$ (window exactness), and beyond the space bound no edge configuration
is reachable (termination).

\begin{definition}[No reachable edge code]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.NoEdge}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.NoEdge}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.edgeLang, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, $x$ a Boolean
input and $s,w\in\mathbb N$. The predicate $\mathrm{NoEdge}(N,x,s,w)$ states that there are no
$u<2^w$ and $v<2^w$ such that $u$ is the radius-$s$ code of the initial configuration of $N$ on
$x$ (the word $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(u),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$ is in the
initial-code language), $v$ is the radius-$s$ code of a configuration of $N$ on $x$ in the
radius-$s$ window with some work head at position $-s$ or $s$ (the word
$\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(v),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$ is in the edge-code language),
and $\mathrm{Reach}_{2^w}^{E_s}(w,u,v)$ holds. Here a configuration lies in the radius-$s$ window when every work head is within distance $s$ of the origin and every work cell farther out is blank, $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,u,v)$ denotes bounded midpoint reachability for a relation $R$ on $\mathbb N$ (at level $0$: $u=v$ or $R(u,v)$; at level $i+1$: there is $m<K$ with $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,u,m)$ and $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,m,v)$), and $E_s(a,b)$ is the code-level step relation (the triple $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(a),\langle\mathrm{bits}(b),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$ belongs to the step-pair language of $N$, i.e.\ $a$ and $b$ are radius-$s$ codes of configurations of $N$ on $x$ in the radius-$s$ window, the second one step after the first).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Defining equation of the no-edge predicate]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.noEdge_iff}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.noEdge_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.edgeLang, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.NoEdge, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, $x$ a Boolean
input and $s,w\in\mathbb N$. Then $\mathrm{NoEdge}(N,x,s,w)$ holds if and only if there are no
$u<2^w$ and $v<2^w$ such that $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(u),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$
lies in the initial-code language of $N$ (so $u$ is the radius-$s$ code of the initial
configuration on $x$), $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(v),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$ lies in
the edge-code language of $N$ (so $v$ is the radius-$s$ code of a configuration in the
radius-$s$ window with a work head at $\pm s$), and $\mathrm{Reach}_{2^w}^{E_s}(w,u,v)$ holds,
where a configuration lies in the radius-$s$ window when every work head is within distance $s$ of the origin and every work cell farther out is blank, $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,u,v)$ denotes bounded midpoint reachability for a relation $R$ on $\mathbb N$ (at level $0$: $u=v$ or $R(u,v)$; at level $i+1$: there is $m<K$ with $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,u,m)$ and $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,m,v)$), and $E_s(a,b)$ is the code-level step relation (the triple $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(a),\langle\mathrm{bits}(b),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$ belongs to the step-pair language of $N$, i.e.\ $a$ and $b$ are radius-$s$ codes of configurations of $N$ on $x$ in the radius-$s$ window, the second one step after the first).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Codes lie below the level bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.window_code_lt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.window_code_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode_lt, Complexity.Codec.codeK, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{2}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with chunk width
$W(N)$, let $x$ be a Boolean input and $s,w\in\mathbb N$, and suppose
$(2W(N)+2)\,(s+\lfloor\log_2|x|\rfloor+2)\le w$ (with $\lfloor\log_2 0\rfloor=0$). Then every
configuration of $N$ on $x$ has radius-$s$ code less than $2^w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reachable codes are midpoint witnesses]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.window_reach_of_rcode}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.window_reach_of_rcode}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}

reachable from the radius-$s$ code $u_0$ of the initial configuration of $N$ on $x$ by finitely
many steps of $E_s$, then $\mathrm{Reach}_{2^w}^{E_s}(w,u_0,v)$ holds, where $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,u,v)$ denotes bounded midpoint reachability for a relation $R$ on $\mathbb N$ (at level $0$: $u=v$ or $R(u,v)$; at level $i+1$: there is $m<K$ with $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,u,m)$ and $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,m,v)$), and
$E_s(a,b)$ is the code-level step relation (the triple $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(a),\langle\mathrm{bits}(b),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$ belongs to the step-pair language of $N$, i.e.\ $a$ and $b$ are radius-$s$ codes of configurations of $N$ on $x$ in the radius-$s$ window, the second one step after the first).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Termination: no edge beyond the space bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.noEdge_of_lt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.noEdge_of_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.mem_edgeLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_initLang, Complexity.ExpBFS.RCode, Complexity.ExpBFS.WinRun.last, Complexity.ExpBFS.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq, Complexity.ExpBFS.inWin_runWith_of_decides, Complexity.ExpBFS.rcode_iff, Complexity.ExpBFS.rcode_iff_reflTransGen, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.NoEdge, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reflTransGen_of_reach, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.Cfg.InWindow.core_bounds, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.NDTM.inWindow_of_coreSum_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet that decides a
language $L$ in space $\mathrm{sp}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ (on every input $x$ all branches of
some common length have halted, each visits at most $\mathrm{sp}(|x|)$ work cells, and
$x\in L$ exactly when some branch accepts). For every Boolean input $x$ and all
$s,w\in\mathbb N$ with $\mathrm{sp}(|x|)<s$, there are no $u,v<2^w$ such that $u$ is the
radius-$s$ code of the initial configuration of $N$ on $x$, $v$ is the radius-$s$ code of a
configuration of $N$ on $x$ in the radius-$s$ window with some work head at $-s$ or $s$, and
$\mathrm{Reach}_{2^w}^{E_s}(w,u,v)$ holds; here a configuration lies in the radius-$s$ window when every work head is within distance $s$ of the origin and every work cell farther out is blank, $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,u,v)$ denotes bounded midpoint reachability for a relation $R$ on $\mathbb N$ (at level $0$: $u=v$ or $R(u,v)$; at level $i+1$: there is $m<K$ with $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,u,m)$ and $\mathrm{Reach}_K^R(i,m,v)$), and $E_s(a,b)$ is the code-level step relation (the triple $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(a),\langle\mathrm{bits}(b),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$ belongs to the step-pair language of $N$, i.e.\ $a$ and $b$ are radius-$s$ codes of configurations of $N$ on $x$ in the radius-$s$ window, the second one step after the first).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Window exactness]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mem_iff_reach_of_noEdge}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mem_iff_reach_of_noEdge}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.codeK, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_edgeLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath, Complexity.Codec.stepWith_eq_apply, Complexity.ExpBFS.WinRun, Complexity.ExpBFS.WinRun.last, Complexity.ExpBFS.WinRun.snoc, Complexity.ExpBFS.inWin_init, Complexity.ExpBFS.rcode_iff, Complexity.ExpBFS.winRun_iff, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.NoEdge, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reflTransGen_of_reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.window_code_lt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.window_reach_of_rcode, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.Cfg.InWindow.apply_of_lt, Turing.Cfg.InWindow.core_bounds, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound, Turing.FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_iff, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil, Turing.pairEncode}

\section{Space Complexity --- Window Clock}

\begin{theorem}[Space bounds the work-tape window]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.inWindow_of_spaceUsed_le}
\label{Turing.FinTM.inWindow_of_spaceUsed_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_pos_lt_card_visited, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.mem_visited_of_ne_none, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape_le_spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead_mono}

Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word,
and let $t,s$ be natural numbers. If the total number of distinct work-tape cells
visited by the computation of $M$ on $x$ through step $t$ is at most $s$, then at every
time $u\le t$ each work-tape head is at a position of absolute value at most $s$, and
every cell at an integer position of absolute value greater than $s$ is blank on every
work tape.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Turing.windowRun_summary_of_halts}

\begin{theorem}[A bounded machine for simulating a windowed run]
\lean{Turing.exists_configWindowRunnerTM}
\label{Turing.exists_configWindowRunnerTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.configBound, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.RecSym, Turing.RecSym.digitEmb, Turing.RecordAt, Turing.WindowExit, Turing.cfgRecord, Turing.fieldsTape, Turing.recordLength, Turing.windowRun}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input and $k$ work tapes. Let $T$
be a finite set with decidable equality, and let
$u:T\times\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\to T$ satisfy $u(\tau,\mathrm{none})=\tau$ for
every $\tau\in T$. There exist a natural number $K$, a finite state set $P$ with
decidable equality, a Turing machine $R$ with $K+1$ work tapes over an alphabet
recording Boolean digits, work-tape cells, states, and tags, an entry state
$p_{\mathrm{in}}$, an injective map $e$ from the three window-exit types to states of
$R$ whose values differ from $p_{\mathrm{in}}$, and a natural number $C$ with the
following property. For every Boolean input $x$, natural number $s$, configuration $c$
of $M$ on $x$ whose work-tape head positions have absolute value at most $s$ and whose
work-tape cells outside that window are blank, and tag $\tau\in T$, suppose a
configuration $d$ of $R$ on the digit encoding of $x$ has state $p_{\mathrm{in}}$, has
on its first work tape the record encoding $(c,\tau)$, and has blank contents on every
other work tape. Then there are a time $t$ and an exit type $o$ such that $t\le
C2^{C(\ell+1)}$, where $\ell=k(2s+1)+\mathrm{posWidth}(|x|)+k+4$, and the state of $R$
after $t$ steps is $e(o)$, while before time $t$ it is never in any exit state. At every
time $v\le t$, each work-tape head of $R$ has moved from its initial position by at most
$C(\ell+1)$, and the output remains unchanged; by time $t$ its total space use is at
most $(K+1)(2C(\ell+1)+1)$. For every $N\le \mathrm{configBound}(M,|x|,s)+1$, if the
$N$-step windowed run from $(c,\tau)$ does not end by clock exhaustion, its exit type is
$o$. If $o$ is not clock exhaustion, there is some $N$ for which that windowed run ends
with type $o$, and at time $t$ the runner's first work tape agrees with the record of
the resulting configuration and updated tag throughout the recorded field; its state is
$e(o)$, and all other tape cells retain their initial contents.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Value of an all-ones binary word]
\lean{Turing.cw_true_value}
\label{Turing.cw_true_value}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every $W\in\mathbb{N}$, the natural number whose binary digits are $W$ ones equals $2^W-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Per-round cost bound]
\lean{Turing.cw_round_cost}
\label{Turing.cw_round_cost}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $L,n,p\in\mathbb{N}$ with $p\le L$ and $n+2\le 2^p$. Then $L+n+1\le 2^{L+1}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clock budget arithmetic]
\lean{Turing.cw_budget}
\label{Turing.cw_budget}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.cw_round_cost}
\difficulty{5}
Let $q,k,n,s,p,L,B,C\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $L=k(2s+1)+p+k+4$, $n+2\le 2^p$ and $B\le
2^{q+p+3k(2s+1)}$. Then \[C(B+1)(L+n+1)\le 2^{(C+q+8)(k(2s+1)+p+2)}-1.\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Single-exponential time envelope]
\lean{Turing.cw_time_bound}
\label{Turing.cw_time_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $c,L,W,A,D\in\mathbb{N}$ with $W\le cL$, and set $C=A+4c+D+10$. Then
\[A(L+1)+\bigl(5(2^W-1)+2W+3\bigr)+(2W+2)+D\le C\cdot 2^{C(L+1)}.\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Linear head envelope with a linear clock]
\lean{Turing.cw_head_bound}
\label{Turing.cw_head_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $c,L,W,C\in\mathbb{N}$ with $W\le cL$. Then $C(L+W+1)\le C(c+1)(L+1)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Total field length of a configuration record]
\lean{Turing.cw_field_total}
\label{Turing.cw_field_total}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.cfgRecord, Turing.cfgRecord_length, Turing.joinFields_cfgRecord_length, Turing.joinFields_length, Turing.posWidth, Turing.recordLength_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a Boolean input, let $s\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a
configuration with $k$ work tapes on input $x$, and let $\tau$ be a tag. Consider the
configuration record of $d$ at radius $s$ with tag $\tau$: the $k+3$ fields consisting of the
state, the input position in binary with as many digits as the bit length $w$ of $|x|+1$, the
cells $-s,\dots,s$ of each work tape with head marks, and the tag. The sum of the lengths of
these fields is $k(2s+1)+w+2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[An all-ones clock covers every round]
\lean{Turing.cw_record_clock}
\label{Turing.cw_record_clock}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.configBound, Turing.FinTM.configBound_le_two_pow, Turing.cfgRecord, Turing.cw_budget, Turing.cw_field_total, Turing.cw_true_value, Turing.posWidth, Turing.recordLength, Turing.recordLength_eq, Turing.record_pos_lt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes and state set
$Q$, let $x$ be a Boolean input of length $n$, let $s,C\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a
configuration of $M$ on $x$ and $\tau$ a tag. Let $w$ be the bit length of $n+1$, let
$\ell=k(2s+1)+w+k+4$ be the record length, let $F$ be the total length of the fields of the
configuration record of $d$ at radius $s$ with tag $\tau$, and set $c=C+|Q|+8$ and $W=cF$. Then
$W\le c\ell$, and for every $N\le (|Q|+1)(n+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k+1$ the value $2^W-1$ of the
binary word of $W$ ones satisfies $CN(\ell+n+1)\le 2^W-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[One-step left move on a tape]
\lean{Turing.cw_leftTM}
\label{Turing.cw_leftTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.tapeAction}
For $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and a work tape $i<k$, the one-step left move on tape $i$ is the Turing
machine with $k$ work tapes and Boolean states, starting in state false, whose every transition
keeps the input head, writes nothing, moves the head of tape $i$ one cell to the left, leaves
every other tape and the output untouched, and enters state true.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Run of the one-step left move]
\lean{Turing.cw_left_run}
\label{Turing.cw_left_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_one, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.cw_leftTM, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.step_of_tapeAction_move}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $i<k$, and consider the Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and
Boolean states whose every transition moves the head of tape $i$ one cell left, writes and
emits nothing, keeps the input head, and enters state true. Let $d$ be a configuration of this
machine whose state is false. Then after one step the configuration is $d$ with state true and
the head of tape $i$ moved from position $p$ to $p-1$, and at time $0$ the state is not true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reading a constant patch]
\lean{Turing.cw_patch_rep}
\label{Turing.cw_patch_rep}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.wordPatch, Turing.wordPatch_of_mem, Turing.wordPatch_of_not_mem}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Gamma$ be an alphabet, let $\gamma$ be a tape over $\Gamma$ (a map from $\mathbb{Z}$ to
cells that are blank or hold a letter), and let $p\in\mathbb{Z}$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and
$e\in\Gamma$. The tape obtained from $\gamma$ by writing $n$ copies of $e$ in the cells
$p,\dots,p+n-1$ holds $e$ at every cell $z$ with $p\le z<p+n$, and holds $\gamma(z)$ at every
other cell $z$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Tape holding a constant word]
\lean{Turing.cw_buffer_rep}
\label{Turing.cw_buffer_rep}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_of_neg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $e$ be a letter and let $z\in\mathbb{Z}$. The tape that holds the
word $e^n$ in cells $0,\dots,n-1$ and is blank elsewhere holds $e$ at cell $z$ if $0\le z<n$,
and is blank at $z$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Joining adjacent constant patches]
\lean{Turing.cw_join}
\label{Turing.cw_join}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.wordPatch, Turing.wordPatch_append}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\gamma$ be a tape over an alphabet $\Gamma$, let $p\in\mathbb{Z}$, $e\in\Gamma$ and
$n,l\in\mathbb{N}$. Writing $e^n$ onto $\gamma$ from cell $p$ and then $e^l$ from cell $p+n$
gives the same tape as writing $e^{n+l}$ onto $\gamma$ from cell $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Constant mapped copy onto a destination tape]
\lean{Turing.cw_copy_constant}
\label{Turing.cw_copy_constant}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.copyMapTM, Turing.copyMapTM_run_ofCfg, Turing.cw_patch_rep, Turing.wordPatch}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\sigma\ne\delta$ be two work tapes among $k$, let $e$ be a letter
and $w$ a word. Consider the mapped copy machine from tape $\sigma$ to tape $\delta$ that
writes $e$ in place of every copied letter, and let $d$ be a configuration of it in its sweep
state such that for every integer $-1\le z\le|w|$ the cell of tape $\sigma$ at offset $z$ from
its head holds the $z$-th letter of $w$ (blank at $z=-1$ and $z=|w|$). Then after $2|w|+2$
steps the machine is in its done state and its configuration is $d$ except that $e^{|w|}$ has
been written on tape $\delta$ in the $|w|$ cells starting at its head; it is not done at any
earlier time; and at every time up to $2|w|+2$ the heads of $\sigma$ and $\delta$ each lie in
$[h-1,h+|w|]$, $h$ being that head's initial position, while every other head is at its initial
position.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clearing a written patch blanks the tape]
\lean{Turing.cw_clear_patch}
\label{Turing.cw_clear_patch}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_left, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.clearTM, Turing.clearTM_run_ofCfg, Turing.wordPatch, Turing.wordPatch_of_mem, Turing.wordPatch_of_not_mem}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $i$ be one of $k$ work tapes, let $w$ be a word, and let $d$ be a
configuration whose tape $i$ is blank at every cell outside $[h,h+|w|)$, where $h$ is the head
position of tape $i$ in $d$. Let $A$ be $d$ with state sweep and with $w$ written on tape $i$
from cell $h$. Then the clear machine on tape $i$, run from $A$ for $2|w|+2$ steps, reaches $d$
with state done and tape $i$ entirely blank; it is not in state done at any earlier time; and
at every time up to $2|w|+2$ the head of tape $i$ lies in $[h-1,h+|w|]$ while every other head
stays at its position in $d$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Phases of the clock runner]
\lean{Turing.cw_Idx}
\label{Turing.cw_Idx}
\leanok
For $c,m\in\mathbb{N}$, the phases of the clock runner form the following finite set with
decidable equality: for each pass $p<c$ and field $j<m$, the copy of field $j$ onto the clock,
the skip past field $j$ on the record tape, the one-cell move back onto the clock's delimiter,
and the skip back over field $j$ on the record tape; the skip past the written clock cells,
indexed either by a pair $(p,j)$ or by a marker for the end of the last pass; the skip back
over the clock word; the windowed runner; the clear of the clock, tagged by a Boolean recording
a halted or a left exit; and the stop phase.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Control sets of the clock runner's phases]
\lean{Turing.cw_Ctrl}
\label{Turing.cw_Ctrl}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.SeekPhase, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.WindowExit, Turing.cw_Idx}
Given a state set $P$ and $c,m\in\mathbb{N}$, each phase of the clock runner is assigned a
control set: the sweep controls (sweep, rewind, done) for the field copies and the clears; the
seek controls (run, gap, back, done) for the record skips, the clock skips, the record
skip-backs and the clock skip-back; the Booleans for the one-cell left moves; $P$ for the
windowed runner; and the three window exits (halted, left, exhausted) for the stop phase.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Machines of the clock runner's phases]
\lean{Turing.cw_rows}
\label{Turing.cw_rows}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.clearTM, Turing.copyMapTM, Turing.cw_Ctrl, Turing.cw_Idx, Turing.cw_leftTM, Turing.skipBackTM, Turing.skipTM}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $e$ be a tape symbol, let $R$ be a Turing machine with $K+2$ work
tapes and state set $P$, and let $c,m\in\mathbb{N}$. Each phase of the clock runner is assigned
a machine on $K+2$ work tapes: each field copy runs the mapped copy from tape $0$ to tape $K+1$
that writes $e$ in every cell; each record skip runs the skip on tape $0$; each clock skip runs
the skip on tape $K+1$; each one-cell left move moves the head of tape $K+1$ one cell left;
each record skip-back runs the skip back on tape $0$; the clock skip-back runs the skip back on
tape $K+1$; the runner phase runs $R$; each clear runs the clear of tape $K+1$; and the stop
phase is the stationary machine, started at the exit exhausted, that keeps its state and moves,
writes and emits nothing.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Continuation after a field's round]
\lean{Turing.cw_next}
\label{Turing.cw_next}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.SeekPhase, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.cw_Ctrl, Turing.cw_Idx}
Let $c,m\in\mathbb{N}$, $p<c$ and $j<m$. The continuation of the clock runner after the round
of field $j$ in pass $p$ is the copy phase of field $j+1$ in pass $p$ with control sweep when
$j+1<m$, and otherwise the skip back over field $j$ in pass $p$ with control run.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Continuation after a record skip-back]
\lean{Turing.cw_prev}
\label{Turing.cw_prev}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.SeekPhase, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.cw_Ctrl, Turing.cw_Idx}
Let $c,m\in\mathbb{N}$, $p<c$ and $j<m$. The continuation of the clock runner after the skip
back over field $j$ in pass $p$ is the skip back over field $j-1$ in pass $p$ with control run
when $j>0$; otherwise the copy phase of field $0$ in pass $p+1$ with control sweep when
$p+1<c$; and otherwise the final clock skip (after the last pass) with control run.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Continuation after a clock skip]
\lean{Turing.cw_afterSkip}
\label{Turing.cw_afterSkip}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.SeekPhase, Turing.cw_Ctrl, Turing.cw_Idx}
Let $c,m\in\mathbb{N}$. After the clock skip indexed by a pair $(p,j)$ with $p<c$ and $j<m$,
the clock runner continues with the one-cell left move of $(p,j)$ in control false; after the
final clock skip, which carries no pair, it continues with the skip back over the clock word in
control run.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Redirect table of the clock runner]
\lean{Turing.cw_red}
\label{Turing.cw_red}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.SeekPhase, Turing.SweepPhase, Turing.WindowExit, Turing.cw_Ctrl, Turing.cw_Idx, Turing.cw_afterSkip, Turing.cw_next, Turing.cw_prev}
Let $P$ be a state set with decidable equality, $p_{\mathrm{en}}\in P$ an entry state,
$\mathrm{ex}$ a map from the window exits (halted, left, exhausted) to $P$, and
$c,m\in\mathbb{N}$. The redirect table sends the copy of field $j$ in pass $p$ at done to the
record skip of $(p,j)$ at run; that record skip at done to the clock skip indexed by $(p,j)$ at
run; a clock skip at done to its continuation (the left move of $(p,j)$ at false, or after the
last pass the clock skip-back at run); the left move of $(p,j)$ at true to the copy of field
$j+1$ in pass $p$ at sweep if $j+1<m$, else to the skip back over field $j$ at run; the skip
back over field $j$ in pass $p$ at done to the skip back over field $j-1$ at run if $j>0$, else
to the copy of field $0$ in pass $p+1$ at sweep if $p+1<c$, else to the final clock skip at
run; the clock skip-back at done to the runner at $p_{\mathrm{en}}$; the runner at
$\mathrm{ex}(\text{halted})$, $\mathrm{ex}(\text{left})$ and $\mathrm{ex}(\text{exhausted})$ to
the clear tagged true at sweep, the clear tagged false at sweep, and the stop phase at
exhausted, respectively; and the clear tagged $b$ at done to the stop phase at halted if $b$ is
true and at left otherwise. Every other phase and control is not redirected.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The clock runner machine]
\lean{Turing.cw_hostTM}
\label{Turing.cw_hostTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.WindowExit, Turing.cw_Ctrl, Turing.cw_Idx, Turing.cw_red, Turing.cw_rows, Turing.phaseHostTM}
Let $K,c,m\in\mathbb{N}$, let $e$ be a tape symbol, and let $R$ be a Turing machine with $K+2$
work tapes whose state set $P$ has decidable equality, with entry state $p_{\mathrm{en}}\in P$
and a map $\mathrm{ex}$ from the window exits to $P$. The clock runner is the Turing machine
with $K+2$ work tapes whose states are pairs of a phase and a control of that phase: at a pair
that the clock runner's redirect table sends to another pair, it takes one stationary, silent
step to that pair; at any other pair it takes the transition of the phase's machine (field
copies, record and clock skips, left moves, skip-backs, the runner $R$, the clear of tape
$K+1$, or the stationary stop machine), tagging the new control with the same phase. Its
initial state is the stop phase at exhausted.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Writer configurations]
\lean{Turing.cw_cfg}
\label{Turing.cw_cfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.wordPatch}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $e$ be a tape symbol, let $d$ be a configuration with $K+2$ work
tapes on an input $x$, let $q$ be a state, let $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The
writer configuration has state $q$, the input head of $d$, the output of $d$, tape $K+1$ equal
to that of $d$ with $n$ copies of $e$ written from the head position of tape $K+1$ in $d$,
every other tape as in $d$, the head of tape $0$ moved by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ moved
by $b$ from their positions in $d$, and every other head as in $d$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Record and clock tapes are distinct]
\lean{Turing.cw_zero_ne_last}
\label{Turing.cw_zero_ne_last}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every $K\in\mathbb{N}$, the indices $0$ and $K+1$ of the work tapes $\{0,1,\dots,K+1\}$ are
distinct.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clock tape of a writer configuration]
\lean{Turing.cw_cfg_clockTape}
\label{Turing.cw_cfg_clockTape}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.cw_cfg, Turing.wordPatch}
\difficulty{1}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a configuration of a Turing machine with $K+2$ work tapes on
some input, and let $e$ be a tape symbol. For a state $q$, integers $a,b$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
let $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ be the configuration obtained from $d$ by setting the state to $q$,
moving the head of tape $0$ by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ by $b$, and writing $n$ copies of
$e$ on tape $K+1$ starting at its head position in $d$; let $h_j$ denote the head position of
tape $j$ in $d$. Then tape $K+1$ of $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ is tape $K+1$ of $d$ with $n$ copies of
$e$ written in the cells starting at $h_{K+1}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clock cell of a writer configuration]
\lean{Turing.cw_cfg_clock}
\label{Turing.cw_cfg_clock}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.cw_cfg, Turing.cw_cfg_clockTape, Turing.cw_patch_rep}
\difficulty{1}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a configuration of a Turing machine with $K+2$ work tapes on
some input, and let $e$ be a tape symbol. For a state $q$, integers $a,b$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
let $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ be the configuration obtained from $d$ by setting the state to $q$,
moving the head of tape $0$ by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ by $b$, and writing $n$ copies of
$e$ on tape $K+1$ starting at its head position in $d$; let $h_j$ denote the head position of
tape $j$ in $d$. Then for every $z\in\mathbb{Z}$, cell $z$ of tape $K+1$ in $\omega(q,a,n,b)$
holds $e$ if $h_{K+1}\le z<h_{K+1}+n$, and otherwise holds the content of cell $z$ of tape
$K+1$ in $d$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Other tapes of a writer configuration]
\lean{Turing.cw_cfg_tape}
\label{Turing.cw_cfg_tape}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.cw_cfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a configuration of a Turing machine with $K+2$ work tapes on
some input, and let $e$ be a tape symbol. For a state $q$, integers $a,b$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
let $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ be the configuration obtained from $d$ by setting the state to $q$,
moving the head of tape $0$ by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ by $b$, and writing $n$ copies of
$e$ on tape $K+1$ starting at its head position in $d$; let $h_j$ denote the head position of
tape $j$ in $d$. Then for every work tape $j\ne K+1$ and every cell $z$, cell $z$ of tape $j$
in $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ equals cell $z$ of tape $j$ in $d$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Record head of a writer configuration]
\lean{Turing.cw_cfg_pos₀}
\label{Turing.cw_cfg_pos₀}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.cw_cfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a configuration of a Turing machine with $K+2$ work tapes on
some input, and let $e$ be a tape symbol. For a state $q$, integers $a,b$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
let $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ be the configuration obtained from $d$ by setting the state to $q$,
moving the head of tape $0$ by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ by $b$, and writing $n$ copies of
$e$ on tape $K+1$ starting at its head position in $d$; let $h_j$ denote the head position of
tape $j$ in $d$. Then the head of tape $0$ in $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ is at position $h_0+a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clock head of a writer configuration]
\lean{Turing.cw_cfg_posL}
\label{Turing.cw_cfg_posL}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.cw_cfg, Turing.cw_zero_ne_last}
\difficulty{1}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a configuration of a Turing machine with $K+2$ work tapes on
some input, and let $e$ be a tape symbol. For a state $q$, integers $a,b$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
let $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ be the configuration obtained from $d$ by setting the state to $q$,
moving the head of tape $0$ by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ by $b$, and writing $n$ copies of
$e$ on tape $K+1$ starting at its head position in $d$; let $h_j$ denote the head position of
tape $j$ in $d$. Then the head of tape $K+1$ in $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ is at position $h_{K+1}+b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Other heads of a writer configuration]
\lean{Turing.cw_cfg_pos}
\label{Turing.cw_cfg_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.cw_cfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a configuration of a Turing machine with $K+2$ work tapes on
some input, and let $e$ be a tape symbol. For a state $q$, integers $a,b$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
let $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ be the configuration obtained from $d$ by setting the state to $q$,
moving the head of tape $0$ by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ by $b$, and writing $n$ copies of
$e$ on tape $K+1$ starting at its head position in $d$; let $h_j$ denote the head position of
tape $j$ in $d$. Then for every work tape $j$ with $j\ne 0$ and $j\ne K+1$, the head of tape
$j$ in $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ is at position $h_j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[State renaming keeps the heads]
\lean{Turing.cw_mapState_pos}
\label{Turing.cw_mapState_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a configuration of a multi-tape Turing machine with state set $S$, and let $f:S\to
S'$. The configuration obtained from $C$ by renaming its state through $f$ has the same
work-tape head positions as $C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[State renaming keeps the tapes]
\lean{Turing.cw_mapState_tapes}
\label{Turing.cw_mapState_tapes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a configuration of a multi-tape Turing machine with state set $S$, and let $f:S\to
S'$. The configuration obtained from $C$ by renaming its state through $f$ has the same
work-tape contents as $C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[State renaming keeps input head and output]
\lean{Turing.cw_mapState_io}
\label{Turing.cw_mapState_io}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState}
\difficulty{1}

Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a configuration of a Turing machine with $K+2$ work tapes on
some input, and let $e$ be a tape symbol. For a state $q$, integers $a,b$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
let $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ be the configuration obtained from $d$ by setting the state to $q$,
moving the head of tape $0$ by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ by $b$, and writing $n$ copies of
$e$ on tape $K+1$ starting at its head position in $d$; let $h_j$ denote the head position of
tape $j$ in $d$. Then for every map $f$ on states, renaming the state of $\omega(q,a,n,b)$
through $f$ gives $\omega(f(q),a,n,b)$.
\end{lemma}

For $k,r\in\mathbb{N}$ and an origin $o\in\mathbb{Z}^k$, a vector of head positions
$\mathrm{pos}\in\mathbb{Z}^k$ lies in the box of radius $r$ around $o$ when
$\abs{\mathrm{pos}_j-o_j}\le r$ for every $j<k$.
\end{definition}

$\ell_0,u_0,\ell_1,u_1\in\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $o_0+\ell_0\le \mathrm{pos}_0\le o_0+u_0$,
$o_{K+1}+\ell_1\le\mathrm{pos}_{K+1}\le o_{K+1}+u_1$, $\mathrm{pos}_j=o_j$ for every
$j\notin\{0,K+1\}$, and $-r\le\ell_0$, $u_0\le r$, $-r\le\ell_1$, $u_1\le r$. Then
$\abs{\mathrm{pos}_j-o_j}\le r$ for every $j$.
\end{lemma}

$u_i\le o_i+r$, and $\abs{s_j-o_j}\le r$ for every $j$. Then $\abs{\mathrm{pos}_j-o_j}\le r$

$p_{\mathrm{en}}\in P$ and a map $\mathrm{ex}$ from the three window exits (halted, left,
exhausted) to $P$. Let $H$ be the clock runner built from these data: the phase host on $K+2$
work tapes whose phases are the clock writer's phases for $c$ passes over $m$ record fields
(acting on the record tape $0$ and the clock tape $K+1$), the runner $R$, the clear of the
clock tape, and a stationary stop phase; the states of the stop phase are called exits. For a
phase $i$, let $M_i$ be its machine and $\rho_i$ its row of the redirect table. Let $a$ be a
configuration of $M_i$, $t\in\mathbb{N}$ and $v$ a control of phase $i$. Suppose the run of
$M_i$ from $a$ is not in state $v$ at any time before $t$, and $\rho_i$ redirects no control
other than $v$. Then at every time $u<t$, the control of that run is not redirected by
$\rho_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Moving back onto the clock delimiter]
\lean{Turing.cw_seg_left}
\label{Turing.cw_seg_left}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.Segment, Turing.WindowExit, Turing.cw_Ctrl, Turing.cw_Idx, Turing.cw_box, Turing.cw_cfg, Turing.cw_cfg_box, Turing.cw_cfg_mapState, Turing.cw_cfg_moveL, Turing.cw_cfg_posL, Turing.cw_guard, Turing.cw_hostTM, Turing.cw_leftTM, Turing.cw_left_run, Turing.cw_next, Turing.cw_red, Turing.cw_seg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K,c,m\in\mathbb{N}$, let $e$ be a tape symbol, and let $R$ be a Turing machine with $K+2$
work tapes whose state set $P$ has decidable equality, together with an entry state
$p_{\mathrm{en}}\in P$ and a map $\mathrm{ex}$ from the three window exits (halted, left,
exhausted) to $P$. Let $H$ be the clock runner built from these data: the phase host on $K+2$
work tapes whose phases are the clock writer's phases for $c$ passes over $m$ record fields
(acting on the record tape $0$ and the clock tape $K+1$), the runner $R$, the clear of the
clock tape, and a stationary stop phase; the states of the stop phase are called exits. For a
configuration $d$ of $H$, a control $q$, integers $a,b$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let
$\omega(q,a,n,b)$ be the configuration obtained from $d$ by setting the state to $q$, moving
the head of tape $0$ by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ by $b$, and writing $n$ copies of $e$ on
tape $K+1$ starting at its head position in $d$; let $h_j$ denote the head position of tape $j$
in $d$. Say that $H$ goes from $A$ to $B$ in $t$ steps within radius $r$ if the run of $H$ from
$A$ reaches $B$ after exactly $t$ steps, is in no exit state at any time before $t$, and at
every time up to $t$ keeps every work-tape head within distance $r$ of its position in $d$. Let
$p<c$, $j<m$, $a,b,b'\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $b'=b-1$, $\abs{a}\le r$ and
$1\le b\le r$. Then $H$ goes from $\omega(q,a,n,b)$ to $\omega(\nu(p,j),a,n,b')$ in $2$ steps
within radius $r$, where $q$ is the left move of $(p,j)$ with control false and $\nu(p,j)$ is
the copy phase of field $j+1$ in pass $p$ with control sweep if $j+1<m$, and otherwise the skip
back over field $j$ in pass $p$ with control run.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Restating a segment's length]
\lean{Turing.cw_seg_time}
\label{Turing.cw_seg_time}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.Segment}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine, $F$ a set of states, $B$ a property of head vectors,
$A,A'$ configurations and $t,t'\in\mathbb{N}$ with $t=t'$. If the run of $M$ from $A$ reaches
$A'$ after exactly $t$ steps, avoids $F$ before time $t$ and satisfies $B$ at every time up to
$t$, then the same holds with $t'$ in place of $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A record field as a delimited word]
\lean{Turing.cw_field}
\label{Turing.cw_field}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}
Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $d$ be a configuration with $K$ work tapes, let $r$ be a work tape,
and let $f_0,\dots,f_{\ell-1}$ be words such that tape $r$ holds, from its head position $h$,
the fields $f_0,\dots,f_{\ell-1}$ separated by single blanks and delimited by blanks at offsets
$-1$ and just after the layout. Let $i<\ell$ and $o_i=\sum_{j<i}(|f_j|+1)$. Then for every
integer $-1\le z\le|f_i|$, the cell $h+o_i+z$ of tape $r$ holds the $z$-th letter of $f_i$, and
is blank at $z=-1$ and at $z=|f_i|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The clock writer's contract]
\lean{Turing.cw_writer}
\label{Turing.cw_writer}

$p_{\mathrm{en}}\in P$ and a map $\mathrm{ex}$ from the three window exits (halted, left,
exhausted) to $P$. Let $H$ be the clock runner built from these data: the phase host on $K+2$
work tapes whose phases are the clock writer's phases for $c$ passes over $m$ record fields
(acting on the record tape $0$ and the clock tape $K+1$), the runner $R$, the clear of the
clock tape, and a stationary stop phase; the states of the stop phase are called exits. For a

the head of tape $0$ by $a$ and the head of tape $K+1$ by $b$, and writing $n$ copies of $e$ on
tape $K+1$ starting at its head position in $d$; let $h_j$ denote the head position of tape $j$
in $d$. Say that $H$ goes from $A$ to $B$ in $t$ steps within radius $r$ if the run of $H$ from

every time up to $t$ keeps every work-tape head within distance $r$ of its position in $d$. Let

offset of field $j$, and let $F=\sum_{j<m}|f_j|$. Let $d$ be a configuration of $H$ in the copy

within radius $r$, where $q'$ is the runner phase at $p_{\mathrm{en}}$, and the output of $H$
at every time up to $t$ equals that of $d$.
\end{lemma}

\section{Time Hierarchy --- Diagonal}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TimeHierarchy.Diagonal
\subsection*{Time Hierarchy --- Diagonal: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.TimeHierarchy.Diagonal}.

\subsection*{Time Hierarchy --- Diagonal: Results}

\begin{definition}[Diagonal language time bound]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang_mem_DTIME}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang_mem_DTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLangOf_mem_DTIME, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagSim}
\difficulty{1}
Let $g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be time-constructible. The language of binary strings
$x$ for which the diagonal simulator does not halt with output $1$ after exactly
$g(|x|)$ steps is decidable by a Turing machine within time $c\bigl(g(n)+1\bigr)$ on
inputs of length $n$, for some constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Quadratic overhead bound]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diag_cost_le}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diag_cost_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For all natural numbers $n,T,c_0,c_1,C$, we have
\[
5n+7+C\bigl(c_1(c_0T+1)^2+1\bigr) \le \bigl(8+C(c_1(c_0+1)^2+1)\bigr)(T+n+1)^2.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Diagonal language outside a time class]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang_not_mem_DTIME}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang_not_mem_DTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.diagLang_not_mem_DTIME, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.sqDiagSimulator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $g,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy the condition that for every
$A,N\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an $n\ge N$ such that $A\bigl(T(n)+n+1\bigr)^2\le g(n)$.
Then the language of binary strings $x$ for which the diagonal simulator does not halt
with output $1$ after exactly $g(|x|)$ steps does not belong to $\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic time hierarchy]
\lean{Complexity.time_hierarchy}
\label{Complexity.time_hierarchy}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.time_hierarchy, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.le_sq_overhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.sqDiagSimulator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and suppose $g$ is time constructible. Suppose also
that for every $A\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n\ge
N$, $A(f(n)+n+1)^2\le g(n)$. Then $\mathrm{DTIME}(f)$ is a proper subset of
$\mathrm{DTIME}(n\mapsto g(n)+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Time hierarchy for positive bounds]
\lean{Complexity.time_hierarchy_of_pos}

\difficulty{1}

$N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n\ge N$, $A(f(n)+n+1)^2\le g(n)$. Then
$\mathrm{DTIME}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{DTIME}(g)$.

\subsection*{Time Hierarchy --- Diagonal: Further results}

\begin{definition}[Fixed effective machine coding]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.exists_effectiveMachineCode}
Fix an effective machine coding: an encoding of coded Boolean Turing machines by Boolean
words and a total decoding map such that every machine is recovered when its code is
followed by any number of padding bits equal to $1$. The coding also includes a finite
Boolean machine that computes the serialization of the machine decoded from any input
word, together with a time bound for that computation.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Universal Boolean Turing machine]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.univTM}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.univTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code, Turing.FinTM, Turing.universal}
For the fixed effective machine coding, choose a finite Boolean Turing machine $U$ that
simulates every decoded machine with the following guarantees. For each code word
$\alpha$, there is a constant $C$ such that every computation of the decoded machine on
input $x$ that produces output $y$ in time $t$ is simulated by $U$ on the paired
encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$, producing $y$ in time $C(t+1)$. Conversely, whenever $U$
on that paired input produces an output, the decoded machine on $x$ produces the same
output in some finite time.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Universal simulation of coded machines]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.univTM_spec}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.univTM_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.univTM, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.universal}
\difficulty{1}
For every bit string $\alpha$, there is a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every
bit string $x$, both of the following hold: if the machine decoded from $\alpha$
computes an output $y$ from $x$ within $t$ steps, then the universal machine computes
$y$ from the paired encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$ within $C(t+1)$ steps; and if the
universal machine computes some output $y$ from that paired encoding within some finite
number of steps, then the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes $y$ from $x$ within
some finite number of steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Diagonal simulation machine]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagSim}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagSim}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.preTM, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.univTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM}
A particular finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, obtained by buffering the
pre-universal machine with the universal machine.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Diagonal language]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagSim, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
For a function $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, define a language of finite binary
strings by declaring $x$ to belong to it exactly when the diagonal simulation machine
does not compute the one-bit output $1$ on input $x$ within $g(|x|)$ steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Diagonal language for a machine]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLangOf}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLangOf}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
Given a finite Turing machine $W$ over the Boolean alphabet and a function $g :
\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, define a language of finite binary strings by declaring $x$
to belong to it exactly when $W$ does not compute the one-bit output $1$ on input $x$
within $g(|x|)$ steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of diagonal languages]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang_eq_diagLangOf}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang_eq_diagLangOf}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLang, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLangOf, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagSim}

which the diagonal simulation machine does not halt within the specified time $g(|x|)$
with output equal to the one-bit string $1$ is equal to the language of bit strings $x$
for which the diagonal simulation does not halt within that time with that output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Diagonal language time bound]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLangOf_mem_DTIME}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLangOf_mem_DTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.clockTM, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.clockTM_spec, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.ctrVal_bits, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagLangOf, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.length_bits_le_self}

in time $c\bigl(g(n)+1\bigr)$ for some constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padded diagonal simulator]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
For a function $\Phi : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, a padded diagonal
simulator consists of a finite Turing machine $W$ over the Boolean alphabet with the
following property: for every time bound $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every
language $L \in \mathrm{DTIME}(T)$, there are natural numbers $A$ and $N_0$ such that,
for every $n \ge N_0$, some binary string $x$ of length $n$ is computed by $W$ with
output the indicator of whether $x \in L$, within $A\Phi(T(n),n)$ steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Monotonicity of diagonal simulation bounds]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.mono}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
Suppose a padded diagonal simulator works with bound function $\Phi$, and let $\Phi' :
\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $K \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $\Phi(t,n)
\le K\Phi'(t,n)$ for all natural numbers $t,n$. Then the same simulating machine is a
padded diagonal simulator with bound function $\Phi'$.
\end{definition}

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Self-simulation structure]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.SelfSimulator}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.SelfSimulator}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairEncode}
For a function $\Psi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, a self-simulation structure consists
of a finite Boolean Turing machine $W$ and a decoder assigning a finite Boolean Turing
machine to each binary string $\alpha$. For each code $\alpha$, there is a constant $C$
such that whenever the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes a one-bit output $b$ on
the paired input $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ within $t$ steps, $W$ computes the same output
on that input within $C(t+|\langle\alpha,w\rangle|+1)$ steps. Moreover, for every time
bound $T$ and every $L \in \mathrm{DTIME}(T)$, there are a code $\alpha$ and a constant
$c$ such that, on every input $x$, the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes the
indicator of membership in $L$ within $c(\Psi(T(|x|))+1)$ steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Diagonal simulator from self-simulation]

padded diagonal simulator with bound function $(t,n) \mapsto \Psi(t)+n+1$.
\end{definition}

A particular self-simulation structure is defined with overhead function $t \mapsto
(t+1)^2$. Its simulating machine is the diagonal simulation machine, and its decoder
maps a binary code to the corresponding coded Turing machine. For each code, it
simulates that machine's one-bit computations on paired inputs with a constant-factor
overhead in the computation time plus input length; it also represents every language in
$\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$ by a code whose decoded machine decides the language on every input
within $c(T(|x|)+1)^2$ steps for some constant $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic overhead dominates time]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.le_sq_overhead}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.le_sq_overhead}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For all natural numbers $t$ and $n$, $t \le (t+n+1)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Quadratic-Time Diagonal Simulator]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.sqDiagSimulator}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.sqDiagSimulator}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.mono, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.SelfSimulator.toDiagSimulator, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.oneTapeSelfSimulator}
There exists a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet that simulates every
language in $\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$ on inputs of length $n$ within a constant multiple of
$(T(n)+n+1)^2$ steps for all sufficiently large $n$: for every time bound $T$ and every
such language $L$, if $L\in\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$, then there are natural numbers $A$ and
$N_0$ such that for every $n\ge N_0$ some binary string $x$ of length $n$ is decided by
the machine in $A(T(n)+n+1)^2$ steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Diagonal simulator component identity]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.sqDiagSimulator_W}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.sqDiagSimulator_W}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.diagSim, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.sqDiagSimulator}
\difficulty{1}
The component $W$ of the square diagonal simulator is equal to the machine obtained by
composing the preliminary machine with the universal machine using buffered composition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Hennie--Stearns normal-form overhead]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead}
\leanok
For a natural number $t$, the normal-form overhead is
\[\Psi(t) = (t+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(t+1)\rfloor+1\bigr),\]
where $\lfloor\log_2\rfloor$ denotes the floor of the binary logarithm.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Formula for the normal-form overhead]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_eq}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $t$, the Hennie--Stearns normal-form overhead $\Psi(t)$ equals
$(t+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(t+1)\rfloor+1\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Diagonal overhead of order $f\log f$]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead}
\leanok
For natural numbers $t$ and $n$, the logarithmic diagonal overhead is
\[\Phi(t,n) = (t+n+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(t+n+1)\rfloor+1\bigr),\]
the $f\log f$ analogue of the quadratic overhead $(t+n+1)^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Formula for the logarithmic diagonal overhead]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead_eq}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $t$ and $n$, the logarithmic diagonal overhead $\Phi(t,n)$ equals
$(t+n+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(t+n+1)\rfloor+1\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic diagonal overhead dominates time]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.le_logDiagOverhead}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.le_logDiagOverhead}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead_eq}
\difficulty{3}
For all natural numbers $t$ and $n$,
$t \le (t+n+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(t+n+1)\rfloor+1\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Input padding at logarithmic overhead]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_add_le}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_add_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead_eq, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_eq}
\difficulty{4}
For all natural numbers $t$ and $n$,
\[(t+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(t+1)\rfloor+1\bigr) + n + 1 \;\le\;
2\,(t+n+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(t+n+1)\rfloor+1\bigr).\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Constant-factor absorption of the normal-form overhead]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_mul_le}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_mul_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_eq}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Psi(t) = (t+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(t+1)\rfloor+1\bigr)$. For all natural numbers $c_0$
and $T$,
\[\Psi(c_0T) \le (c_0+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(c_0+1)\rfloor+2\bigr)\,\Psi(T).\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic diagonal overhead versus $f\log f$]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead_le_book}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead_le_book}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $2 \le n \le f$. Then
\[(f+n+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(f+n+1)\rfloor+1\bigr) \le 12\, f\,\lfloor\log_2 f\rfloor.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[From $f\log f = o(g)$ to the diagonal bound]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.eventually_logDiagOverhead_le}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.eventually_logDiagOverhead_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead_le_book}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $n \le f(n)$ for every $n$, and suppose that for
every natural number $A$ there is $N$ with $A\,f(n)\lfloor\log_2 f(n)\rfloor \le g(n)$ for all
$n \ge N$ (with $\lfloor\log_2 0\rfloor = 0$). Then for every natural number $A$ there is $N$
such that $A\,(f(n)+n+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(f(n)+n+1)\rfloor+1\bigr) \le g(n)$ for all
$n \ge N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Fixed two-work-tape representation scheme]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code₂}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code₂}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.EffectiveMachineCode2, Turing.exists_effectiveMachineCode2}
A fixed, arbitrarily chosen effective representation scheme for Turing machines with two
work tapes over the binary alphabet: an encoding of such machines by binary strings
together with a decoding map, such that decoding an encoded machine returns it and the
serialization of the decoded machine is computable by a Turing machine.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Choice of the two-work-tape scheme]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code₂_eq}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code₂_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code₂, Turing.exists_effectiveMachineCode2}
\difficulty{1}
The fixed two-work-tape representation scheme is, by definition, the scheme selected by
the axiom of choice from the nonempty collection of effective representation schemes for
binary Turing machines with two work tapes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Two-tape self-simulation structure]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.SelfSimulator, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code₂, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_eq, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_mul_le, Turing.Code2TM.toFinTM, Turing.EffectiveCodeK.toFinTM, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode2.toK, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode2.toK_toFinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.two_work_tapes_binary, Turing.MachineCode2.decode_encode, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.exists_code2TM, Turing.exists_selfUniversalK, Turing.pairEncode}
A self-simulation structure with overhead function
$\Psi(t) = (t+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(t+1)\rfloor+1\bigr)$. Its simulating machine $W$ is a
self-application universal machine for the fixed two-work-tape representation scheme, and
its decoder sends a binary code $\alpha$ to the two-work-tape machine that the scheme decodes
from $\alpha$. Thus, for each code $\alpha$ there is a constant $C$ such that whenever the
decoded machine outputs a single bit $b$ on the paired input $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ within
$t$ steps, $W$ outputs $b$ on that input within $C(t+|\langle\alpha,w\rangle|+1)$ steps; and
for every time bound $T$ and every $L\in\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$ there are a code $\alpha$ and a
constant $c$ such that the decoded machine computes the indicator of $x\in L$ within
$c\bigl(\Psi(T(|x|))+1\bigr)$ steps on every input $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Machine of the two-tape self-simulator]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator_W}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator_W}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code₂, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode2.toK, Turing.exists_selfUniversalK}
\difficulty{1}
The simulating machine of the two-tape self-simulation structure is the chosen
self-application universal machine $U$ for the fixed two-work-tape representation scheme,
viewed as a scheme for machines with $k=2$ work tapes: for every code $\alpha$ there is a
constant $C>0$ such that, for every $w$, whenever the machine coded by $\alpha$ halts on
$\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ with some output within $t$ steps, $U$ halts on
$\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ with the same output within $C(t+1)$ steps using at most $C(s+1)$
cells, where $s$ is the space used by the coded machine by time $t$; and every output of $U$
on $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ is an output of the coded machine on that input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Decoder of the two-tape self-simulator]
\lean{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator_decode}
\label{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator_decode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code₂, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator, Turing.Code2TM.toFinTM}
\difficulty{1}
For every binary string $\alpha$, the machine that the two-tape self-simulation structure
assigns to $\alpha$ is the two-work-tape machine decoded from $\alpha$ by the fixed
two-work-tape representation scheme, regarded as a finite Turing machine.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Time hierarchy at overhead $f\log f$]
\lean{Complexity.time_hierarchy_log}
\label{Complexity.time_hierarchy_log}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.mono, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.time_hierarchy, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.SelfSimulator.toDiagSimulator, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.le_logDiagOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logDiagOverhead_eq, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_add_le, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $g$ time-constructible, and suppose that for every
natural number $A$ there is $N$ such that
\[A\,(f(n)+n+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(f(n)+n+1)\rfloor+1\bigr) \le g(n)\quad\text{for all } n\ge N.\]
Then $\mathrm{DTIME}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{DTIME}(g+1)$, where $g+1$ denotes
$n\mapsto g(n)+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Time Hierarchy Theorem]
\lean{Complexity.time_hierarchy_book}
\label{Complexity.time_hierarchy_book}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.mono, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.time_hierarchy, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.SelfSimulator.toDiagSimulator, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.eventually_logDiagOverhead_le, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.le_logDiagOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_add_le, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $g$ time-constructible and $n\le f(n)$ for every $n$.
Suppose $f(n)\log f(n) = o(g(n))$ in the sense that for every natural number $A$ there is $N$
with $A\,f(n)\lfloor\log_2 f(n)\rfloor\le g(n)$ for all $n\ge N$ (with
$\lfloor\log_2 0\rfloor = 0$). Then $\mathrm{DTIME}(f)$ is a proper subset of
$\mathrm{DTIME}(g+1)$, where $g+1$ denotes $n\mapsto g(n)+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Time Hierarchy Theorem for a positive bound]
\lean{Complexity.time_hierarchy_book_of_pos}
\label{Complexity.time_hierarchy_book_of_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.mono, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.DiagSimulator.time_hierarchy_of_pos, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.SelfSimulator.toDiagSimulator, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.eventually_logDiagOverhead_le, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.le_logDiagOverhead, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.logOverhead_add_le, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.twoTapeSelfSimulator}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $g$ time-constructible, $g(n)>0$ for every $n$, and
$n\le f(n)$ for every $n$. Suppose that for every natural number $A$ there is $N$ with
$A\,f(n)\lfloor\log_2 f(n)\rfloor\le g(n)$ for all $n\ge N$ (with $\lfloor\log_2 0\rfloor = 0$).
Then $\mathrm{DTIME}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{DTIME}(g)$.
\end{theorem}

\chapter{Chapter02 — Correlated Gaussian Limit}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter02.NoiseStability.CorrelatedGaussianLimit
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter02.NoiseStability.CorrelatedGaussianLimit}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Correlation plane]
\lean{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003}
\label{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
\leanok
The correlation plane is $\mathbb R^2$ equipped with its usual Euclidean norm.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Correlated sign vector]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignVector}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b005
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p007-b003}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignVector}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
Given a pair of signs, form the vector in the correlation plane whose two coordinates
are the real values of those signs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Correlated sign projection]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
For $t=(t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and signs $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^{\times}$, the correlated sign projection
of $t$ at $(x,y)$ is $xt_1+yt_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling the sign projection]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_smul}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedSignProjection}
\difficulty{3}
For every real scalar $a$, vector $t$ in the real two-dimensional correlation plane, and
pair of signs $(x,y)$, the projection at $a t$ is $a$ times the projection at $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign projection as an inner product]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_eq_inner}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_eq_inner}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedSignProjection, FABL.correlatedSignVector}
\difficulty{3}
For every vector $t$ in the real two-dimensional correlation plane and every pair of
signs $(x,y)$, the projection $x t_1+y t_2$ equals the inner product of $t$ with the
vector $(x,y)$, where signs are viewed as real numbers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Correlation quadratic form]
\lean{FABL.correlationQuadraticForm}
\label{FABL.correlationQuadraticForm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
For a real number $\rho$ and a point $t=(t_1,t_2)$ in the real correlation plane, the
correlation quadratic form is $t_1^2+2\rho t_1t_2+t_2^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of the correlated sign projection]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_expectation}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_expectation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF_expect_signValue_fst, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF_expect_signValue_snd, FABL.correlatedSignProjection, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_mul_const}
\difficulty{3}
For every $\rho\in[-1,1]$ and every vector $t=(t_1,t_2)$ in the real two-dimensional
correlation plane, the expected value of $X t_1+Y t_2$ under the correlated sign-pair
law with parameter $\rho$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment of the correlated sign projection]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_secondMoment}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignProjection_secondMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF_expect_signValue_mul, FABL.correlatedSignProjection, FABL.correlationQuadraticForm, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one}
\difficulty{5}
For every $\rho\in[-1,1]$ and every vector $t=(t_1,t_2)$ in the real two-dimensional
correlation plane, the expected square of $X t_1+Y t_2$ under the correlated sign-pair
law with parameter $\rho$ is $t_1^2+2\rho t_1t_2+t_2^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Correlated sign vector measure]
\lean{FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p214-b005
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p007-b003}
\label{FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignVector}
For a real parameter $\rho\in[-1,1]$, the correlated sign vector measure is the
probability distribution on the correlation plane obtained by mapping a sign pair drawn
according to the correlated sign-pair law with parameter $\rho$ to the vector of its two
real sign values.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling a correlated sign-vector characteristic function]
\lean{FABL.charFun_correlatedSignVectorMeasure_smul}
\label{FABL.charFun_correlatedSignVectorMeasure_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.correlatedSignProjection, FABL.correlatedSignProjection_eq_inner, FABL.correlatedSignProjection_smul, FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $a\in\mathbb R$, and let $t=(t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb R^2$. The
characteristic function of the correlated sign-vector measure at $at$ equals the
characteristic function at $a$ of the real projection $s_1t_1+s_2t_2$ under the
correlated sign-pair distribution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characteristic Function Expansion at Zero]
\lean{FABL.taylor_charFun_two_of_secondMoment}
\label{FABL.taylor_charFun_two_of_secondMoment}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space, measurable up to a null set,
with finite second moment, mean zero, and second moment $q$. Then, as $t\to0$, its
characteristic function satisfies $\mathbb{E}[e^{itX}]=1-qt^2/2+o(t^2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characteristic Function Limit from the Second Moment]
\lean{FABL.tendsto_charFun_inv_sqrt_mul_pow_of_secondMoment}
\label{FABL.tendsto_charFun_inv_sqrt_mul_pow_of_secondMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.taylor_charFun_two_of_secondMoment}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space, measurable up to a null set,
with finite second moment, mean zero, and second moment $q$. If $\varphi$ is its
characteristic function, then $\varphi(1/\sqrt{n})^n\to\exp(-q/2)$ as the positive
integer $n$ tends to infinity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Normalized correlated sign sum]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003
}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure}
For $\rho\in[-1,1]$ and a natural number $n$, take $n$ independent vectors, each with
the correlated sign vector distribution at parameter $\rho$, sum them, and scale the
result by $1/\sqrt n$. The resulting probability distribution on the correlation plane
is the normalized correlated sign sum measure.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characteristic function of a normalized correlated sum]
\lean{FABL.charFun_normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\label{FABL.charFun_normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedSignVectorMeasure, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $t\in\mathbb R^2$. The
characteristic function of the measure of the normalized sum of $n$ independent
correlated sign vectors, with normalization $1/\sqrt n$, at $t$ equals $\displaystyle
\left(\varphi\left(t/\sqrt n\right)\right)^n$, where $\varphi$ is the characteristic
function of one correlated sign-vector measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian correlation map]
\lean{FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b004
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002}
\label{FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
For each real number $\rho$, define a map from $\mathbb R^2$ to the correlation plane by
sending $(u,v)$ to $(u,\rho u+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,v)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Continuity of the Gaussian correlation map]
\lean{FABL.continuous_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\label{FABL.continuous_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
\difficulty{1}
For each real number $\rho$, define a map on the real plane equipped with the $2$-norm
by $(u,v)\mapsto (u,\rho u+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,v)$. This map is continuous.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Correlated Gaussian measure]
\lean{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b003,

\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002}
\label{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.continuous_gaussianCorrelationMap, FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
For a real parameter $\rho$, let $\gamma$ be the probability measure on $\mathbb R^2$
obtained as the pushforward of the product of two independent standard Gaussian measures
under the Gaussian correlation map with parameter $\rho$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Inner product of Gaussian correlation images]
\lean{FABL.inner_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\label{FABL.inner_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $\rho$, every pair $(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, and every vector $t$ in
the real correlation plane, the inner product of the Gaussian correlation image of
$(u,v)$ with $t$ is $u$ times the sum of the first coordinate of $t$ and $\rho$ times
its second coordinate, plus $v$ times $\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$ times the second coordinate of
$t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characteristic function of a correlated Gaussian]
\lean{FABL.charFun_correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\label{FABL.charFun_correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.continuous_gaussianCorrelationMap, FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure, FABL.correlationQuadraticForm, FABL.gaussianCorrelationMap, FABL.inner_gaussianCorrelationMap}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $t=(t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb R^2$. The characteristic function of
the correlated Gaussian probability measure with correlation parameter $\rho$, evaluated
at $t$, is $\displaystyle \exp\!\left(-\frac{t_1^2+2\rho t_1t_2+t_2^2}{2}\right)$.
\end{theorem}

bivariate Gaussian law with unit marginal variances and correlation $\rho$.

\begin{definition}[Pairwise coordinate correspondence]
\lean{FABL.pairCoordinatesEquiv}
\label{FABL.pairCoordinatesEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
For each nonnegative integer $n$, pairs of sign vectors of length $n$ are in bijection
with functions assigning a pair of signs to each of the $n$ coordinates. The
correspondence pairs the two signs at each coordinate, and its inverse recovers the two
sign vectors from those coordinatewise pairs.
\end{definition}

\lean{FABL.correlatedPairPMF_map_pairCoordinatesEquiv}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $\rho\in[-1,1]$. For a correlated pair $(X,Y)$ of sign vectors
in $\{\pm1\}^n$, formed by choosing $X$ uniformly and applying independent coordinate
noise with retention probability $(1+\rho)/2$, rearrange the pair as
$((X_i,Y_i))_{i=1}^n$. Its law is the product of $n$ copies of the law of a single sign
pair formed by choosing the first sign uniformly from $\{\pm1\}$ and applying the same
noise rule to obtain the second.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Measure of an independent product distribution]
\lean{FABL.independentProductPMF_toMeasure}

I$, with every singleton measurable. For a probability mass function $p_i$ on each
$A_i$, the measure associated with their independent product distribution equals the
product measure of the associated coordinate measures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Normalized correlated sign-vector sum]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignVectorSum}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{

For $n\in\mathbb N$ and a sequence $z$ of length $n$ whose entries are pairs of signs,
take the sum of the correlated sign vectors associated with its entries and multiply by
$1/\sqrt n$. The result lies in the two-dimensional Euclidean plane.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Normalized sum of correlated sign vectors]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b001,

}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum}
\leanok

For $n\in\mathbb N$ and a pair $(x,y)$ of sign vectors in $\{-1,1\}^n$, define their
normalized correlated pair sum to be the normalized sum of correlated sign vectors
obtained by reindexing the coordinates of $(x,y)$ into paired coordinates. The result
lies in the two-dimensional Euclidean plane.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of normalized sum distributions]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedSignSumMeasure_eq_map_correlatedPairPMF}

\difficulty{3}
Let $-1\leq \rho\leq 1$ and let $n$ be a natural number. The probability measure

point in the plane, summing those points, and dividing by $\sqrt n$ equals the
distribution of the normalized pair sum when the first sign vector is uniform and each

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Field pairing coefficient]
\lean{FABL.fieldPairingCoefficient}
\label{FABL.fieldPairingCoefficient}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryExtensionField, FABL.F₂Cube}
Let $\gamma$ be a binary vector of length $d$, and let $a$ assign an element of the binary
extension field of degree $\ell$ to each index in $\mathrm{Fin}(d)$. Define their field pairing
coefficient to be the sum over all indices $i$ of the scalar multiple of $a_i$ by the
binary coefficient $\gamma_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Field pairing generator]
\lean{FABL.fieldPairingGenerator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p153-b003}
\label{FABL.fieldPairingGenerator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryExtensionField, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryExtensionEncode, FABL.f₂DotProduct}
Let $d,\ell$ be natural numbers with $\ell\ne0$, let $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}$ be elements of
the binary extension field of degree $\ell$, and let $s$ be another element of that
field. Define a binary vector of length $d$ whose $i$-th coordinate is the binary dot
product of the binary encodings of $a_i$ and $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Pairing through a binary extension field]
\lean{FABL.f₂DotProduct_fieldPairingGenerator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BinaryExtensionField, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryExtensionEncode, FABL.fieldPairingCoefficient, FABL.fieldPairingGenerator, FABL.f₂DotProduct}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\ell$ be a nonzero integer, and let $d$ be a nonnegative integer. Use a basis of
the degree-$\ell$ binary extension field to encode its elements as binary vectors of
length $\ell$. For $\gamma\in\bbr_2^d$, a family $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}$ in that field, and
an element $s$ of the field, the dot product of $\gamma$ with the vector whose $i$th
coordinate pairs the encodings of $a_i$ and $s$ equals the dot product of the encodings
of $\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}\gamma_i a_i$ and $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Walsh characters and field pairings]
\lean{FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_fieldPairingGenerator}
\label{FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_fieldPairingGenerator}
