Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Parse

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# A configuration codec for nondeterministic machines

Configuration-graph algorithms in small space — Savitch's midpoint recursion, the `PATH`
reduction, the inductive counting of Immerman and Szelepcsényi [AB09, §4.1.1, §4.2, §4.3]
— store configurations of a fixed machine `N` on the real input `x` as numbers in
registers. This file fixes that representation: the **code** of a configuration whose work
heads and nonblank work cells lie in the window `[-s, s]` is a word of `O(s + log |x|)` bits,
read as a little-endian number.

## Layout

The code word `Complexity.Codec.cfgWord N s C` is

* `2s + 1` **chunks**, one per work-tape cell `z ∈ [-s, s]` in increasing order, each of the
  fixed width `Complexity.Codec.W N`: a one-hot *header slot* (nonzero only in the leftmost
  chunk, where it names the control state and the output summary), then three bits per work
  tape (`nonblank`, `symbol`, `head here`), then a constant `1`;
* the input head position in binary, little-endian, padded to the fixed width
  `|bits (|x| + 1)|`;
* a final `1`, so that the word is the binary word of its value.

Fixed widths make field extraction position arithmetic, and the cell-major order makes one
machine step a *local* relation between neighbouring chunks (the checks of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec.Checks`). The code records exactly the
configuration-graph vertex `Turing.NDTM.coreSum` (state, input position, windowed work tapes,
work heads, output summary), so it is injective on window-bounded configurations up to that
vertex, and that is all the graph algorithms need.

This codec is configuration-graph infrastructure, not a result of [AB09]; its conventions
(the window `Turing.Cfg.InWindow` of radius `s`, the output summary) are those of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.Codec.CellV`, `Complexity.Codec.encChunk` — cell values and their chunks.
* `Complexity.Codec.cfgWord`, `Complexity.Codec.cfgCode` — the code word and the code.
* `Complexity.Codec.decodeCfg` — the decoder.

## Main results

* `Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode` — the binary word of the code is the code word.
* `Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_congr` — the code depends only on the vertex `coreSum`.
* `Complexity.Codec.coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq` — on window-bounded configurations the code
  determines the vertex.
* `Complexity.Codec.length_cfgWord`, `Complexity.Codec.cfgCode_lt` — the code has at most
  `codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1)` bits.
* `Complexity.Codec.decodeCfg_cfgCode` — decoding a code recovers the vertex.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1: configurations and configuration graphs.)
-/

namespace Complexity.Codec

open Turing LogProg

variable (N : FinNDTM Bool)

/-! ## Words -/

/-- The index of an output summary. -/
def sumIdx : OutSummary → Fin 3
  | .empty => 0
  | .accept => 1
  | .dead => 2

/-- Distinct summaries have distinct indices. -/
lemma sumIdx_injective : Function.Injective sumIdx := by
  intro a b h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [sumIdx]

/-- The header datum of a configuration: its control state and output-summary index. -/
abbrev Hd := Option N.State × Fin 3

/-- A cell value: the header (present only in the leftmost cell) and, per work tape, the
symbol in the cell and whether the head is on it. -/
abbrev CellV := Option (Hd N) × (Fin N.k → Option Bool × Bool)

set_option synthInstance.maxSize 1000 in
/-- Cell values have decidable equality. -/
instance CellV.instDecidableEq : DecidableEq (CellV N) := inferInstance

/-- The width of the header slot: the number of header data. -/
def hH : ℕ := Fintype.card (Hd N)

/-- The width of a chunk: header slot, three bits per work tape, a final `1`. -/
def W : ℕ := hH N + 3 * N.k + 1

/-- The chunk width: the header slot, three bits per work tape, and the closing `1`. -/
lemma W_eq : W N = hH N + 3 * N.k + 1 := rfl

/-- The position of a header datum in the one-hot header slot. -/
noncomputable def hdNum (h : Hd N) : ℕ := (Fintype.equivFin (Hd N) h).val

/-- Header positions lie in the slot. -/
lemma hdNum_lt (h : Hd N) : hdNum N h < hH N := (Fintype.equivFin (Hd N) h).isLt

/-- Distinct header data have distinct positions. -/
lemma hdNum_injective : Function.Injective (hdNum N) := by
  intro a b h
  exact (Fintype.equivFin (Hd N)).injective (Fin.ext h)

/-- Bit `t` of the chunk of a cell value: the one-hot header slot, then per tape `nonblank`,
`symbol`, `head here`, then `1`. -/
noncomputable def chunkBit (cv : CellV N) (t : ℕ) : Bool :=
  if t < hH N then decide (cv.1.map (hdNum N) = some t)
  else if h : (t - hH N) / 3 < N.k then
    if (t - hH N) % 3 = 0 then (cv.2 ⟨(t - hH N) / 3, h⟩).1.isSome
    else if (t - hH N) % 3 = 1 then (cv.2 ⟨(t - hH N) / 3, h⟩).1.getD false
    else (cv.2 ⟨(t - hH N) / 3, h⟩).2
  else true

/-- The chunk of a cell value. -/
noncomputable def encChunk (cv : CellV N) : List Bool :=
  List.ofFn fun t : Fin (W N) => chunkBit N cv t

/-- Chunks have the fixed width `W N`. -/
@[simp] lemma length_encChunk (cv : CellV N) : (encChunk N cv).length = W N := by
  simp only [encChunk, List.length_ofFn]

/-- Bits of a chunk below its width are `chunkBit`. -/
lemma getD_encChunk (cv : CellV N) (t : ℕ) (ht : t < W N) :
    (encChunk N cv).getD t false = chunkBit N cv t := by
  simp only [encChunk, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_ofFn, ht, dite_true,
    Option.getD_some]

/-- The header-slot bits of a chunk. -/
lemma chunkBit_slot (cv : CellV N) (t : ℕ) (ht : t < hH N) :
    chunkBit N cv t = decide (cv.1.map (hdNum N) = some t) := by
  simp [chunkBit, ht]

/-- The three bits of tape `i` in a chunk. -/
lemma chunkBit_tape (cv : CellV N) (i : Fin N.k) (r : ℕ) (hr : r < 3) :
    chunkBit N cv (hH N + 3 * i + r) =
      if r = 0 then (cv.2 i).1.isSome else if r = 1 then (cv.2 i).1.getD false
      else (cv.2 i).2 := by
  have e1 : (hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) / 3 = i := by omega
  have e2 : (hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) % 3 = r := by omega
  have hi : (hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) / 3 < N.k := by rw [e1]; exact i.isLt
  simp only [chunkBit, show ¬ hH N + 3 * i + r < hH N by omega, ↓reduceIte, dif_pos hi, e2]
  have : (⟨(hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) / 3, hi⟩ : Fin N.k) = i := Fin.ext e1
  rw [this]

/-- **Chunks are injective**: a cell value is determined by its chunk.

**Proof sketch.** Compare the chunks bit by bit (`getD_encChunk`): the one-hot header slot
determines the header (positions are injective, `hdNum_injective`), and the three bits of each
tape determine the optional symbol and the head flag (`chunkBit_tape`). -/
theorem encChunk_injective : Function.Injective (encChunk N) := by
  intro a b h
  have hb : ∀ t < W N, chunkBit N a t = chunkBit N b t := by
    intro t ht
    rw [← getD_encChunk N a t ht, ← getD_encChunk N b t ht, h]
  obtain ⟨a1, a2⟩ := a
  obtain ⟨b1, b2⟩ := b
  have slot : a1 = b1 := by
    have key : ∀ (u v : Option (Hd N)), (∀ t < hH N, decide (u.map (hdNum N) = some t) =
        decide (v.map (hdNum N) = some t)) → ∀ h, u = some h → v = some h := by
      intro u v hu h hh
      have := hu (hdNum N h) (hdNum_lt N h)
      subst hh
      simp only [Option.map_some, decide_true] at this
      cases v with
      | none => simp at this
      | some g =>
        simp at this
        rw [hdNum_injective N this]
    have hs : ∀ t < hH N, decide (a1.map (hdNum N) = some t) =
        decide (b1.map (hdNum N) = some t) := by
      intro t ht
      have := hb t (by simp only [W]; omega)
      rwa [chunkBit_slot N _ t ht, chunkBit_slot N _ t ht] at this
    cases a1 with
    | some hd => exact (key _ _ hs hd rfl).symm
    | none =>
      cases b1 with
      | none => rfl
      | some g => exact absurd (key _ _ (fun t ht => (hs t ht).symm) g rfl) (by simp)
  subst slot
  congr 1
  funext i
  have bit (r : ℕ) (hr : r < 3) := hb (hH N + 3 * i + r) (by simp only [W]; omega)
  have e0 := bit 0 (by omega)
  have e1 := bit 1 (by omega)
  have e2 := bit 2 (by omega)
  simp only [chunkBit_tape N _ i _ (by omega : (0 : ℕ) < 3),
    chunkBit_tape N _ i _ (by omega : (1 : ℕ) < 3),
    chunkBit_tape N _ i _ (by omega : (2 : ℕ) < 3)] at e0 e1 e2
  simp only [↓reduceIte, one_ne_zero, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, OfNat.ofNat_ne_one] at e0 e1 e2
  revert e0 e1 e2
  obtain ⟨o, hh⟩ := a2 i
  obtain ⟨o', hh'⟩ := b2 i
  intro e0 e1 e2
  simp only at e0 e1 e2
  subst e2
  congr 1
  cases o <;> cases o' <;> simp_all

/-- Concatenated fixed-width blocks: block `j` is recovered by dropping `W · j` letters and
taking `W`. -/
lemma take_drop_flatten {α : Type} (L : List (List α)) (w : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ b ∈ L, b.length = w) (j : ℕ) (hj : j < L.length) :
    ((L.flatten).drop (w * j)).take w = L[j] := by
  induction L generalizing j with
  | nil => simp at hj
  | cons b L ih =>
    have hb := hL b (by simp)
    cases j with
    | zero => simp [← hb]
    | succ j =>
      simp only [List.flatten_cons, List.getElem_cons_succ]
      rw [show w * (j + 1) = b.length + w * j by rw [hb]; ring, ← List.drop_drop,
        List.drop_left]
      exact ih (fun c hc => hL c (by simp [hc])) j (by simpa using hj)

/-- Concatenated blocks of width `w` have length `w` times their number. -/
lemma length_flatten_const {α : Type} (L : List (List α)) (w : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ b ∈ L, b.length = w) : (L.flatten).length = w * L.length := by
  induction L with
  | nil => simp
  | cons b L ih =>
    simp only [List.flatten_cons, List.length_append, List.length_cons,
      hL b (by simp), ih (fun c hc => hL c (by simp [hc]))]
    ring

/-- The word of `m` chunks with cell values `f 0, …, f (m - 1)`. -/
noncomputable def chunksWord (f : ℕ → CellV N) (m : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (f j)).flatten

/-- A chunk word has `W N` letters per chunk. -/
lemma length_chunksWord (f : ℕ → CellV N) (m : ℕ) :
    (chunksWord N f m).length = W N * m := by
  rw [chunksWord, length_flatten_const _ (W N) (by simp)]
  simp

/-- Equal chunk words have equal cell values. -/
lemma chunksWord_inj {f g : ℕ → CellV N} {m : ℕ} (h : chunksWord N f m = chunksWord N g m)
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j < m) : f j = g j := by
  have e1 := take_drop_flatten (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (f j)) (W N)
    (by simp) j (by simpa using hj)
  have e2 := take_drop_flatten (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (g j)) (W N)
    (by simp) j (by simpa using hj)
  have e : (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (f j))[j]'(by simpa using hj) =
      (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (g j))[j]'(by simpa using hj) := by
    rw [← e1, ← e2]
    exact congrArg (fun w => (w.drop (W N * j)).take (W N)) h
  simp only [List.getElem_ofFn] at e
  exact encChunk_injective N e

/-! ## The code of a configuration -/

variable {N} {x : List Bool}

/-- The cell value of cell `j` (work position `j - s`) of a configuration: the header in the
leftmost cell, then per tape the symbol at `j - s` and whether the head is there. -/
def cellOf (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) (j : ℕ) : CellV N :=
  (if j = 0 then some (C.state, sumIdx (outSummary C.output)) else none,
    fun i => (C.workTapes i ((j : ℤ) - s), decide (C.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s)))

/-- The head flag of tape `i` in cell `j`: whether the head of tape `i` is at work position
`j - s`. -/
lemma cellOf_head (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) (j : ℕ) (i : Fin N.k) :
    ((cellOf s C j).2 i).2 = decide (C.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s) := rfl

/-- The width of the input-position field on inputs of length `n`: `|bits (n + 1)|`. -/
def wP (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length

/-- The position-field width is the binary length of `n + 1`. -/
lemma wP_eq (n : ℕ) : wP n = (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length := rfl

/-- The binary word of `v` padded with `0`s to width `w`. -/
def padBits (w v : ℕ) : List Bool := Nat.bits v ++ List.replicate (w - (Nat.bits v).length) false

/-- **The code word** of a configuration at window radius `s`: the `2s + 1` cell chunks, the
padded input position, and a final `1`. -/
noncomputable def cfgWord (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : List Bool :=
  chunksWord N (cellOf s C) (2 * s + 1) ++ padBits (wP x.length) C.inputPos.val ++ [true]

/-- **The code** of a configuration at window radius `s`: the value of its code word. -/
noncomputable def cfgCode (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : ℕ := bitsVal (cfgWord s C)

/-- The value of a word does not see trailing `0`s. -/
lemma bitsVal_append_replicate (w : List Bool) (z : ℕ) :
    bitsVal (w ++ List.replicate z false) = bitsVal w := by
  induction w with
  | nil =>
    induction z with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ z ih => simp [List.replicate_succ, bitsVal] at ih ⊢; exact ih
  | cons b w ih => simp [bitsVal, ih]

/-- Every word is the binary word of its value followed by `0`s.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the word: a leading letter `b` contributes `b + 2 v`; the
binary word of that value is `b` followed by that of `v`, unless both vanish, when the word
is all `0`s. -/
lemma eq_bits_append_replicate (w : List Bool) :
    w = Nat.bits (bitsVal w) ++
      List.replicate (w.length - (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length) false := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [bitsVal, Nat.zero_bits]
  | cons b w ih =>
    have hl : (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length ≤ w.length := by
      have := congrArg List.length ih
      simp only [List.length_append, List.length_replicate] at this
      omega
    simp only [bitsVal, List.length_cons]
    rw [show b.toNat + 2 * bitsVal w = 2 * bitsVal w + b.toNat by ring]
    by_cases hz : bitsVal w = 0 ∧ b = false
    · obtain ⟨h0, rfl⟩ := hz
      rw [h0] at ih ⊢
      simp only [Nat.zero_bits, List.length_nil, Nat.sub_zero, List.nil_append] at ih ⊢
      simp only [Bool.toNat_false, Nat.mul_zero, Nat.add_zero, Nat.zero_bits, List.length_nil,
        Nat.sub_zero, List.nil_append, List.replicate_succ]
      rw [← ih]
    · rw [bits_two_mul_add _ _ (fun h0 => by
          cases b
          · exact absurd ⟨h0, rfl⟩ hz
          · rfl)]
      simp only [List.length_cons, List.cons_append, List.cons.injEq, true_and]
      rw [show w.length + 1 - ((Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length + 1) =
        w.length - (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length by omega]
      exact ih

/-- A padded word has the padding width when the value fits. -/
lemma length_padBits {w v : ℕ} (h : (Nat.bits v).length ≤ w) : (padBits w v).length = w := by
  simp [padBits]; omega

/-- The value of a padded word. -/
@[simp] lemma bitsVal_padBits (w v : ℕ) : bitsVal (padBits w v) = v := by
  rw [padBits, bitsVal_append_replicate, bitsVal_bits]

/-- A word of length `w` is the padding of its value to width `w`. -/
lemma eq_padBits (p : List Bool) : p = padBits p.length (bitsVal p) := by
  conv_lhs => rw [eq_bits_append_replicate p]
  rfl

/-- Input positions fit their field. -/
lemma length_bits_pos_le (v n : ℕ) (hv : v ≤ n + 1) : (Nat.bits v).length ≤ wP n :=
  length_bits_mono hv

/-- The number of letters of the code word. -/
lemma length_cfgWord (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    (cfgWord s C).length = W N * (2 * s + 1) + wP x.length + 1 := by
  have := C.inputPos.isLt
  simp only [cfgWord, List.length_append, length_chunksWord, List.length_singleton]
  rw [length_padBits (length_bits_pos_le _ _ (by omega))]

/-- The code word ends with `1`, so it is the binary word of its value. -/
lemma canon_cfgWord (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : Canon (cfgWord s C) := by
  intro h
  simp [cfgWord]

/-- **The binary word of the code is the code word.** -/
theorem bits_cfgCode (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    Nat.bits (cfgCode s C) = cfgWord s C :=
  (canon_eq_bits _ (canon_cfgWord s C)).symm

/-- The cell values depend only on the configuration-graph vertex. -/
lemma cellOf_congr {s : ℕ} {C D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x} (h : NDTM.coreSum C = NDTM.coreSum D) :
    cellOf s C = cellOf s D := by
  simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨hs, -, hw, hp⟩, ho⟩ := h
  funext j
  simp only [cellOf, hs, hw, hp, ho]

/-- **The code depends only on the configuration-graph vertex** `coreSum`. -/
theorem cfgWord_congr {s : ℕ} {C D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x}
    (h : NDTM.coreSum C = NDTM.coreSum D) : cfgWord s C = cfgWord s D := by
  have hi : C.inputPos = D.inputPos := by
    simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
    exact h.1.2.1
  simp only [cfgWord, cellOf_congr h, hi]

/-- **On window-bounded configurations the code determines the vertex**: equal code words
give equal `coreSum`.

**Proof sketch.** The two words have the same length, so their chunk prefixes, position
fields and final letters align. Equal chunks give equal cell values (`chunksWord_inj`):
the leftmost cell yields the state and the summary (`sumIdx` is injective, and summaries
determine the vertex component), every cell yields the tape symbols and head flags at its
position, and outside `[-s, s]` both tapes are blank and no head lies there (window
hypotheses). Equal position fields have equal values (`bitsVal_padBits`). -/
theorem coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq {s : ℕ} {C D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x}
    (hC : Cfg.InWindow s C) (hD : Cfg.InWindow s D) (h : cfgWord s C = cfgWord s D) :
    NDTM.coreSum C = NDTM.coreSum D := by
  have hlen : (chunksWord N (cellOf s C) (2 * s + 1)).length =
      (chunksWord N (cellOf s D) (2 * s + 1)).length := by simp [length_chunksWord]
  simp only [cfgWord, List.append_assoc] at h
  obtain ⟨hc, hrest⟩ := List.append_inj h hlen
  have hpos := congrArg bitsVal (List.append_inj_left' hrest rfl)
  simp only [bitsVal_padBits] at hpos
  have cell := chunksWord_inj N hc
  have c0 := cell 0 (by omega)
  simp only [cellOf, ↓reduceIte, Prod.mk.injEq, Option.some.injEq] at c0
  obtain ⟨⟨hst, hsum⟩, -⟩ := c0
  have hsum' := sumIdx_injective hsum
  have tape : ∀ i (z : ℤ), |z| ≤ s → C.workTapes i z = D.workTapes i z ∧
      (C.workTapePos i = z ↔ D.workTapePos i = z) := by
    intro i z hz
    have := cell (z + s).toNat (by rw [abs_le] at hz; omega)
    simp only [cellOf, Prod.mk.injEq] at this
    have e := congrFun this.2 i
    simp only [Prod.mk.injEq, decide_eq_decide] at e
    have hz' : (((z + s).toNat : ℕ) : ℤ) - s = z := by rw [abs_le] at hz; omega
    rwa [hz'] at e
  simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq]
  refine ⟨⟨hst, Fin.ext hpos, ?_, ?_⟩, hsum'⟩
  · funext i z
    by_cases hz : |z| ≤ s
    · exact (tape i z hz).1
    · have h1 : C.workTapes i z = none := hC.2 i z (not_le.mp hz)
      have h2 : D.workTapes i z = none := hD.2 i z (not_le.mp hz)
      rw [h1, h2]
  · funext i
    exact ((tape i _ (hC.1 i)).2.mp rfl).symm

/-- The constant of the code length: `2 W + 2`. -/
def codeK (N : FinNDTM Bool) : ℕ := 2 * W N + 2

/-- **The code is short**: the code word has at most `codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1)`
letters, so the code is below `2 ^ (codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1))`. The input field
has `|bits (|x| + 1)| ≤ logSpace |x| + 1` letters.

**Proof sketch.** Count `W (2s + 1)` chunk letters, the position field, and the final `1`;
`|bits (n + 1)| ≤ ⌊log₂ (n + 1)⌋ + 1 ≤ logSpace n + 1` and `W ≥ 1`. -/
theorem length_cfgWord_le (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    (cfgWord s C).length ≤ codeK N * (s + logSpace x.length + 1) := by
  rw [length_cfgWord]
  have h1 : wP x.length ≤ logSpace x.length + 1 := by
    have e := length_bits_le_log (x.length + 1)
    have e2 : Nat.log 2 (x.length + 1) ≤ Nat.log 2 x.length + 1 := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos x.length with h | h
      · rw [h]; simp
      · have := Nat.log_mul_base (b := 2) (n := x.length) (by norm_num) (by omega)
        have := Nat.log_mono_right (b := 2) (show x.length + 1 ≤ x.length * 2 by omega)
        omega
    simp only [wP, logSpace]; omega
  have hW : 1 ≤ W N := by simp [W]
  simp only [codeK]
  have e1 : W N * (2 * s + 1) = 2 * (W N * s) + W N := by ring
  have e2 : (2 * W N + 2) * (s + logSpace x.length + 1) =
      2 * (W N * s) + 2 * (W N * logSpace x.length) + 2 * W N + 2 * s +
        2 * logSpace x.length + 2 := by ring
  rw [e1, e2]
  omega

/-- **The code is below `2 ^ (codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1))`.** -/
theorem cfgCode_lt (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    cfgCode s C < 2 ^ (codeK N * (s + logSpace x.length + 1)) :=
  (bitsVal_lt_two_pow _).trans_le
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (length_cfgWord_le s C))

/-! ## Decoding -/

open Classical in
/-- **The decoder**: a window-bounded configuration with code `c` at radius `s`, if any
(chosen; it is determined up to the configuration-graph vertex,
`decodeCfg_cfgCode`). -/
noncomputable def decodeCfg (x : List Bool) (s c : ℕ) : Option (Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :=
  if h : ∃ C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x, Cfg.InWindow s C ∧ cfgCode s C = c then
    some (Classical.choose h)
  else none

/-- **Decoding a code recovers the vertex**: the decoder succeeds on the code of a
window-bounded configuration, with a window-bounded result of the same code and vertex.

**Proof sketch.** The chosen configuration has the same code, hence the same code word
(`bits_cfgCode`), hence the same vertex (`coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq`). -/
theorem decodeCfg_cfgCode (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) (hC : Cfg.InWindow s C) :
    ∃ D, decodeCfg x s (cfgCode s C) = some D ∧ Cfg.InWindow s D ∧ cfgCode s D = cfgCode s C ∧
      NDTM.coreSum D = NDTM.coreSum C := by
  classical
  have h : ∃ D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x, Cfg.InWindow s D ∧ cfgCode s D = cfgCode s C :=
    ⟨C, hC, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨Classical.choose h, by simp [decodeCfg, h], (Classical.choose_spec h).1,
    (Classical.choose_spec h).2, ?_⟩
  apply coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq (Classical.choose_spec h).1 hC
  rw [← bits_cfgCode, ← bits_cfgCode, (Classical.choose_spec h).2]

/-- The decoder fails exactly on numbers that are not codes. -/
theorem decodeCfg_eq_none (s c : ℕ) :
    decodeCfg (N := N) x s c = none ↔
      ¬ ∃ C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x, Cfg.InWindow s C ∧ cfgCode s C = c := by
  classical
  unfold decodeCfg
  split_ifs with h <;> simp [h]

end Complexity.Codec
```

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import Mathlib.Logic.Relation
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.VWord

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The nondeterministic walk for `PATH`: walks and the instance layout

[AB09, §4.1.2]: `PATH ∈ NL` by guessing a path vertex by vertex. This file holds the
combinatorics of the proof in `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.PathWalkProof`,
over the raw instance format `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨M, ⟨bits s, bits t⟩⟩⟩` (row-major adjacency word `M` of
length `n²`), so that it does not depend on `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.Path`.

* **Walks.** `Complexity.WalkLe E n j c t`: `t` is reachable from `c` in at most `j` edges of
  `E` through vertices `< n`. Every reachable vertex is reachable in at most `n` edges
  (`Complexity.walkLe_short`, a pigeonhole on the sets reachable within `j` edges).
* **Layout.** `Complexity.DblAt x q u` (the input carries `dbl u ++ [0, 1]` at position `q`)
  and `Complexity.PlainAt x r u` (the input ends with `u` from position `r`), and the
  decomposition of the raw instance format into them (`Complexity.eq_pathRaw_iff`).
* **What the walk machine checks.** `Complexity.PathAcc x` — a unary prefix, a matrix field of
  `n²` aligned pairs, endpoint fields of values `s, t < n`, and a walk of at most `n` edges of
  the matrix read off the input — is membership in the raw language
  (`Complexity.pathAcc_iff`).

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.WalkLe`, `Complexity.DblAt`, `Complexity.PlainAt`.
* `Complexity.pathRaw`, `Complexity.rawEdge`, `Complexity.pathRawLang` — the raw `PATH`
  language.
* `Complexity.pathEdge`, `Complexity.UnaryRest`, `Complexity.MatRest`, `Complexity.PathAcc`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.walkLe_short`, `Complexity.reach_iff_walkLe` — path shortening.
* `Complexity.walkLe_zero_iff` — a walk of no edges stays put.
* `Complexity.walkLe_succ_iff_head` — a longer walk stays put or begins with an edge.
* `Complexity.walkLe_succ_iff` — a longer walk is a shorter one, or one followed by an edge.
* `Complexity.eq_pathRaw_iff` — the layout of a raw instance.
* `Complexity.pathAcc_iff` — what the machine checks is membership in `pathRawLang`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.2.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-! ## Walks of bounded length -/

section Walks

variable (E : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) (n : ℕ)

/-- `WalkLe E n j c t`: `t` is reachable from `c` by at most `j` edges of `E`, every vertex
after `c` below `n`. -/
def WalkLe : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop
  | 0, c, t => c = t
  | j + 1, c, t => c = t ∨ ∃ v, v < n ∧ E c v ∧ WalkLe j v t

variable {E n}

/-- `Complexity.WalkLe` with no edge allowed: the endpoints are equal. -/
lemma walkLe_zero_iff {c t : ℕ} : WalkLe E n 0 c t ↔ c = t := Iff.rfl

/-- `Complexity.WalkLe` with at most `j + 1` edges, read at the front: the endpoints are equal,
or an edge from `c` to some `v < n` is followed by a walk of at most `j` edges from `v` to `t`. -/
lemma walkLe_succ_iff_head {j c t : ℕ} :
    WalkLe E n (j + 1) c t ↔ c = t ∨ ∃ v, v < n ∧ E c v ∧ WalkLe E n j v t := Iff.rfl

/-- Every vertex reaches itself. -/
lemma walkLe_refl (j c : ℕ) : WalkLe E n j c c := by
  cases j
  · rfl
  · exact Or.inl rfl

/-- One more allowed edge. -/
lemma walkLe_succ {j c t : ℕ} (h : WalkLe E n j c t) : WalkLe E n (j + 1) c t := by
  induction j generalizing c with
  | zero => exact Or.inl h
  | succ j ih =>
    rcases h with h | ⟨v, hv, he, hw⟩
    · exact Or.inl h
    · exact Or.inr ⟨v, hv, he, ih hw⟩

/-- More allowed edges. -/
lemma walkLe_mono {j k c t : ℕ} (hjk : j ≤ k) (h : WalkLe E n j c t) : WalkLe E n k c t := by
  induction hjk with
  | refl => exact h
  | step _ ih => exact walkLe_succ ih

/-- A bounded walk from a vertex below `n` is a path of the edge relation on vertices
below `n`. -/
lemma walkLe_reach {j c t : ℕ} (hc : c < n) (h : WalkLe E n j c t) :
    Relation.ReflTransGen (fun u v => u < n ∧ v < n ∧ E u v) c t := by
  induction j generalizing c with
  | zero => cases h; exact Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
  | succ j ih =>
    rcases h with rfl | ⟨v, hv, he, hw⟩
    · exact Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
    · exact Relation.ReflTransGen.head ⟨hc, hv, he⟩ (ih hv hw)

/-- A path is a walk of some length. -/
lemma exists_walkLe {c t : ℕ}
    (h : Relation.ReflTransGen (fun u v => u < n ∧ v < n ∧ E u v) c t) :
    ∃ j, WalkLe E n j c t := by
  induction h using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on with
  | refl => exact ⟨0, rfl⟩
  | head hab _ ih =>
    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := ih
    exact ⟨j + 1, Or.inr ⟨_, hab.2.1, hab.2.2, hj⟩⟩

/-- **Path shortening**: a vertex below `n` reachable within some number of edges is
reachable within `n` edges.

**Proof sketch.** Let `S j` be the set of vertices below `n` reaching `t` within `j` edges.
The sets grow with `j`, and once `S j = S (j + 1)` they are constant from `j` on (`S (j + 2)`
is determined by `S (j + 1)` as `S (j + 1)` is by `S j`). They cannot grow strictly `n` times,
since `t ∈ S 0` and `|S j| ≤ n`; so some `j < n` has `S j = S (j + 1)`, and every `S k` is
contained in `S n`. -/
lemma walkLe_short {j c t : ℕ} (ht : t < n) (hc : c < n) (h : WalkLe E n j c t) :
    WalkLe E n n c t := by
  classical
  let S : ℕ → Finset ℕ := fun j => (Finset.range n).filter fun c => WalkLe E n j c t
  have memS : ∀ j c, c ∈ S j ↔ c < n ∧ WalkLe E n j c t := by
    intro j c; simp [S]
  have hmono : ∀ j k, j ≤ k → S j ⊆ S k := by
    intro j k hjk c hcj
    rw [memS] at hcj ⊢
    exact ⟨hcj.1, walkLe_mono hjk hcj.2⟩
  have hstab : ∀ j, S j = S (j + 1) → S (j + 1) = S (j + 2) := by
    intro j he
    ext c
    rw [memS, memS]
    have key : ∀ v, v < n → (WalkLe E n (j + 1) v t ↔ WalkLe E n j v t) := by
      intro v hv
      have := congrArg (fun S : Finset ℕ => v ∈ S) he
      simp only [memS, eq_iff_iff] at this
      exact ⟨fun h => (this.mpr ⟨hv, h⟩).2, fun h => (this.mp ⟨hv, h⟩).2⟩
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hc, h | ⟨v, hv, he, hw⟩⟩
      · exact ⟨hc, Or.inl h⟩
      · exact ⟨hc, Or.inr ⟨v, hv, he, (key v hv).mpr hw⟩⟩
    · rintro ⟨hc, h | ⟨v, hv, he, hw⟩⟩
      · exact ⟨hc, Or.inl h⟩
      · exact ⟨hc, Or.inr ⟨v, hv, he, (key v hv).mp hw⟩⟩
  have hex : ∃ j₀, j₀ ≤ n ∧ S j₀ = S (j₀ + 1) := by
    by_contra hne
    push_neg at hne
    have hcard : ∀ j, j ≤ n → j + 1 ≤ (S j).card := by
      intro j hj
      induction j with
      | zero =>
        exact Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨t, (memS 0 t).mpr ⟨ht, rfl⟩⟩
      | succ j ih =>
        have hlt : (S j).card < (S (j + 1)).card :=
          Finset.card_lt_card (Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.mpr
            ⟨hmono j (j + 1) (by omega), hne j (by omega)⟩)
        have := ih (by omega)
        omega
    have h1 := hcard n le_rfl
    have h2 : (S n).card ≤ n := by
      calc (S n).card ≤ (Finset.range n).card := Finset.card_filter_le _ _
        _ = n := Finset.card_range n
    omega
  obtain ⟨j₀, hj₀, he⟩ := hex
  have hconst : ∀ i, S (j₀ + i) = S (j₀ + i + 1) := by
    intro i
    induction i with
    | zero => exact he
    | succ i ih => exact hstab (j₀ + i) ih
  have hfix : ∀ i, S (j₀ + i) = S j₀ := by
    intro i
    induction i with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ i ih => rw [← Nat.add_assoc, ← hconst i, ih]
  have hsub : S j ⊆ S n := by
    rcases Nat.le_total j n with hjn | hnj
    · exact hmono j n hjn
    · obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ : ∃ i, j = j₀ + i := ⟨j - j₀, by omega⟩
      rw [hfix i]
      exact hmono j₀ n hj₀
  exact ((memS n c).mp (hsub ((memS j c).mpr ⟨hc, h⟩))).2

/-- **Reachability is walking within `n` edges** (for endpoints below `n`). -/
lemma reach_iff_walkLe {c t : ℕ} (hc : c < n) (ht : t < n) :
    Relation.ReflTransGen (fun u v => u < n ∧ v < n ∧ E u v) c t ↔ WalkLe E n n c t := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := exists_walkLe h
    exact walkLe_short ht hc hj
  · exact walkLe_reach hc

/-- **Walks extend at the end**: a walk of at most `j + 1` steps is a walk of at most `j`
steps, or one followed by a step into a vertex below `n`.

**Proof sketch.** `WalkLe` unfolds at the front (a walk is empty or a first step followed by
a shorter walk), so induct on `j` generalizing the start `c`. For `j = 0` both sides are the
empty walk or a single step. For `j + 1`, a walk that begins with a step `c → v` has its tail
split by the induction hypothesis at `v`; conversely, a last step appended to a walk is
pushed into the tail of that walk by the induction hypothesis (or, when the walk is empty, is
itself a one-step walk). -/
lemma walkLe_succ_iff (j c t : ℕ) : WalkLe E n (j + 1) c t ↔
    WalkLe E n j c t ∨ ∃ w, WalkLe E n j c w ∧ E w t ∧ t < n := by
  induction j generalizing c with
  | zero =>
    simp only [walkLe_succ_iff_head, walkLe_zero_iff]
    constructor
    · rintro (h | ⟨v, hv, he, rfl⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨c, rfl, he, hv⟩
    · rintro (h | ⟨w, rfl, he, ht⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr ⟨t, ht, he, rfl⟩
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [walkLe_succ_iff_head (j := j + 1)]
    constructor
    · rintro (h | ⟨v, hv, he, hw⟩)
      · exact Or.inl (walkLe_succ_iff_head.mpr (Or.inl h))
      · rcases (ih v).mp hw with h | ⟨w, hw', hwt, ht⟩
        · exact Or.inl (walkLe_succ_iff_head.mpr (Or.inr ⟨v, hv, he, h⟩))
        · exact Or.inr ⟨w, walkLe_succ_iff_head.mpr (Or.inr ⟨v, hv, he, hw'⟩), hwt, ht⟩
    · rintro (h | ⟨w, hw, hwt, ht⟩)
      · rcases walkLe_succ_iff_head.mp h with h | ⟨v, hv, he, hw⟩
        · exact Or.inl h
        · exact Or.inr ⟨v, hv, he, walkLe_succ hw⟩
      · rcases walkLe_succ_iff_head.mp hw with hw | ⟨v, hv, he, hw⟩
        · subst hw
          exact Or.inr ⟨t, ht, hwt, walkLe_refl _ t⟩
        · exact Or.inr ⟨v, hv, he, (ih v).mpr (Or.inr ⟨w, hw, hwt, ht⟩)⟩

end Walks

/-! ## The layout of an instance -/

section Layout

/-- A `true` bit read with default `false` is inside the word. -/
lemma lt_of_getD_true {l : List Bool} {i : ℕ} (h : l.getD i false = true) : i < l.length := by
  by_contra hi
  rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_eq_none (by omega)] at h
  simp at h

/-- Two words agreeing in length and at every position are equal. -/
lemma ext_getD' {l₁ l₂ : List Bool} (hl : l₁.length = l₂.length)
    (h : ∀ i < l₁.length, l₁.getD i false = l₂.getD i false) : l₁ = l₂ := by
  apply List.ext_getElem hl
  intro i h1 h2
  have := h i h1
  rwa [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_eq_getElem h1, Option.getD_some,
    List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_eq_getElem h2, Option.getD_some] at this

/-- `DblAt x q u`: the input `x` carries `dbl u` followed by the separator `[0, 1]` at
position `q`. -/
def DblAt (x : List Bool) (q : ℕ) (u : List Bool) : Prop :=
  (∀ i < u.length, x.getD (q + 2 * i) false = u.getD i false ∧
    x.getD (q + 2 * i + 1) false = u.getD i false) ∧
  x.getD (q + 2 * u.length) false = false ∧ x.getD (q + 2 * u.length + 1) false = true

/-- `PlainAt x r u`: the input `x` ends with `u`, from position `r`. -/
def PlainAt (x : List Bool) (r : ℕ) (u : List Bool) : Prop :=
  (∀ i < u.length, x.getD (r + i) false = u.getD i false) ∧ x.length = r + u.length

/-- **The layout at a position**: `x` carries `dbl u ++ [0, 1]` at `q` iff the suffix from
`q` is a pair with first component `u`.

**Proof sketch.** Read positions of the suffix with `pairEncode_getD`; conversely the
separator bit `1` places `q + 2|u| + 1` inside `x`, the lengths agree, and every position
of the suffix is a doubled bit, a separator bit, or a bit of the rest. -/
lemma dblAt_iff (x : List Bool) (q : ℕ) (u : List Bool) :
    DblAt x q u ↔ x.drop q = pairEncode u (x.drop (q + 2 * u.length + 2)) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hb, h0, h1⟩
    have hlen := lt_of_getD_true h1
    refine ext_getD' (by simp only [List.length_drop, length_pairEncode]; omega) fun i _ => ?_
    rw [getD_drop, pairEncode_getD]
    split_ifs with c1 c2 c3
    · have := hb (i / 2) (by omega)
      rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one i with h | h
      · rw [show q + i = q + 2 * (i / 2) by omega]; exact this.1
      · rw [show q + i = q + 2 * (i / 2) + 1 by omega]; exact this.2
    · subst c2; exact h0
    · subst c3; rw [← Nat.add_assoc]; exact h1
    · rw [getD_drop]; congr 1; omega
  · intro h
    have key : ∀ j, x.getD (q + j) false = (pairEncode u (x.drop (q + 2 * u.length + 2))).getD j
        false := by intro j; rw [← h, getD_drop]
    refine ⟨fun i hi => ⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [key, pairEncode_getD, if_pos (by omega)]; congr 1; omega
    · rw [Nat.add_assoc, key, pairEncode_getD, if_pos (by omega)]; congr 1; omega
    · rw [key, pairEncode_getD, if_neg (by omega), if_pos rfl]
    · rw [Nat.add_assoc, key, pairEncode_getD, if_neg (by omega), if_neg (by omega), if_pos rfl]

/-- The input ends with `u` from position `r` iff `r` is inside and the suffix is `u`. -/
lemma plainAt_iff (x : List Bool) (r : ℕ) (u : List Bool) :
    PlainAt x r u ↔ r ≤ x.length ∧ x.drop r = u := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hb, hl⟩
    refine ⟨by omega, ext_getD' (by simp; omega) fun i hi => ?_⟩
    rw [getD_drop]
    exact hb i (by simp at hi; omega)
  · rintro ⟨hr, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨fun i hi => by rw [getD_drop], by simp; omega⟩

/-- **The raw `PATH` instance** `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨M, ⟨bits s, bits t⟩⟩⟩`. -/
def pathRaw (n : ℕ) (M : List Bool) (s t : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (List.replicate n true) (pairEncode M (pairEncode (Nat.bits s) (Nat.bits t)))

/-- The edge relation of the row-major adjacency word `M` on vertices below `n`. -/
def rawEdge (n : ℕ) (M : List Bool) (u v : ℕ) : Prop :=
  u < n ∧ v < n ∧ M.getD (u * n + v) false = true

/-- **The raw `PATH` language**: raw instances (matrix word of length `n²`, endpoints
below `n`) whose target is reachable from their source. -/
def pathRawLang : Language Bool :=
  {x | ∃ (n : ℕ) (M : List Bool) (s t : ℕ), M.length = n * n ∧ s < n ∧ t < n ∧
    x = pathRaw n M s t ∧ Relation.ReflTransGen (rawEdge n M) s t}

/-- **The layout of a raw instance**: `x = ⟨1ⁿ, ⟨M, ⟨bits s, bits t⟩⟩⟩` iff `x` carries the
four fields at the positions `0`, `2n + 2`, `2n + 2 + 2|M| + 2` and
`2n + 2 + 2|M| + 2 + 2|bits s| + 2`.

**Proof sketch.** `dblAt_iff` three times and `plainAt_iff` once, peeling one pair at a
time (`Turing.pairEncode_drop`, `List.drop_drop`). -/
lemma eq_pathRaw_iff (x : List Bool) (n : ℕ) (M : List Bool) (s t : ℕ) :
    x = pathRaw n M s t ↔
      DblAt x 0 (List.replicate n true) ∧ DblAt x (2 * n + 2) M ∧
      DblAt x (2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2) (Nat.bits s) ∧
      PlainAt x (2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2 + 2 * (Nat.bits s).length + 2) (Nat.bits t) := by
  constructor
  · rintro rfl
    have d1 : (pathRaw n M s t).drop (2 * n + 2) =
        pairEncode M (pairEncode (Nat.bits s) (Nat.bits t)) := by
      have := Turing.pairEncode_drop (List.replicate n true)
        (pairEncode M (pairEncode (Nat.bits s) (Nat.bits t)))
      simpa using this
    have d2 : (pathRaw n M s t).drop (2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2) =
        pairEncode (Nat.bits s) (Nat.bits t) := by
      rw [show 2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2 = (2 * n + 2) + (2 * M.length + 2) by omega,
        ← List.drop_drop, d1, Turing.pairEncode_drop]
    have d3 : (pathRaw n M s t).drop
        (2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2 + 2 * (Nat.bits s).length + 2) = Nat.bits t := by
      rw [show 2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2 + 2 * (Nat.bits s).length + 2 =
        (2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2) + (2 * (Nat.bits s).length + 2) by omega,
        ← List.drop_drop, d2, Turing.pairEncode_drop]
    refine ⟨(dblAt_iff _ _ _).mpr ?_, (dblAt_iff _ _ _).mpr ?_, (dblAt_iff _ _ _).mpr ?_,
      (plainAt_iff _ _ _).mpr ⟨?_, d3⟩⟩
    · simp only [List.drop_zero, Nat.zero_add, List.length_replicate]
      rw [show (pathRaw n M s t).drop (2 * n + 2) = _ from d1]; rfl
    · rw [d1, show 2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2 = (2 * n + 2) + (2 * M.length + 2) by omega,
        ← List.drop_drop, d1, Turing.pairEncode_drop]
    · rw [d2, show 2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2 + 2 * (Nat.bits s).length + 2 =
        (2 * n + 2 + 2 * M.length + 2) + (2 * (Nat.bits s).length + 2) by omega,
        ← List.drop_drop, d2, Turing.pairEncode_drop]
    · simp [pathRaw, length_pairEncode]; omega
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩
    rw [dblAt_iff] at h1 h2 h3
    rw [plainAt_iff] at h4
    simp only [List.drop_zero, Nat.zero_add, List.length_replicate] at h1
    rw [h1, h2, h3, h4.2]
    rfl

/-- A row-major index is below `n²`. -/
lemma rowMajor_lt {n u v : ℕ} (hu : u < n) (hv : v < n) : u * n + v < n * n := by
  have : (u + 1) * n ≤ n * n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right n hu
  rw [Nat.succ_mul] at this
  omega

end Layout

/-! ## What the machine checks -/

/-- The matrix bit of the edge `u → v`, read off the input at its row-major position. -/
def pathEdge (x : List Bool) (n u v : ℕ) : Prop :=
  x.getD (2 * n + 2 + 2 * (u * n + v)) false = true

/-- The unary prefix from pair `k` on: aligned `11` pairs up to pair `n`, then `01`. -/
def UnaryRest (x : List Bool) (k n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, k ≤ i → i < n → x.getD (2 * i) false = true ∧ x.getD (2 * i + 1) false = true) ∧
  x.getD (2 * n) false = false ∧ x.getD (2 * n + 1) false = true

/-- The matrix field from pair `i` on: aligned data pairs up to pair `n²`, then `01`. -/
def MatRest (x : List Bool) (n i : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ j, i ≤ j → j < n * n →
    x.getD (2 * n + 2 + 2 * j) false = x.getD (2 * n + 2 + 2 * j + 1) false) ∧
  x.getD (2 * n + 2 + 2 * (n * n)) false = false ∧
  x.getD (2 * n + 2 + 2 * (n * n) + 1) false = true

/-- **What the walk machine accepts**: a unary prefix `1ⁿ`, a matrix field of `n²` aligned
pairs, a doubled source field `bits s` and a plain target field `bits t` ending the input,
with `s, t < n` and `t` reachable from `s` within `n` edges of `pathEdge`. -/
def PathAcc (x : List Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ n, UnaryRest x 0 n ∧ MatRest x n 0 ∧
    ∃ s, s < n ∧ DblAt x (2 * n + 2 + 2 * (n * n) + 2) (Nat.bits s) ∧
      ∃ t, t < n ∧
        PlainAt x (2 * n + 2 + 2 * (n * n) + 2 + 2 * (Nat.bits s).length + 2) (Nat.bits t) ∧
        WalkLe (pathEdge x n) n n s t

/-- The unary prefix is the doubled word `1ⁿ` followed by the separator. -/
lemma unaryRest_iff (x : List Bool) (n : ℕ) :
    UnaryRest x 0 n ↔ DblAt x 0 (List.replicate n true) := by
  have hr : ∀ i < n, (List.replicate n true).getD i false = true := by
    intro i hi
    rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_replicate, if_pos hi]; rfl
  simp only [UnaryRest, DblAt, List.length_replicate, Nat.zero_add, Nat.zero_le, true_imp_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
    exact ⟨fun i hi => by rw [hr i hi]; exact h1 i hi, h2, h3⟩
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
    exact ⟨fun i hi => by rw [← hr i hi]; exact h1 i hi, h2, h3⟩

/-- The matrix field is a doubled word of length `n²` followed by the separator. -/
lemma matRest_iff (x : List Bool) (n : ℕ) :
    MatRest x n 0 ↔ ∃ M : List Bool, M.length = n * n ∧ DblAt x (2 * n + 2) M := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
    let M := (List.range (n * n)).map fun j => x.getD (2 * n + 2 + 2 * j) false
    have hM : M.length = n * n := by simp [M]
    have hg : ∀ j < n * n, M.getD j false = x.getD (2 * n + 2 + 2 * j) false := by
      intro j hj
      simp [M, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_range hj]
    refine ⟨M, hM, fun i hi => ?_, by rw [hM]; exact h2, by rw [hM]; exact h3⟩
    rw [hM] at hi
    rw [hg i hi]
    exact ⟨rfl, (h1 i (Nat.zero_le _) hi).symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨M, hM, h1, h2, h3⟩
    rw [hM] at h1 h2 h3
    refine ⟨fun j _ hj => ?_, h2, h3⟩
    have := h1 j hj
    rw [this.1, this.2]

/-- **`PathAcc` is membership in the raw `PATH` language.**

**Proof sketch.** `eq_pathRaw_iff` matches the four fields; the matrix word is read off the
input (`matRest_iff`), so `pathEdge` is its edge relation below `n`; reachability is walking
within `n` edges (`reach_iff_walkLe`). -/
theorem pathAcc_iff (x : List Bool) : PathAcc x ↔ x ∈ pathRawLang := by
  have hedge : ∀ n (M : List Bool), M.length = n * n → DblAt x (2 * n + 2) M →
      ∀ u v, u < n → v < n → (pathEdge x n u v ↔ M.getD (u * n + v) false = true) := by
    intro n M hM hD u v hu hv
    have := (hD.1 (u * n + v) (by rw [hM]; exact rowMajor_lt hu hv)).1
    simp only [pathEdge, this]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨n, hU, hMat, s, hs, hD, t, ht, hP, hW⟩
    obtain ⟨M, hM, hDM⟩ := (matRest_iff x n).mp hMat
    refine ⟨n, M, s, t, hM, hs, ht, (eq_pathRaw_iff x n M s t).mpr
      ⟨(unaryRest_iff x n).mp hU, hDM, by rwa [hM], by rwa [hM]⟩, ?_⟩
    refine ((reach_iff_walkLe hs ht).mpr hW).mono fun u v ⟨hu, hv, he⟩ => ?_
    exact ⟨hu, hv, (hedge n M hM hDM u v hu hv).mp he⟩
  · rintro ⟨n, M, s, t, hM, hs, ht, hx, hr⟩
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩ := (eq_pathRaw_iff x n M s t).mp hx
    rw [hM] at h3 h4
    refine ⟨n, (unaryRest_iff x n).mpr h1, (matRest_iff x n).mpr ⟨M, hM, h2⟩, s, hs, h3, t, ht,
      h4, (reach_iff_walkLe hs ht).mp (hr.mono fun u v ⟨hu, hv, he⟩ => ?_)⟩
    exact ⟨hu, hv, (hedge n M hM h2 u v hu hv).mpr he⟩

/-! ## Fields and counters -/

/-- The binary digits of a positive number: its parity, then the digits of its half. -/
lemma bits_eq_cons {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    Nat.bits w = decide (w % 2 = 1) :: Nat.bits (w / 2) := by
  have h1 := LogProg.bits_head_odd w
  rw [if_neg hw] at h1
  have h2 := LogProg.bits_half w
  cases hl : Nat.bits w with
  | nil => rw [hl] at h1; simp at h1
  | cons b t =>
    rw [hl] at h1 h2
    simp only [List.head?_cons, Option.some.injEq, List.tail_cons] at h1 h2
    rw [h1, h2]

/-- A doubled field with a first bit. -/
lemma dblAt_cons (x : List Bool) (q : ℕ) (b : Bool) (u : List Bool) :
    DblAt x q (b :: u) ↔
      (x.getD q false = b ∧ x.getD (q + 1) false = b) ∧ DblAt x (q + 2) u := by
  simp only [DblAt, List.length_cons]
  have e1 : ∀ i, q + 2 * (i + 1) = q + 2 + 2 * i := fun i => by ring
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
    refine ⟨by simpa using h1 0 (by omega), fun i hi => ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · have := h1 (i + 1) (by omega)
      rw [e1, List.getD_cons_succ] at this
      exact this
    · rw [← e1]; exact h2
    · rw [← e1]; exact h3
  · rintro ⟨⟨h0, h0'⟩, h1, h2, h3⟩
    refine ⟨fun i hi => ?_, by rw [e1]; exact h2, by rw [e1]; exact h3⟩
    cases i with
    | zero => simpa using ⟨h0, h0'⟩
    | succ i => rw [e1, List.getD_cons_succ]; exact h1 i (by omega)

/-- A plain suffix with a first bit. -/
lemma plainAt_cons (x : List Bool) (r : ℕ) (b : Bool) (u : List Bool) :
    PlainAt x r (b :: u) ↔ x.getD r false = b ∧ PlainAt x (r + 1) u := by
  simp only [PlainAt, List.length_cons]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
    refine ⟨by simpa using h1 0 (by omega), fun i hi => ?_, by omega⟩
    have := h1 (i + 1) (by omega)
    rw [← Nat.add_assoc, List.getD_cons_succ] at this
    rw [Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm 1 i, ← Nat.add_assoc]; exact this
  · rintro ⟨h0, h1, h2⟩
    refine ⟨fun i hi => ?_, by omega⟩
    cases i with
    | zero => simpa using h0
    | succ i =>
      rw [show r + (i + 1) = r + 1 + i by omega, List.getD_cons_succ]; exact h1 i (by omega)

/-- Advancing a row-major counter: the column wraps at `n` into the next row. -/
lemma divmod_succ {n i : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    (i % n + 1 = n → (i + 1) / n = i / n + 1 ∧ (i + 1) % n = 0) ∧
    (i % n + 1 ≠ n → (i + 1) / n = i / n ∧ (i + 1) % n = i % n + 1) := by
  have h1 := Nat.div_add_mod i n
  have h2 := Nat.mod_lt i hn
  refine ⟨fun h => (Nat.div_mod_unique hn).mpr ⟨?_, hn⟩, fun h => (Nat.div_mod_unique hn).mpr
    ⟨by omega, by omega⟩⟩
  rw [Nat.mul_succ]; omega

/-- The row counter reaches `n` exactly at pair `n²`. -/
lemma div_eq_self_iff {n i : ℕ} (hi : i ≤ n * n) : i / n = n ↔ i = n * n := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
  · simp at hi ⊢; omega
  · constructor
    · intro h
      have := Nat.div_mul_le_self i n
      rw [h] at this; omega
    · rintro rfl; exact Nat.mul_div_cancel n hn

end Complexity
```

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import Mathlib.Tactic.DeriveFintype
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Sigma
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Sum
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Option
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Layout

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Register-tape programs with subroutine calls, and their compiled machines

A *register-tape program* (`Complexity.LogProg.RProg`) is a multi-tape machine over `m`
work tapes (its *registers*) in which some states are *call nodes*: in a call node the
program asks a fixed decider whether a *virtual input* — a part of its own input followed by
the words on some of its registers, `Complexity.LogProg.vword` — belongs to the decider's
language, and continues in one of two states. This is the "pretend there is a virtual input
tape" device of [AB09, proof of Lemma 4.17, Fig. 4.3], packaged once.

This file defines the program model and the machine `Complexity.LogProg.compileTM` that
realizes it: the registers become work tapes `0, …, m - 1`, the decider's work tapes follow,
and a call node is executed by simulating the decider step for step on the virtual input.
The virtual input head is represented by the real input head and the register heads
(`Complexity.LogProg.TPos`), so the simulation needs no extra space.

Related model: `Complexity.CounterProg` (`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CounterProg`) is a
goto program over unary counters for the polynomial-time emitters of [AB09, §6.2]. It overlaps
in spirit with the programs here, which store registers in binary (as logarithmic space
requires) and call deciders on virtual inputs; the two are kept separate, and a polynomially
running counter program is simulated by an abstract register machine in
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.CounterProgSim`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.Mode` — which part of the real input opens the virtual input: all of
  it, doubled (`whole`, giving `Turing.pairEncode x _` when the call has at least one
  argument), or its leading run of `1`s, plain (`unaryFst`, giving `Turing.pairEncode 1ⁿ _`
  on inputs `Turing.pairEncode 1ⁿ _`, again with at least one argument). A call with no
  arguments has a single-segment virtual input with no separator — for `whole` on `x = []`
  it is the empty word, not a pair encoding (P0 round 1, finding 3).
* `Complexity.LogProg.CallSpec`, `Complexity.LogProg.RProg` — call nodes and programs.
* `Complexity.LogProg.callSegs` — the segments of the virtual input of a call.
* `Complexity.LogProg.CSt`, `Complexity.LogProg.ctr`, `Complexity.LogProg.compileTM` — the
  compiled machine.
* `Complexity.LogProg.seam` — the compiled configuration of a program configuration.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.step_seam_prog` — away from call nodes the compiled machine runs the
  program in lockstep.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.3, proof of Lemma 4.17.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

open Turing

/-- Which part of the real input opens a virtual input. -/
inductive Mode where
  /-- the whole input, doubled: virtual inputs `pairEncode x _` (when the call has at
  least one argument; with none, the virtual input is the doubled input alone, with no
  separator) -/
  | whole
  /-- the leading run of `1`s of the input, plain: on an input `pairEncode 1ⁿ _` this is
  `1²ⁿ`, so the virtual inputs are `pairEncode 1ⁿ _` (again given at least one argument) -/
  | unaryFst
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The first segment of a virtual input. -/
def Mode.seg0 : Mode → List Bool → Seg
  | .whole, x => (x, true)
  | .unaryFst, x => (x.takeWhile (· = true), false)

/-- The register segments: every word but the last is doubled. -/
def argSegs : List (List Bool) → List Seg
  | [] => []
  | [w] => [(w, false)]
  | w :: v :: ws => (w, true) :: argSegs (v :: ws)

/-- There is one register segment per argument word. -/
@[simp] lemma length_argSegs (ws : List (List Bool)) : (argSegs ws).length = ws.length := by
  induction ws with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons w ws ih => cases ws with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons v ws => simp [argSegs] at ih ⊢; omega

/-- Segment `i` of the register segments is register word `i`, doubled unless last. -/
lemma seg_argSegs (ws : List (List Bool)) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < ws.length) :
    seg (argSegs ws) i = (ws[i], decide (i + 1 < ws.length)) := by
  induction ws generalizing i with
  | nil => simp at hi
  | cons w ws ih =>
    cases ws with
    | nil =>
      have : i = 0 := by simp at hi; omega
      subst this; simp [argSegs, seg]
    | cons v ws =>
      cases i with
      | zero => simp [argSegs, seg]
      | succ i =>
        simp only [argSegs, seg_cons_succ]
        rw [ih i (by simp at hi ⊢; omega)]
        simp

/-- A call node: the decider to call, the virtual-input mode, the argument registers, and
the two continuation states. -/
structure CallSpec (m d : ℕ) (Λ : Type) where
  /-- which decider -/
  dec : Fin d
  /-- the first segment of the virtual input -/
  mode : Mode
  /-- the registers whose words follow, in order -/
  args : List (Fin m)
  /-- the state after a positive answer -/
  yes : Λ
  /-- the state after a negative answer -/
  no : Λ

/-- A register-tape program over `m` registers calling `d` deciders: a machine on the
registers together with the set of call nodes (on which its transition table is ignored). -/
structure RProg (m d : ℕ) (Λ : Type) where
  /-- the transitions at the ordinary nodes -/
  tm : MultiTapeTM m Bool Λ
  /-- the call nodes -/
  call : Λ → Option (CallSpec m d Λ)

/-- The segments of the virtual input of a call on input `x` with register words `W`. -/
def callSegs {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (cs : CallSpec m d Λ) (x : List Bool)
    (W : Fin m → List Bool) : List Seg :=
  cs.mode.seg0 x :: argSegs (cs.args.map W)

/-- Two calls with the same mode and the same argument words have the same virtual input. -/
lemma callSegs_congr {m d m' d' : ℕ} {Λ Λ' : Type} {cs : CallSpec m d Λ} {cs' : CallSpec m' d' Λ'}
    {x : List Bool} {W : Fin m → List Bool} {W' : Fin m' → List Bool} (hmode : cs'.mode = cs.mode)
    (hargs : cs'.args.map W' = cs.args.map W) : callSegs cs' x W' = callSegs cs x W := by
  simp only [callSegs, hmode, hargs]

/-- A call's virtual input has one segment per argument register plus the leading segment. -/
@[simp] lemma length_callSegs {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (cs : CallSpec m d Λ) (x : List Bool)
    (W : Fin m → List Bool) : (callSegs cs x W).length = cs.args.length + 1 := by
  simp [callSegs]

set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
set_option synthInstance.maxSize 1000 in
/-- The states of the compiled machine. -/
inductive CSt (Λ SD : Type) (m : ℕ) where
  /-- running the program at node `l` -/
  | prog (l : Λ)
  /-- simulating the decider (state `q`) for the call at `l`: current segment `s`, parity,
  direction of the last track move, and the decider's emitted bit so far -/
  | sim (l : Λ) (q : SD) (s : Fin (m + 1)) (par dir : Bool) (res : Option Bool)
  /-- returning: the mandatory first left move of the input rewind -/
  | ret1 (l : Λ) (s : Fin (m + 1)) (dir res : Bool)
  /-- returning: scanning the input head left -/
  | ret2 (l : Λ) (s : Fin (m + 1)) (dir res : Bool)
  /-- returning: restoring the head of argument register number `a` (`scan`: in its left
  scan) -/
  | retR (l : Λ) (s : Fin (m + 1)) (dir res : Bool) (a : Fin m) (scan : Bool)
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- Track bookkeeping of one simulated step (a pure function): from the segment `s`, parity,
direction of the last move, whether the current track reads a cell, and the virtual head
move, compute the new segment, parity, direction, and the move of the current track's real
head. `dbl`: the segment is doubled; `last`/`first`: it is the last/first segment. -/
def gstep (dbl last first : Bool) (s : ℕ) (par dir isChar : Bool) :
    SignType → ℕ × Bool × Bool × SignType
  | .zero => (s, par, dir, 0)
  | .pos =>
    if isChar then (if dbl ∧ par = false then (s, true, dir, 0) else (s, false, true, .pos))
    else if dir then (if last then (s, par, dir, 0) else (s + 1, true, false, 0))
    else (s, false, true, .pos)
  | .neg =>
    if isChar then (if dbl ∧ par = true then (s, false, dir, 0) else (s, true, false, .neg))
    else if dir then (s, true, false, .neg)
    else (if first then (s, par, dir, 0) else (s - 1, false, true, 0))

/-- Clamp a natural number into `Fin (m + 1)`. -/
def toFin (m s : ℕ) : Fin (m + 1) := ⟨min s m, by omega⟩

/-- The rendering flag of segment `s` of a call (from the mode for `s = 0`). -/
def segDbl {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (cs : CallSpec m d Λ) (s : ℕ) : Bool :=
  if s = 0 then decide (cs.mode = .whole) else decide (s < cs.args.length)

/-- The register read by segment `s ≥ 1` (a default otherwise). -/
def segReg {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (cs : CallSpec m d Λ) (s : ℕ) (h : 0 < m) : Fin m :=
  cs.args.getD (s - 1) ⟨0, h⟩

/-- Whether segment `s`'s current reading is a cell of its word: a bit on a register or
on the input in `whole` mode, a `1` in `unaryFst` mode. -/
def isCharRead (mode : Mode) (s : ℕ) (rd : Option Bool) : Bool :=
  if s = 0 ∧ mode = .unaryFst then decide (rd = some true) else rd.isSome

/-- The virtual symbol presented to the decider. -/
def virtSym (mode : Mode) (s nseg : ℕ) (dir : Bool) (rd : Option Bool) : Option Bool :=
  if isCharRead mode s rd then (if s = 0 ∧ mode = .unaryFst then some true else rd)
  else if dir then (if s + 1 = nseg then none else some false)
  else (if s = 0 then none else some true)

/-- The register action of a return step on argument register `r`: move `mv`. -/
def regMove {m : ℕ} (r : Fin m) (mv : SignType) : Fin m → Option (Option Bool) × SignType :=
  fun r' => (none, if r' = r then mv else 0)

/-- The state after finishing argument register `a` of a return: the next argument register,
or back to the program. -/
def nextRet {Λ SD : Type} {m d : ℕ} (cs : CallSpec m d Λ) (l : Λ) (s : Fin (m + 1))
    (dir res : Bool) (a : ℕ) : CSt Λ SD m :=
  if h : a < cs.args.length ∧ a < m then .retR l s dir res ⟨a, h.2⟩ false
  else .prog (if res then cs.yes else cs.no)

section Compile

variable {m d kD : ℕ} {Λ SD : Type}

/-- The idle action on the decider block. -/
def dIdle : Fin kD → Option (Option Bool) × SignType := fun _ => (none, 0)

/-- **The transition table of the compiled machine.** See the module docstring; at a call
node the setup step moves the argument heads one cell left (onto the left blanks of their
words) and starts the decider; a simulated step reads the virtual symbol from the current
track, performs the decider's work-tape actions on the decider block, moves the current
track's real head according to `gstep`, and records the decider's emission; when the decider
halts the return phase rewinds the input head and the argument heads. -/
def ctr (P : RProg m d Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD) (q0 : Fin d → SD) :
    CSt Λ SD m → Option Bool → (Fin (m + kD) → Option Bool) → Action (m + kD) Bool (CSt Λ SD m)
  | .prog l, inp, w =>
    match P.call l with
    | none =>
      let a := P.tm.tr l inp (fun r => w (Fin.castAdd kD r))
      ⟨a.inputTape, Fin.append a.workTapes dIdle, a.output, a.state.map .prog⟩
    | some cs =>
      ⟨0, Fin.append (fun r => (none, if r ∈ cs.args then -1 else 0)) dIdle, none,
        some (.sim l (q0 cs.dec) 0 false true none)⟩
  | .sim l q s par dir res, inp, w =>
    match P.call l with
    | none => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, none⟩
    | some cs =>
      let rd : Option Bool :=
        if s.val = 0 then inp
        else if hm : 0 < m then w (Fin.castAdd kD (segReg cs s hm)) else none
      let ic := isCharRead cs.mode s rd
      let vs := virtSym cs.mode s (cs.args.length + 1) dir rd
      let a := D.tr q vs (fun i => w (Fin.natAdd m i))
      let g := gstep (segDbl cs s) (decide (s.val + 1 = cs.args.length + 1))
        (decide (s.val = 0)) s par dir ic a.inputTape
      let res' := res <|> a.output
      ⟨if s.val = 0 then g.2.2.2 else 0,
        Fin.append (fun r => (none, if h : 0 < m then
            (if s.val ≠ 0 ∧ r = segReg cs s h then g.2.2.2 else 0) else 0)) a.workTapes,
        none,
        some (match a.state with
          | some q' => .sim l q' (toFin m g.1) g.2.1 g.2.2.1 res'
          | none => .ret1 l (toFin m g.1) g.2.2.1 (res'.getD false))⟩
  | .ret1 l s dir res, _, _ => ⟨-1, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some (.ret2 l s dir res)⟩
  | .ret2 l s dir res, inp, _ =>
    match inp with
    | some _ => ⟨-1, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some (.ret2 l s dir res)⟩
    | none =>
      match P.call l with
      | none => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, none⟩
      | some cs => ⟨1, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some (nextRet cs l s dir res 0)⟩
  | .retR l s dir res a scan, _, w =>
    match P.call l with
    | none => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, none⟩
    | some cs =>
      let r := cs.args.getD a a
      let rd := w (Fin.castAdd kD r)
      let leftSide : Bool := decide (s.val < a.val + 1) || (decide (s.val = a.val + 1) && !dir)
      if scan then
        match rd with
        | some _ => ⟨0, Fin.append (regMove r (-1)) dIdle, none, some (.retR l s dir res a true)⟩
        | none => ⟨0, Fin.append (regMove r 1) dIdle, none,
            some (nextRet cs l s dir res (a.val + 1))⟩
      else
        match rd with
        | none =>
          if leftSide then
            ⟨0, Fin.append (regMove r 1) dIdle, none, some (nextRet cs l s dir res (a.val + 1))⟩
          else ⟨0, Fin.append (regMove r (-1)) dIdle, none, some (.retR l s dir res a true)⟩
        | some _ => ⟨0, Fin.append (regMove r (-1)) dIdle, none, some (.retR l s dir res a true)⟩

/-- **The compiled machine** of a program `P` with start node `l₀`, calling the deciders
`D` from the start states `q0 j`. -/
def compileTM (P : RProg m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD) (q0 : Fin d → SD) :
    MultiTapeTM (m + kD) Bool (CSt Λ SD m) where
  q₀ := .prog l₀
  tr := ctr P D q0

/-- At a call node the compiled machine starts the simulation: it moves each argument head
one cell left, leaves the input head and the decider block in place, emits nothing, and enters
the simulation of the call's decider from its start state. -/
lemma compileTM_tr_prog_call (P : RProg m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD)
    (q0 : Fin d → SD) {l : Λ} {cs : CallSpec m d Λ} (hcall : P.call l = some cs)
    (inp : Option Bool) (w : Fin (m + kD) → Option Bool) :
    (compileTM P l₀ D q0).tr (.prog l) inp w =
      ⟨0, Fin.append (fun r => (none, if r ∈ cs.args then -1 else 0)) dIdle, none,
        some (.sim l (q0 cs.dec) 0 false true none)⟩ := by
  simp only [compileTM, ctr, hcall]

/-- The first return step moves the input head one cell left and nothing else, and enters the
input rewind. -/
lemma compileTM_tr_ret1 (P : RProg m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD)
    (q0 : Fin d → SD) (l : Λ) (s : Fin (m + 1)) (dir res : Bool) (inp : Option Bool)
    (w : Fin (m + kD) → Option Bool) :
    (compileTM P l₀ D q0).tr (.ret1 l s dir res) inp w =
      ⟨-1, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some (.ret2 l s dir res)⟩ := rfl

/-- The compiled configuration of a program configuration: the program's registers, the
decider block blank with heads at the origin. -/
def seam {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg m Bool Λ x) : Cfg (m + kD) Bool (CSt Λ SD m) x :=
  ⟨c.state.map .prog, c.inputPos, Fin.append c.workTapes (fun _ _ => none),
    Fin.append c.workTapePos (fun _ => 0), c.output⟩

/-- The initial configuration of the compiled machine is the seam of the program's. -/
lemma seam_init (P : RProg m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD) (q0 : Fin d → SD)
    (x : List Bool) :
    (compileTM P l₀ D q0).initCfg x = seam (kD := kD) (Cfg.init (k := m) l₀ x) := by
  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl
  · funext i z
    refine Fin.addCases (fun r => ?_) (fun j => ?_) i <;> simp [seam, Cfg.init]
  · funext i
    refine Fin.addCases (fun r => ?_) (fun j => ?_) i <;> simp [seam, Cfg.init]

/-- **Lockstep away from calls**: at a non-call node the compiled machine makes exactly the
program's step.

**Proof sketch.** At a non-call program node the compiled transition is the program's
transition, relabelled (`ctr` on `prog` states), with the decider tapes untouched. Unfold one
step on both sides and compare the components of `seam`. -/
lemma step_seam_prog (P : RProg m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD)
    (q0 : Fin d → SD) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg m Bool Λ x) (l : Λ) (hl : c.state = some l)
    (hcall : P.call l = none) :
    (compileTM P l₀ D q0).step (seam c) = seam (P.tm.step c) := by
  have hstate : (seam (kD := kD) (SD := SD) c).state = some (.prog l) := by
    simp [seam, hl]
  unfold MultiTapeTM.step
  rw [hstate, hl]
  have hin : (seam (kD := kD) (SD := SD) c).inputSymbol = c.inputSymbol := rfl
  have hw : (fun r => (seam (kD := kD) (SD := SD) c).workTapeSymbols (Fin.castAdd kD r)) =
      c.workTapeSymbols := by
    funext r; simp [seam, Cfg.workTapeSymbols]
  simp only [compileTM, ctr, hcall, hin, hw]
  refine Cfg.ext ?_ rfl ?_ ?_ rfl
  · simp [seam]
  · funext i z
    refine Fin.addCases (fun r => ?_) (fun j => ?_) i
    · simp only [Action.apply, Fin.append_left, seam]
    · simp [Action.apply, seam, dIdle]
  · funext i
    refine Fin.addCases (fun r => ?_) (fun j => ?_) i
    · simp [Action.apply, seam]
    · simp [Action.apply, seam, dIdle]

/-- A halted program configuration is a halted compiled configuration. -/
lemma seam_state_none {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg m Bool Λ x) (h : c.state = none) :
    (seam (kD := kD) (SD := SD) c).state = none := by
  simp [seam, h]

end Compile

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-

import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Setup

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The outer search of the Savitch register machine

After the setup, `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A` runs a register `U` through the codes
below `K = 2 ^ w`, keeping those the initial-code decider accepts, and for each such `U` a
register `V` through the codes the accepting-code decider accepts; for each candidate pair
it evaluates the midpoint recursion at the root level `w`
(`Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec`) and accepts on success
(`outerV_run`, `outerU_run`). Together with the setup (`setup_run`), the machine answers
whether some initial code reaches some accepting code by midpoint reachability
(`savitch_halts`).

Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.14]; not itself a result of the book.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt` — the register files of the outer search.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO`, `AccO` — the code tests read from the oracle, with
  their defining equations `initO_iff_orc`, `accO_iff_orc`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run` — the outer search.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_toV` — the outer search's register files, as registers.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.savitch_halts` — the whole run.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2.1, Theorem 4.14.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

namespace SavitchARM

open Turing

/-- **The register files of the outer search**: after the setup, with candidate codes `u`,
`v` and midpoint register `M`. -/
def outerSt (s w u v M : ℕ) : St := { setSt s w with U := u, V := v, M := M }

/-- The initial-code test read from the oracle: decider `1` accepts `⟨x, ⟨bits u, bits s⟩⟩`. -/
def InitO (orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool) (s u : ℕ) : Prop :=
  orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s))) = true

/-- `InitO orc x s u` holds exactly when decider `1` accepts `⟨x, ⟨bits u, bits s⟩⟩`:
`orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (bits u) (bits s))) = true`. -/
theorem initO_iff_orc {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s u : ℕ} :
    InitO orc x s u ↔ orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s))) = true :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The accepting-code test read from the oracle: decider `2` accepts
`⟨x, ⟨bits v, bits s⟩⟩`. -/
def AccO (orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool) (s v : ℕ) : Prop :=
  orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s))) = true

/-- `AccO orc x s v` holds exactly when decider `2` accepts `⟨x, ⟨bits v, bits s⟩⟩`:
`orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (bits v) (bits s))) = true`. -/
theorem accO_iff_orc {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s v : ℕ} :
    AccO orc x s v ↔ orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s))) = true :=
  Iff.rfl

section Outer

variable {s w u v M : ℕ}

/-- The `U` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_U : (outerSt s w u v M).U = u := rfl
/-- The `V` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_V : (outerSt s w u v M).V = v := rfl
/-- The `M` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_M : (outerSt s w u v M).M = M := rfl
/-- The `I` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_I : (outerSt s w u v M).I = 0 := rfl
/-- The `K` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_K : (outerSt s w u v M).K = 2 ^ w := rfl
/-- The `w` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_w : (outerSt s w u v M).w = w := rfl
/-- The `s` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_s : (outerSt s w u v M).s = s := rfl

/-- **The outer search's register files, as registers**: the setup's file with the candidate
registers `U`, `V` and `M` written. -/
theorem outerSt_toV (s w u v M : ℕ) : (outerSt s w u v M).toV =
    Function.update (Function.update (Function.update (setSt s w).toV rU u) rV v) rM M := by
  rw [St.upd_U, St.upd_V, St.upd_M]
  rfl

/-- The register files of the outer search are bounded by `2 ^ (w · w)`. -/
lemma outerSt_bd (hsw : s ≤ w) (hu : u ≤ 2 ^ w) (hv : v ≤ 2 ^ w) (hM : M ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    (outerSt s w u v M).Bd (2 ^ (w * w)) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  simp only [St.Bd, outerSt, setSt, St.zero]
  omega

/-- The register files of the outer search, with the level set to `w`, meet the invariant
of the root level. -/
lemma outerSt_inv (hu : u < 2 ^ w) (hv : v < 2 ^ w) (hM : M ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    Inv s w w { outerSt s w u v M with I := w } :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, hu, hv, hM, rfl,
    by simp [outerSt, setSt, St.zero], by simp [outerSt, setSt, St.zero]⟩

end Outer

variable {E : ℕ} {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s w : ℕ}

open Classical in
/-- **The inner search**: from `OV` with candidate initial code `u` and counter `v`, the
machine answers whether some accepting code `v' ∈ [v, 2 ^ w)` has
`Reach (2 ^ w) R w u v'`, and otherwise continues as from `NU` (answering `b₀`).

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `2 ^ w - v`. At `v = 2 ^ w` the machine clears `V` and goes
to `NU`. Below, it asks decider `2` about `v`; on acceptance it sets `I := w` and runs the
recursion (`call_spec`), accepting if it answers `true`; otherwise it moves to `v + 1`. -/
theorem outerV_run (hsw : s ≤ w) (u : ℕ) (hu : u < 2 ^ w) (b₀ : Bool)
    (hNU : ∀ M ≤ 2 ^ w, AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some .NU, (outerSt s w u 0 M).toV, none) b₀) :
    ∀ k v M, v + k = 2 ^ w → M ≤ 2 ^ w →
      AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .OV, (outerSt s w u v M).toV, none)
        (decide (∃ v', v ≤ v' ∧ v' < 2 ^ w ∧ AccO orc x s v' ∧
          Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v') || b₀) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v M hk hM
    have hbd := outerSt_bd hsw hu.le (le_of_eq (by omega)) hM
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep_jeq (show A E .OV = _ from rfl), outerSt_V, outerSt_K,
      if_pos (show v = 2 ^ w by omega)]
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep_clr (show A E .OVend = _ from rfl)]
    rw [decide_eq_false (by rintro ⟨v', h1, h2, -⟩; omega), Bool.false_or]
    exact hNU M hM
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v M hk hM
    have hv : v < 2 ^ w := by omega
    have hbd := outerSt_bd hsw hu.le hv.le hM
    obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
    have shift : ∀ (hn : ¬ (AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v)) (M' : ℕ),
        M' ≤ 2 ^ w → AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
          (some .NV, (outerSt s w u v M').toV, none)
          (decide (∃ v', v ≤ v' ∧ v' < 2 ^ w ∧ AccO orc x s v' ∧
            Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v') || b₀) := by
      intro hn M' hM'
      refine AHalt.step (gb_of (outerSt_bd hsw hu.le hv.le hM') _) ?_
      regs [astep_inc (show A E .NV = _ from rfl), outerSt_V]
      have e := exists_shift (R₁ := fun m => AccO orc x s m)
        (R₂ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u m) (a := v) (K := 2 ^ w) hn
      beta_reduce at e
      rw [← decide_eq_decide.mpr e]
      exact ih (v + 1) M' (by omega) hM'
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep_jeq (show A E .OV = _ from rfl), outerSt_V, outerSt_K,
      if_neg (show v ≠ 2 ^ w by omega)]
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    simp only [astep_call (show A E .OVc = _ from rfl), vword_whole₂]
    regs [outerSt_V, outerSt_s]
    by_cases ha : AccO orc x s v
    · have ha' : orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s))) = true := ha
      rw [if_pos ha']
      -- `root`: set `I := w` and run the recursion
      refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
      regs [astep_clr (show A E .root = _ from rfl)]
      refine (cp_run .rootW _ (by simp only [St.Bd, outerSt, setSt, St.zero]; omega) rfl
        (by regs [cpDst, cpSrc]; simp only [outerSt, setSt, St.zero]; omega)).halt ?_
      regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit]
      obtain ⟨M', hM', hc⟩ := call_spec (E := E) (orc := orc) (x := x) hsw w le_rfl _
        (outerSt_inv (s := s) hu hv hM)
      refine contH (st' := { outerSt s w u v M with I := w }) (by ext <;> simp [outerSt, setSt,
        St.zero]) (hc.halt ?_)
      dsimp only
      have hbd' : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w)) { outerSt s w u v M' with I := w } := by
        simp only [St.Bd, outerSt, setSt, St.zero]; omega
      refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd' _) ?_
      regs [astep_jeq (show A E (.rt _) = _ from rfl), outerSt_U, outerSt_V, outerSt_w, if_true]
      by_cases hr : Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v
      · simp only [hr, decide_true, ↓reduceIte]
        rw [decide_eq_true ⟨v, le_rfl, hv, ha, hr⟩, Bool.true_or]
        exact AHalt.ret rfl (gb_of hbd' _)
      · simp only [hr, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte]
        refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd' _) ?_
        regs [astep_clr (show A E .rootF = _ from rfl)]
        exact shift (fun hh => hr hh.2) M' hM'
    · have ha' : ¬ orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s))) = true := ha
      rw [if_neg ha']
      exact shift (fun hh => ha hh.1) M hM

open Classical in
/-- **The outer search**: from `OU` with candidate `u` (and `V = 0`), the machine answers
whether some initial code `u' ∈ [u, 2 ^ w)` reaches some accepting code `v < 2 ^ w` by
midpoint reachability at level `w`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `2 ^ w - u`. At `u = 2 ^ w` the machine rejects. Below, it
asks decider `1` about `u`; on acceptance it runs the inner search (`outerV_run`), which
falls through to `u + 1` (the induction hypothesis, through `NU`); otherwise it moves to
`u + 1` directly. -/
theorem outerU_run (hsw : s ≤ w) : ∀ k u M, u + k = 2 ^ w → M ≤ 2 ^ w →
    AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .OU, (outerSt s w u 0 M).toV, none)
      (decide (∃ u', u ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ w ∧ InitO orc x s u' ∧
        ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u' v)) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro u M hk hM
    have hbd := outerSt_bd hsw (le_of_eq (by omega)) (Nat.zero_le _) hM
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep_jeq (show A E .OU = _ from rfl), outerSt_U, outerSt_K,
      if_pos (show u = 2 ^ w by omega)]
    rw [decide_eq_false (by rintro ⟨u', h1, h2, -⟩; omega)]
    exact AHalt.ret rfl (gb_of hbd _)
  | succ k ih =>
    intro u M hk hM
    have hu : u < 2 ^ w := by omega
    have hbd := outerSt_bd hsw hu.le (Nat.zero_le _) hM
    have hNU : ∀ M' ≤ 2 ^ w, AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
        (some .NU, (outerSt s w u 0 M').toV, none)
        (decide (∃ u', u + 1 ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ w ∧ InitO orc x s u' ∧
          ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u' v)) := by
      intro M' hM'
      refine AHalt.step (gb_of (outerSt_bd hsw hu.le (Nat.zero_le _) hM') _) ?_
      regs [astep_inc (show A E .NU = _ from rfl), outerSt_U]
      exact ih (u + 1) M' (by omega) hM'
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep_jeq (show A E .OU = _ from rfl), outerSt_U, outerSt_K,
      if_neg (show u ≠ 2 ^ w by omega)]
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    simp only [astep_call (show A E .OUc = _ from rfl), vword_whole₂]
    regs [outerSt_U, outerSt_s]
    by_cases hi : InitO orc x s u
    · have hi' : orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s))) = true := hi
      rw [if_pos hi']
      have h := outerV_run hsw u hu _ hNU (2 ^ w) 0 M (by omega) hM
      have e : decide (∃ u', u ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ w ∧ InitO orc x s u' ∧
          ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u' v) =
          (decide (∃ v', 0 ≤ v' ∧ v' < 2 ^ w ∧ AccO orc x s v' ∧
            Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v') ||
          decide (∃ u', u + 1 ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ w ∧ InitO orc x s u' ∧
            ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u' v)) := by
        rw [Bool.eq_iff_iff]
        simp only [Bool.or_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq]
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨u', h1, h2, h3, v, hv, h4, h5⟩
          rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le h1 with rfl | h1
          · exact Or.inl ⟨v, Nat.zero_le _, hv, h4, h5⟩
          · exact Or.inr ⟨u', h1, h2, h3, v, hv, h4, h5⟩
        · rintro (⟨v, -, hv, h4, h5⟩ | ⟨u', h1, h2, h3, h4⟩)
          · exact ⟨u, le_rfl, hu, hi, v, hv, h4, h5⟩
          · exact ⟨u', by omega, h2, h3, h4⟩
      rw [e]
      exact h
    · have hi' : ¬ orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s))) = true := hi
      rw [if_neg hi']
      have e := exists_shift (R₁ := fun m => InitO orc x s m)
        (R₂ := fun m => ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w m v)
        (a := u) (K := 2 ^ w) (fun hh => hi hh.1)
      beta_reduce at e
      rw [← decide_eq_decide.mpr e]
      exact hNU M hM

open Classical in
/-- **The run of the Savitch machine** [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.14]: with
`n = |x|`, `s = (n + 2) ^ E` and `w = (n + 2) ^ (2E)`, the machine `A E` (with `E ≥ 1`),
started with all registers clear and decider `0` answering length queries, answers whether
some initial code `u < 2 ^ w` reaches some accepting code `v < 2 ^ w` by midpoint
reachability at level `w`, through register values at most `2 ^ (w · w)`.

**Proof sketch.** `setup_run` followed by `outerU_run` from `u = 0`. -/
theorem savitch_halts (hE : 1 ≤ E)
    (hq : ∀ k ≤ x.length, orc 0 (pairEncode x (Nat.bits k)) = decide (k < x.length)) :
    AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) * (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E))))
      (some .scan, fun _ => 0, none)
      (decide (∃ u < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), InitO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) u ∧
        ∃ v < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), AccO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) v ∧
          Reach (2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) (Rel orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E))
            ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) u v)) := by
  have hsw : (x.length + 2) ^ E ≤ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  obtain ⟨-, f2⟩ := size_facts ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E))
  rw [St.toV_zero]
  refine (setup_run hE hq f2).halt ?_
  have h := outerU_run (E := E) (orc := orc) (x := x) hsw _ 0 0 (zero_add _) (Nat.zero_le _)
  have e : (∃ u', 0 ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) ∧
      InitO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) u' ∧
      ∃ v < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), AccO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) v ∧
        Reach (2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) (Rel orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E))
          ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) u' v) ↔
      ∃ u < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), InitO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) u ∧
        ∃ v < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), AccO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) v ∧
          Reach (2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) (Rel orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E))
            ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) u v :=
    ⟨fun ⟨u, _, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨u, h1, h2⟩, fun ⟨u, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨u, Nat.zero_le _, h1, h2⟩⟩
  rw [decide_eq_decide.mpr e] at h
  exact h

end SavitchARM

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
