Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Run
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Reach

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The midpoint recursion of the Savitch register machine

The recursive part of `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A` computes midpoint reachability:
started at label `cl` on a node `(U, V)` at level `I = i`, with any stack contents of the
right size below it, the machine returns at label `rt b` with `b` the truth value of
`Reach (2 ^ w) R i U V` — with the same registers, except the scratch midpoint register `M`
(`Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec`). Here `R` is the step relation answered by
decider `3` on codes at radius `s`.

The proof is an induction on the level, mirroring the recursion of [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of
Theorem 4.14]: at a positive level the midpoint loop (`loop_spec`) descends into the first
half (`desc1`, pushing `(V, 0)`), and, if that half is reachable, into the second half
(`desc2`, pushing `(U, 1)`); every return pops the frame it pushed (`pop_run`) and dispatches
on its phase bit. The stack invariant `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv` bounds the
`w`-bit-digit stack `SE` by `2 ^ (w (w - i))` and the phase stack `SP` by `2 ^ (w - i)`, so
every register stays below `2 ^ (w · w)`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel` — the step relation read from the oracle, with its
  defining equation `rel_iff_orc`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv` — the register invariant at a level.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec` — the recursion computes `Reach`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2.1, Theorem 4.14.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

namespace SavitchARM

open Turing

/-- **The step relation read from the oracle**: decider `3` accepts
`⟨x, ⟨bits u, ⟨bits v, bits s⟩⟩⟩`. -/
def Rel (orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool) (s u v : ℕ) : Prop :=
  orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s)))) = true

/-- `Rel orc x s u v` holds exactly when decider `3` accepts `⟨x, ⟨bits u, ⟨bits v, bits s⟩⟩⟩`:
`orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (bits u) (pairEncode (bits v) (bits s)))) = true`. -/
theorem rel_iff_orc {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s u v : ℕ} :
    Rel orc x s u v ↔
      orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s)))) =
        true :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- **The register invariant at level `i`**: the setup registers and the scratch registers
are clear, the radius, width and code bound are in place, the node's codes are below
`2 ^ w`, the midpoint is at most `2 ^ w`, and the two stacks hold at most `w - i` frames. -/
structure Inv (s w i : ℕ) (st : St) : Prop where
  /-- the input-length counter is clear -/
  hn : st.n = 0
  /-- the base register is clear -/
  ha : st.a = 0
  /-- the exponent counter is clear -/
  hX : st.X = 0
  /-- the power accumulator is clear -/
  hP : st.P = 0
  /-- the scratch register `T` is clear -/
  hT : st.T = 0
  /-- the scratch register `Z` is clear -/
  hZ : st.Z = 0
  /-- the loop counter is clear -/
  hC : st.C = 0
  /-- the scratch register `Q` is clear -/
  hQ : st.Q = 0
  /-- the popped-endpoint register is clear -/
  hE : st.E = 0
  /-- the radius is `s` -/
  hs : st.s = s
  /-- the width is `w` -/
  hw : st.w = w
  /-- the code bound is `2 ^ w` -/
  hK : st.K = 2 ^ w
  /-- the source code is below `2 ^ w` -/
  hU : st.U < 2 ^ w
  /-- the target code is below `2 ^ w` -/
  hV : st.V < 2 ^ w
  /-- the midpoint is at most `2 ^ w` -/
  hM : st.M ≤ 2 ^ w
  /-- the level is `i` -/
  hI : st.I = i
  /-- the endpoint stack holds at most `w - i` digits of `w` bits -/
  hSE : st.SE < 2 ^ (w * (w - i))
  /-- the phase stack holds at most `w - i` bits -/
  hSP : st.SP < 2 ^ (w - i)

/-- The basic size facts: `w ≤ 2 ^ w ≤ 2 ^ (w · w)`. -/
lemma size_facts (w : ℕ) : w < 2 ^ w ∧ 2 ^ w ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) :=
  ⟨Nat.lt_two_pow_self, Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (Nat.le_mul_self w)⟩

/-- **The invariant bounds the registers** by `2 ^ (w · w)`. -/
lemma Inv.bd {s w i : ℕ} {st : St} (h : Inv s w i st) (hsw : s ≤ w) (hi : i ≤ w) :
    st.Bd (2 ^ (w * w)) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have g1 : 2 ^ (w * (w - i)) ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega))
  have g2 : 2 ^ (w - i) ≤ 2 ^ w := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
  have := h.hn; have := h.ha; have := h.hX; have := h.hP; have := h.hT; have := h.hZ
  have := h.hC; have := h.hQ; have := h.hE; have := h.hs; have := h.hw; have := h.hK
  have := h.hU; have := h.hV; have := h.hM; have := h.hI; have := h.hSE; have := h.hSP
  simp only [St.Bd]
  omega

/-- **Pushing a digit keeps the stack within one more frame**: `SE < 2 ^ (w (w - (i + 1)))`
and `v < 2 ^ w` give `SE · 2 ^ w + v < 2 ^ (w (w - i))`. -/
lemma push_lt {w i SE v : ℕ} (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (hSE : SE < 2 ^ (w * (w - (i + 1))))
    (hv : v < 2 ^ w) : SE * 2 ^ w + v < 2 ^ (w * (w - i)) := by
  have e : w * (w - i) = w * (w - (i + 1)) + w := by
    rw [show w - i = w - (i + 1) + 1 by omega, Nat.mul_succ]
  rw [e, pow_add]
  have : (SE + 1) * 2 ^ w ≤ 2 ^ (w * (w - (i + 1))) * 2 ^ w :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hSE
  rw [Nat.add_mul, one_mul] at this
  omega

/-- Pushing a phase bit keeps the phase stack within one more frame. -/
lemma pushP_lt {w i SP : ℕ} (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (hSP : SP < 2 ^ (w - (i + 1))) :
    2 * SP + 1 < 2 ^ (w - i) := by
  rw [show w - i = w - (i + 1) + 1 by omega, pow_succ]
  omega

variable {E : ℕ} {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s w : ℕ}

open Classical in
/-- **The base case**: at level `0` the machine answers `U = V ∨ R U V`.

**Proof sketch.** `cl` sees `I = 0` and calls decider `3` on `⟨x, ⟨bits U, ⟨bits V, bits s⟩⟩⟩`;
on a negative answer it compares `U` with `V`. -/
theorem base_spec (hsw : s ≤ w) (st : St) (h : Inv s w 0 st) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .cl, st.toV, none)
      (some (.rt (decide (Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) 0 st.U st.V))), st.toV, none) := by
  have hbd := h.bd hsw (Nat.zero_le _)
  refine step_of hbd ?_
  regs [astep_jz (show A E .cl = _ from rfl), h.hI, ↓reduceIte]
  refine step_of hbd ?_
  simp only [astep_call (show A E .base = _ from rfl), vword_whole₃]
  regs [h.hs]
  by_cases hr : Rel orc x s st.U st.V
  · have hr' : orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits st.U)
        (pairEncode (Nat.bits st.V) (Nat.bits s)))) = true := hr
    rw [if_pos hr', decide_eq_true (show Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) 0 st.U st.V from Or.inr hr)]
    exact AReach.refl _
  · have hr' : ¬ orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits st.U)
        (pairEncode (Nat.bits st.V) (Nat.bits s)))) = true := hr
    rw [if_neg hr']
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep_jeq (show A E .baseEq = _ from rfl)]
    by_cases he : st.U = st.V
    · rw [if_pos he, decide_eq_true (show Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) 0 st.U st.V from Or.inl he)]
      exact AReach.refl _
    · rw [if_neg he, decide_eq_false (show ¬ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) 0 st.U st.V by
        rintro (h1 | h1) <;> contradiction)]
      exact AReach.refl _

/-- Close a register-file bound from the unfolded bounds in context. -/
scoped macro "bdt" : tactic => `(tactic| (simp only [St.Bd]; omega))

variable (E orc x s w) in
open Classical in
/-- **The recursion is correct at level `i`**: from `cl` on any register file meeting the
invariant at level `i`, the machine reaches `rt b`, `b` the truth value of
`Reach (2 ^ w) R i U V`, changing only the midpoint register (to a value at most `2 ^ w`). -/
def CallOK (i : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ st, Inv s w i st → ∃ M', M' ≤ 2 ^ w ∧
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .cl, st.toV, none)
      (some (.rt (decide (Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U st.V))),
        St.toV { st with M := M' }, none)

open Classical in
/-- **The first descent**: from `loop` at level `i + 1` with midpoint `m = M < 2 ^ w`, the
machine pushes `(V, 0)`, evaluates the first half `(U, m)` at level `i`, pops the frame, and
reaches `cp (push true)` if the first half is reachable and `a0F` otherwise, with `V = m`
and the popped endpoint in `E`.

**Proof sketch.** `pushV_run`, the move of `M` into `V` and the decrement of `I`; the
recursion at level `i` (`CallOK`); at `rt b` the level is below `w`, so `pop_run` restores
`SE` and returns the saved `V` in `E`; `I` is incremented, the even phase stack selects
`h0`, which halves it back. -/
theorem desc1 (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (IH : CallOK E orc x s w i) (st : St)
    (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st) (hm : st.M < 2 ^ w) :
    ∃ M1, M1 ≤ 2 ^ w ∧ AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .loop, st.toV, none)
      (some (if decide (Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U st.M) then .cp (.push true) 0
        else .a0F), St.toV { st with V := st.M, M := M1, E := st.V }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hbd := h.bd hsw hi
  have hSE1 := push_lt hi h.hSE h.hV
  have hSP1 := pushP_lt hi h.hSP
  have g1 : 2 ^ (w * (w - i)) ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega))
  have g2 : 2 ^ (w - i) ≤ 2 ^ w := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
  have h3 : Inv s w i
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.V, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := 0, I := i } :=
    ⟨h.hn, h.ha, h.hX, h.hP, h.hT, h.hZ, h.hC, h.hQ, h.hE, h.hs, h.hw, h.hK, h.hU, hm,
      Nat.zero_le _, rfl, hSE1, by show 2 * st.SP < 2 ^ (w - i); omega⟩
  obtain ⟨M1, hM1, hc⟩ := IH _ h3
  dsimp only at hc
  refine ⟨M1, hM1, ?_⟩
  have hw := h.hw
  -- `loop`: the midpoint is below `K`
  refine step_of hbd ?_
  regs [astep_jeq (show A E .loop = _ from rfl),
    if_neg (show st.M ≠ st.K by rw [h.hK]; exact hm.ne)]
  -- push `(V, 0)`
  refine (pushV_run st h.hC h.hT h.hZ hbd (by rw [hw]; omega) (by omega)).trans ?_
  have hbd1 : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ st.w + st.V, V := 0, SP := 2 * st.SP } := by
    have := hbd; simp only [St.Bd] at this ⊢; rw [hw]; omega
  have hMB : st.M ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) := by omega
  refine (mv_run .descM _ hbd1 (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  have hbd2 : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ st.w + st.V, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := 0 } := by
    have := hbd; simp only [St.Bd] at this ⊢; rw [hw]; omega
  refine step_of hbd2 ?_
  regs [astep_dec (show A E .descDec = _ from rfl)]
  refine cont (by ext <;> simp [hw, h.hI]) (hc.trans ?_)
  -- `rt b`: not the root, pop the frame
  have hbd4 := (h3.bd hsw (by omega))
  have hbd4' : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.V, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := M1, I := i } := by
    simp only [St.Bd] at hbd4 ⊢; omega
  refine step_of hbd4' ?_
  regs [astep_jeq (show A E (.rt _) = _ from rfl), if_neg (show i ≠ st.w by omega)]
  refine (pop_run _
    { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.V, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := M1, I := i }
    st.SE st.V h.hC h.hT h.hZ h.hQ h.hE hbd4' (by simp [hw]) (by simp [hw]; exact h.hV)).trans ?_
  have hbd5 : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := M1, I := i, E := st.V } := by
    have := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right st.SE (Nat.two_pow_pos w)
    simp only [St.Bd] at hbd4 ⊢; have := h.hV; omega
  refine step_of hbd5 ?_
  regs [astep_inc (show A E (.incI _) = _ from rfl)]
  have hbd6 : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := M1, I := i + 1, E := st.V } := by
    simp only [St.Bd] at hbd5 ⊢; omega
  refine step_of hbd6 ?_
  regs [astep_jodd (show A E (.par _) = _ from rfl), Nat.mul_mod_right, zero_ne_one, if_false]
  refine step_of hbd6 ?_
  regs [astep_half (show A E (.h0 _) = _ from rfl)]
  refine reach_of_eq (AReach.refl _) ?_
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hI]

open Classical in
/-- **The second descent**: from `cp (push true)` after a reachable first half (`V = m`,
`E` the saved target), the machine pushes `(U, 1)`, evaluates the second half `(m, V)` at
level `i`, pops the frame, and reaches `a1T` if the second half is reachable and `a1F`
otherwise, with `U = m` and the saved source in `E`.

**Proof sketch.** `pushU_run`, the increment of the phase stack, the moves `V → U`,
`E → V` and the decrement of `I`; the recursion at level `i`; `pop_run` restores `SE` and
returns the saved `U` in `E`; the odd phase stack selects `h1`, which halves it back. -/
theorem desc2 (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (IH : CallOK E orc x s w i) (st : St)
    (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st) (hm : st.M < 2 ^ w) (M1 : ℕ) (hM1 : M1 ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    ∃ M2, M2 ≤ 2 ^ w ∧ AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some (.cp (.push true) 0), St.toV { st with V := st.M, M := M1, E := st.V }, none)
      (some (if decide (Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.M st.V) then .a1T else .a1F),
        St.toV { st with U := st.M, M := M2, E := st.U }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hbd := h.bd hsw hi
  have hB := hbd
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB
  have hSE1 := push_lt hi h.hSE h.hU
  have hSP1 := pushP_lt hi h.hSP
  have g1 : 2 ^ (w * (w - i)) ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega))
  have g2 : 2 ^ (w - i) ≤ 2 ^ w := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
  have hle := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right st.SE (Nat.two_pow_pos w)
  have h3 : Inv s w i
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.U, U := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP + 1, M := M1, I := i } :=
    ⟨h.hn, h.ha, h.hX, h.hP, h.hT, h.hZ, h.hC, h.hQ, h.hE, h.hs, h.hw, h.hK, hm, h.hV,
      hM1, rfl, hSE1, hSP1⟩
  obtain ⟨M2, hM2, hc⟩ := IH _ h3
  dsimp only at hc
  refine ⟨M2, hM2, ?_⟩
  have hw := h.hw
  have hV := h.hV
  have hU := h.hU
  have hSEw : st.SE * 2 ^ st.w = st.SE * 2 ^ w := by rw [hw]
  -- push `(U, 1)`
  refine (pushU_run { st with V := st.M, M := M1, E := st.V } h.hC h.hT h.hZ (by bdt)
    (by show st.SE * 2 ^ st.w + st.U ≤ _; rw [hw]; omega)
    (by show 2 * st.SP ≤ _; omega)).trans ?_
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_inc (show A E .pushInc = _ from rfl)]
  refine (mv_run .a0T1 _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine (mv_run .a0T2 _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_dec (show A E .a0Dec = _ from rfl)]
  refine cont (by ext <;> simp [hw, h.hI, h.hE]) (hc.trans ?_)
  -- `rt b`: not the root, pop the frame
  have hB3 := h3.bd hsw (by omega)
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB3
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_jeq (show A E (.rt _) = _ from rfl), if_neg (show i ≠ st.w by omega)]
  refine (pop_run _
    { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.U, U := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP + 1, M := M2, I := i }
    st.SE st.U h.hC h.hT h.hZ h.hQ h.hE (by bdt) (by simp [hw]) (by simp [hw]; exact hU)).trans ?_
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_inc (show A E (.incI _) = _ from rfl)]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_jodd (show A E (.par _) = _ from rfl), Nat.mul_add_mod, if_true]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_half (show A E (.h1 _) = _ from rfl)]
  refine reach_of_eq (AReach.refl _) ?_
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hI]
  omega

/-- **The tail after an unreachable first half**: from `a0F`, the machine sets `M := V + 1`,
moves the saved target back into `V`, and returns to `loop`.

**Proof sketch.** A clear, two moves and an increment. -/
theorem tail0F (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (st : St) (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st)
    (hm : st.M < 2 ^ w) (M1 : ℕ) (hM1 : M1 ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some .a0F, St.toV { st with V := st.M, M := M1, E := st.V }, none)
      (some .loop, St.toV { st with M := st.M + 1 }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hB := h.bd hsw hi
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB
  have hV := h.hV
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_clr (show A E .a0F = _ from rfl)]
  refine (mv_run .a0FM _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_inc (show A E .a0Finc = _ from rfl)]
  refine reach_of_eq (mv_run .a0FV _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)) ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hE]

/-- **The tail after a reachable second half**: from `a1T`, the machine moves the saved
source back into `U` and answers `true`.

**Proof sketch.** A clear and a move. -/
theorem tail1T (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (st : St) (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st)
    (M2 : ℕ) (hM2 : M2 ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some .a1T, St.toV { st with U := st.M, M := M2, E := st.U }, none)
      (some (.rt true), St.toV { st with M := M2 }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hB := h.bd hsw hi
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB
  have hU := h.hU
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_clr (show A E .a1T = _ from rfl)]
  refine reach_of_eq (mv_run .a1TU _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)) ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hE]

/-- **The tail after an unreachable second half**: from `a1F`, the machine sets
`M := U + 1`, moves the saved source back into `U`, and returns to `loop`.

**Proof sketch.** A clear, two moves and an increment. -/
theorem tail1F (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (st : St) (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st)
    (hm : st.M < 2 ^ w) (M2 : ℕ) (hM2 : M2 ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some .a1F, St.toV { st with U := st.M, M := M2, E := st.U }, none)
      (some .loop, St.toV { st with M := st.M + 1 }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hB := h.bd hsw hi
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB
  have hU := h.hU
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_clr (show A E .a1F = _ from rfl)]
  refine (mv_run .a1FM _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep_inc (show A E .a1Finc = _ from rfl)]
  refine reach_of_eq (mv_run .a1FU _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)) ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hE]

/-- The invariant does not constrain the midpoint beyond `M ≤ 2 ^ w`. -/
lemma Inv.setM {s w i : ℕ} {st : St} (h : Inv s w i st) {M' : ℕ} (hM : M' ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    Inv s w i { st with M := M' } :=
  ⟨h.hn, h.ha, h.hX, h.hP, h.hT, h.hZ, h.hC, h.hQ, h.hE, h.hs, h.hw, h.hK, h.hU, h.hV, hM,
    h.hI, h.hSE, h.hSP⟩

/-- Skipping a failing candidate does not change a bounded search. -/
lemma exists_shift {R₁ R₂ : ℕ → Prop} {a K : ℕ} (h : ¬ (R₁ a ∧ R₂ a)) :
    (∃ m, a + 1 ≤ m ∧ m < K ∧ R₁ m ∧ R₂ m) ↔ (∃ m, a ≤ m ∧ m < K ∧ R₁ m ∧ R₂ m) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨m, h1, h2, h3⟩
    exact ⟨m, by omega, h2, h3⟩
  · rintro ⟨m, h1, h2, h3⟩
    rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le h1 with rfl | h1
    · exact absurd h3 h
    · exact ⟨m, h1, h2, h3⟩

open Classical in
/-- **The midpoint loop**: from `loop` at level `i + 1` with midpoint `M`, the machine
answers at `rt b` whether some `m` with `M ≤ m < 2 ^ w` has both halves reachable at level
`i`, changing only `M`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `2 ^ w - M`. At `M = 2 ^ w` the machine answers `false`.
Below, the first descent (`desc1`) evaluates the first half; if it fails, `tail0F` moves to
`M + 1`; otherwise the second descent (`desc2`) evaluates the second half, and `tail1T`
answers `true` or `tail1F` moves to `M + 1`. Moving past a failing candidate leaves the
answer unchanged (`exists_shift`). -/
theorem loop_spec (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (IH : CallOK E orc x s w i) :
    ∀ k (st : St), Inv s w (i + 1) st → st.M + k = 2 ^ w → ∃ M', M' ≤ 2 ^ w ∧
      AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .loop, st.toV, none)
        (some (.rt (decide (∃ m, st.M ≤ m ∧ m < 2 ^ w ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U m ∧
          Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i m st.V))), St.toV { st with M := M' }, none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro st h hk
    refine ⟨st.M, h.hM, ?_⟩
    refine step_of (h.bd hsw hi) ?_
    regs [astep_jeq (show A E .loop = _ from rfl), if_pos (show st.M = st.K by rw [h.hK]; omega)]
    rw [decide_eq_false (by rintro ⟨m, h1, h2, -⟩; omega)]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro st h hk
    have hm : st.M < 2 ^ w := by omega
    have hnext := h.setM (M' := st.M + 1) (by omega)
    obtain ⟨M1, hM1, h1⟩ := desc1 hsw i hi IH st h hm
    by_cases r1 : Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U st.M
    · simp only [r1, decide_true, if_true] at h1
      obtain ⟨M2, hM2, h2⟩ := desc2 hsw i hi IH st h hm M1 hM1
      by_cases r2 : Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.M st.V
      · simp only [r2, decide_true, if_true] at h2
        refine ⟨M2, hM2, ?_⟩
        rw [decide_eq_true ⟨st.M, le_rfl, hm, r1, r2⟩]
        exact h1.trans (h2.trans (tail1T hsw i hi st h M2 hM2))
      · simp only [r2, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false] at h2
        obtain ⟨M', hM', h3⟩ := ih _ hnext (by show st.M + 1 + k = 2 ^ w; omega)
        dsimp only at h3
        have e := exists_shift (R₁ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U m)
          (R₂ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i m st.V) (a := st.M) (K := 2 ^ w)
          (fun hh => r2 hh.2)
        beta_reduce at e
        rw [decide_eq_decide.mpr e] at h3
        exact ⟨M', hM', h1.trans (h2.trans ((tail1F hsw i hi st h hm M2 hM2).trans h3))⟩
    · simp only [r1, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false] at h1
      obtain ⟨M', hM', h3⟩ := ih _ hnext (by show st.M + 1 + k = 2 ^ w; omega)
      dsimp only at h3
      have e := exists_shift (R₁ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U m)
        (R₂ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i m st.V) (a := st.M) (K := 2 ^ w)
        (fun hh => r1 hh.1)
      beta_reduce at e
      rw [decide_eq_decide.mpr e] at h3
      exact ⟨M', hM', h1.trans ((tail0F hsw i hi st h hm M1 hM1).trans h3)⟩

/-- **The recursion computes midpoint reachability** [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of
Theorem 4.14]: for every level `i ≤ w`, from `cl` on a register file meeting the invariant at
level `i`, the machine reaches `rt b` with `b` the truth value of `Reach (2 ^ w) R i U V`,
changing only `M` (`CallOK`).

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `i`. Level `0` is `base_spec`. At level `i + 1`, `cl` clears
`M` and enters the midpoint loop (`loop_spec`, using the induction hypothesis for the two
descents); the loop's answer from `M = 0` is `Reach (2 ^ w) R (i + 1) U V` by definition. -/
theorem call_spec (hsw : s ≤ w) : ∀ i, i ≤ w → CallOK E orc x s w i := by
  intro i
  induction i with
  | zero =>
    intro _ st h
    exact ⟨st.M, h.hM, base_spec hsw st h⟩
  | succ i ih =>
    intro hi st h
    have IH := ih (by omega)
    have hbd := h.bd hsw hi
    obtain ⟨M', hM', hl⟩ := loop_spec hsw i hi IH (2 ^ w) _ (h.setM (M' := 0) (Nat.zero_le _))
      (by show 0 + 2 ^ w = 2 ^ w; omega)
    refine ⟨M', hM', ?_⟩
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep_jz (show A E .cl = _ from rfl), if_neg (show st.I ≠ 0 by rw [h.hI]; omega)]
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep_clr (show A E .lInit = _ from rfl)]
    dsimp only at hl
    have e : (∃ m, 0 ≤ m ∧ m < 2 ^ w ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U m ∧
        Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i m st.V) ↔ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) (i + 1) st.U st.V :=
      ⟨fun ⟨m, _, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨m, h1, h2⟩, fun ⟨m, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨m, Nat.zero_le _, h1, h2⟩⟩
    rw [decide_eq_decide.mpr e] at hl
    exact hl

end SavitchARM

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Recursion

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The setup and the outer search of the Savitch register machine

The non-recursive parts of `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A`. The setup (`setup_run`)
measures the input, computes the radius `s = (|x| + 2) ^ E`, the width
`w = (|x| + 2) ^ (2E)` and the code bound `K = 2 ^ w` by counting loops, leaving every other
register clear. The outer search (`outerU_run`, `outerV_run`) runs through the candidate
initial codes `U < K` and accepting codes `V < K` and evaluates the midpoint recursion at the
root level `w` for each candidate pair (`Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec`).

Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.14]; not itself a result of the book.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt` — the register files of the outer search.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setup_run` — the setup.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt_toV` — the register file after the setup, as registers.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run` — the outer search answers whether an initial
  and an accepting code are joined by midpoint reachability at level `w`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2.1, Theorem 4.14.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

namespace SavitchARM

open Turing

variable {E : ℕ} {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {B : ℕ}

/-! ## The setup -/

/-- Close a bound on a named register file, reducing its projections first. -/
scoped macro "sbd" : tactic =>
  `(tactic| ((try simp only [St.Bd, St.zero]) <;> (try dsimp only) <;>
    (try simp only [one_mul, zero_add, if_true, ↓reduceIte]) <;> omega))

/-- **Loading the constant `E`**: from `ld j` with `X = j`, the machine counts `X` up to `E`,
then sets `P := P + 1` and reaches `pw`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `E - j`. -/
theorem ld_run : ∀ (k j : ℕ) (hj : j < E + 1) (st : St), j + k = E → st.X = j → st.Bd B →
    E ≤ B → st.P + 1 ≤ B →
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x B) (some (.ld ⟨j, hj⟩), st.toV, none)
      (some .pw, St.toV { st with X := E, P := st.P + 1 }, none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro j hj st hk hX hbd hE hP
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep_inc (show A E (.ld ⟨j, hj⟩) = .inc rP .pw from
      dif_neg (show ¬ j < E by omega))]
    refine reach_of_eq (AReach.refl _) ?_
    congr 3
    ext <;> simp; omega
  | succ k ih =>
    intro j hj st hk hX hbd hE hP
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep_inc (show A E (.ld ⟨j, hj⟩) = .inc rX (.ld ⟨j + 1, by omega⟩) from
      dif_pos (show j < E by omega))]
    have hbd1 : St.Bd B { st with X := st.X + 1 } := by simp only [St.Bd] at hbd ⊢; omega
    refine reach_of_eq (ih (j + 1) (by omega) _ (by omega) (by simp [hX]) hbd1 hE hP) ?_
    rfl

/-- **The power loop**: from `pw` with `X = j` and `C = T = Z = 0`, the machine multiplies
`P` by `a ^ j`, clears `X`, and reaches `cp sP`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `j`: each round decrements `X` and multiplies `P` by `a`
(`mul_run`). -/
theorem pw_run : ∀ (j : ℕ) (st : St), st.X = j → st.C = 0 → st.T = 0 → st.Z = 0 → st.Bd B →
    1 ≤ st.a → st.P * st.a ^ j ≤ B →
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x B) (some .pw, st.toV, none)
      (some (.cp .sP 0), St.toV { st with X := 0, P := st.P * st.a ^ j }, none) := by
  intro j
  induction j with
  | zero =>
    intro st hX hC hT hZ hbd ha hb
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep_jz (show A E .pw = _ from rfl), hX, if_true]
    refine reach_of_eq (AReach.refl _) ?_
    congr 3
    ext <;> simp [hX]
  | succ j ih =>
    intro st hX hC hT hZ hbd ha hb
    have h1 : st.P ≤ st.P * st.a ^ (j + 1) :=
      Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (Nat.pow_pos (by omega))
    have h2 : st.P * st.a ≤ st.P * st.a ^ (j + 1) := by
      apply Nat.mul_le_mul_left
      calc st.a = st.a ^ 1 := (pow_one _).symm
        _ ≤ st.a ^ (j + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right ha (by omega)
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep_jz (show A E .pw = _ from rfl), hX, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, if_false]
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep_dec (show A E .pwDec = _ from rfl), hX, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have hbd1 : St.Bd B { st with X := j } := by simp only [St.Bd] at hbd ⊢; omega
    refine (mul_run false { st with X := j } hC hT hZ hbd1 (by simp; omega)).trans ?_
    simp only [mvExit, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
    have hbd2 : St.Bd B { st with X := j, P := st.P * st.a } := by
      simp only [St.Bd] at hbd ⊢; omega
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ rfl hC hT hZ hbd2 ha (by
      show st.P * st.a * st.a ^ j ≤ B
      rw [mul_assoc, ← pow_succ']; exact hb)) ?_
    congr 3
    ext <;> simp [pow_succ']
    ring

/-- **The register file after the setup**: radius `s`, width `w`, code bound `2 ^ w`, every
other register clear. -/
def setSt (s w : ℕ) : St := { St.zero with s := s, w := w, K := 2 ^ w }

/-- **The register file after the setup, as registers**: `s`, `w` and `2 ^ w` in the radius,
width and code-bound registers, every other register clear. -/
theorem setSt_toV (s w : ℕ) : (setSt s w).toV =
    Function.update (Function.update (Function.update (fun _ => 0) rs s) rw w) rK (2 ^ w) := by
  rw [St.toV_zero, St.upd_s, St.upd_w, St.upd_K]
  rfl

/-- **The setup** [AB09, §4.2.1: the radius and the vertex-code width are computed first]:
from `scan` with all registers clear, the machine reaches `OU` with radius
`s = (|x| + 2) ^ E`, width `w = (|x| + 2) ^ (2E)` and code bound `2 ^ w`, everything else
clear, through register values at most `B ≥ 2 ^ w`.

**Proof sketch.** Count `n = |x|` (`Complexity.LogProg.inputLength_loop`, asking decider `0`),
move it into `a` and add two, load `X = E` and `P = 1` (`ld_run`), take `P := a ^ E`
(`pw_run`), copy it into `s`, square `P` (`mul_run`), move it into `w`, clear `a`, and shift
`K = 1` left by `w` (`sh_run`). -/
theorem setup_run (hE : 1 ≤ E)
    (hq : ∀ k ≤ x.length, orc 0 (pairEncode x (Nat.bits k)) = decide (k < x.length))
    (hB : 2 ^ ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) ≤ B) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x B) (some .scan, St.zero.toV, none)
      (some .OU, (setSt ((x.length + 2) ^ E) ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E))).toV, none) := by
  have hw1 : (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) < 2 ^ ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
  have haE : x.length + 2 ≤ (x.length + 2) ^ E := by
    calc x.length + 2 = (x.length + 2) ^ 1 := (pow_one _).symm
      _ ≤ (x.length + 2) ^ E := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) hE
  have hEw : (x.length + 2) ^ E ≤ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  have hsq : (x.length + 2) ^ E * (x.length + 2) ^ E = (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) := by
    rw [← pow_add]; ring_nf
  have hEa : E < (x.length + 2) ^ E :=
    (Nat.lt_two_pow_self).trans_le (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by omega) _)
  -- count `n = |x|`
  have h1 := inputLength_loop (A E) orc x rn 0 .scan .incN (.mv .aN 0) rfl rfl hq B
    (by omega) St.zero.toV (fun r => by fin_cases r <;> simp [St.toV, St.zero])
    (by simp [St.zero])
  refine (h1.mono fun _ h => h).trans ?_
  regs [St.zero]
  refine (mv_run .aN _ (by sbd) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by sbd) ?_
  regs [astep_inc (show A E .incA1 = _ from rfl)]
  refine step_of (by sbd) ?_
  regs [astep_inc (show A E .incA2 = _ from rfl)]
  refine cont (st' := { St.zero with a := x.length + 2 }) (by ext <;> simp [St.zero]) ?_
  -- load `X = E`, `P = 1`
  refine (ld_run E 0 (by omega) _ (by omega) rfl (by sbd) (by omega) (by sbd)).trans ?_
  -- `P := a ^ E`
  refine (pw_run E _ rfl rfl rfl rfl (by sbd) (by sbd) (by sbd)).trans ?_
  -- `s := P`, `P := P · P`, `w := P`
  refine (cp_run .sP _ (by sbd) rfl (by regs [cpDst, cpSrc]; sbd)).trans ?_
  regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit, zero_add, one_mul]
  refine (mul_run true _ rfl rfl rfl (by sbd) (by sbd)).trans ?_
  simp only [mvExit, if_true]
  refine (mv_run .wP _ (by sbd) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; sbd)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by sbd) ?_
  regs [astep_clr (show A E .clrA = _ from rfl)]
  refine step_of (by sbd) ?_
  regs [astep_inc (show A E .kInit = _ from rfl), zero_add]
  -- `K := 2 ^ w`
  refine (cp_run .kW _ (by sbd) rfl (by regs [cpDst, cpSrc]; sbd)).trans ?_
  regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit, zero_add]
  refine reach_of_eq (sh_run .kK _ (by sbd) rfl
    (by regs [shReg]; simp only [St.zero, zero_add, one_mul, hsq]; omega)) ?_
  regs [shReg, shExit]
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [setSt, St.zero, hsq]

end SavitchARM

end Complexity.LogProg
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Oracle.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import Mathlib.Computability.Language
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Deterministic
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.StateRenaming
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CfgFacts

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Oracle Turing machines

An oracle Turing machine [AB09, §3.4, Definition 3.4; pulled forward to Chapter 1 to
validate the model architecture] is a multi-tape machine with one additional designated
*query tape* and three designated states `qQuery`, `qYes`, `qNo`. Whenever the machine
enters `qQuery`, the string currently written on the query tape is submitted to the oracle
`O`: in a single step the machine moves to `qYes` if the query is in `O` and to `qNo`
otherwise, with all tapes and heads unchanged.

## Design

This file is the architectural test of the `Action`/`Action.apply` split: an oracle machine
reuses the configurations `Turing.Cfg (k + 1)` (the query tape is the extra work tape, at
index `Fin.last k`) and the action application of the plain model, and differs *only* in how
the next action is chosen — the step function is parametrized by the oracle
`O : Language Symbol`. Time and space measures therefore transfer unchanged.

Definitional choices worth auditing:

* **The query string** (`OracleTM.queryString`) is read from cell `0` of the query tape
  rightward up to (excluding) the first blank cell; if the whole nonnegative half-tape is
  blank-free (possible for an arbitrary configuration, though not for one reachable from an
  initial configuration), the query is defined to be `[]`. [AB09] leaves the extraction
  convention implicit; this is one concrete faithful reading.
* **The answer step** changes only the state; heads and tapes stay put. Some texts
  instead erase the query tape on each answer. The two conventions are equivalent up to
  *polynomial* overhead, but **not** constant overhead: computing the parity of `n`
  distinct length-`n` queries takes `O(n)` steps with a persistent tape and `Ω(n²)`
  steps with auto-erasure (`audits/phase1-findings.md`, finding 3, case 12).
  Consequently, exact `DTIME`-level bounds must never be transferred across this
  convention; class-level results (`Pᴼ` etc.) are unaffected.
* `qYes`/`qNo` are ordinary states from the machine's point of view (its transition
  function handles them); only `qQuery` triggers special behavior. The machine may query
  repeatedly. This reading presumes the three special states are pairwise distinct,
  which the raw structure does not enforce (e.g. with `qYes = qQuery` the machine
  re-queries forever after a positive answer): results at the faithful interface assume
  `OracleTM.WellFormed`. Note that
  `q₀ = qQuery` is legitimate and deliberately allowed (the machine then submits the
  empty query on its first step).

## Main definitions

* `Turing.OracleTM` — the oracle machine. [AB09, Definition 3.4]
* `Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed` — the three special states are pairwise distinct; the
  standing hypothesis of the faithful interface (oracle complexity classes will require
  it).
* `Turing.OracleTM.step`, `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom` — semantics relative to an oracle.
* `Turing.OracleTM.relabel` (with `relabel_wellFormed`, `relabel_step`, `relabel_runFrom`,
  `relabel_computesInTime`) — transport along a state equivalence.
* `Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime` — output and time bound relative to an oracle.
* `Turing.Action.extend`, `Turing.Cfg.embedOracle`, `Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM` —
  the embedding of plain machines as oracle machines that never query (state renaming
  via `Turing.Action.mapState`, now in `TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.StateRenaming`).
* `Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle` — the converse direction: an oracle machine run
  with the empty oracle, as a plain `k + 1`-tape machine in exact lockstep.

## Main results (sanity checks for the architecture)

* `Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_ne_qQuery` — away from `qQuery`, the step does not depend
  on the oracle.
* `Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM_wellFormed` — the embedding produces well-formed
  machines.
* `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_ofMultiTapeTM` — an embedded plain machine runs in lockstep
  with the original, under every oracle.
* `Turing.OracleTM.computesInTime_ofMultiTapeTM` — hence its input/output behavior and
  time bounds are oracle-independent and agree with the plain machine's.
* `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_plainEmptyOracle` — the empty-oracle elimination runs in
  exact lockstep.
* `Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le` — in an initialized run, the query after `t`
  steps has length at most `t`.
* `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_workTapes_blank` — in an initialized run, cells at distance
  `≥ t` are still blank after `t` steps; the certificate that the no-blank fallback in
  `queryString` is unreachable from initialization.
* `Turing.OracleTM.step_radius`, `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_radius` — the radius bound:
  from a head within `n` of the origin with every cell at distance `≥ n` blank, after `s`
  steps the head is within `n + s` and every cell at distance `≥ n + s` is blank; the one
  shared argument behind the initialized invariants and the preloaded query bound (added
  2026-10-11, wave-1 statement gate, round 1, finding 2).
* `Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le_of_blank`, `Turing.OracleTM.queryString_eq_of_cells`
  — the extraction contract: a blank query cell bounds the query, and a query tape holding
  `w` from cell `0` with a blank at `|w|` reads back exactly `w` (the first promoted from
  C1c's private bound, backlog C1-P1; added 2026-10-11, B1).
* `Turing.OracleTM.step_of_halt`, `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'`,
  `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_add`, `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_of_halt`,
  `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_comm_of_step`, `Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime.mono`,
  `Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique` — the oracle run algebra, mirroring the
  plain machine's (added 2026-10-11, B1).
* `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_forall_ne_qQuery`, `Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_plainEmptyOracle`
  — a run that never sits in `qQuery` is oracle-independent from any configuration, and is
  then the run of the plain table `plainEmptyOracle`: the bridge through which the
  plain-machine library contracts apply to an oracle machine on its query-free segments
  (added 2026-10-11, B1).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§3.4: oracle machines; Definition 3.4.)
-/

namespace Turing

variable {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type*} {input : List Symbol}

/-- An oracle Turing machine with `k` ordinary work tapes, one query tape (the work tape
of index `Fin.last k` in its configurations `Cfg (k + 1)`), and designated query and
answer states. Finiteness of `State` is deferred exactly as for `MultiTapeTM`, and so is
distinctness of the three special states: the raw structure allows them to coincide
(with degenerate behavior, e.g. `qYes = qQuery` re-queries forever after a positive
answer), and the faithful interface imposes `OracleTM.WellFormed`.
[AB09, Definition 3.4] -/
structure OracleTM (k : ℕ) (Symbol State : Type*) where
  /-- initial state -/
  q₀ : State
  /-- entering this state submits the query tape's contents to the oracle -/
  qQuery : State
  /-- the state the oracle answer step moves to on a positive answer -/
  qYes : State
  /-- the state the oracle answer step moves to on a negative answer -/
  qNo : State
  /-- transition function on the `k + 1` work tapes (the last being the query tape);
  consulted in every state except `qQuery` -/
  tr (q : State) (input : Option Symbol) (work : Fin (k + 1) → Option Symbol) :
    Action (k + 1) Symbol State

namespace OracleTM

variable {M : OracleTM k Symbol State}

/-- Well-formedness of an oracle machine: the query state and the two answer states are
pairwise distinct. Without this, the advertised semantics degenerates: with
`qYes = qQuery` a positive answer re-queries the unchanged tape forever (a negative
answer may still reach a distinct `qNo` and halt normally), and with all three states
collapsed the machine loops once the common query state is reached (an initial state
elsewhere can still halt via the table without ever querying). Moreover `qYes = qNo`
alone makes the step function — hence every run — oblivious to the oracle. This is the
standing hypothesis of the faithful oracle interface —
oracle complexity classes will require it. `q₀ = qQuery` is deliberately allowed: such a
machine simply submits the empty query on its first step.
(`audits/phase1-findings.md`, finding 2.) -/
structure WellFormed (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) : Prop where
  /-- the query state is not the positive-answer state -/
  qQuery_ne_qYes : M.qQuery ≠ M.qYes
  /-- the query state is not the negative-answer state -/
  qQuery_ne_qNo : M.qQuery ≠ M.qNo
  /-- the two answer states are distinct -/
  qYes_ne_qNo : M.qYes ≠ M.qNo

/-- The index of the query tape among the `k + 1` work tapes. -/
def queryTapeIdx (k : ℕ) : Fin (k + 1) := Fin.last k

open Classical in
/-- The query string of a configuration: the contents of the query tape from cell `0`
rightward, up to (excluding) the first blank cell. If no blank cell exists on the
nonnegative half-tape — impossible in configurations reachable from an initial
configuration, but possible for an arbitrary one — the query is `[]`. -/
noncomputable def queryString (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) : List Symbol :=
  if h : ∃ n : ℕ, cfg.workTapes (queryTapeIdx k) (n : ℤ) = none then
    (List.range (Nat.find h)).filterMap fun n => cfg.workTapes (queryTapeIdx k) (n : ℤ)
  else []

open Classical in
/-- One step of the oracle machine `M` relative to the oracle `O`. In state `qQuery` the
machine moves to `qYes` or `qNo` according to whether the current query string is in `O`,
leaving tapes, head positions and output unchanged; in every other state it steps by its
transition function exactly like a plain machine. [AB09, §3.4] -/
noncomputable def step (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input :=
  match cfg.state with
  | none => cfg
  | some q =>
    if q = M.qQuery then
      { cfg with state := some (if queryString cfg ∈ O then M.qYes else M.qNo) }
    else
      (M.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).apply cfg

/-- The initial configuration of an oracle machine: all `k + 1` work tapes (including the
query tape) blank. -/
@[simp]
def initCfg (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol) :
    Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input :=
  Cfg.init M.q₀ input

/-- The configuration reached by running `M` with oracle `O` for `t` steps from `cfg`. -/
noncomputable def runFrom (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input :=
  (M.step O)^[t] cfg

/-- `M` with oracle `O` halts on `input` within `t` steps with `output` on its output
tape. Time-only, mirroring `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime`. -/
def ComputesInTime (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (input output : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (M.runFrom O (M.initCfg input) t).state = none ∧
  (M.runFrom O (M.initCfg input) t).output = output

/-- Away from the query state, a step of an oracle machine does not depend on the oracle. -/
theorem step_eq_of_ne_qQuery (O₁ O₂ : Language Symbol)
    {cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input} (h : cfg.state ≠ some M.qQuery) :
    M.step O₁ cfg = M.step O₂ cfg := by
  unfold step
  cases hs : cfg.state with
  | none => rfl
  | some q =>
    have hne : q ≠ M.qQuery := fun hq => h (by rw [hs, hq])
    dsimp only
    rw [if_neg hne, if_neg hne]

/-- A halted configuration is fixed by the oracle step, under every oracle: halting is
absorbing, as for plain machines (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt`). [AB09, §3.4] -/
@[simp]
theorem step_of_halt (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    {cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input} (h : cfg.state = none) : M.step O cfg = cfg := by
  unfold step; rw [h]

/-- One more step of an oracle run is one oracle step from the configuration reached:
`runFrom O cfg (t + 1) = step O (runFrom O cfg t)`, the oracle counterpart of
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'`. -/
theorem runFrom_succ_eq_step' (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    M.runFrom O cfg (t + 1) = M.step O (M.runFrom O cfg t) :=
  Function.iterate_succ_apply' _ _ _

/-- Oracle runs compose: running `a + b` steps is running `b` steps from the configuration
reached after `a`, under the same oracle (the counterpart of
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add`). -/
theorem runFrom_add (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (a b : ℕ) :
    M.runFrom O cfg (a + b) = M.runFrom O (M.runFrom O cfg a) b := by
  unfold runFrom
  rw [show a + b = b + a from Nat.add_comm a b, Function.iterate_add_apply]

/-- A halted configuration is fixed by every oracle run, under every oracle. -/
theorem runFrom_of_halt (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (h : cfg.state = none) {n : ℕ} :
    M.runFrom O cfg n = cfg :=
  Function.iterate_fixed (step_of_halt M O h) n

/-- **Time monotonicity**: if `M` with oracle `O` produces `out` from `x` within `t`
steps, it does so within any `t' ≥ t` steps, halting being absorbing (the oracle
counterpart of `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono`). [AB09, §3.4]

**Proof sketch.** Factor the run to `t'` through `t` (`runFrom_add`); the configuration
at `t` is halted, so `runFrom_of_halt` fixes it. -/
theorem ComputesInTime.mono {M : OracleTM k Symbol State} {O : Language Symbol}
    {x out : List Symbol} {t t' : ℕ} (h : M.ComputesInTime O x out t) (hle : t ≤ t') :
    M.ComputesInTime O x out t' := by
  obtain ⟨hh, ho⟩ := h
  have hrun : M.runFrom O (M.initCfg x) t' = M.runFrom O (M.initCfg x) t := by
    rw [← Nat.add_sub_of_le hle, runFrom_add, runFrom_of_halt M O _ hh]
  exact ⟨hrun ▸ hh, hrun ▸ ho⟩

/-- **Determinism of completed outputs**: relative to a fixed oracle, a machine has at
most one completed output on a given input; computations of `w` and of `w'` from `x`
force `w = w'`. [AB09, §3.4]

**Proof sketch.** Absorb both computations to the later time (`ComputesInTime.mono`);
both outputs are then the output of one and the same configuration. -/
theorem ComputesInTime.output_unique {M : OracleTM k Symbol State} {O : Language Symbol}
    {x w w' : List Symbol} {t t' : ℕ} (h : M.ComputesInTime O x w t)
    (h' : M.ComputesInTime O x w' t') : w = w' := by
  have h₁ := h.mono (Nat.le_max_left t t')
  have h₂ := h'.mono (Nat.le_max_right t t')
  rw [← h₁.2, ← h₂.2]

/-- **Run commutation from step commutation**: a map of configurations that commutes with
one oracle step of two machines (each under its own oracle) commutes with their runs,
the oracle counterpart of `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_comm_of_step`. -/
theorem runFrom_comm_of_step {k' : ℕ} {State' : Type*} {input' : List Symbol}
    {M : OracleTM k Symbol State} {M' : OracleTM k' Symbol State'} {O O' : Language Symbol}
    (f : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input → Cfg (k' + 1) Symbol State' input')
    (hstep : ∀ cfg, M'.step O' (f cfg) = f (M.step O cfg))
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (n : ℕ) :
    M'.runFrom O' (f cfg) n = f (M.runFrom O cfg n) :=
  (Function.Semiconj.iterate_right (fun c => (hstep c).symm) n cfg).symm

/-- **Oracle independence of query-free runs**, from any configuration: if the run with
oracle `O` never sits in `qQuery` before time `t`, its first `t` steps are the same under
every other oracle `O'`. [AB09, §3.4: the oracle is consulted only in the query state]

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `t`: equal configurations at time `s`, not in the query
state, take equal steps by `step_eq_of_ne_qQuery`. -/
theorem runFrom_eq_of_forall_ne_qQuery (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O O' : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (t : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ s < t, (M.runFrom O cfg s).state ≠ some M.qQuery) :
    M.runFrom O cfg t = M.runFrom O' cfg t := by
  induction t with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [runFrom_succ_eq_step', runFrom_succ_eq_step', ← ih (fun s hs => h s (by omega))]
    exact step_eq_of_ne_qQuery O O' (h t (by omega))

/-- A work-tape head moves by at most one cell in a single oracle step. -/
lemma workTapePos_step_le (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (i : Fin (k + 1)) :
    |(M.step O cfg).workTapePos i - cfg.workTapePos i| ≤ 1 := by
  unfold step
  split
  · simp
  · split
    · simp
    · exact workTapePos_apply_le _ cfg i

/-- An oracle step writes only at the old head position. -/
lemma workTapes_step_eq_of_ne (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    {cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input} (i : Fin (k + 1)) {z : ℤ}
    (hz : z ≠ cfg.workTapePos i) :
    (M.step O cfg).workTapes i z = cfg.workTapes i z := by
  unfold step
  split
  · rfl
  · split
    · rfl
    · exact Action.apply_workTapes_of_ne _ cfg i hz

/-- **The one-step radius bound** ([AB09, proof of Theorem 3.7]: a machine reaches at most
one new cell per step). If work head `i` is within distance `n` of the origin and every
cell of tape `i` at distance at least `n` is blank, then after one oracle step the head is
within `n + 1`, and every cell at distance at least `n + 1` is still blank. Shared by the
initialized invariants here and in `OracleNondeterministic`, and by the preloaded query
bound of `Build/OracleSim` (wave-1 statement gate, round 1, finding 2).

**Proof sketch.** The head moves by at most one cell (`workTapePos_step_le`), and the step
writes only at the old head (`workTapes_step_eq_of_ne`), which lies strictly inside the
radius `n + 1`. -/
theorem step_radius (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (i : Fin (k + 1)) (n : ℕ)
    (hpos : |cfg.workTapePos i| ≤ (n : ℤ))
    (hblank : ∀ z : ℤ, (n : ℤ) ≤ |z| → cfg.workTapes i z = none) :
    |(M.step O cfg).workTapePos i| ≤ ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ∧
      ∀ z : ℤ, ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ |z| → (M.step O cfg).workTapes i z = none := by
  refine ⟨?_, fun z hz => ?_⟩
  · have h1 := M.workTapePos_step_le O cfg i
    rw [abs_le] at h1 hpos ⊢
    push_cast
    omega
  · push_cast at hz
    have hne : z ≠ cfg.workTapePos i := by
      intro he
      rw [← he] at hpos
      omega
    rw [M.workTapes_step_eq_of_ne O i hne]
    exact hblank z (by omega)

/-- **The radius bound along a run**: from radius `n`, after `s` steps work head `i` is
within `n + s` of the origin, and every cell at distance at least `n + s` is blank.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `s`, with `runFrom_succ_eq_step'` and `step_radius`. -/
theorem runFrom_radius (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (i : Fin (k + 1)) (n : ℕ)
    (hpos : |cfg.workTapePos i| ≤ (n : ℤ))
    (hblank : ∀ z : ℤ, (n : ℤ) ≤ |z| → cfg.workTapes i z = none) (s : ℕ) :
    |(M.runFrom O cfg s).workTapePos i| ≤ ((n + s : ℕ) : ℤ) ∧
      ∀ z : ℤ, ((n + s : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ |z| → (M.runFrom O cfg s).workTapes i z = none := by
  induction s with
  | zero => exact ⟨hpos, hblank⟩
  | succ s ih =>
    rw [runFrom_succ_eq_step']
    exact M.step_radius O _ i (n + s) ih.1 ih.2

/-- The two run invariants of an initialized oracle run: after `t` steps every work
head is within distance `t` of the origin, and every cell at distance at least `t` is
still blank. -/
private lemma runFrom_workTapes_invariant (M : OracleTM k Symbol State)
    (O : Language Symbol) (x : List Symbol) : ∀ t : ℕ,
    (∀ i, |(M.runFrom O (M.initCfg x) t).workTapePos i| ≤ (t : ℤ)) ∧
    (∀ i (z : ℤ), (t : ℤ) ≤ |z| → (M.runFrom O (M.initCfg x) t).workTapes i z = none) := by
  intro t
  have h := fun i => M.runFrom_radius O (M.initCfg x) i 0 (by simp [initCfg])
    (fun z _ => by simp [initCfg]) t
  exact ⟨fun i => by simpa using (h i).1, fun i z hz => (h i).2 z (by simpa using hz)⟩

/-- **A blank query cell bounds the query**: if the query tape of any configuration is
blank at the nonnegative cell `n`, the extracted query has length at most `n`, extraction
stopping at the first blank. Promoted from a private lemma of
`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.OracleNondeterministic` (backlog C1-P1).

**Proof sketch.** The least blank exists, with witness `n`, and is at most `n`
(`Nat.find_le`); filtering the preceding range cannot increase its length. -/
theorem queryString_length_le_of_blank (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input)
    (n : ℕ) (h : cfg.workTapes (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx k) (n : ℤ) = none) :
    (OracleTM.queryString cfg).length ≤ n := by
  classical
  rw [OracleTM.queryString, dif_pos ⟨n, h⟩]
  refine (List.length_filterMap_le _ _).trans ?_
  simpa using (Nat.find_le (h := ⟨n, h⟩) h)

/-- **The extraction contract**: if the query tape holds the word `w` in cells
`0, …, |w| - 1` and is blank at cell `|w|`, the extracted query is exactly `w`, whatever
lies beyond cell `|w|` or at negative cells. [AB09, Definition 3.4, with this file's
extraction convention `queryString`]

**Proof sketch.** Cell `|w|` is the first blank, the earlier cells holding symbols; by
induction on `m ≤ |w|`, filtering the first `m` cells yields the length-`m` prefix of `w`.
(The definition lifts `List.range` into `ℤ` through the list monad, which is first
rewritten to a `List.map`.) -/
theorem queryString_eq_of_cells (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (w : List Symbol)
    (hw : ∀ i (hi : i < w.length), cfg.workTapes (queryTapeIdx k) (i : ℤ) = some w[i])
    (hb : cfg.workTapes (queryTapeIdx k) (w.length : ℤ) = none) :
    queryString cfg = w := by
  classical
  have hex : ∃ n : ℕ, cfg.workTapes (queryTapeIdx k) (n : ℤ) = none := ⟨w.length, hb⟩
  have hfind : Nat.find hex = w.length := by
    apply le_antisymm (Nat.find_min' hex hb)
    by_contra hlt
    push_neg at hlt
    have := Nat.find_spec hex
    rw [hw _ hlt] at this
    exact Option.some_ne_none _ this
  rw [queryString, dif_pos hex, hfind]
  have key : ∀ m ≤ w.length, (List.range m).filterMap
      (fun n : ℕ => cfg.workTapes (queryTapeIdx k) (n : ℤ)) = w.take m := by
    intro m
    induction m with
    | zero => intro _; simp
    | succ m ih =>
      intro hm
      rw [List.range_succ, List.filterMap_append, ih (by omega), List.take_succ,
        List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by omega)]
      simp [hw m (by omega)]
  have hmap : ∀ l : List ℕ,
      (do let a ← l; pure (a : ℤ) : List ℤ) = l.map (fun a : ℕ => (a : ℤ)) := by
    intro l; induction l with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons a l ih => simp only [List.map_cons] at ih ⊢; rw [← ih]; rfl
  rw [hmap, List.filterMap_map]
  exact (key w.length le_rfl).trans List.take_length

/-- In an initialized run, the query after `t` steps has length at most `t`. In
particular the no-blank fallback branch of `queryString` is unreachable from an initial
configuration.

**Proof sketch.** By induction on `t`, every write performed in the first `t` steps
happened at a head position of absolute value at most `t - 1` (heads start at `0` and
move at most one cell per step, `Turing.workTapePos_apply_le`). Hence cell `t` of the
query tape is still blank at time `t`, so the least-blank search in `queryString`
terminates at an index `≤ t`.

**C1-P1 appendix.** That last step is the shared blank-cell bound
`Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le_of_blank`. -/
theorem queryString_length_le (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (x : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) :
    (queryString (M.runFrom O (M.initCfg x) t)).length ≤ t :=
  queryString_length_le_of_blank _ t
    ((runFrom_workTapes_invariant M O x t).2 _ _ (le_abs_self _))

/-- In an initialized run, every work-tape cell at distance at least `t` from the
origin is still blank after `t` steps. This is the certificate that the no-blank
fallback branch of `queryString` is unreachable from initialization (the length bound
`queryString_length_le` alone does not certify this, since the fallback also returns a
short list).

**Proof sketch.** Simultaneous induction on `t` with the head-position bound
`|workTapePos i| ≤ t`: at `t = 0` all tapes are blank and heads are at `0`; an ordinary
step writes only at the *old* head position (of absolute value `≤ t`, hence `< t + 1`;
`Action.apply` writes before moving) and moves each head by at most one cell
(`Turing.workTapePos_apply_le`); oracle-answer and halted steps change no tape. -/
theorem runFrom_workTapes_blank (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (x : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 1)) (z : ℤ) (hz : (t : ℤ) ≤ |z|) :
    (M.runFrom O (M.initCfg x) t).workTapes i z = none :=
  (runFrom_workTapes_invariant M O x t).2 i z hz

/-! ### State relabelling of oracle machines -/

/-- Transport an oracle machine along a state equivalence: every distinguished state is mapped
forward, and the ordinary transition reads the table through the inverse (the oracle analogue of
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState`). -/
def relabel {S' : Type*} (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (e : State ≃ S') : OracleTM k Symbol S' where
  q₀ := e M.q₀
  qQuery := e M.qQuery
  qYes := e M.qYes
  qNo := e M.qNo
  tr q inp work := (M.tr (e.symm q) inp work).mapState e

/-! The relabelled machine's fields, as equations: generated by `simps` without the `simp`
attribute. -/
attribute [simps (config := { isSimp := false })] relabel

/-- Relabelling along an equivalence preserves well-formedness (injectivity keeps the three
distinguished states apart). -/
theorem relabel_wellFormed {S' : Type*} (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (e : State ≃ S')
    (wf : M.WellFormed) : (M.relabel e).WellFormed :=
  ⟨e.injective.ne wf.qQuery_ne_qYes, e.injective.ne wf.qQuery_ne_qNo, e.injective.ne wf.qYes_ne_qNo⟩

/-- Renaming the states keeps the query string. -/
theorem queryString_mapState {S' : Type*} (f : State → S') (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) :
    queryString (cfg.mapState f) = queryString cfg := by
  have hw : (cfg.mapState f).workTapes = cfg.workTapes := by
    funext i z
    rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapes]
  unfold queryString
  rw [hw]

/-- **One oracle step commutes with relabelling**, including the query-answer step and absorbing
halted configurations.

**Proof sketch.** Split the optional state. A halted configuration is fixed. At the query state,
injectivity identifies the same query branch; the query string ignores the state, and mapping the
answer commutes with its conditional. Elsewhere the inverse recovers the original table row, the
renamed configuration reads the same symbols, and `Turing.Cfg.mapState_apply` transports the
action. -/
theorem relabel_step {S' : Type*} (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (e : State ≃ S')
    (O : Language Symbol) (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) :
    (M.relabel e).step O (cfg.mapState e) = (M.step O cfg).mapState e := by
  classical
  have hin : (cfg.mapState e).inputSymbol = cfg.inputSymbol :=
    Cfg.inputSymbol_congr _ _ (by rw [Cfg.mapState_inputPos])
  have hwork : (cfg.mapState e).workTapeSymbols = cfg.workTapeSymbols := by
    funext i
    rw [Cfg.workTapeSymbols_eq, Cfg.workTapeSymbols_eq, Cfg.mapState_workTapePos,
      Cfg.mapState_workTapes]
  unfold OracleTM.step
  cases hs : cfg.state with
  | none => simp only [Cfg.mapState_state, hs, Option.map_none]
  | some q =>
    simp only [Cfg.mapState_state, hs, Option.map_some, relabel_qQuery, e.injective.eq_iff]
    by_cases hq : q = M.qQuery
    · rw [if_pos hq, if_pos hq]
      refine Cfg.ext ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
      · simp only [Cfg.mapState_state, queryString_mapState, relabel_qYes, relabel_qNo,
          Option.map_some, apply_ite e]
      · simp only [Cfg.mapState_inputPos]
      · funext i z
        simp only [Cfg.mapState_workTapes]
      · funext i
        simp only [Cfg.mapState_workTapePos]
      · simp only [Cfg.mapState_output]
    · rw [if_neg hq, if_neg hq, hin, hwork, relabel_tr, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
      exact Cfg.mapState_apply e _ cfg

/-- Runs from any configuration commute with relabelling. -/
theorem relabel_runFrom {S' : Type*} (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (e : State ≃ S')
    (O : Language Symbol) (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    (M.relabel e).runFrom O (cfg.mapState e) t = (M.runFrom O cfg t).mapState e :=
  runFrom_comm_of_step (Cfg.mapState e) (relabel_step M e O) cfg t

/-- **Relabelling preserves every time-bounded output verdict.**

**Proof sketch.** The relabelled initial configuration is the renamed one (`Cfg.init`'s and
`Cfg.mapState`'s field equations); run transport (`relabel_runFrom`) preserves the output, and
renaming preserves haltedness (`Option.map_eq_none_iff`). -/
theorem relabel_computesInTime {S' : Type*} (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (e : State ≃ S')
    (O : Language Symbol) (x out : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) :
    (M.relabel e).ComputesInTime O x out t ↔ M.ComputesInTime O x out t := by
  have hinit : (M.relabel e).initCfg x = (M.initCfg x).mapState e := by
    refine Cfg.ext ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · rw [Cfg.mapState_state, initCfg, initCfg, Cfg.init_state, Cfg.init_state, relabel_q₀,
        Option.map_some]
    · rw [Cfg.mapState_inputPos, initCfg, initCfg, Cfg.init_inputPos, Cfg.init_inputPos]
    · funext i z
      rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapes, initCfg, initCfg, Cfg.init_workTapes, Cfg.init_workTapes]
    · funext i
      rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapePos, initCfg, initCfg, Cfg.init_workTapePos, Cfg.init_workTapePos]
    · rw [Cfg.mapState_output, initCfg, initCfg, Cfg.init_output, Cfg.init_output]
  unfold ComputesInTime
  rw [hinit, relabel_runFrom, Cfg.mapState_state, Cfg.mapState_output, Option.map_eq_none_iff]

end OracleTM

/-- Extend an action on `k` work tapes to `k + 1` work tapes: the extra (last) tape is
neither written nor moved. -/
def Action.extend (a : Action k Symbol State) : Action (k + 1) Symbol State where
  inputTape := a.inputTape
  workTapes := fun i =>
    if h : (i : ℕ) < k then a.workTapes ⟨i, h⟩ else (none, 0)
  output := a.output
  state := a.state

/-- Embed a `k`-tape configuration into a `k + 1`-tape configuration over the extended
state type `State ⊕ Fin 3`: the extra work tape is blank with its head at `0`, and the
state is renamed along `Sum.inl`. -/
def Cfg.embedOracle (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    Cfg (k + 1) Symbol (State ⊕ Fin 3) input where
  state := cfg.state.map Sum.inl
  inputPos := cfg.inputPos
  workTapes := fun i =>
    if h : (i : ℕ) < k then cfg.workTapes ⟨i, h⟩ else fun _ => none
  workTapePos := fun i => if h : (i : ℕ) < k then cfg.workTapePos ⟨i, h⟩ else 0
  output := cfg.output

/-- The embedding preserves the scanned input symbol. -/
lemma Cfg.embedOracle_inputSymbol (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    cfg.embedOracle.inputSymbol = cfg.inputSymbol := rfl

/-- The embedding preserves the scanned work symbols on the original tapes. -/
lemma Cfg.embedOracle_workTapeSymbols (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (i : Fin k) :
    cfg.embedOracle.workTapeSymbols i.castSucc = cfg.workTapeSymbols i := by
  simp [Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Cfg.embedOracle]

/-- The embedding preserves haltedness. -/
lemma Cfg.embedOracle_state_eq_none {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} :
    cfg.embedOracle.state = none ↔ cfg.state = none := by
  simp [Cfg.embedOracle, Option.map_eq_none_iff]

/-- The embedding preserves the output tape. -/
lemma Cfg.embedOracle_output (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    cfg.embedOracle.output = cfg.output := rfl

/-- Applying an extended, state-renamed action to an embedded configuration is the
embedding of applying the original action. -/
lemma Cfg.embedOracle_apply (a : Action k Symbol State) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    ((a.mapState (Sum.inl : State → State ⊕ Fin 3)).extend).apply cfg.embedOracle =
      (a.apply cfg).embedOracle := by
  refine Cfg.ext ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · simp [Action.apply, Action.extend, Action.mapState, Cfg.embedOracle]
  · simp [Action.apply, Action.extend, Action.mapState, Cfg.embedOracle]
  · funext i
    by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < k
    · simp only [Action.apply, Action.extend, Action.mapState, Cfg.embedOracle,
        dif_pos hi]
    · simp only [Action.apply, Action.extend, Action.mapState, Cfg.embedOracle,
        dif_neg hi]
  · funext i
    by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < k
    · simp only [Action.apply, Action.extend, Action.mapState, Cfg.embedOracle,
        dif_pos hi]
    · simp only [Action.apply, Action.extend, Action.mapState, Cfg.embedOracle,
        dif_neg hi]
      simp
  · simp [Action.apply, Action.extend, Action.mapState, Cfg.embedOracle]

/-- The embedding sends initial configurations to initial configurations. -/
lemma Cfg.embedOracle_init (q₀ : State) (input : List Symbol) :
    (Cfg.init q₀ input : Cfg k Symbol State input).embedOracle =
      Cfg.init (Sum.inl q₀ : State ⊕ Fin 3) input := by
  refine Cfg.ext ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ <;> simp [Cfg.embedOracle]

namespace OracleTM

/-- Embed a plain machine as an oracle machine that never queries: the state type is
extended by three fresh states serving as `qQuery`, `qYes`, `qNo`, and the transition
function acts as before on original states (never moving into the fresh states, and
ignoring the query tape). The fresh states are unreachable from the initial
configuration. The *transition table* halts immediately from all three fresh states;
note that from `qQuery` itself the query override fires first (one answer step into
`qYes`/`qNo`, whose table entries then halt) — the table's `qQuery` row is dead code. -/
def ofMultiTapeTM (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) : OracleTM k Symbol (State ⊕ Fin 3) where
  q₀ := .inl tm.q₀
  qQuery := .inr 0
  qYes := .inr 1
  qNo := .inr 2
  tr q inp work :=
    match q with
    | .inl q => ((tm.tr q inp fun i => work i.castSucc).mapState Sum.inl).extend
    | .inr _ => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, none⟩

/-- The embedding of a plain machine is well-formed: its three fresh special states are
pairwise distinct by construction. -/
theorem ofMultiTapeTM_wellFormed (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) :
    (ofMultiTapeTM tm).WellFormed := by
  constructor <;> simp [ofMultiTapeTM]

/-- One step of an embedded plain machine, under any oracle, is the embedding of one
step of the original machine: the embedded state is never `qQuery = Sum.inr 0`, so the
oracle step reduces to applying the extended action, and `Cfg.embedOracle_apply` turns
that into the embedding of the original step. -/
lemma step_ofMultiTapeTM (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    (ofMultiTapeTM tm).step O cfg.embedOracle = (tm.step cfg).embedOracle := by
  unfold OracleTM.step MultiTapeTM.step
  cases hs : cfg.state with
  | none =>
    have h : cfg.embedOracle.state = none := by simp [Cfg.embedOracle, hs]
    rw [h]
  | some q =>
    have h : cfg.embedOracle.state = some (Sum.inl q) := by simp [Cfg.embedOracle, hs]
    rw [h]
    dsimp only
    have hne : (Sum.inl q : State ⊕ Fin 3) ≠ (ofMultiTapeTM tm).qQuery := by
      simp [ofMultiTapeTM]
    rw [if_neg hne]
    have hw : (fun i => cfg.embedOracle.workTapeSymbols i.castSucc) =
        cfg.workTapeSymbols :=
      funext fun i => Cfg.embedOracle_workTapeSymbols cfg i
    have htr : (ofMultiTapeTM tm).tr (Sum.inl q) cfg.embedOracle.inputSymbol
        cfg.embedOracle.workTapeSymbols =
        ((tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).mapState Sum.inl).extend := by
      show ((tm.tr q cfg.embedOracle.inputSymbol
        fun i => cfg.embedOracle.workTapeSymbols i.castSucc).mapState Sum.inl).extend = _
      rw [Cfg.embedOracle_inputSymbol, hw]
    rw [htr, Cfg.embedOracle_apply]

/-- **Sanity check for the oracle architecture** (plan §3.1): an embedded plain machine
runs in lockstep with the original under every oracle — `step_ofMultiTapeTM` pointwise,
then induction on `t`. -/
theorem runFrom_ofMultiTapeTM (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    (ofMultiTapeTM tm).runFrom O cfg.embedOracle t = (tm.runFrom cfg t).embedOracle := by
  induction t with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ t ih =>
    have h1 : (ofMultiTapeTM tm).runFrom O cfg.embedOracle (t + 1) =
        (ofMultiTapeTM tm).step O ((ofMultiTapeTM tm).runFrom O cfg.embedOracle t) :=
      Function.iterate_succ_apply' _ _ _
    rw [h1, ih, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', step_ofMultiTapeTM]

/-- An embedded plain machine has the same input/output behavior and time bounds as the
original, relative to every oracle. In particular its behavior is oracle-independent.

**Proof sketch.** `Cfg.embedOracle` sends the initial configuration of `tm` to the initial
configuration of the embedded machine (both have blank work tapes and heads at `0`); by
`runFrom_ofMultiTapeTM` the runs correspond, and `Cfg.embedOracle` preserves haltedness
and the output tape. -/
theorem computesInTime_ofMultiTapeTM (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (input output : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) :
    (ofMultiTapeTM tm).ComputesInTime O input output t ↔
      ((tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) t).state = none ∧
        (tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) t).output = output) := by
  have hinit : (ofMultiTapeTM tm).initCfg input = (tm.initCfg input).embedOracle := by
    simp only [OracleTM.initCfg, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, ofMultiTapeTM]
    exact (Cfg.embedOracle_init tm.q₀ input).symm
  simp only [OracleTM.ComputesInTime, hinit, runFrom_ofMultiTapeTM,
    Cfg.embedOracle_state_eq_none, Cfg.embedOracle_output]

open Classical in
/-- The converse of `ofMultiTapeTM` for the empty oracle: an oracle machine run with the
empty oracle is eliminated into a plain `k + 1`-tape machine over the *same* state type,
by replacing the query behavior with a stationary transition into `qNo` (the empty
oracle always answers no). (`audits/phase1-findings.md`, finding 8.) -/
noncomputable def plainEmptyOracle (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) :
    MultiTapeTM (k + 1) Symbol State where
  q₀ := M.q₀
  tr q inp work :=
    if q = M.qQuery then ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some M.qNo⟩
    else M.tr q inp work

/-- One step of the empty-oracle elimination coincides with one step of the oracle
machine on the empty oracle: on a halted configuration both sides are fixed; in state
`qQuery` the empty oracle answers `qNo` and the stationary action's `Action.apply`
changes only the state; elsewhere both sides apply the same transition-table action. -/
lemma step_plainEmptyOracle (M : OracleTM k Symbol State)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) :
    M.plainEmptyOracle.step cfg = M.step (0 : Language Symbol) cfg := by
  unfold MultiTapeTM.step OracleTM.step plainEmptyOracle
  cases hs : cfg.state with
  | none => rfl
  | some q =>
    dsimp only
    by_cases hq : q = M.qQuery
    · rw [if_pos hq, if_pos hq, if_neg (Language.notMem_zero _)]
      refine Cfg.ext ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ <;> simp [Action.apply]
    · rw [if_neg hq, if_neg hq]

/-- **Sanity check, converse direction**: the empty-oracle elimination runs in exact
lockstep with the oracle machine on the empty oracle — same configurations at every
step, from every starting configuration (`step_plainEmptyOracle` pointwise, then
induction on `t`). -/
theorem runFrom_plainEmptyOracle (M : OracleTM k Symbol State)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    -- `0` is the empty language (`Language`'s `Zero` instance)
    M.plainEmptyOracle.runFrom cfg t = M.runFrom (0 : Language Symbol) cfg t := by
  induction t with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ t ih =>
    have h1 : M.runFrom (0 : Language Symbol) cfg (t + 1) =
        M.step 0 (M.runFrom (0 : Language Symbol) cfg t) :=
      Function.iterate_succ_apply' _ _ _
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', h1, ih, step_plainEmptyOracle]

/-- **The transfer bridge**: while the run of the plain table `plainEmptyOracle` from `cfg`
avoids `qQuery`, the oracle run under *any* oracle `O` is that plain run. Hence the
plain-machine library contracts (W1 capture, the R1/R2 rows, the catalog) apply to an
oracle machine on the run segments where it does not query.

**Proof sketch.** The plain run is the run under the empty oracle
(`runFrom_plainEmptyOracle`); a run under the empty oracle that avoids `qQuery` is the
run under `O` (`runFrom_eq_of_forall_ne_qQuery`). -/
theorem runFrom_eq_plainEmptyOracle (M : OracleTM k Symbol State) (O : Language Symbol)
    (cfg : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol State input) (t : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ s < t, (M.plainEmptyOracle.runFrom cfg s).state ≠ some M.qQuery) :
    M.runFrom O cfg t = M.plainEmptyOracle.runFrom cfg t := by
  rw [runFrom_plainEmptyOracle]
  refine (runFrom_eq_of_forall_ne_qQuery M 0 O cfg t fun s hs => ?_).symm
  rw [← runFrom_plainEmptyOracle]
  exact h s hs

end OracleTM

end Turing

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan, Hydroxyi
-/
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Size
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Digits.Defs

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The binary length of a natural number

Machines and register programs store numbers as little-endian binary words `Nat.bits n` (least
significant bit first, no redundant zeros). This file is the one home of the elementary bounds on
the length `|Nat.bits n|` of such a word, below both the machine layer
(`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Encoding` imports it) and the register-program layer
(`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Bin` imports it). It imports no TCSlib module.

## Main definitions

None — this file states bounds on Mathlib's `Nat.bits` only.

## Main results

* `Turing.length_bits_le_self` — `|bits m| ≤ m`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le` — `|bits n| ≤ m` when `n < 2^m`;
  `Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_succ_le` — `|bits (m + 1)| ≤ e + 2` when `m ≤ 2^e + 1`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.lt_two_pow_bits` — `n < 2^{|bits n|}`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.two_pow_bits_le` — `2^{|bits L|} ≤ 2L` for `L ≥ 1`;
  `Complexity.LogProg.two_pow_bits_le_two_mul_add_one` — `2^{|bits n|} ≤ 2n + 1` for every `n`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_mono` — `|bits n|` is monotone in `n`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le_log` — `|bits n| ≤ ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1`;
  `Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_eq_log` — `|bits n| = ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1` for `n ≠ 0`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.ofDigits_lt_two_pow` — a word's `Nat.ofDigits` value is below
  `2^{length}`. (The `bitsVal` form, `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal_lt_two_pow`, stays with
  `bitsVal` in `Machines/Bin`.)

## Implementation notes

The declarations retain their names in the `Turing` and `Complexity.LogProg` namespaces so
that machine and register-program consumers keep their existing references. This module sits
below both layers and gives them a shared home for binary-length bounds.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1: counters in logarithmic space.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-- The binary expansion of `m` has at most `m` bits. -/
lemma length_bits_le_self (m : ℕ) : m.bits.length ≤ m := by
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len]
  exact Nat.size_le.mpr Nat.lt_two_pow_self

end Turing

namespace Complexity.LogProg

/-- The binary word of `n` has at most `m` letters when `n < 2^m`. -/
lemma length_bits_le {n m : ℕ} (h : n < 2 ^ m) : (Nat.bits n).length ≤ m := by
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len]
  exact Nat.size_le.mpr h

/-- A number `m ≤ 2 ^ e + 1` has at most `e + 2` binary digits after one increment: the width
bound for a register value `m` with `m ≤ 2 ^ e`.

**Proof sketch.** `m + 1 ≤ 2 ^ e + 2 < 4 · 2 ^ e = 2 ^ (e + 2)` since `2 ^ e ≥ 1`, then
`length_bits_le`. -/
lemma length_bits_succ_le {m e : ℕ} (h : m ≤ 2 ^ e + 1) : (Nat.bits (m + 1)).length ≤ e + 2 := by
  apply length_bits_le
  have : 2 ^ e + 2 < 2 ^ (e + 2) := by
    rw [pow_add]; have := Nat.one_le_two_pow (n := e); omega
  omega

/-- `n < 2^{|bits n|}`. -/
theorem lt_two_pow_bits (n : ℕ) : n < 2 ^ (Nat.bits n).length := by
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len]; exact Nat.lt_size_self n

/-- `2 ^ |bits L| ≤ 2L` for `L ≥ 1`.

**Proof sketch.** `|bits L| = Nat.size L ≥ 1`, and `2 ^ (Nat.size L - 1) ≤ L` (`Nat.size_le`), so
`2 ^ |bits L| = 2 · 2 ^ (Nat.size L - 1) ≤ 2L`. -/
lemma two_pow_bits_le (L : ℕ) (hL : 1 ≤ L) : 2 ^ (Nat.bits L).length ≤ 2 * L := by
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len]
  have hpos : 1 ≤ Nat.size L := Nat.size_pos.mpr (by omega)
  have hlt : ¬ L < 2 ^ (Nat.size L - 1) := by
    rw [← Nat.size_le]; omega
  have e : 2 ^ Nat.size L = 2 * 2 ^ (Nat.size L - 1) := by
    rw [← pow_succ']; congr 1; omega
  omega

/-- For every `n`, including `0`, two to the binary length of `n` is at most `2n + 1`:
`2 ^ |bits n| ≤ 2n + 1`. (Technical glue; the counter widths of [AB09, §4.1].)

**Proof sketch.** At `n = 0` the word is empty and `2 ^ 0 = 1`. Otherwise
`2 ^ |bits n| ≤ 2n` (`Complexity.LogProg.two_pow_bits_le`). -/
theorem two_pow_bits_le_two_mul_add_one (n : ℕ) : 2 ^ (Nat.bits n).length ≤ 2 * n + 1 := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
  · simp
  · exact (two_pow_bits_le n hn).trans (Nat.le_succ _)

/-- Binary words of larger numbers are not shorter. -/
lemma length_bits_mono {a b : ℕ} (h : a ≤ b) : (Nat.bits a).length ≤ (Nat.bits b).length := by
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len, Nat.size_eq_bits_len]; exact Nat.size_le_size h

/-- The binary word of `n` has at most `⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1` letters. -/
lemma length_bits_le_log (n : ℕ) : (Nat.bits n).length ≤ Nat.log 2 n + 1 :=
  length_bits_le (Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self (by norm_num) n)

/-- For `n ≠ 0`, the binary word of `n` has exactly `⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1` letters:
`|bits n| = Nat.log 2 n + 1`. (At `n = 0` the word is empty while the right side is `1`.)
(Technical glue; the logarithmic counter widths of [AB09, §4.1].)

**Proof sketch.** The upper bound is `Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le_log`. For the lower
bound, `|bits n| = Nat.size n`, and `2 ^ ⌊log₂ n⌋ ≤ n` since `n ≠ 0`, so
`⌊log₂ n⌋ < Nat.size n`. -/
theorem length_bits_eq_log {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : (Nat.bits n).length = Nat.log 2 n + 1 := by
  refine le_antisymm (length_bits_le_log n) ?_
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len]
  exact Nat.succ_le_of_lt (Nat.lt_size.mpr (Nat.pow_log_le_self 2 hn))

/-- A word `w` of `|w|` letters, read as a little-endian binary number
`Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)`, has value below `2 ^ |w|`. This is the `Nat.ofDigits` form
of `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal_lt_two_pow`. (Technical glue; the binary counters of
[AB09, §4.1].)

**Proof sketch.** Every digit `b.toNat` is below `2`, so Mathlib's
`Nat.ofDigits_lt_base_pow_length` applies, and mapping keeps the length. -/
theorem ofDigits_lt_two_pow (w : List Bool) :
    Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) < 2 ^ w.length := by
  have h := Nat.ofDigits_lt_base_pow_length (b := 2) (l := w.map Bool.toNat) (by norm_num)
    (by
      intro d hd
      obtain ⟨a, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hd
      cases a <;> decide)
  rwa [List.length_map] at h

end Complexity.LogProg
```
